Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
lu-xing-jiaozhi: 263 CE, Jiaozhi (Hanoi): a riverside government compound in the Red River delta; local soldiers swarm through the gate, the Wu governor's banners torn down, and a messenger boat sets off downstream with a sealed letter, palms and paddy fields around. Small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and green and ochre washes on silk.
zhong-hui-revolt: 264 CE, Chengdu: a palace compound inside the city walls at night; soldiers storm through the gates with torches, banners overturned, smoke rising above the halls as officers flee across the courtyards and Wei troops crowd the walls of the newly conquered Shu capital. Seen from a distance, no gore. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on pale ground.
liu-shan-happy-here: 264 CE, Luoyang: a banquet in a Wei mansion where musicians perform Shu music and dancers sway; the former Shu ruler, seen from behind in silk robes, laughs and raises his cup, while his former Shu officials at the side tables hide their tears and the host observes him. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral colour on aged silk.
sun-hao-enthroned: 264 CE, Jianye (Nanjing): ministers in wide-sleeved Wu robes escort a young prince up the steps of the palace hall to the throne; the courtyard is crowded with guards and banners, and beyond the walls the Yangtze and the Zhongshan hills. Small figures, figures seen from behind. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
sima-zhao-five-ranks: 264 CE, Luoyang: in a palace hall nobles in five grades of ceremonial dress and caps stand in ordered rows receiving tallies and jade insignia, while scholars at tables compile ritual and legal texts on bamboo slips. Formal, hierarchical composition, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and mineral red and green on aged silk.
sun-hao-wuchang: 265 CE, the Yangtze: a long convoy of boats laden with court officials, furniture, chests and soldiers is towed upstream against the current toward Wuchang on its hill, labourers hauling ropes on the riverbank, the cliffs and the wide river under a heavy sky. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey-blue washes on aged silk.
pei-xiu-maps: 267 CE, Luoyang: in an office of the Ministry of Works, a scholar-minister in robes and cap supervises clerks drawing a large map on silk, ruled with a square grid, rivers and mountains in ink, other sheets of maps spread across low tables, measuring cords and rods nearby. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
taishi-code: 268 CE, Luoyang: an official in a black court robe reads aloud from a long scroll at a palace gate to rows of officials and townspeople, clerks distributing copies of a law code written on paper and bamboo slips, banners of the new Jin dynasty overhead. Small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on pale ground.
yang-hu-xiangyang: 269 CE, Xiangyang on the Han River: a general in light robes rather than armour rides along a riverbank past soldiers farming wheat fields, granaries being filled, and across the river a Wu messenger delivering a gift of wine, the two sides' banners on opposite banks under a calm sky. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
tufa-shujineng-revolt: 270 CE, Liangzhou (Wuwei) in the Hexi corridor: Xianbei horsemen in fur caps and felt coats, riding without stirrups, sweep across a dry plain toward a Jin frontier town with rammed-earth walls, smoke rising from outlying farms, the snow-capped Qilian mountains behind. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick from Jiayuguan, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
battle-of-xiling: 272 CE, Xiling (Yichang) at the mouth of the Three Gorges: a riverside fortress on cliffs above the Yangtze surrounded by long new siege walls and ditches; Wu soldiers man the outer lines facing both inward and outward, while a Jin relief army halts on the northern hills and war boats patrol the river. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
wang-jun-fleet: 272 CE, a riverside shipyard near Chengdu: carpenters build huge towered warships with multi-storey wooden cabins, ramparts and gates on their decks, enough room for horses to ride; wood shavings float downstream on the Min River, timber piled on the banks, green hills of the Sichuan basin. Small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
bamboo-annals: 279 CE, Ji County (Weihui, Henan): an opened ancient tomb chamber of earth and timber, lit by burning bundles of bamboo slips used as torches; a robber's tools lie aside and officials and scholars in Jin robes later kneel to gather scattered black-inked bamboo slips into baskets. Small figures, dim interior. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and ochre on aged silk.
zhantian-system: 280 CE, the Luoyang plain: rural officials with measuring cords and registers mark out field plots for households beside a village of tiled and thatched houses; farmers bring bolts of silk and sacks of grain to a tax office, clerks recording on bamboo slips. Peaceful farmland, small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick from Jiayuguan showing farming and silk, quick ink and ochre on pale ground.
jin-disarms-provinces: 280 CE, a provincial commandery town: soldiers hand in spears, crossbows and armour at an arsenal gate, stacks of weapons being loaded onto carts, and men in plain tunics walking home along a road through fields; a prince's fortified mansion with armed retainers visible in the distance. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
liu-yi-nine-rank: 282 CE, Luoyang: in a palace hall an elderly official in a black gauze cap kneels before the throne dais presenting a long memorial scroll, while aristocrats in rich silk robes stand in the front ranks and humble scholars in plain robes stand far behind at the door. Small figures, emperor seen at a distance. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and mineral colour on aged silk.
shi-chong-wang-kai: 285 CE, Luoyang: a lavish garden of a magnate's estate, its avenue lined for a long distance with screens of brocade and silk; in a pavilion a servant has smashed a tall red coral tree on the floor while the host's servants bring out several even taller coral trees, guests in silk robes watching. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and red and green mineral colour on silk.
murong-hui-buyeo: 285 CE, Buyeo (Jilin City): a timber-palisaded capital beside the Songhua River in forested northeastern hills, set ablaze, smoke rising over thatched halls, while Xianbei horsemen in fur caps drive away captives and livestock along the riverbank. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and black outlines, lively horsemen on an ochre plaster ground.
sanguozhi: 290 CE, Luoyang: an elderly historian in a plain robe and cap sits in a quiet study writing with a brush on paper scrolls, bundles of older bamboo-slip records and silk documents piled around him, a candle burning, a window looking onto a bare winter tree. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
yang-jun-regency: 290 CE, Luoyang: a palace in white mourning for a dead emperor; in the hall a dignified elderly man in court robes stands beside the throne, guards with halberds lining the corridors, while officials crowd uneasily outside the closed inner gate. Small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
qi-wannian-rebellion: 296 CE, Guanzhong (Shaanxi): Di and Qiang warriors in felt cloaks and braided hair, with spears and horses, camp on loess hills above the Wei valley; below, long lines of famine refugees with carts and bundles trudge south toward the Qinling mountains. Wide panoramic view, small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick from the Hexi corridor, quick ink outlines with red and ochre on pale ground.
xi-rong-lun: 299 CE, Luoyang: an official in a scholar's cap writes a long essay at a low desk, a map of the northern frontier on silk unrolled beside him showing scattered tent encampments; through the window, a city street where Xiongnu, Di and Qiang people in their own dress mingle with Han townspeople. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
crown-prince-yu-deposed: 299 CE, Luoyang: a night scene in a palace chamber where a young prince, made drunk, sits slumped at a table with a brush and a sheet of paper while a palace lady stands beside him dictating; candles flicker, a shadowy figure watches from behind a screen. Small figures, no faces in close-up. Painted in the style of the Admonitions of the Instructress scroll attributed to Gu Kaizhi, fine line, soft colour on silk.
jia-nanfeng: 300 CE, Luoyang: soldiers with torches enter a palace at night through an opened gate, banners of a prince advancing across the courtyard, palace ladies fleeing along a covered gallery, a gilded carriage waiting to take someone away. Distant view, small figures, no violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral red on aged silk.
li-te-uprising: 301 CE, Mianzhu in the Sichuan basin: thousands of refugees from the north in ragged clothes camp in fields beside a road, then gather under a Di chief's banners with spears and farm tools, a government post burning in the distance, bamboo groves and misty mountains. Wide view, small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on pale ground.
zhang-gui-liangzhou: 301 CE, Guzang (Wuwei): a prosperous walled oasis city in the Hexi corridor, its governor's compound orderly, farmers ploughing irrigated fields, camel caravans arriving at the gate, schools in session, the snowy Qilian range behind. Calm frontier scene, small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick from Jiayuguan, lively ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
princes-against-lun: 301 CE, the plains around Luoyang: three separate armies with different banners converge on the capital from north, east and west, camps and columns spread over the countryside, smoke over battlefields, and in the city a gate opens to welcome a returning emperor's carriage. Distant panoramic view, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
zhang-chang-rebellion: 303 CE, Anlu in Jing province: rebels wearing red headcloths, many of them escaped conscripts with spears and farm tools, march along a river road past rice paddies toward a walled county town, while far behind government troops gather under banners on a hill. Small figures, wide view. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral red on aged silk.
lu-ji-executed: 303 CE, near Luoyang: a defeated army camp at dusk, broken banners on the ground; a southern poet in a scholar's robe, seen from behind, sits alone outside his tent gazing at a flock of cranes flying south across a red evening sky, guards waiting nearby. No violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale vermilion on aged silk.
han-zhao: 304 CE, Lishi (Shanxi): on a loess plateau, a great gathering of Xiongnu horsemen in fur-trimmed coats and Han-style officials surrounds an earthen altar, a ruler in robes seen from behind ascending it under banners, felt tents and wagons spread across the valley, the Yellow River gorge in the distance. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
li-xiong-cheng-han: 304 CE, Chengdu: a ruler in simple robes, seen from behind, receives local elders and farmers in a modest palace courtyard; outside, peaceful fields and markets of the Sichuan basin, farmers carrying light tax baskets, Daoist recluses on a nearby mountain. Calm prosperous scene, small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on pale ground.
battle-of-dangyin: 304 CE, Dangyin (Tangyin, Henan): a routed imperial army on a plain, soldiers scattering, banners fallen; amid the chaos a single imperial carriage with a torn canopy stands abandoned in a field, an emperor in robes, seen from behind, sitting alone beside it as enemy horsemen approach. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
wang-dao-jianye: 307 CE, Jianye (Nanjing): a procession in the riverside city, a prince in a canopied sedan with a dignified adviser riding beside him, northern émigré officials in tall caps following; local southern gentry in wide-sleeved robes line the road and bow from the roadside, willows and the Qinhuai river behind. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
fotudeng-arrives: 310 CE, Luoyang: a foreign monk from Kucha in a patched robe, seen from behind, stands before a basin of water in a courtyard as a lotus blossom miraculously rises from it, a crowd of soldiers and townspeople in northern dress staring; a pagoda and city walls in the background. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite and lapis on plaster.
battle-of-ningping: 311 CE, Ningping (Dancheng, Henan): a vast flat plain where an army escorting a draped funeral cart is completely ringed by galloping cavalry, a circle of horsemen with bows around the stalled column, dust rising in a huge cloud. Seen from far above, small figures, no gore. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on pale ground.
zu-ti: 313 CE, the Yangtze at Jingkou: a general in armour stands at the prow of a boat crossing the wide river northward, striking his oar against the side in a vow, a small band of followers and a few boats behind, the southern shore receding in the morning mist. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale blue-grey washes on aged silk.
sogdian-ancient-letters: 313 CE, a frontier watch post near Dunhuang: a Sogdian merchant in a belted red kaftan and pointed felt cap sits at a low table in a mud-brick watchtower, sealing a folded paper letter in a silk pouch; outside, resting camels with bales, a beacon tower and a long rammed-earth wall crossing the desert under a pale sky. Painted in the manner of a Sogdian wall painting from Panjakent, rich reds and blues, fine contours.
shi-le-captures-wang-jun: 314 CE, Jicheng (Beijing): Shi Le's horsemen ride in through the open city gate driving herds of cattle and sheep as gifts, while guards stand aside; inside the walls soldiers suddenly surround a lord's mansion. Wide view of a northern city in winter, small figures, no violence shown. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red ochre on plaster.
tuoba-yilu-dai: 315 CE, Shengle (Horinger, Inner Mongolia): on open grassland near the Yin mountains, a Tuoba chief in a Xianbei hood with flaps, seen from behind, receives Jin envoys in robes who present a seal and title; felt tents, horse herds and mounted warriors spread across the steppe. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, quick ink and red ochre on plaster.
fall-of-changan-316: 316 CE, Chang'an: a starving, ruined city in winter; outside the eastern gate a young emperor in a plain carriage drawn by a sheep, bare-shouldered and holding a jade seal, comes out to surrender to a Han Zhao army camped before the walls. Figures small and seen from a distance. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey washes on aged silk.
ge-hong: 317 CE, a mountain near Jurong (Jiangsu): a Daoist scholar in a simple robe tends a clay alchemical furnace and crucibles in a cave beside a pine forest, herbs drying on racks, a scroll and brush on a rock, mist rolling over the hills. Small figure. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral green on aged silk.
liu-kun-killed: 318 CE, Jicheng (Beijing): a loyalist general in plain robes, seen from behind, stands at a window of a guarded room looking at the moon, a flute laid on the table; Xianbei guards in fur caps stand at the door. Quiet, ominous scene, no violence shown. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
jin-zhun-coup: 318 CE, Pingyang (Linfen): smoke rises over a palace compound inside a walled city in the Fen River valley; soldiers storm the gates, and two armies with different banners approach from the hills on either side. Distant panoramic view, small figures, no gore. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, quick ink outlines with red and ochre on plaster.
later-zhao-founded: 319 CE, Xiangguo (Xingtai): a Jie ruler in robes and a soft cap, seen from behind, receives the homage of officials and armoured cavalry in a palace courtyard; nobles of different peoples in kaftans and robes kneel in rows, banners in the wind, the Taihang mountains behind. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
zu-ti-dies: 321 CE, Yongqiu (Henan): a frontier camp at dusk, a general's tent with a lamp lit inside, and soldiers ploughing recovered fields around it; above, a strange star blazes in the western sky, and farmers in the fields look up in sorrow. No body shown. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale vermilion on aged silk.
wang-dun: 322 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a rebel army with banners advances downriver in a fleet of warships and lands at the Stone City fortress on the Yangtze; palace guards line the walls, and officials in tall caps watch anxiously from the city gate. Distant view, small figures. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
su-jun-rebellion: 327 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): smoke rises over the palace quarter of the capital, rebel soldiers crowd the streets, and on the river a great coalition fleet with banners approaches from upstream. Townspeople flee across the Zhuque pontoon bridge over the Qinhuai. Small figures, seen from far above, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey washes on aged silk.
shi-le-liu-yao: 328 CE, west of Luoyang: two great armies clash on a plain below the city, cavalry in lamellar armour with early single stirrups charging, and in the midst a commander's horse falling on the ice of a frozen stream as soldiers close in. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, quick ink outlines with red and ochre on plaster.
later-zhao-destroys-former-zhao: 329 CE, Shanggui (Tianshui): a walled city in the loess hills of eastern Gansu, its gates opened to a besieging army of cavalry and infantry under banners, smoke rising from the palace, refugees streaming out along a valley road. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
shi-hu-capital-ye: 335 CE, Ye: a vast new palace complex under construction, with towering terraces, gilded roofs and colonnades; thousands of labourers carry timber and earth, and outside the city a royal hunting park with a great mounted hunt chasing deer across the plain. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red ochre and green on plaster.
former-yan-founded: 337 CE, Jicheng (Chaoyang, Liaoning): in a timber palace hall on the Daling River, a Xianbei ruler in a Han-style robe and cap, seen from behind, accepts the title of king while armoured Murong cavalry with horse armour stand outside in ranks, rolling hills beyond. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and black outlines on an ochre plaster ground.
shiyijian-dai: 338 CE, Shengle (Horinger): on the grassland, a new settlement of earthen walls and timber halls rises beside felt tents; a Tuoba ruler in a Xianbei hood presides as officials record laws on scrolls, and herds of horses graze along the river below the Yin mountains. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
yan-sacks-hwando: 342 CE, Hwando (Ji'an): Xianbei armoured cavalry with stirrups and horse armour pour over a mountain fortress wall, smoke rising from the burnt palace, while a long train of captives, carts and treasure leaves along the Yalu valley; an opened burial mound on the hillside. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and black outlines on ochre plaster.
huan-wen-shu: 347 CE, Chengdu: an Eastern Jin army that has sailed up the Yangtze gorges stands before the walls of Chengdu; the gate opens and the Cheng ruler, bound with his hands behind and a coffin carried behind him in token of surrender, walks out with his officials. Small figures, no faces. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
ran-min: 350 CE, Ye: the palace gates of a great northern city shut, soldiers seizing the walls, smoke rising over the city, and crowds fleeing out of the gates onto the frozen plain. Seen from far away, symbolic and calm, no gore, no bodies. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on plaster.
former-qin-founded: 351 CE, Chang'an: Di horsemen in felt cloaks and lamellar armour ride through the gates of the old Han capital, its ancient walls partly ruined; on a hill an altar with banners where a Di chief in robes, seen from behind, is proclaimed Heavenly King, crowds on the plain below. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
ran-min-captured: 352 CE, Liantai (Wuji, Hebei): a flat plain where heavily armoured Xianbei cavalry, horses linked together by chains, form a solid square, encircling a small band of infantry and one rider on a red horse. Distant view, dust and banners, no gore. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on plaster.
huan-wen-first-expedition: 354 CE, Bashang outside Chang'an: an Eastern Jin army camped by the Ba River, its tents and banners on the bank; local elders bring ox-meat and wine to welcome the soldiers, and in a tent a scholar in a coarse robe sits talking with a general, casually picking lice from his collar. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
huan-wen-recovers-luoyang: 356 CE, Luoyang: the overgrown ruins of the old capital beside the Luo and Yi rivers; Jin soldiers restore grassy imperial burial mounds, planting trees and repairing spirit-path stones, while an army camp lies beyond the broken walls. Melancholy autumn landscape, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
fu-jian-wang-meng: 357 CE, Chang'an: in a timber palace hall a Di ruler in Han-style robes, seen from behind, sits across a low table from a Han Chinese scholar in a plain robe and cap, both leaning over scrolls of laws and maps; outside, officials and Di nobles in kaftans wait in the courtyard. Calm reforming mood, small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red ochre and green on plaster.
gengxu-tuduan: 364 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): in a county office courtyard clerks at long tables enter names into household registers on paper scrolls while lines of northern émigré families in travel-worn robes wait their turn, and young men are measured for military service; tiled roofs and willows around. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
fangtou: 369 CE, Fangtou (Xun County, Henan): a long Jin river fleet stranded in a shallow, dried-up canal near the Yellow River, boats being burned by their own crews, while soldiers retreat overland and Xianbei armoured cavalry close in from the plain under a hot summer sky. Distant view, smoke and dust, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and ochre washes on aged silk.
former-qin-conquers-yan: 370 CE, Ye: Former Qin cavalry and infantry stand before the gates of the Former Yan capital; the gates are open and a procession of Xianbei nobles in robes and hoods comes out to surrender, a carriage in the middle, captured banners laid on the ground. Small figures, wide northern plain. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on plaster.
huan-wen-deposes-emperor: 371 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a palace courtyard where an emperor in plain white robes, seen from behind, walks out of the main hall and boards a simple ox-cart, while a powerful general's armoured guards line the steps and officials in tall caps stand silent. Small figures, subdued autumn light. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
former-qin-takes-shu: 373 CE, the mountain roads to Sichuan: a Former Qin army with banners crosses the Jianmen pass along cliffside plank roads, the green Chengdu plain opening beyond, a walled city in the distance with its gates open. Panoramic mountain landscape, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral blue-green on aged silk.
former-qin-unites-north: 376 CE, Chang'an: a great audience hall where envoys and nobles from many northern peoples, Xianbei in hoods, Qiang in felt cloaks, Han officials in robes, and men from the western oases, kneel in long rows with tribute, a ruler seen at a distance on the dais. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red ochre and green on plaster.
beifu-army: 377 CE, Jingkou (Zhenjiang) on the Yangtze: tough northern refugee recruits in short tunics drill with spears and shields on a parade ground below a riverside fort, a general in armour watching from a platform, boats moored on the river and green hills behind. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
siege-of-xiangyang-378: 378 CE, Xiangyang on the Han River: a walled city under siege, and at one corner an elderly woman leads a group of women and maids building a second inner wall with baskets of earth, while soldiers defend the outer wall above the river. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
gu-kaizhi: 380 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a painter in a loose robe kneels on a mat before a long silk handscroll on a low table, brush raised to dot the eyes of a slender figure, servants grinding ink and mixing mineral pigments, scrolls and an incense burner around, a bamboo garden outside. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll itself, fine continuous gossamer line, delicate colour on aged silk.
lu-guang-western-expedition: 382 CE, Kucha in the Tarim basin: a Former Qin army with banners and baggage camels approaches an oasis city with mud-brick walls and Buddhist stupas, poplars and irrigated fields around it, the Tianshan mountains behind; later a column leaves eastward with a monk riding among the troops. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Kizil cave mural from Kucha, lapis blue and malachite green on plaster, diamond-pattern mountains.
later-yan-founded: 384 CE, Zhongshan (Dingzhou, Hebei): a Xianbei general in a hood and lamellar armour, seen from behind, raises the old Yan banner before a gathering of Murong warriors and armoured cavalry, while a Former Qin garrison withdraws over the plain; a walled city in the distance. Small figures. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink outlines with red and ochre washes on plaster.
fu-jian-killed: 385 CE, Xinping (Bin County, Shaanxi): a small Buddhist temple in the loess hills, its gate surrounded by Qiang soldiers in felt cloaks; inside, a defeated ruler in robes sits alone before an image of the Buddha, seen from behind. Dusk, quiet and ominous, no violence shown. Rendered like a Sixteen Kingdoms tomb mural from Jiuquan, ink and red ochre on plaster.
northern-wei-founded: 386 CE, Shengle (Horinger): a gathering of Xianbei chiefs on the grassland near the Yin mountains, horsemen in hooded caps and kaftans around an earthen altar where a young chief, seen from behind, is proclaimed king; felt tents, horse herds and banners stretch to the horizon. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
later-liang-founded: 386 CE, Guzang (Wuwei): a returning army with thousands of camels laden with treasures from the Western Regions and a captive elephant enters the gates of an oasis city in the Hexi corridor, a Kuchean monk riding in the column; the snowy Qilian range behind. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite green and lapis on plaster.
battle-of-canhe: 395 CE, Canhe Slope (Inner Mongolia): at dawn, Northern Wei cavalry appear on a ridge above a Later Yan army camped in a frozen valley beside a lake, the camp waking in panic. Distant panoramic view of rolling steppe, small figures, no gore and no prisoners shown. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
northern-liang-founded: 397 CE, Zhangye in the Hexi corridor: rebel horsemen of the Lushui Hu in felt hats and kaftans gather in an oasis outside a walled frontier town, raising banners around a Han official in robes who is placed at their head; poplar trees, irrigated fields and the Qilian mountains behind. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite and lapis on plaster.
wang-gong-revolt: 397 CE, Jingkou (Zhenjiang): an army camps by the Yangtze under banners, and a mounted general rides out at the head of the Beifu troops; across the field another column turns away as its commander changes sides. Small figures, wide view of river and hills. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
pingcheng-capital: 398 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): a new capital rising on a windswept northern plain, labourers building rammed-earth walls and timber palace halls, long columns of resettled farmers and craftsmen with carts arriving, Xianbei horsemen in hooded caps guarding them. Small figures, panoramic view. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
faxian: 399 CE, leaving Chang'an: an elderly monk in a patched robe and straw sandals walks west with a few companions carrying staffs and bundles of supplies, crossing a desert of shifting dunes toward distant snowy mountains, a beacon tower on the horizon. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, malachite green and lapis blue, flaking pigment texture.
sun-en: 399 CE, Kuaiji coast (Shaoxing): a rebel fleet of small boats with Daoist banners sweeps along a rocky Zhejiang shore, peasants with farm tools climbing aboard, coastal villages and paddy fields behind, distant island hills. Thatched fishing huts and a burning county office on the shore. Wide seascape, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-green washes on aged silk.
western-liang-founded: 400 CE, Dunhuang: a Han governor in robes, seen from behind, opens a new school hall in the oasis city, boys bowing to teachers, while outside farmers dig irrigation channels among wheat fields and poplars, the Mingsha dunes and Buddhist caves on the cliffs beyond. Small figures. Rendered like a Wei-Jin painted tomb brick from Dunhuang, quick ink outlines with red and ochre washes on a pale ground.
kumarajiva: 401 CE, Chang'an: a vast translation hall where hundreds of monks sit in rows with brushes and paper scrolls, and at the front a Kuchean monk in a dark robe, seen from behind, reads aloud from a Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscript; scribes write, assistants compare texts. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, earthy red, malachite green and lapis on plaster.
huiyuan-lushan: 402 CE, Mount Lu (Jiujiang): the Donglin Temple below misty peaks and waterfalls, a stream with a small stone bridge, and inside a hall a large group of monks and lay scholars kneel before an image of Amitabha Buddha, making a vow together. Small figures, pines and clouds. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral green on aged silk.
huan-xuan-usurps: 403 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): banners of a new state hang over the palace gate as officials in tall caps file into the throne hall; an abdicating emperor, seen from behind, departs by a side gate in a plain carriage. Small figures, grey wintry sky. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
liu-yu-jingkou: 404 CE, Jingkou (Zhenjiang): at dawn a small band of officers and soldiers bursts out of the riverside town, seizing the fort, then marches along the Yangtze toward Jiankang with banners raised, townspeople joining. Small figures, river and hills in the background. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
tao-yuanming: 405 CE, Xunyang (Jiujiang): a poet in a plain robe walks home along a country path toward a thatched farmhouse by a stream, chrysanthemums by the eastern fence, willows at the gate, a boy waiting, Mount Lu rising softly behind. Peaceful autumn evening, small figure. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
helian-bobo-xia: 407 CE, Tongwan (Jingbian, Shaanxi): on the edge of the Ordos sands, labourers build massive white-plastered rammed-earth walls and towers for a new capital, a Xiongnu ruler on horseback, seen from behind, inspecting the work as an overseer tests the hardness of the wall with an awl. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
southern-yan: 410 CE, Guanggu (Qingzhou, Shandong): a hilltop fortress city ringed by siege lines; Jin soldiers raise tall siege towers and scale ladders while defenders on the walls hold out, and at last the gates open. Distant panoramic view of Shandong hills, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
faxian-returns: 412 CE, Laoshan (Qingdao): a weather-battered merchant ship with matting sails lands on a rocky Shandong shore after a long voyage; an aged monk with a bundle of palm-leaf texts steps onto the beach, local hunters watching from the pines, the Laoshan granite peaks behind. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-green washes on aged silk.
yixi-tuduan: 413 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): officials with registers inspect a great estate, counting farmhouses and tenants hidden on the land, clerks writing on paper scrolls; at the estate gate, armed guards lead away its magnate in robes. Small figures, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
western-shu-conquered: 413 CE, Chengdu: an Eastern Jin army arrives by the Min River through the hills, banners advancing toward the city walls, while defenders abandon the ramparts and townspeople open the gates. Farmers in the paddy fields pause to watch the long column pass. Small figures, green Sichuan landscape. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral blue-green on aged silk.
gwanggaeto-stele: 414 CE, Guonei (Ji'an, Jilin): a massive rough-hewn stone stele, about six metres tall, stands on a plain beside the Yalu River near a great stepped stone tomb; Goguryeo officials in feathered caps and long robes gather for its dedication, mountains behind. Surface of the stele left plain, no legible writing. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and black outlines on ochre plaster.
liu-yu-changan: 417 CE, Chang'an: an Eastern Jin army enters the gates of the old capital after sailing up the Wei River in covered boats, the boats moored on the riverbank, banners on the walls, townspeople kneeling in welcome, the Qinling mountains in the distance. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
queyue-formation: 417 CE, north bank of the Yellow River (Hua County, Henan): a crescent-shaped line of a hundred wagons with shields and crossbows, its two horns resting on the river, while Northern Wei cavalry charge against it and fall back under volleys of bolts; boats on the river behind. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and ochre on aged silk.
xia-takes-changan: 418 CE, Chang'an: Xia cavalry in felt caps and lamellar armour with stirrups ride up to the walls, while a southern army's banners retreat east along the Wei River valley; smoke rises from camps. Distant panoramic view of the Guanzhong plain, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
xie-lingyun-landscape: 422 CE, Yongjia (Wenzhou): an aristocrat poet in a loose robe and wooden clogs with removable teeth climbs a mountain path among pines and waterfalls, servants carrying a zither and wine behind him, mist-shrouded peaks and a river winding toward the sea. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral green on aged silk.
wei-takes-hulao: 423 CE, Hulao (Xingyang, Henan): a fortress pass on a loess cliff above the Yellow River, besieged by Northern Wei armies whose camps cover the hills; soldiers have tunnelled to cut the defenders' well, and banners finally rise over the walls. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
emperor-shao-deposed: 424 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): at dawn soldiers enter a palace garden where a boat for pleasure outings is moored by an artificial lake; a youthful emperor is escorted away along a corridor, while a procession sets out upriver to fetch a new emperor. Small figures, no violence. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
wei-takes-tongwan: 427 CE, Tongwancheng (Jingbian, Shaanxi): the white walls of a fortress city on the edge of the Ordos sands; Northern Wei cavalry with stirrups and armour turn back in a feigned retreat, drawing out a Xia army, then wheel round as a sandstorm blows across the field. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
taiwu-crushes-rouran: 429 CE, the Mongolian steppe: vast Northern Wei cavalry columns sweep across grassland, Rouran felt tents abandoned, and immense herds of horses, cattle and sheep being driven south across the plain under a huge sky. Distant panoramic view, small figures, no gore. Rendered in the style of a Northern Wei tomb mural, red and black outlines on a pale plaster ground.
shishuo-xinyu: 430 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a prince in a loose robe sits in a garden pavilion surrounded by scholars and secretaries copying anecdotes onto paper scrolls, others lounging, holding fly-whisks and laughing, wine cups and a zither on a mat, bamboo and rocks around. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief like the Seven Sages bricks, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
dao-yanzhi-expedition: 430 CE, Huatai (Hua County, Henan): a retreating southern army camp at night; soldiers measure out heaps of sand in baskets, pouring a thin layer of rice on top to fool watching enemy scouts on a distant hill, while the army packs up to withdraw. Small figures, lamplight. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and ochre washes on aged silk.
xia-destroyed: 431 CE, the Yellow River near Linxia (Gansu): a Xia army crosses the river on rafts and inflated-skin boats, and in the middle of the crossing Tuyuhun horsemen in felt hats ambush them from the cliffs and riverbank. Distant view of mountains and a broad river, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
northern-yan-destroyed: 436 CE, Longcheng (Chaoyang, Liaoning): the palace of a walled city is on fire, smoke rising, while a long column of people and carts flees east toward the mountains escorted by Goguryeo horsemen in feathered caps, and Northern Wei cavalry approach from the west. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and black outlines on ochre plaster.
tan-daoji-executed: 436 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a veteran general in plain robes, seen from behind, is led out of a palace gate by guards, his cap thrown to the ground beside him, while on the northern horizon beyond the Yangtze the sky darkens. No violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey washes on aged silk.
four-academies: 438 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): four separate school halls near Jilong Hill, in each a teacher in a scholar's cap lecturing to students on mats with scrolls, one hall with classics, one with Daoist texts, one with histories, one with poems; willows and courtyards between. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
kou-qianzhi-taoism: 440 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): a tall Daoist altar terrace of several tiers rises in the capital, banners and incense smoke around it; a Daoist master in a crown and patterned robe leads a ceremony while an emperor in Xianbei-style robes, seen from behind, receives talismanic registers, ranks of officials kneeling. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
juqu-gaochang: 442 CE, Gaochang (Turpan): survivors of a northern state ride with camels and carts through a scorching desert toward a mud-brick oasis city below the red Flaming Mountains, vineyards and poplars around the walls, Buddhist stupas inside. Small figures, heat haze. Painted in the style of a Turfan Buddhist cave mural from Bezeklik, warm reds and blues on plaster, fine contours.
yuanjia-calendar: 443 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): an astronomer in a scholar's robe stands on an observation terrace at night beside a bronze armillary sphere and a gnomon, assistants with counting rods and paper charts recording the moon's positions, a full moon over the city roofs. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and deep blue washes on aged silk.
hou-han-shu: 445 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a historian in a black gauze cap sits writing at a desk piled with paper scrolls and older chronicles, a lamp casting light in a book-lined study, while outside the window guards approach through the courtyard at dusk. No violence shown. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
gai-wu-rebellion: 445 CE, Guanzhong (Shaanxi): a huge rebel host of Lushui Hu and local peasants in felt caps and tunics gathers in the loess hills with spears and banners, while in Chang'an soldiers searching a Buddhist monastery carry out bundles of hidden bows and spears from the halls. Two scenes, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
taiwu-persecution: 446 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): a Buddhist temple with its gate broken open, soldiers carrying out bronze and clay Buddha images and scrolls, smoke rising from a burning pagoda, monks in robes being led away to lay life, townspeople watching sadly. Distant view, no violence or bodies. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite and lapis, flaking plaster.
yuanjia-campaign: 450 CE, Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze opposite Jiankang: Northern Wei cavalry with stirrups and armoured horses camp along the riverbank, their tents and banners stretching for miles, while across the wide river the southern capital's walls bristle with defenders and warships. Small figures, wide view. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
cui-hao: 450 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): beside a main road, large stone tablets carved with a state history stand in a row, while Xianbei nobles in hooded caps and kaftans gather angrily before them; a Han minister in court robes is led away by guards. Surfaces of the tablets left blank, no legible writing, no violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, cinnabar and yellow on black.
siege-of-xuyi: 451 CE, Xuyi on the Huai River: a hilltop city with strong walls besieged by a Northern Wei army in winter; siege hooks and battering rams strike the walls while defenders above drop logs and hold firm, the Wei camps across the frozen river plain. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey washes on aged silk.
taiwu-assassinated: 452 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): a dark palace corridor at night with lanterns, a lone eunuch in palace robes slipping away from a closed bedchamber door, guards asleep at their posts, the palace roofs under a cold moon. No violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
wencheng-restores-buddhism: 452 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): monks in robes return to a rebuilt temple, carrying bronze images and scrolls through a newly painted gate, a young emperor's procession in Xianbei dress arriving with offerings, a pagoda rising behind and townspeople bowing. Small figures, joyful scene. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite green and lapis.
liu-shao-patricide: 453 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): before dawn, armed soldiers stream through the palace gates with torches, palace attendants fleeing across courtyards, and the lamps of the emperor's hall glowing in the dark. A crown prince's banner is carried at the head of the column. Distant view, small figures, no violence or bodies shown. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
liu-yixuan-revolt: 454 CE, the Yangtze below Jiangling: a great rebel fleet with banners sails downriver and meets government warships at Liangshan, where the river narrows between hills; boats clash and the rebel fleet scatters, smoke drifting over the water. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-grey washes on aged silk.
sasanian-embassy: 455 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): Persian envoys in belted tunics, trousers and crenellated caps lead camels to a Northern Wei palace gate, carrying silver bowls and ewers with hunting scenes, glass vessels and textiles; Xianbei officials in hooded caps receive them. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures, Sasanian silver motifs.
zu-chongzhi: 462 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a mathematician in a scholar's robe sits on a mat surrounded by rows of red and black counting rods laid out in long calculations, a large circle with inscribed polygons drawn on a board, a water clock and calendar charts nearby, students watching. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
empress-dowager-feng-regency: 466 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): an empress dowager in rich layered robes and headdress sits behind a curtain screen in a palace hall, seen only as a silhouette, while officials in Xianbei and Han dress kneel before her and guards lead a disgraced minister away. Small figures, no violence. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures.
yijia-war: 466 CE, Xunyang (Jiujiang): rival fleets with different banners face each other on the Yangtze near Mount Lu, armies camped on both shores, one fleet advancing and the other in disarray. Distant panoramic view of river and mountains, small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
wei-takes-huaibei: 469 CE, Dongyang (Qingzhou, Shandong): a walled city in the Shandong hills surrounded by a Northern Wei army with armoured cavalry and siege towers; the gates open after a long siege and a column of captives and officials files out. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
xianwen-abdicates: 471 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): in a palace hall a young man in imperial robes, seen from behind, steps down from the throne as a small boy in miniature imperial robes is led up the dais by officials; Xianbei nobles and Han ministers kneel in rows. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Yungang-period cave mural, red ochre, malachite and white on plaster.
cangwu-murdered: 477 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a single night scene outside a palace, the great gate standing open, guards holding torches beside it while a general's soldiers wait in silent ranks on the paved approach; a full moon over dark trees and palace roofs, lantern light spilling through the gateway. Distant view, small figures, no violence shown, one unbroken picture without dividing bands. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
wa-king-bu-memorial: 478 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): envoys from Wa with bound hair and long robes arrive by sea, kneeling in a Liu Song palace courtyard to present a long paper memorial and gifts, while officials in tall caps prepare a seal of office and military title. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
yongming-era: 483 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a peaceful riverside city, markets busy along the Qinhuai, scholars reciting poetry in garden pavilions, farmers bringing grain, Buddhist temples with pagodas on the hills, boats on the Yangtze under a clear sky. Small figures, panoramic view. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
salary-system: 484 CE, Pingcheng (Datong): clerks at a government granary and treasury measure out silk bolts and grain into officials' carts by register, officials in Xianbei hooded caps and kaftans lining up, while at one side a corrupt official is led away. Orderly scene, small figures. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
equal-field: 485 CE, the plains near Pingcheng: officials with measuring cords and registers allot strips of fields to farming households, families of different sizes standing by their plots, ox-drawn ploughs turning soil, mulberry trees being planted along the edges. Small figures, wide spring landscape. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural showing ploughing, earthy reds and malachite on plaster.
tang-yuzhi-rebellion: 485 CE, Fuyang (Zhejiang): peasants with farm tools and makeshift banners gather along the Fuchun River among green hills, burning a pile of paper household registers, then marching on a walled town by the river. Bamboo groves and tea slopes line the river. Small figures, misty mountains. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral green on aged silk.
three-elders-system: 486 CE, a northern village near Pingcheng: three elders in plain robes and caps sit at a table under a tree registering households, villagers in tunics lining up with their families, rammed-earth houses and fields beyond. Small figures, quiet rural scene. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
jingling-eight-friends: 487 CE, Jiming Hill, Jiankang (Nanjing): a prince's garden villa on a wooded hill, eight poets in loose robes seated on mats with scrolls and brushes, a monk debating among them, wine cups and zithers, the city and lake below. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief like the Seven Sages bricks, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
four-tones: 489 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): two scholars in wide-sleeved robes sit facing each other in a study, one chanting aloud while the other marks a paper scroll, a zither and a set of bronze bells beside them for testing sounds, bamboo outside the window. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
fan-zhen-shenmie: 489 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a debate in a prince's hall, a plainly dressed scholar standing to make his point holding up a sword blade, while monks in robes and courtiers in silk sit around listening, incense rising. Small figures, no faces in close-up. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
longmen-grottoes: 493 CE, Longmen (Luoyang): limestone cliffs on both sides of the Yi River, where stonecutters on scaffolds carve the first cave, a slender seated Buddha emerging inside, monks and donors in Han-style robes watching from the riverbank. Chisels ring and stone dust drifts over the water. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite green and lapis, flaking plaster texture.
xiao-luan-usurps: 494 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a palace hall with banners where a middle-aged regent, seen from behind, ascends the throne steps while officials kneel in tense silence; guards stand at every door. Outside, the courtyard is empty, lanterns unlit, and rain falls on the tiled roofs. Small figures, dark mood, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
ban-xianbei-customs: 495 CE, Luoyang: officials in a palace courtyard change from Xianbei hooded caps and tight-sleeved kaftans into Han-style wide-sleeved robes and tall caps, piles of Xianbei garments on one side, an emperor watching from a hall. Tailors measure courtiers for new garments. Small figures. Painted in the style of the Northern Wei Binyang Cave relief of an imperial procession, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
shaolin-founded: 495 CE, Mount Song (Dengfeng): a new temple of timber halls rises in a pine forest at the foot of the Shaoshi peaks; an Indian monk in an ochre robe stands with a few Chinese disciples at the gate as builders finish the roofs. Small figures, mountain mist. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds and malachite green on plaster.
taihe-wuzhu: 495 CE, Luoyang: one unified scene in a walled courtyard of a Northern Wei state mint opening onto a street market; workers pour molten bronze into clay coin moulds at a furnace while others thread round square-holed coins onto cords, and just beyond the open gate merchants hand over strings of coins for bolts of silk. A single continuous space, no bands or dividing borders, small figures, no text. Painted in the manner of Northern Wei lacquer painting, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
han-surnames: 496 CE, Luoyang: a court ceremony in a palace hall where Xianbei nobles now in Han-style robes and caps receive genealogical scrolls from officials, an emperor in Han robes presiding from the dais, seen at a distance. Small figures, orderly rows. Painted in the style of the Northern Wei Binyang Cave relief of an imperial procession, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
xiaowen-dies: 499 CE, Gutang (Dengzhou, Henan): a Northern Wei army camp in spring, the emperor's tent with banners lowered to half-mast, generals in armour gathering silently, and a covered funeral carriage setting out north toward Luoyang. No body shown. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
tao-hongjing-materia-medica: 500 CE, Mount Mao (Jurong): a Daoist recluse in a robe and cap sits in a mountain pavilion sorting medicinal herbs, minerals and roots into labelled trays on shelves, a scroll of plant drawings beside him, a pine-covered mountain and clouds below. Small figure. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral green on aged silk.
wenxin-diaolong: 501 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a scholar in a plain robe sits at a desk in a Buddhist temple library writing on a paper scroll, shelves of sutras around him, a carved dragon on a lacquer stand beside the inkstone, monks passing in the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
zu-geng-sphere: 504 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a mathematician in a scholar's robe examines a wooden sphere cut into thin slices set beside a cube and nested square box, counting rods arranged on the table, a lamp and paper notes, a student watching beside a window onto a quiet courtyard. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk.
xiao-hong-expedition: 505 CE, Luokou (Huainan): a stormy night over a huge army camp on the Huai River; a prince in silk robes flees by boat in the rain, and the vast camp of tents and banners dissolves into panic as soldiers scatter. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and dark grey washes on aged silk.
empress-dowager-hu: 515 CE, Luoyang: an empress dowager in elaborate robes and headdress, seen from behind, rides in a canopied carriage through the city to a great Buddhist temple, courtiers and monks following, gilded pagodas and temple halls everywhere. Small figures. Painted in the style of the Northern Wei Binyang Cave relief of the empress's procession, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
shuijingzhu: 515 CE, Luoyang: a Northern Wei official in robes sits by a river with an assistant, sketching its course on a paper scroll; around him the river winds past towns, bridges, ferries, mills and temples into distant mountains. Small figures, wide landscape. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral blue-green on aged silk.
mahayana-rebellion: 515 CE, Jizhou (Hebei): a rebel army of peasants and monks in robes with red headbands marches across a plain under banners, smoke rising from a burning temple in the distance, villagers fleeing. Small figures, distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line.
fushan-dam: 516 CE, Fushan on the Huai River: a long earthen dam across the river has burst, a great wave pouring through the breach and spreading over the plain downstream, villages and trees half submerged, small boats scattered. Seen from far above, small figures, no bodies. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and grey-blue washes on aged silk.
yongning-pagoda: 516 CE, Luoyang: a colossal nine-storey square wooden pagoda with gilded finials and bells on every eave rises above the city's temple roofs, its tip catching the sunset light; monks, pilgrims and carriages crowd the temple gate below. Its shadow falls across the walled city of Luoyang. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, gold, malachite and lapis on plaster.
song-yun-mission: 518 CE, Gandhara (Peshawar): two Chinese travellers in robes, seen from behind, arrive with pack horses at a great Buddhist stupa surrounded by monasteries in a green valley, local people in draped garments and turbans, snowy peaks of the Hindu Kush behind, monks carrying bundles of palm-leaf sutras to the travellers' horses. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gandhara schist relief, carved stone figures in soft grey tones.
bodhidharma: 520 CE, Mount Song (Dengfeng): a bearded Indian monk in a plain robe sits in meditation facing the rock wall of a small cave on a mountainside, seen from behind, pine trees and snow outside, a disciple waiting at the cave mouth. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei Dunhuang cave mural, earthy reds, malachite green and lapis, flaking plaster texture.
yuan-cha-coup: 520 CE, Luoyang: soldiers guard the gates of a palace courtyard, an inner hall sealed with locked doors, while a figure in rich robes is confined inside; a powerful minister and a eunuch confer in the courtyard. Small figures, tense mood, no violence. Painted in the style of the Northern Wei Binyang Cave relief, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
liang-iron-coins: 523 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a busy market where merchants push carts piled high with strings of iron coins, coin-counting clerks overwhelmed, and a mint nearby with smoky furnaces. Shoppers haul baskets of heavy coins to buy a single bolt of silk, and a shopkeeper weighs strings of coins on a large balance beside a cart. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties moulded brick relief from Nanjing, rendered as a soft ink rubbing.
tongtai-temple: 527 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a great Buddhist temple complex with a nine-storey pagoda beside the palace; an elderly emperor in a monk's plain robe, seen from behind, sweeps the temple courtyard, while officials in court robes arrive with carts of treasure to ransom him. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on aged silk.
lao-ai: 238 BCE, Yong, the old Qin ritual capital: before a walled palace compound of rammed earth and tiled halls, ranks of Qin crossbowmen and halberdiers in lamellar armour advance in tight formation against a scattering band of rebels fleeing through the gate, dust rising. A young king in a black robe and tall cap stands small on a terrace with attendants, watching from afar. Morning light over loess hills. Painted in ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of late Warring States pictorial art, black, cinnabar and ochre palette.
lord-chunshen-killed: 238 BCE, Shouchun, capital of Chu: at dusk outside a great palace gate with timber towers and red lacquered doors, a nobleman's carriage has halted while armed men in Chu-style robes rush from hiding behind the gate pillars; attendants scatter across the stone courtyard, seen from a distance, with no violence shown in detail. Willow trees and the Huai plain beyond the walls. Rendered as a Chu lacquer painting, black ground with cinnabar and ochre figures, flowing curvilinear lines.
li-si-against-expulsion: 237 BCE, Xianyang: inside a timber hall of the Qin palace, a minister kneels on a reed mat before a raised dais, presenting bound bamboo-slip scrolls with both hands, while robed officials in black kneel in rows along the walls and lacquered tables hold brushes and ink stones. Through the open doors, carts of departing foreign scholars wait in the courtyard. Soft daylight, bronze lamps. Painted in ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted black, cinnabar and ochre.
death-of-lu-buwei: 235 BCE, the road into Shu: a lone elderly official in a dark silk robe sits in a modest timber guesthouse on a misty mountain path in Sichuan, a lacquered cup set on a low table before him, a bamboo-slip letter unrolled beside it; servants wait outside by an ox cart, steep green ranges and cloud below. Quiet, melancholy evening light. Rendered in the style of a late Warring States lacquer painting, black ground, cinnabar and ochre, fine flowing lines.
han-fei: 233 BCE, Xianyang: a scholar in a plain robe sits alone in a bare rammed-earth prison cell, bundles of bamboo-slip writings stacked beside him, light falling through a high barred window; outside in the courtyard, Qin guards with halberds stand by a gate and a messenger approaches carrying a covered lacquer vessel. Restrained, sombre mood. Painted in ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, faded mineral tones and brown silk texture.
battle-of-fei: 233 BCE, Fei on the north China plain: a Zhao army with horse archers in short tunics and trousers and lines of chariots sweeps across open grassland toward a retreating Qin column under black banners; dust clouds, distant hills, a frontier fortress of rammed earth on the horizon. Figures small, battle seen from afar, riders without stirrups. Rendered as a bronze-age lacquer painting with a black, cinnabar and ochre palette, lively silhouetted horses and chariots.
li-mu-executed: 229 BCE, Handan, capital of Zhao: in a palace courtyard of timber halls on rammed-earth terraces, a veteran general in armour is led away between guards toward the gate, his helmet left on the steps; courtiers in silk robes whisper behind pillars, and beyond the walls Qin campfires smoke on the horizon. Grey overcast afternoon. Painted in ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of late Warring States pictorial art, ochre, black and cinnabar.
qin-commanderies: 221 BCE, Xianyang: in a great Qin palace hall, officials in black robes and tall caps kneel in rows as clerks unroll a large map painted on silk across lacquered tables, marking rivers and mountains; bundles of bamboo-slip appointment documents and bronze tallies are being handed to departing officials, while carriages wait in the courtyard below to carry them to every corner of the empire. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, earthy reds and ochres on plaster.
qin-baiyue: 221 BCE, Lingnan near present-day Guangzhou: a long column of Qin infantry in lamellar armour with crossbows and halberds marches along a riverbank through dense subtropical forest, banana palms and misty karst hills around them; Yue villagers in stilted thatched houses watch from across the river, dugout canoes drawn up on the shore. Humid morning haze. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, earthy red, ochre and black pigments on plaster, simplified figures.
title-of-huangdi: 221 BCE, Xianyang: a vast imperial audience hall on a high rammed-earth terrace, black banners and bronze bells, hundreds of ministers in black robes kneeling in long ordered rows on the stone forecourt; at the far end, a small figure in a black robe and crown with hanging bead strings sits on a raised dais beneath a canopy, seen from behind the courtiers. Bright clear morning. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper with strong flat silhouettes.
unified-script: 221 BCE, Xianyang: in a palace scriptorium, scribes in plain robes kneel at low lacquered desks copying characters with brushes onto bamboo slips and wooden boards, piles of old regional documents being sorted and bundled aside; a senior minister supervises from the side. Ink stones, knives for scraping slips, scroll racks along timber walls, soft window light. Characters shown only as indistinct marks. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and black on plaster.
unified-weights-and-coins: 221 BCE, Xianyang market: officials set out bronze standard weights, bronze measuring vessels and wooden measuring rods on a long table while merchants line up with sacks of grain; a foundry nearby pours bronze into moulds for round coins with square holes, strings of coins hanging from poles, and ox carts with matched axles roll past. Busy daylight scene, many small figures. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black and grey tones, crisp outlines.
twelve-metal-colossi: 221 BCE, Xianyang: in a vast foundry yard outside the palace, heaps of confiscated bronze swords, spears and halberds are fed into glowing furnaces by labourers; nearby, twelve colossal bronze figures in robes stand in a row, dwarfing the workers on wooden scaffolding, and huge bronze bells hang from frames. Smoke drifts across a grey sky. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black mineral pigments on plaster.
imperial-highways: 220 BCE, outside Xianyang: a broad, raised earthen road lined on both sides with young pine trees stretches across the loess plain toward distant hills, gangs of labourers tamping the roadbed with wooden rammers, overseers in robes directing them; a column of horse-drawn chariots and supply carts rolls along a finished stretch. Late afternoon golden light. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with rhythmic rows of trees and figures.
taishan-feng: 219 BCE, Mount Tai: a long imperial procession of officials, attendants and guards climbs a steep stone path among ancient pines and granite cliffs toward the summit, banners fluttering; on a cleared platform at the top, a small altar smokes and a tall blank stone stele stands, the emperor a tiny robed figure among his retinue. Clouds swirl below the peak. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, cinnabar and green on plaster, flat stylised mountains.
xu-fu: 219 BCE, Langya on the Shandong coast: a fleet of large wooden plank ships with matting sails is moored off a sandy shore beneath a terraced hill, and long lines of young men and women in simple robes board by gangplanks carrying baskets, seeds and tools; a robed magician stands at a prow facing the misty sea, where faint islands float on the horizon. Dawn light. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, soft reds, ochres and blue-greys.
langya-stele: 219 BCE, Langya terrace near the sea: on a high rammed-earth terrace overlooking the bay, stonemasons on wooden scaffolding finish a tall stone stele whose face is covered with tiny indistinct marks, while officials in black robes and the imperial retinue stand nearby; tents and banners of the emperor's camp spread below, the sea glittering beyond. Clear spring day. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, bold outlines.
bolangsha: 218 BCE, Bolangsha in Henan: a sandy road through low dunes and scrub, a procession of identical imperial carriages drawn by horses passes under guard, and from behind a dune a large iron hammer flies through the air to smash the roof of one carriage; a young man and a burly strongman flee in the distance as guards wheel around. Dust and confusion, figures small. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
shuihudi-qin-slips: 217 BCE, Shuihudi near Yunmeng: a modest wooden-chambered tomb pit in a quiet field, family members in plain Qin robes lowering a lacquered coffin, beside it bundles of bamboo slips tied with cords, lacquered cups, a brush and ink stone placed with care; willow trees and a small village beyond, overcast light. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted ochre, red and black on plaster, simple flat figures.
land-self-reporting: 216 BCE, a county town near Xianyang: farming households in hemp clothing queue before a timber government office, while clerks at low desks record each family's fields on bamboo slips and wooden boards; outside the walls, terraced loess fields of millet stretch into the distance, a surveyor measuring a plot with a rope. Bright autumn day. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, grey and black ink, rhythmic rows of figures.
meng-tian-takes-ordos: 215 BCE, the Ordos inside the Yellow River bend: a vast Qin army of infantry in lamellar armour, crossbowmen and chariots advances across dry steppe grassland beside the broad bending river, while Xiongnu horsemen in felt caps and their herds retreat over low hills; new rammed-earth forts rise on the plain. Huge sky, figures small, riders without stirrups. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, earthy red, ochre and black on plaster.
southern-commanderies: 214 BCE, Panyu near Guangzhou: settlers, convicts and merchants with shoulder poles and ox carts arrive at a new walled outpost of rammed earth beside the Pearl River, Qin soldiers on guard at the gate; banana groves, lychee trees and green hills surround it, river boats unload goods. Humid hazy sunlight. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochres, reds and soft greens, simplified figures.
epang: 212 BCE, south of the Wei River near Xianyang: a gigantic rammed-earth platform rises from the plain, swarming with thousands of forced labourers carrying baskets of earth on shoulder poles and pounding layers with wooden rammers, overseers with whips at a distance; timber frames of enormous halls begin to rise, the river and the city walls visible behind. Dusty midday haze. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
qin-straight-road: 212 BCE, the hills north of Yunyang: a broad military road cut straight through the folded loess ridges, labourers filling ravines and levelling hilltops with baskets and rammers, while a column of Qin cavalry and supply wagons travels along a completed section toward the northern horizon. Wide, dramatic landscape, late afternoon light. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments on plaster.
dongjun-meteorite: 211 BCE, Dong Commandery: a dark, pitted meteorite stone lies in a field, its face scratched with indistinct marks, while Qin officials in black robes and armed guards stand around it and question villagers kneeling at a distance; thatched farmhouses, bare trees and a grey winter sky behind. Ominous, quiet mood. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper with heavy contrast.
shaqiu: 210 BCE, Shaqiu in Hebei: a summer palace of timber halls on the plain at night, an imperial travelling carriage with closed curtains parked in a courtyard under lanterns; inside a lit chamber two officials bend over a document by a bronze lamp, whispering, while guards stand unaware outside. Heavy, secretive atmosphere, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark reds, ochre and black on plaster.
terracotta-army: 210 BCE, Mount Li near present-day Xi'an: in long earthen pits roofed with timber beams, rows upon rows of life-size clay soldiers painted in bright colours stand in battle formation with real bronze weapons, clay horses and chariots among them; workers in hemp clothes place the last figures under torchlight, the forested mound of Mount Li beyond. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre, green and black pigments.
death-of-fusu: 210 BCE, Shang Commandery on the northern frontier: in a garrison camp of tents and rammed-earth walls among bare loess hills, a messenger presents a sealed decree to a young prince in a dark robe, who stands with bowed head beside a general in armour; soldiers watch in silence, a sword resting on a table. Cold wind and grey sky. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, solemn composition.
zhang-chu-proclaimed: 209 BCE, the walled city of Chen: rebel peasants and conscripts in rough hemp clothing, armed with wooden staves, farm tools and a few captured spears, crowd before a city gate while a leader stands on a raised mound; improvised banners fly, and horsemen ride out of the gates in several directions to raise other regions. Bright day, energetic crowd. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments on plaster.
xiang-liang-rises: 209 BCE, Wu (present-day Suzhou): outside the walls of a southern city with canals and reed beds, eight thousand young warriors from the lower Yangzi gather in ranks with spears and shields, a tall young commander and his older uncle standing on a platform before them, banners rising; boats crowd the waterways. Misty morning. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of small figures.
liu-bang-pei: 209 BCE, Pei county town: townspeople and local men with farm tools and old weapons gather inside an earthen-walled town, opening the gate to a band of rebels; a modest local officer in a simple robe stands among elders as they acclaim him, and a crude red banner is raised on a pole. Plain countryside of wheat fields and willows outside. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, earthy reds and ochres on plaster.
er-shi-purges-siblings: 209 BCE, Xianyang: a sombre palace courtyard at dusk, closed lacquered gates, a row of guards in black armour standing before the empty halls of the princes; abandoned silk robes and overturned lacquered tables suggest a purge, while officials hurry away under the colonnades. No bodies shown, only stillness and long shadows. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark ochre, red and black pigments on plaster.
zhou-wen-reaches-xi: 209 BCE, Xi near Mount Li: a huge rebel host with improvised banners spreads across the plain within sight of Xianyang's distant walls, while from the slopes of Mount Li columns of hastily armed convict labourers led by Qin officers in armour charge down toward them. Dust clouds, battle seen from far away, small figures. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with dramatic diagonal movement.
li-si-death: 208 BCE, Xianyang: in front of the city's market gate on a cold morning, an aged official in a plain robe is led between guards toward the crowd, glancing back toward the open countryside where a hound runs across fields; townspeople watch from a distance and officials stand on a platform. No violence shown. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted red, ochre and black pigments.
chen-sheng-killed: 208 BCE, near Xiacheng: a lonely retreat along a muddy road across the Huai plain, a battered war chariot halted beside a stand of reeds, its driver standing over the empty car; a few exhausted rebels wander off in the distance as a Qin army's banners appear on the horizon.
