Grey wintry light. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, sparse composition.
king-huai-enthroned: 208 BCE, Xuyi: on a grassy hillside a young shepherd in a rough robe stands among his sheep as a delegation of nobles and armoured warriors kneel before him; nearby a carriage waits to carry him to a hastily built hall where Chu banners fly. Gentle evening light over rice paddies and the Huai river. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and green on plaster.
battle-of-dingtao: 208 BCE, Dingtao: at night during heavy rain, a sleeping Chu camp of tents and wooden palisades is suddenly overrun by Qin troops pouring in through the gates with torches, horses rearing and banners falling; the action seen from a hill at a distance, flames reflected on wet ground. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black and grey ink on paper, slanting rain lines.
wangyi-palace-coup: 207 BCE, Wangyi Palace near Xianyang: a detached palace among trees by the Jing River, armed men in armour storming through the gate and up the steps of the main hall as eunuchs and attendants flee along the colonnades; the event shown from outside the walls, at a distance. Overcast afternoon. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments on plaster.
deer-horse: 207 BCE, Xianyang palace hall: a powerful eunuch minister stands beside a spotted deer led on a rope before the throne, while rows of courtiers in black robes and caps kneel, some glancing at one another nervously, others nodding; a young emperor on the dais leans forward in puzzlement, seen small from behind. Bronze lamps and lacquered pillars. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, clear silhouettes.
ziying-kills-zhao-gao: 207 BCE, Xianyang: in a dim inner chamber of the palace, a man in court robes enters through a doorway while armed attendants step out from behind painted screens; a figure lies on a couch feigning illness. The scene is shown through an open doorway from the corridor, at a distance, without violence. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black on plaster.
liu-bang-takes-wu-pass: 207 BCE, Wu Pass in the Qinling mountains: a fortified gatehouse of rammed earth and timber in a narrow valley between steep forested ridges, its gates thrown open as a rebel army with red banners streams through; Qin defenders lay down weapons on the walls. River below, mist in the gorges. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments, stylised mountains.
liu-bang-three-article-covenant: 206 BCE, near Xianyang in Guanzhong: under a large tree outside a village, a rebel leader in a simple robe stands addressing a gathering of grey-bearded elders and farmers, soldiers behind him standing at ease; in the background, palace storehouses with sealed doors and guards. Warm, calm daylight over wheat fields. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, earthy reds, ochres and soft greens.
xiang-yu-eighteen-kingdoms: 206 BCE, Xianyang: the Qin palace halls burn on the horizon, smoke billowing, while in a vast military camp a commander in armour sits beneath a canopy before kneeling lords and generals, receiving tallies and seals laid out on a long table; banners of many colours ring the camp. Dramatic red sky. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with strong flat forms.
han-reconquers-guanzhong: 206 BCE, Chencang: a Han army winds out of the Qinling mountains along a hidden valley path, soldiers crossing a shallow river at dawn, while far away on the other side a burnt plank road clings to a cliff, drawing the enemy's attention. Dense forests, mist, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, flat stylised peaks.
battle-of-pengcheng: 205 BCE, Pengcheng: a vast coalition army breaks and flees in disorder along the banks of the Sui River as a smaller force of cavalry charges in from the west through morning haze; banners trampled, horses rearing, the river crowded with fleeing soldiers seen from far away. Riders without stirrups. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, sweeping diagonal movement.
battle-of-jingxing: 204 BCE, Jingxing Pass: in a mountain valley a Han army stands with its back to a river, fighting a larger Zhao force, while on a hilltop behind the Zhao camp a small hidden detachment has torn down the enemy's banners and raised two thousand red flags. Steep cliffs, dust, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments, many small banners.
siege-of-xingyang: 204 BCE, Xingyang: at night a walled city is ringed by the campfires of a besieging army; from the east gate, a royal carriage with a yellow canopy emerges surrounded by women in armour as a decoy, while far away through the west gate a small band of horsemen slips out into the dark. Moonlight over the plain. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
battle-of-wei-river: 203 BCE, the Wei River in Shandong: upstream, sandbags burst from a breached dam and a wall of water surges down the river, splitting an army caught midway across the ford; troops on the far bank are cut off, banners floating. Wide view of the river valley, figures small, no gore. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, blue-grey and red pigments.
treaty-of-hong-canal: 203 BCE, Guangwu near Xingyang: two fortified camps face each other across a canal in a broad ravine, envoys meeting on a plank bridge between them; on one side, an elderly man and a woman in plain robes are escorted across to the opposite camp. Banners of both armies lining the ridges, calm but tense. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, symmetrical composition.
liu-bang-enthroned-dingtao: 202 BCE, north of the Si River at Dingtao: an open-air altar of earth on a riverside plain, a newly crowned ruler in a black robe and cap standing small on top as generals and lords kneel in ranks below, banners and halberds raised, sacrificial smoke rising into a bright sky. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and black pigments, flat ceremonial figures.
han-xin-demoted: 201 BCE, Chen: at a lakeside meeting place on the road to Yunmeng, a general in court robes arrives to greet the emperor's procession and is quietly seized by guards who bind his arms; carriages with umbrella canopies, banners and courtiers stand around, with marshes, reeds and flocks of water birds behind. Figures small, restrained drama, soft grey daylight. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper with crisp silhouettes.
changan-capital: 200 BCE, Chang'an: the newly built Weiyang Palace rises on high rammed-earth terraces with broad tiled halls and gate towers, while a long procession of carriages, officials and guards enters through the main gate; workers still finish walls and roads nearby, the Wei River and loess plain behind. Bright spring day. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and green pigments on plaster.
shusun-tong-court-ritual: 200 BCE, Changle Palace in Chang'an: at dawn hundreds of officials in black robes and caps file into a vast courtyard in perfect order, civil officials on one side and military on the other, guards with halberds lining the steps, banners and drums set out; the emperor's canopy at the far end. Solemn, ordered atmosphere. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rhythmic rows.
first-heqin: 198 BCE, leaving Chang'an for the steppe: a princess's carriage with a silk canopy and a long baggage train of carts loaded with bolts of silk, jars of wine and sacks of grain sets out through the northern gate, escorted by Han horsemen; far ahead lie grasslands and felt tents. Wistful morning light. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, soft reds, ochres and greens.
chen-xi-rebellion: 197 BCE, the northern region of Dai: a Han army led by an imperial carriage under a canopy marches across a cold frontier plateau toward a walled town where rebel banners fly, rammed-earth ramparts and beacon towers on the hills; snow lies on distant mountains and cavalry without stirrups scout ahead across the dry grass. Figures small, wide wintry sky. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black and grey ink on paper.
han-xin-death: 196 BCE, Changle Palace, Chang'an: a general in court robes walks alone through a tall palace gate into a quiet courtyard beside a bell tower, where hidden guards wait behind lacquered pillars; the empress's attendants watch from a long colonnade, and lanterns are being lit. Shown from a distance at dusk, no violence depicted, long shadows across the paving. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments on plaster.
peng-yue-executed: 196 BCE, Luoyang: before a palace gate of timber and tile, a lord in rich silk robes is led away by guards in armour while an official reads a decree from an unrolled bamboo-slip scroll; townspeople look on from a distance, and the lord's empty carriage and horses stand abandoned by the roadside. Grey sky, solemn and still mood, figures small. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with heavy contrast.
ying-bu-rebellion: 196 BCE, Kuaizhui in Anhui: two armies clash on a broad plain under massed banners, Han crossbowmen loosing volleys of arrows and horse-drawn chariots advancing, while at the rear an emperor in a canopied carriage is surrounded by guards raising shields as a stray arrow flies past. Hazy dust, distant view, small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments on plaster.
lu-jia-nanyue-mission: 196 BCE, Panyu, capital of Nanyue: in a palace hall with southern-style raised floors and wooden pillars, a Han envoy in a black robe and cap presents a bronze seal on a lacquered tray to a king seated on a dais, Yue courtiers with short hair and southern clothing looking on; palm trees outside. Rendered as a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and green pigments.
empress-lu: 195 BCE, Chang'an: in a hall of the Weiyang Palace, a woman in rich layered silk robes sits behind a translucent gauze screen on a raised dais, a young emperor seated beside her, as ministers in black robes and caps kneel in rows presenting bamboo-slip memorials. Bronze lamps, lacquered pillars and painted beams, soft afternoon light through lattice windows. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, figures small.
death-of-gaozu: 195 BCE, Chang'an: in the Changle Palace, lords and generals in court robes kneel around a ritual altar where a white horse stands tethered beside bronze vessels, swearing an oath before an ailing emperor reclining on a couch under a canopy; a young heir stands nearby among attendants. Bronze lamps, painted beams, solemn evening light, figures small and seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted red, ochre and black mineral pigments on plaster.
liu-ruyi-poisoned: 194 BCE, Chang'an: in a quiet palace chamber at dawn, an empty child's sleeping couch with rumpled silk covers and an overturned lacquered cup on a low table; through the open lattice doors, a young emperor in hunting dress returns across a frosty courtyard with his bow, attendants hurrying toward him. No violence shown, cold still atmosphere. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, sparse and sombre composition.
xiao-gui-cao-sui: 193 BCE, Chang'an: in the chancellor's residence, a relaxed elderly official in a black robe sits drinking wine with guests in a garden pavilion under willow trees, while bundles of old bamboo-slip statutes lie untouched on a lacquered stand; clerks waiting at the gate with petitions are invited to drink instead. Calm sunny afternoon, peaceful mood. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and soft green pigments on plaster.
abolish-book-ban: 191 BCE, Chang'an: scholars in plain robes carry bundles of bamboo-slip books out of hiding places in a walled courtyard, untying them on reed mats while young students gather eagerly around; one elderly master unrolls slips beside a brazier, and an official messenger with a decree stands at the gate. Bright spring morning, plum blossoms. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, lively small figures.
ernian-statutes: 186 BCE, Jiangling: in a county office of timber and tile beside the Yangtze, Han clerks in black caps and robes kneel at low desks copying statutes onto long bamboo slips with brushes, tying finished bundles with silk cords; a magistrate hears a case outside on a veranda while petitioners wait. Rice paddies and river boats beyond. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, simple flat figures.
zhao-tuo-emperor: 183 BCE, Panyu, capital of Nanyue: an elderly king in imperial yellow robes rides out of a southern palace with raised wooden halls and tiled roofs, a large army of Yue and Han-style soldiers with bronze weapons and long shields assembling on the riverbank, war boats waiting on the Pearl River. Palm trees, humid haze, figures small. Rendered as a Han tomb mural, warm reds, ochres and greens on plaster.
wen-jing: c. 180 BCE, the Guanzhong plain near Chang'an: a prosperous farming landscape, peasants harvesting millet and wheat with sickles, granaries overflowing with grain, ox carts on country roads, children playing by a village of rammed-earth houses with tiled roofs; a modest official in a plain robe inspects fields with a few attendants. Golden autumn light, peaceful abundance. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rhythmic rows of workers.
lu-clan-disturbance: 180 BCE, Chang'an: at dawn inside the camp of the Northern Army, a general stands on a platform calling to rows of soldiers, who bare their left arms in a show of loyalty to the Liu house; banners flutter, armoured guards close the palace gates beyond, smoke rises over part of the city. Seen from a distance, no gore. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black on plaster.
xiongnu-conquer-yuezhi: 176 BCE, the Hexi Corridor: Xiongnu horsemen in felt caps and fur-trimmed coats sweep across wide arid grassland between the snow-capped Qilian Mountains and the desert, driving away Yuezhi herders whose wagons, felt tents and flocks flee westward in long columns. Huge sky, dust, riders without stirrups, small figures. Painted in a style drawing on steppe animal-art motifs and Han tomb murals, ochre, rust red and black pigments.
jia-yi-changsha: 176 BCE, Changsha: a young scholar in a black robe sits on the veranda of a modest timber house overlooking the Xiang River, writing on bamboo slips, a lacquered wine cup and brush beside him; a boat that brought him rests at the jetty, misty green hills across the water, and an owl perches on a nearby branch. Melancholy grey dusk. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, soft ochres, greens and black.
chao-cuo-frontier: 169 BCE, the northern frontier: settlers in hemp clothing build rammed-earth houses within a walled farming village beside a watchtower, ploughing fields with oxen and digging irrigation ditches; families unload tools and seed from carts while soldiers patrol the ramparts, and the open steppe stretches beyond. Bright, dry day with distant mountains. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
mawangdui: 168 BCE, Mawangdui near Changsha: deep inside an earthen pit, labourers lower nested lacquered coffins painted with swirling cloud patterns into a timber burial chamber packed with charcoal and white clay; side compartments hold silk garments, lacquer dishes, wooden figurines and rolled silk paintings. Torchlight and mourners in white at the pit's rim. Painted in the manner of a Han silk banner painting, cinnabar, black and ochre with flowing cloud scrolls.
abolish-mutilating-punishments: 167 BCE, Chang'an: at a palace gate, a young girl in a plain robe kneels on the stone paving, holding up a bamboo-slip petition toward officials who take it inside, while her father, a bound official in a cart under guard, watches from behind; courtiers in black robes look on. Soft morning light, compassionate mood. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm red, ochre and black pigments.
xiongnu-raid-xiao-pass: 166 BCE, Xiao Pass in Ningxia: a vast host of Xiongnu horsemen pours through a mountain pass, smoke rising from a burning palace on the plain behind; on a distant ridge, mounted scouts gaze toward the far-off walls of the Han capital and beacon fires blaze on hilltop towers. Riders without stirrups, figures small. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with sweeping horses.
xiliu-camp: 158 BCE, Xiliu near Xianyang: at the gate of a strictly guarded army camp with wooden palisades, armoured sentries with crossbows block an imperial carriage and its retinue; an officer reads a tally while the emperor's escort waits, and inside the camp soldiers stand in perfect ranks. Clear winter day, banners still. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black on plaster, orderly composition.
land-tax-one-thirtieth: 156 BCE, a village near Chang'an: farmers bring modest baskets of grain to a county granary where clerks measure them with bronze measuring vessels, keeping a tally on wooden boards; behind them stand large private granaries full to the brim, fields of millet rolling to the horizon. Contented harvest scene in golden autumn light. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, many small figures.
seven-states: 154 BCE, the eastern plain near Suiyang: great armies of the rebel kingdoms under many coloured banners camp along a river, while imperial Han forces move along roads to cut their grain convoys; smoke from burning supply carts rises, horsemen gallop between camps. Wide panoramic view, figures small, no gore. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, earthy red, ochre and black pigments.
defense-of-suiyang: 154 BCE, Suiyang: a strong walled city of rammed earth with gate towers is surrounded by besieging rebel armies of Wu and Chu, their siege ladders and tents encircling it, while defenders on the walls shoot crossbows and throw stones; far in the distance, columns of imperial troops intercept supply carts. Dramatic grey sky. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
emperor-wu-accession: 141 BCE, Weiyang Palace, Chang'an: in a grand audience hall, a teenage emperor in black robes and a crown with hanging bead strings sits on a dais, seen small from behind the ranks of kneeling ministers and generals; bronze incense burners smoke, musicians with bells and chime stones play in the courtyard. Bright ceremonial morning. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and black on plaster.
wen-weng-school: 141 BCE, Chengdu: in the courtyard of a new stone-built school hall with tiled roof, young students in plain robes kneel on mats reading bamboo-slip texts aloud while a teacher instructs them; the governor watches from a veranda, and outside, a cart prepares to carry selected students to the capital. Green Sichuan hills and bamboo groves behind. Painted as a Han pictorial brick relief from Sichuan, impressed lines, earth tones.
first-era-name: 140 BCE, Chang'an: in the palace observatory courtyard, court astronomers and ritual officials in black robes gather around a bronze sundial and a large wooden calendar board marked with indistinct symbols, consulting bamboo records; an official announces the new year to kneeling ministers. Dawn light, cranes overhead. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments, flat ceremonial figures.
huainanzi: 139 BCE, Shouchun: in a refined pavilion of the King of Huainan, scholars and Daoist adepts in loose robes debate around low tables piled with bamboo-slip manuscripts, a bronze incense burner shaped like a mountain smoking in the centre; a finished bundle of books is wrapped in silk for presentation. Garden of pines and a pond outside. Painted in the manner of a Han silk painting, ink and colour with flowing lines.
dong-ou-moves-north: 138 BCE, the coast of Dong'ou near Wenzhou: a Han fleet of wooden ships with matting sails approaches a rocky shore where a fortified Yue town stands, while on the beach Yue families with short hair, tattoos and baskets board boats to move north. Green coastal hills, misty sea, gulls. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, soft blue-grey, ochre and red pigments.
confucian-orthodoxy: 136 BCE, Chang'an: in a palace hall, five erudite scholars in wide-sleeved robes and scholars' caps sit on mats before stacked bamboo-slip editions of the classics, lecturing to rows of kneeling officials; the emperor's dais visible far behind a curtain. Bronze ritual vessels and lamps, calm daylight. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, ordered rows of figures.
tang-meng-yelang: 135 BCE, Yelang in Guizhou: a Han envoy in a black robe and his escort, with porters carrying bolts of silk and bronze gifts on shoulder poles, meet a local chief in feathered headdress and his people outside a village of stilted wooden houses in a valley of karst peaks and terraced fields. Misty morning. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red mineral pigments.
dong-zhongshu-three-responses: 134 BCE, Chang'an: a scholar in a plain robe kneels at a low desk in a quiet study with a garden beyond the lattice, writing on bamboo slips by lamplight, a cosmological diagram of Heaven and Earth painted on a silk hanging behind him; finished bundles are being carried away by a palace messenger. Night scene, gentle light. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
filial-incorrupt-recommendation: 134 BCE, a commandery seat: a provincial governor in a black robe receives two modest young men in plain robes at his office gate, one carrying an aged parent's walking stick, while clerks prepare a carriage to take them to the capital; villagers watch from the road. Ordinary town of rammed-earth walls and willows, morning light. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre and red pigments.
mayi: 133 BCE, near Mayi in northern Shanxi: on the open steppe, a Xiongnu cavalry host halts and turns back as its leader notices livestock grazing untended in the fields; in the hills and valleys around, hundreds of thousands of hidden Han soldiers wait among the rocks and gullies, banners lowered. Wide, tense landscape, figures small. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
sima-xiangru-southwest: 130 BCE, Qiong near Xichang: a Han envoy in a black robe on a horse leads a party along a newly cut mountain road through steep forested valleys, labourers building plank bridges over a gorge, while local chiefs of the Qiong people in wool capes come down to greet him. Clouds clinging to peaks. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised mountains.
battle-of-longcheng: 129 BCE, Longcheng in Mongolia: Han cavalry with long spears and crossbows charge into a Xiongnu gathering place of felt tents and ritual poles on the open steppe, horses and herds scattering, felt banners falling; snow-dusted hills and a vast sky. Riders without stirrups, small figures, battle seen from afar. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with galloping horses.
recovery-of-henan: 127 BCE, the Ordos loop of the Yellow River: Han cavalry drive Xiongnu herders and flocks northward across the river while, on the near bank, labourers raise the rammed-earth walls of a new city and settlers with carts, oxen and tools arrive in long columns. Dry grassland, broad river, clear sky. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, earthy reds, ochres and black.
edict-of-grace: 127 BCE, a princely court: in a king's hall, an aging king divides a painted silk map of his realm among many sons in robes kneeling before him, each receiving a small bronze seal and bamboo-slip deed from an official sent by the emperor. Lacquered pillars, bronze lamps, ceremonial mood. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of kneeling figures.
zhang-qian-returns: 126 BCE, Chang'an: a weather-beaten envoy holding a yak-tail envoy's staff, with a single companion of steppe appearance and a few tired horses, arrives at the city gate where officials hurry out to greet him; behind lie the long dusty road and distant mountains. Evening light, emotional homecoming. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, flat figures.
imperial-academy: 124 BCE, Chang'an: in a large courtyard school south of the city, fifty young students in black robes and caps kneel in neat rows on mats before erudite masters, each with bundles of bamboo-slip classics; a bell tower and tiled lecture halls behind, pines in the yard. Bright morning, orderly study. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
huainan-conspiracy: 122 BCE, Shouchun: imperial troops in armour surround a princely palace with tiled roofs and gate towers, officials in black carrying decrees enter through the gates, and servants carry chests of documents out into the courtyard while the Daoist pavilion stands silent among pines. Shown from outside the walls, grey dusk. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments.
hexi-campaign: 121 BCE, the Hexi Corridor near Zhangye: a fast-moving column of Han light cavalry gallops across arid grassland beneath the snow-capped Qilian Mountains, kicking up dust, as Xiongnu herds and tents scatter far ahead; oasis poplars and a river glint in the distance. Riders without stirrups, small figures. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, galloping horses in rhythmic rows.
hunye-surrender: 121 BCE, the Hexi Corridor in Gansu: on the bank of the Yellow River, tens of thousands of Xiongnu men, women and herds with wagons and felt tents cross toward a Han army camp, where a young general rides out to meet a Xiongnu king; banners of both sides on the plain. Wide view, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black.
salt-iron: 119 BCE, a state ironworks and salt works: workers in hemp clothing pump bellows at tall brick blast furnaces pouring molten iron into moulds for ploughshares and tools, while nearby labourers boil brine in large iron pans and stack salt; officials in black caps record output on bamboo slips. Smoke and fire glow. Painted as a Han pictorial brick relief from Sichuan, impressed earthen tones and lively figures.
wuzhu: 118 BCE, a Han state mint near Chang'an: workers pour molten bronze into clay and bronze coin moulds, others break apart cooled trees of round coins with square holes and string them on cords, overseers weigh strings on balances. Furnace glow, stacks of coins in baskets, many small figures. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rhythmic workshop scene.
zhang-qian-wusun: 115 BCE, the shore of Issyk-Kul: a Han embassy with a train of horses and camels carrying silk bales and gold arrives at a Wusun camp of round felt tents by a deep blue lake ringed by snow-capped Tianshan peaks; Wusun nobles in pointed caps and long coats greet the envoy. Crisp clear air. Painted in a style blending Han tomb mural with steppe motifs, ochre, blue and red.
gaomin-edict: 114 BCE, a Chang'an market: officials and soldiers carry chests, bolts of silk and strings of coins out of a merchant's walled compound, recording them on bamboo slips, while the merchant family stands dejected at the gate and neighbours whisper. Market stalls and tiled shops along a straight street. Grey day. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
mancheng-tombs: 113 BCE, Mancheng in Hebei: inside a vast tomb cut into a rocky hillside, workers by torchlight arrange bronze vessels, chariots and pottery in stone chambers, while a funeral suit made of thousands of small jade plates linked with gold wire lies on a bier; a gilt bronze lamp shaped as a kneeling servant girl glows nearby. Rendered as a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and jade-green pigments.
music-bureau: 112 BCE, Chang'an: in a palace courtyard, musicians in robes play bronze bells, chime stones, zithers and pan pipes, dancers with long sleeves twirl, and clerks write down songs on bamboo slips as folk singers from the provinces perform; officials watch from a veranda. Festive daylight, tiled roofs and a drum on a stand beside a pine. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, lively dancing figures.
hexi-four-commanderies: 111 BCE, near Dunhuang: in the Hexi desert, Han soldiers and settlers build rammed-earth garrison walls and beacon towers along a road at the edge of sand dunes, a camel caravan passing by, irrigated fields and poplars in an oasis; snowy Qilian peaks in the distance. Clear dry sky. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and soft green pigments.
southwest-yi-commanderies: 111 BCE, Yelang in Guizhou: a Han army column in armour winds through misty karst mountain valleys, while local chieftains in feathered headdresses and wool capes come down from hilltop villages of stilted houses to submit, presenting bronze drums. Terraced fields, waterfalls and drifting cloud below the ridges. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised peaks.
pingzhun-junshu: 110 BCE, Chang'an: long lines of carts and riverboats bring sacks of grain, bolts of cloth and salt to huge state granaries and warehouses, where officials weigh goods on balances and set prices on wooden boards; merchants and common buyers crowd the market outside. Busy morning along the canal, porters with shoulder poles. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, many small figures.
fengshan-mount-tai: 110 BCE, Mount Tai: the imperial cortege climbs through pines and granite crags toward the summit, where a raised earthen altar sends up sacrificial smoke and officials in ceremonial robes and caps bow in rows; a jade tablet box is placed on the altar. Clouds swirl around the peak, golden morning light. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and green pigments.
minyue-conquered: 110 BCE, Dongye near Fuzhou: Han war boats with matting sails sail up a river estuary between green coastal hills while army columns march along the shore toward a Yue stronghold; later, families of the Yue people with baskets and boats move north along the road. Humid hazy light. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, river and boats in rhythm.
gojoseon: 109 BCE, Wanggeom near Pyongyang: a Han army with crossbowmen and siege ladders surrounds a walled city of earth and timber on the Taedong River, a fleet of Han ships moored on the river, Gojoseon defenders in leather armour on the ramparts. Pine-covered hills, autumn colours. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
dian-submits: 109 BCE, Dian by Lake Dian near Kunming: a Dian king with attendants in local dress, beside large bronze drums and cowrie containers, kneels before a Han envoy who presents a small gold seal with a coiled snake knob, while Han troops stand by the lakeshore. Blue lake, hills, clear sky. Rendered in the manner of Dian bronze sculpture scenes and Han murals, bronze, ochre and lake blue.
huzi-dike: 109 BCE, Huzi on the Yellow River: tens of thousands of labourers drive bamboo and wooden stakes, carry bundles of brushwood and stones on shoulder poles, and fill a vast breach in the river dike while the muddy waters swirl; officials and an imperial canopy watch from the bank, ceremonial jade cast into the river. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
loulan-gushi-captured: 108 BCE, Loulan in the Tarim basin: a small force of Han light cavalry gallops across salt flats and tamarisk dunes toward an oasis town of mud-brick and poplars beside Lop Nur, while defenders scatter; the desert stretches to the horizon. Riders without stirrups, small figures. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, sand yellow and red pigments.
princess-xijun-wusun: 105 BCE, Chigu by Issyk-Kul: a Han princess in silk robes sits alone in a round felt tent of the Wusun camp, playing a pipa-like lute, looking out toward the snowy Tianshan mountains and a flight of geese heading east; Wusun horsemen and herds graze by the lake. Wistful evening light. Painted in a Han tomb mural style with steppe elements, soft ochre, blue and red.
taichu-calendar: 104 BCE, Chang'an: court astronomers in black robes gather at night on an observatory terrace with bronze armillary instruments and gnomons, measuring the stars and noting results on bamboo slips; a large calendar diagram is being laid out on a table by lamplight. Clear starry sky. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, constellations shown as linked dots.
heavenly-horses: 104 BCE, the Ferghana Valley: a huge Han army with supply carts and camels crosses a high mountain pass into a fertile green valley, approaching the walls of a Dayuan city where tall, fine-limbed horses graze in pastures beyond; snow peaks above. Riders without stirrups, small figures. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments, elegant horses.
su-wu-detained: 100 BCE, by Lake Baikal: a lone envoy in tattered robes and a fur cap herds a flock of rams along a frozen lakeshore, holding a tall envoy's staff whose yak-tail tassels have fallen away; snowy forests and grey sky, a single felt tent in the distance. Cold, lonely atmosphere. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, stark spare composition.
li-ling-surrenders: 99 BCE, Mount Junji in Mongolia: a small Han infantry force behind a ring of carts fights on a rocky hillside, crossbowmen shooting as tens of thousands of Xiongnu cavalry encircle them across the steppe below; arrows fly, dust rises, figures small. No gore, battle seen from afar. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
bai-canal: 95 BCE, Jingyang on the Guanzhong plain: labourers dig a long canal with spades and baskets, leading water from the Jing River through sluices of wood and stone into a network of channels; farmers open ditches to green fields of wheat and millet. Bright spring day, wide flat landscape. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, many small workers.
witchcraft-scandal: 91 BCE, Chang'an: smoke rises over the city's tiled roofs as troops of the crown prince and imperial forces clash in the broad streets near the palace gates; townspeople flee into alleys, and in a palace garden officials dig up small wooden figures from the ground. Seen from a distance, no gore. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments.
li-guangli-surrenders: 90 BCE, the Yanran Mountains in Mongolia: an exhausted Han army column with carts and drooping banners is surrounded by Xiongnu cavalry on a wide steppe valley; a general on horseback rides slowly forward toward the Xiongnu ranks. Snow on distant peaks, a cold wind tugging the banners at dusk, no gore shown. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, figures small.
luntai-edict: 89 BCE, Chang'an: an aging emperor in black robes sits at a lacquered desk in a quiet hall, seen small from behind, as a scribe writes on bamboo slips; through the open doors farmers plough fields with oxen and soldiers return home from the west. Gentle afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and green pigments.
zhao-guo-daitian: 89 BCE, fields near Chang'an: farmers in hemp clothing work alternating ridges and furrows of millet with an iron ox-drawn plough pulled by two oxen, and a three-legged seed drill sowing rows; an official watches with assistants. Neat stripes of ridges and furrows run across the land toward a village of rammed-earth houses, bright spring sun. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
death-of-emperor-wu: 87 BCE, Wuzuo Palace near Zhouzhi: in a palace chamber at the foot of wooded hills, an old emperor rests on a couch under a canopy while three ministers kneel before him, a small boy heir in robes standing beside them; a painting on the wall shows a regent carrying a child. Dim lamplight. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted ochre, red and black.
salt-iron-debate: 81 BCE, Chang'an: in a palace hall, two groups face each other across mats — dozens of Confucian scholars in plain robes from the provinces on one side, government ministers in rich black robes and caps on the other — gesturing in heated debate as scribes record on bamboo slips. Daylight through lattice windows. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
su-wu: 81 BCE, Chang'an: a white-haired, weather-beaten envoy in worn fur clothing, carrying a bare envoy's staff, rides into the city gate with a few companions, while crowds of townspeople and officials line the road, some weeping; Chang'an's walls and towers behind. Bright spring day, willows in new leaf along the road. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, warm red, ochre and black pigments.
shangguan-plot: 80 BCE, Chang'an: at night in the palace precinct, guards in armour with torches surround a princess's mansion and a minister's residence, officials carrying sealed decrees enter through the gates, while a hidden band of armed men is led out of a side courtyard. Tiled roofs, bare trees, lanterns swaying in the wind. Seen from a distance, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black mineral pigments on plaster.
fu-jiezi-loulan: 77 BCE, Loulan oasis: inside a mud-brick hall with poplar beams, a Han envoy and his small escort sit at a banquet with the local king and nobles in Central Asian robes and felt caps, gold and silk gifts laid out on carpets; the moment of sudden commotion is glimpsed from the doorway as attendants spring up. Desert dunes and Lop Nur beyond. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, figures small.
huo-guang: 74 BCE, Weiyang Palace, Chang'an: in a grand audience hall, a stern regent in black robes stands before rows of ministers as a young man is escorted down from the throne dais and led out, his imperial seal ribbon removed by attendants; later a modest young man in plain clothes is brought in at the far gate. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and black on plaster, figures small.
five-generals-campaign: 71 BCE, the Ili valley: Han cavalry columns and Wusun horsemen in pointed caps sweep together across green mountain pastures beneath the snowy Tianshan, driving Xiongnu herds of horses, cattle and sheep before them as felt tents are abandoned. Wide panoramic landscape, riders without stirrups, small figures. Rendered in a Han tomb-mural style enriched with steppe animal motifs, ochre, green and rust red pigments.
zheng-ji-jushi: 67 BCE, Jiaohe near Turpan: Han agricultural soldiers in short tunics leave irrigated millet fields with spears and crossbows, marching toward a fortified city carved from a long loess plateau between two river gorges; the Flaming Mountains glow red in the distance under a hot summer sky. Small figures, battle implied rather than shown. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
huo-clan-exterminated: 66 BCE, Chang'an: imperial troops in black armour surround a great mansion with gate towers and walled gardens, soldiers carrying out chests and sealing doors, servants kneeling in the courtyard while officials read a decree; empty carriages stand abandoned in the street. Grey overcast morning, viewed from a distance, no gore. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted red, ochre and black pigments.
feng-fengshi-yarkand: 65 BCE, Yarkand oasis: a Han envoy on horseback with a yak-tail staff leads a combined army of troops from local Tarim states, in varied Central Asian dress and armour, toward a walled mud-brick city among poplars and irrigation channels, the Kunlun mountains rising behind. Dust in the bright desert light, small figures. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
zhao-chongguo-qiang: 61 BCE, the Huangshui valley near Xining: an elderly white-bearded general in armour rides slowly along a river where soldiers plough fields, dig irrigation ditches and build farm compounds; on distant hills, Qiang herders in wool cloaks watch with their yaks and sheep. High plateau, clear sky, calm mood. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments.
ever-normal-granary: 54 BCE, a frontier commandery: large raised granaries with tiled roofs and ventilation windows stand in a walled compound, officials measuring grain with bronze vessels as farmers sell carts of millet in a good harvest year; tally records kept on wooden boards. Golden autumn light, broad fields beyond. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, orderly granary buildings.
huhanye: 51 BCE, Ganquan Palace in the hills north of Chang'an: a Xiongnu chanyu in fur-trimmed robes and his nobles kneel before a raised throne hall as Han officials in black robes present gifts of silk, gold and a seal; horses and steppe attendants wait outside the gates among pines. Bright ceremonial day, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and black pigments.
shiqu-pavilion: 51 BCE, the Shiqu Pavilion in Weiyang Palace: a library pavilion of stone and timber by a water channel, where scholars in wide-sleeved robes and caps sit facing each other on mats, debating over bundles of bamboo-slip classics, clerks taking notes, an emperor's canopy at the far end. Calm daylight, willows. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
xiao-wangzhi-suicide: 47 BCE, Chang'an: outside the walled residence of an elderly Confucian tutor, palace guards with halberds surround the gate, while inside the courtyard a white-haired scholar in plain robes stands quietly beside a low table with a cup, his students kneeling and weeping. Restrained, sombre dusk. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted ochre, red and black pigments.
abandon-zhuya: 46 BCE, Zhuya on Hainan island: Han soldiers and officials board wooden ships with matting sails at a tropical harbour, carrying bundles and records, leaving a small rammed-earth fort behind; coconut palms and green hills line the shore, and local Li people watch from the trees. Hazy sea, departing mood. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, blue-grey and green pigments.
zhizhi: 36 BCE, Zhizhi city near Taraz: a Han and Central Asian allied army surrounds a fortress with a double timber palisade and earthen walls on a river plain, soldiers advancing with shields and crossbows, smoke rising from burning gates; the Tianshan foothills behind. Battle seen from far away, small figures, no gore. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
wang-feng-regent: 33 BCE, Chang'an: in a palace hall, five brothers in rich court robes and caps kneel side by side to receive enfeoffment seals on lacquered trays from palace officials, while an older man in a grand marshal's robe stands to one side and the young emperor watches from a curtained dais. Bronze lamps, lacquered pillars. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and black.
yellow-river-dongjun: 29 BCE, Dong Commandery on the Yellow River: thousands of labourers roll huge woven bamboo baskets filled with stones into a breach in the dike, building it up while muddy floodwaters swirl; boats ferry baskets, an official directs from the embankment, flooded fields beyond. Overcast sky. Rain clouds clear over the far bank. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, dynamic diagonal composition.
sunspot-record: 28 BCE, Chang'an: on a raised observatory terrace, court astronomers in black robes and caps gaze at a hazy setting sun through a thin veil of dust, one pointing to a small dark spot on its disk while another records on bamboo slips; bronze instruments and a gnomon on the terrace. Orange evening sky. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
liu-xiang-collation: 26 BCE, the imperial library in Chang'an: in a long hall lined with wooden shelves of bamboo-slip bundles and silk scrolls, an elderly scholar and a team of clerks compare versions on low tables, repairing cords, sorting slips and writing catalogue lists by lamplight. Quiet, studious atmosphere. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of shelves.
limit-land-slaves: 7 BCE, the countryside near Chang'an: a vast estate with high walled manor, watchtowers and rows of bonded labourers working the fields, while in the foreground two officials in black robes measure land with a rope and discuss a bamboo-slip document; a manor lord watches disdainfully from his gate. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
qilue: 6 BCE, the imperial library in Chang'an: a scholar in black robes kneels at a long desk sorting bundles of bamboo slips and silk scrolls into seven tagged groups on wooden racks, assistants carrying armfuls between shelves; a lamp and brushes on the desk, tidy rows of bundles. Calm daylight. Rendered as a Han pictorial brick relief, impressed lines and warm earth tones.
queen-mother-west-movement: 3 BCE, the streets of Chang'an in drought: crowds of common people in hemp clothing march along dusty roads and gather in lanes, singing, dancing, beating drums and passing small straw and hemp tokens hand to hand; some set up altars with lamps, and a parched sky hangs over cracked fields outside the walls. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, lively crowd.
yicun-buddhist-sutra: 2 BCE, Chang'an: in a quiet guesthouse for foreign envoys, a Yuezhi envoy in a Central Asian robe and cap sits cross-legged reciting from memory to a young Han student in black robes who kneels writing on bamboo slips; a lamp and incense burner between them, camels and horses resting in the courtyard. Soft evening light. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
dong-xian-falls: 1 BCE, Chang'an: a luxurious mansion with carved beams and gardens is sealed by palace guards, servants carrying out treasures as officials read a decree at the gate; meanwhile an official carriage arrives at the palace bringing a robed minister recalled to court. Winter dusk, bare trees. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted ochre, red and black pigments, figures small.
census-2ce: 2 CE, a county office: clerks in black caps kneel at low desks writing household registers on wooden boards and bamboo slips, while farming families queue at the gate to be counted; stacks of tied registers are loaded onto carts bound for the capital. Busy morning, rammed-earth walls and willows. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of small figures.
mingtang-biyong: 4 CE, south of Chang'an: a new ritual complex rises, a square multistorey hall on a high round terrace encircled by a ring-shaped moat, with gates on four sides; scholars in robes and caps walk in procession across bridges, and labourers finish the walls. Bright spring day. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and green pigments, ordered geometry.
wang-mang-regent: 6 CE, Weiyang Palace, Chang'an: a minister in rich black robes and a high cap stands beside the throne dais, holding audience as ministers kneel in rows, while a nursemaid holds a swaddled infant heir on a cushion behind a gauze curtain. Bronze incense burners, lacquered pillars, solemn atmosphere, figures small. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
zhai-yi-uprising: 7 CE, Dong Commandery: a large army raises banners outside a walled commandery seat on the eastern plain, soldiers with spears and crossbows forming ranks while the governor in armour addresses them from a chariot; later imperial columns approach from the west under dust clouds. Wide view, small figures. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
kings-land-decree: 9 CE, the Guanzhong countryside: officials in black robes set up boundary stakes and read a decree to villagers in a field, while farmers with hoes gather around; a manor lord's land markers are pulled up, and a market of bonded servants stands empty. Grey spring sky over wheat fields. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
xiongnu-seal-dispute: 9 CE, the Xiongnu court on the steppe: inside a large felt tent, Han envoys in black robes hand a new seal on a lacquered tray to a chanyu in fur-trimmed robes, while an old seal is taken away and Xiongnu nobles frown; horses and wagons outside under a wide sky. Rendered in a Han tomb-mural style with steppe motifs, ochre, red and black.
xin-coinage: 10 CE, a Chang'an market: confused merchants and buyers examine a jumble of strange currencies laid on mats — knife-shaped and spade-shaped bronze money, tortoise shells, cowrie shells, silver and gold pieces — arguing over values while officials post rules; stalls of grain and cloth lie idle. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and bronze-green pigments.
five-equalizations-six-monopolies: 10 CE, a city market office: officials at a raised pavilion in a walled market square set prices on wooden boards, weigh goods and lend coins to merchants, while stalls of salt, iron tools and jars of wine are under official control; traders and townspeople crowd the lanes. Busy daylight. Rendered as a Han pictorial brick relief from Sichuan, impressed lines and earth tones.
yellow-river-11: 11 CE, the north China plain near Puyang: the Yellow River has burst its dikes and spread across the land, a vast sheet of muddy water covering fields, villages of rammed-earth houses standing half submerged, people on rooftops and in small boats, broken dikes in the distance. Grey stormy sky. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, sweeping water lines.
wangtian-repealed: 12 CE, a county market near Chang'an: farmers and landlords crowd around an official notice board as a clerk reads aloud, land deeds on wooden boards change hands at tables, and a few families celebrate; behind, fields and village walls. Mixed relief and unrest in the crowd, overcast light. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
goguryeo-renamed: 12 CE, Goguryeo near Huanren: in a mountain valley with a fortress on a high plateau of cliffs, Xin troops in armour confront Goguryeo warriors in leather armour with long spears, a Han official reading a decree; the Hun River winds below forested ridges. Autumn colours, figures small. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre, red and black on plaster.
western-regions-lost: 13 CE, Yanqi near Karashahr: a Han protector's fortified compound of mud-brick walls by a lake in an oasis burns, smoke rising into a clear sky, as local cavalry ride away and Xiongnu horsemen appear on the hills; poplars and the Tianshan in the distance. Seen from far, no gore. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
lu-mu-uprising: 14 CE, Haiqu on the Shandong coast: a grey-haired widow in plain robes stands on a rocky shore beside young men with spears and oars boarding fishing boats, a small walled county town smoking in the distance behind them; waves and islands offshore. Windy dawn, defiant mood. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, blue-grey and red pigments.
huoquan-huobu: 14 CE, a Chang'an mint: workers pour bronze into moulds, others string newly cast round coins and stack spade-shaped bronze money on tables, while old coins are heaped in baskets to be melted down; officials check weights on balances. Furnace glow, smoky air. Clerks tie coins into strings of a hundred and load them onto carts in the yard. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, workshop scene.
wang-sunqing-dissection: 16 CE, Chang'an: in a sparse palace workshop, court physicians in black caps and robes gather around a long table covered with a cloth, measuring with bamboo rods and writing notes on bamboo slips, a chart of the body's channels pinned to a screen; no body or organs visible, only instruments and records. Lamplight. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, muted ochre and black pigments.
red-eyebrows: 18 CE, Ju county in Shandong: crowds of starving peasants with farm tools and wooden staves gather on a barren hillside, painting each other's eyebrows red; their leader stands on a rock, dry fields and a famine-stricken village below. Harsh sunlight, determined mood, figures small. Thin oxen and empty granaries stand by the road. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper with red accents.
flying-man-experiment: 19 CE, Chang'an: on a high palace terrace, a man wearing large wings of bird feathers and a feathered headdress glides out over a courtyard while officials and soldiers watch from below; behind him, other recruits with strange devices wait. Clear sky, curious onlookers, figures small. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, lively composition.
nine-temples: 20 CE, south of Chang'an: labourers dismantle old palace halls, carrying timber beams and tiles to a vast construction site where nine grand temple halls rise on terraces; thin, hungry workers carry earth in baskets under overseers, while grey famine-dry fields lie beyond. Dusty light. Smoke from cooking fires drifts over the workers' camp. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, many small figures.
liu-xiu-rises: 22 CE, Chongling in Nanyang: two brothers, one in a farmer's plain clothes and the other in armour, lead a band of local men and kinsmen out of a walled village with spears and a red banner; ox carts and horses follow along a path between rice fields and hills. Morning light. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
lulin-split: 22 CE, the Lülin mountains near Dangyang: a rebel mountain camp of thatched huts in a forested valley, many sick men lying under shelters as others pack up and depart in two separate columns along different trails, banners lowered. Misty, gloomy day. Some carry the sick on litters while smoke from cooking fires drifts between the trees. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, sombre composition.
battle-of-chengchang: 22 CE, Chengchang in Shandong: a peasant army with red-painted eyebrows charges across a plain with staves and spears, routing the disciplined ranks of a government army whose banners fall and chariots overturn; dust and confusion seen from a distance, small figures, no gore. A broad river and a walled town lie beyond. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
gengshi: 23 CE, Nanyang: on a riverside plain, rebel leaders and soldiers gather around a hastily built earthen altar where a man in imperial robes and crown stands awkwardly as banners are raised; tents and horses of the Lülin army surround the scene. Bright spring day. Drummers beat large drums on stands nearby. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, crowd of small figures.
wang-mang-death: 23 CE, Chang'an: smoke rises over the Weiyang Palace as rebel soldiers swarm through the gates; in a palace lake, a terrace pavilion on the water is surrounded by boats and soldiers, viewed from far away across the gardens. Evening sky glowing red, no gore. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments.
liu-yan-killed: 23 CE, Wan in Nanyang: in a rebel camp of tents, guards lead a general away under a grey sky while a younger brother in plain robes bows before the new emperor's tent, hiding his grief; officers watch suspiciously. Figures small, restrained mood. Horses are tethered by the tents and banners hang limp in still air. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
liu-xin-plot: 23 CE, Chang'an: at night in a scholar's study, three men in court robes huddle by lamplight over a bamboo-slip plan, while outside in the courtyard a servant slips away toward the palace; later guards with torches arrive at the gate. Tense, shadowy atmosphere. Bamboo groves rustle beside the wall. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black.
wei-ao-rises: 23 CE, Tianshui in the Longxi hills: local gentry and their retainers in robes and armour gather at a hilltop altar to acclaim a leader, sacrificial smoke rising, banners of the Han restored; loess ridges and terraced fields below. Clear autumn day. Horses and armed retainers wait along the slope while drums are beaten. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
liu-xiu-hebei: 24 CE, Handan: a walled city on the north China plain is besieged by an army of Hebei cavalry and infantry, siege ladders against the walls and gates opening; a commander on horseback watches from a rise. Dust clouds, figures small. Columns of horsemen without stirrups ride in from surrounding commanderies under many banners. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
gongsun-shu-shu: 24 CE, Chengdu: in a palace hall with Sichuan-style timber pillars, a governor in rich robes sits on a newly raised throne as local officials kneel; outside, the walls of Chengdu and fertile irrigated fields stretch to misty mountains. Officials carry seals and banners of the new kingdom across the courtyard while guards line the gate. Rendered as a Sichuan Han pictorial brick relief, impressed lines and warm earth tones.
chimei-take-changan: 25 CE, Chang'an: a peasant army with red-painted eyebrows pours through the city gates, carrying looted goods out of palace halls as smoke rises; in a camp outside, a young cowherd in plain clothing sits uneasily on a makeshift throne. Seen from a distance, no gore. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
chimei-surrender: 27 CE, Yiyang in Henan: a vast crowd of starving rebels with red eyebrows lays down spears, swords and shields, which pile up into a hill of weapons on a plain, while armies with banners stand in orderly ranks around them. Grey winter day, figures small. Ragged men sit exhausted by the road while soldiers distribute bowls of food. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
guangwu-slave-edicts: 30 CE, Luoyang: officials read an edict at a county office gate as freed bondservants and families in plain clothing leave a manor with bundles, while farmers bring modest grain payments to a granary. Calm spring day, willows and tiled roofs. Children run along the road behind their parents. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and soft green pigments.
longxi-campaign: 32 CE, Tianshui: an imperial army in armour with banners advances through steep loess hills and narrow valleys toward a walled town on a ridge, an imperial carriage among them; snowy mountains in the distance. Figures small. Supply carts struggle along a narrow track above a river gorge, and scouts on horseback ride ahead along the ridgeline under a pale winter sky. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
conquest-of-shu: 36 CE, Chengdu: Han war boats with oars sail up the Yangtze and Min rivers through gorges, while armies advance on the walled city of Chengdu, smoke rising from its gates; misty mountains of Sichuan around. Seen from far, no gore. Soldiers march along cliff-side plank roads while terraced fields and bamboo groves line the riverbanks. Painted as a Sichuan Han pictorial brick relief, warm earth tones.
land-survey-39: 39 CE, a commandery near Luoyang: officials measure fields with ropes and stakes and record households on wooden boards, while powerful local landlords in rich robes watch from walled manor towers; farmers stand nervously nearby. Overcast day. Clerks tie record boards into bundles while armed retainers stand at the manor gates. Rendered in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
trung-sisters: 40 CE, the Red River delta near Hanoi: two women leaders in local dress ride on elephants at the head of a crowd of armed villagers with bronze spears and axes, rice paddies, thatched stilt houses and palm trees around them; Han garrison walls in the distance. Rendered in the manner of Dong Son bronze-drum engraving, flowing figures in bronze and earth tones.
ma-yuan-jiaozhi: 43 CE, Me Linh in the Red River delta: a Han army in lamellar armour with red banners and halberds marches in a long file along an earthen dike between flooded rice paddies, approaching a village of thatched stilt houses beneath palm and banana trees; in the middle distance, beside the dike, soldiers haul ropes to raise a tall bronze boundary pillar. One continuous scene in a single unified landscape, humid haze, figures small, no gore. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red mineral pigments on plaster.
xiongnu-split: 48 CE, the Ordos: on the steppe inside the Yellow River bend, a Xiongnu chanyu and his nobles in felt caps lead herds and wagons toward a Han frontier fort, while to the north another Xiongnu host rides away in the opposite direction. Wide sky, riders without stirrups, small figures. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
ma-yuan-death: 49 CE, Hutou near Yuanling in Hunan: a Han army camp of tents and palisades clings to a riverbank in steep, humid gorges, soldiers resting listlessly under the heat; in a tent, an elderly white-bearded general lies ill on a mat, his armour and helmet set aside, officers kneeling beside him. Mist hangs over green cliffs and the swift river. Sombre, sweltering light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, green and dark red pigments on plaster.
guangwu-fengshan: 56 CE, Mount Tai: an imperial procession of officials in ceremonial robes and caps winds up stone steps among ancient pines and granite cliffs to a summit altar where incense smoke rises; attendants carry lacquered boxes of jade tablets and bundles of bamboo-slip texts. Sea of clouds below, golden morning light, the emperor a tiny figure among the retinue. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, flat stylised mountains.
na-gold-seal: 57 CE, Luoyang: in a palace hall of the Eastern Han court, an envoy from the Wa people of the eastern islands, in a simple wrapped robe with his hair tied in loops, kneels to receive a small square gold seal with a coiled snake knob on a lacquered tray from Han officials in black robes and caps. Courtiers watch from the side, bronze lamps glow. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, cinnabar, ochre and black pigments.
yuntai-generals: 60 CE, the Yuntai pavilion in Luoyang's Southern Palace: court painters on wooden scaffolds paint large wall murals of many armoured generals standing in rows, their faces stylised and indistinct, while officials in robes watch and attendants hold pigment bowls. Tall timber pillars, soft daylight through lattice windows, figures small. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of figures within figures.
liu-ying-buddhism: 65 CE, Pengcheng: in the garden of a princely palace, a king in Han court robes kneels before a small gilt Buddha image on an altar, offering incense, while foreign monks in ochre robes and Daoist adepts in loose garments stand together nearby; servants prepare a vegetarian feast on lacquered tables. Pines and a pond, calm morning. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and soft gold pigments.
wang-jing-yellow-river: 69 CE, near Xingyang: several hundred thousand labourers build long earthen dikes and stone sluice gates along the Yellow River, carrying earth in baskets on shoulder poles and ramming layers, while engineers in robes direct work from a mound; a separate canal branches off through a new channel. Wide flat plain, muddy water, bright day. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, many small figures.
yongchang-commandery: 69 CE, Buwei near Baoshan in western Yunnan: a long procession of Ailao people in wrapped cloth and feathered headdresses, carrying bronze drums, ivory and woven cloth, descends a mountain trail to meet Han officials in black robes at a new walled outpost; high forested ranges, terraced slopes and river valleys around. Misty morning light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red mineral pigments.
battle-of-pulei-sea: 73 CE, Lake Barkol in Xinjiang: one continuous wide view of Han cavalry with long banners charging across the grassy shore of a pale lake beneath snow-capped Tianshan peaks, while Xiongnu horsemen flee toward the far end of the shore driving their herds of horses and sheep before them. Riders without stirrups, small figures, dust rising, no gore. A single unbroken scene with no borders or registers. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, grey ink on paper, galloping horses in strong silhouette.
siege-of-shule-city: 75 CE, Shule fort near Qitai: a small Han garrison inside a mud-brick fortress on a hill digs a deep well within the walls while Xiongnu horsemen encircle the fort on the snowy plain below; on the ramparts, gaunt soldiers boil leather armour in a cauldron over a fire. Bitter winter sky. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, grey and red pigments, stark composition.
white-tiger-hall: 79 CE, the White Tiger Hall in Luoyang palace: scholars in wide-sleeved robes and scholars' caps sit in facing rows on mats, debating points of the classics over bundles of bamboo slips, while a historian at a side desk writes a record; the emperor sits on a curtained dais at the far end. Calm daylight, painted beams. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, ordered rows.
wang-chong-lunheng: 80 CE, Shangyu in Zhejiang: an elderly scholar in a plain robe sits in a simple thatched study among rice paddies and rolling green hills, writing on bamboo slips at a low table piled with manuscripts, a window open to a sky with drifting clouds and a distant rainstorm. Quiet, contemplative mood, soft southern light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, soft ochre, green and black pigments.
hanshu-completed: 82 CE, Luoyang: in a court library, a historian in black robes works at a long desk surrounded by stacked bamboo-slip bundles and silk scrolls, assistants copying and tying chapters, while a young woman scholar reads a draft beside him. Lamplight, wooden shelves, quiet industry, figures small. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, rows of shelves and scrolls.
dou-xian-xiongnu: 89 CE, Mount Yanran in Mongolia: a huge Han army with banners and cavalry stands at the foot of a rocky mountain on the steppe, while stonemasons on a scaffold carve a long inscription of indistinct marks into a cliff face; captured Xiongnu horses and herds graze on the plain. Vast sky, figures small. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
kushan-attack-ban-chao: 90 CE, Shule near Kashgar: one single continuous scene of a large Kushan army in Central Asian armour and tunics, with horsemen and camels, camped on a dry plain before a walled oasis city, its tents and campfires sprawling toward the foot of the Pamir mountains, while small Han defenders guard the city gates and empty granaries stand open in the fields. Dusty, hot light. Rendered as one unified Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, small figures, a single picture with no horizontal registers, bands, borders or panels, no text.
battle-of-jinwei-mountain: 91 CE, the Altai Mountains: Han cavalry with long spears and crossbows sweep through a high mountain valley of larch forests and alpine meadows, Xiongnu horsemen and wagons fleeing westward over a pass; snow peaks above, dust and banners. Riders without stirrups, figures small, no gore. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments.
fall-of-dou-xian: 92 CE, Luoyang: at night palace guards with torches seal the gates of a great general's mansion, officials carry decrees, and a young emperor watches from a palace tower with a eunuch attendant in a tall cap beside him; soldiers line the streets. Tense lamplight, figures small. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, dark sombre composition.
ban-chao-yanqi: 94 CE, Yanqi near Karashahr: a Han general with grey hair on horseback leads a combined army of troops from eight oasis states in varied dress toward a lakeside walled city, while local princes kneel offering hostages and tribute at the gate; poplars, reed beds and the Tianshan behind. Bright day. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
gan-ying: 97 CE, on the shore of the Persian Gulf: a Han envoy in a black robe and his small escort, with camels and horses, stand on a sandy beach looking out at a vast sea, while Parthian sailors in tunics and trousers point to their wooden ships and warn of the long voyage. Palm trees and a mud-brick port behind. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
shuowen: 100 CE, Luoyang: a scholar in a plain robe kneels at a low desk surrounded by stacks of bamboo slips, sorting them into many groups by component, each bundle tagged; brushes, ink stones and a lamp beside him, while students copy entries on slips. Characters shown only as indistinct marks. Quiet study, soft light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, warm ochre, red and black pigments.
deng-sui-regency: 105 CE, Luoyang palace: a woman regent in modest dark silk robes sits behind a gauze screen on a dais, a swaddled infant emperor held by a nurse beside her, as ministers kneel presenting reports on floods; plain undecorated hall, few ornaments, reflecting frugality. Soft daylight. Rain falls on flooded fields seen beyond the open doors. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, figures small.
ban-zhao-lessons: 106 CE, Luoyang palace: an elderly woman scholar in modest robes sits at a low desk writing on bamboo slips, while young palace ladies kneel on mats around her listening attentively; a bronze lamp, a zither and scroll bundles in the room, a garden visible through lattice doors. Calm afternoon light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, soft ochre, red and green pigments.
great-qiang-rebellion: 107 CE, Lintao in Gansu: Qiang warriors in wool cloaks with spears, on horseback and on foot, sweep down from loess hills toward a Han frontier town, smoke rising from abandoned farms, while Han conscripts flee along a road; yaks and sheep on distant slopes. Dry wind, dusty sky, figures small. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
western-regions-abandoned: 107 CE, Qiuci near Kucha: a Han protector's garrison leaves a mud-brick fortress in an oasis, soldiers and officials loading carts and camels with records and supplies, banners lowered; local people watch from poplar-lined irrigation channels, the red cliffs and snowy Tianshan behind. Melancholy evening light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
zhang-heng-armillary: 117 CE, Luoyang: in an observatory courtyard, a large bronze armillary sphere of interlocking rings stands on a stand, driven by a water wheel fed from a clepsydra tank, while astronomers in robes and caps observe it turning and compare with the night sky; stars and a crescent moon overhead. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, intricate rings.
ban-yong-western-regions: 123 CE, Liuzhong near Turpan: a Han commander leads a garrison of soldiers into an oasis town of mud-brick walls and vineyards, while others build farm fields and irrigation channels; the red Flaming Mountains rise behind, and Xiongnu riders retreat over the distant desert. Hot bright day. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
nineteen-eunuchs: 125 CE, Luoyang palace at night: a group of nineteen eunuchs in tall caps and dark robes escort a young boy in imperial robes through torch-lit corridors toward a throne hall, guards opening the gates; in a distant courtyard, armed men take control. Seen from a distance, no gore. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, shadowy composition.
yangjia-xiaolian-reform: 132 CE, Luoyang: in the courtyard of the rebuilt Imperial Academy, middle-aged candidates in plain robes kneel at low desks writing examination answers on bamboo slips, while examiners in black caps walk between rows; new tiled lecture halls and pines surround the yard. Bright morning. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, orderly rows.
longxi-earthquake-detected: 138 CE, Luoyang: in a palace hall stands a large bronze seismoscope shaped like a wine jar ringed by eight dragons, with bronze toads below; a bronze ball has just dropped from one dragon's mouth into a toad's open mouth, and officials in robes gather around it puzzled; through the doorway a messenger arrives on horseback. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
emperor-zhi-poisoned: 146 CE, Luoyang palace: a quiet palace chamber at dawn, an empty child's seat beside a low table with an overturned bowl of soup cake, attendants kneeling in grief in the doorway while a powerful general in rich robes strides away down a colonnade. No violence shown, sombre mood. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, muted ochre, red and black pigments.
an-shigao-translations: 148 CE, Luoyang: in a modest monastery hall, a foreign monk in ochre robes from Parthia sits cross-legged reciting from palm-leaf texts, while Chinese assistants in robes kneel at low desks writing translations on bamboo slips; a small Buddha image and incense burner on an altar. Lamplight and quiet focus. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
tanshihuai-confederation: 156 CE, Danhan Mountain in Inner Mongolia: on vast grassland beneath a rounded mountain, Xianbei chieftains in fur hats and braided hair ride in from all directions to gather around a large felt tent, banners and horse herds everywhere; cooking fires smoke under a huge sky. Riders without stirrups, figures small. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural enriched with steppe animal-art motifs, ochre, rust red and black.
liang-ji: 159 CE, Luoyang: one single continuous courtyard scene of the vast mansion of Liang Ji with carved beams and walled gardens, palace guards with halberds standing at the forced-open gate as officials carry out lacquered chests, while bolts of silk and bronze vessels pile up in the courtyard; a few eunuch officials in tall caps direct the work from the steps of a hall, and townspeople watch from the street outside the wall. Grey day, no gore. Rendered as one unified Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, a single picture with no dividing bands, registers or panels, no text.
laozi-sacrifice: 165 CE, Ku in Henan: at a small shrine among ancient cypress trees, officials in ceremonial robes and caps make offerings of incense and wine on a stone altar, a tablet of the sage set within, musicians playing bells and chime stones; villagers watch from beyond the wall. Calm morning. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
partisan-prohibitions: 166 CE, Luoyang: guards with halberds lead a line of scholar-officials in plain robes and caps out of the city gate toward prison carts, while students and townspeople gather at a distance, some bowing in respect; eunuchs in tall caps watch from a palace tower. Overcast winter day. Bare willows line the moat. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
daqin-envoy: 166 CE, Rinan in central Vietnam: on a tropical riverbank, foreign travellers in tunics and cloaks, with curly hair and beards, present elephant ivory tusks, rhinoceros horn and tortoise shell to Han officials in black robes; wooden sailing ships rest in the river mouth, palm trees and green hills around. Hazy humid light. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments.
duan-jiong-qiang: 167 CE, Gaoping near Guyuan: Han cavalry and infantry in armour march through dry, eroded loess gullies under banners, pursuing Qiang warriors in wool cloaks who retreat over distant ridges with their herds; smoke from abandoned camps rises. Bleak landscape, figures small, no gore. Supply carts and pack horses follow the columns along a dry riverbed under a pale sky. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
chen-fan-dou-wu-coup: 168 CE, Luoyang: at night, eunuchs in tall caps and palace guards with torches hurry a young emperor through corridors, while at the palace gates armed troops clash with a small band led by an elderly official; seen from a distance through the gate, no gore. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments.
second-partisan-prohibition: 169 CE, Luoyang: a long line of scholar-officials in plain robes is led between guards into a walled prison compound, while families wait outside the gate in grief and eunuch officials in tall caps watch from horseback. Cold dusk, bare trees. A few scholars look back at the city walls, their hands bound, while a prison clerk records names on wooden boards by the gate. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, solemn composition.
xiping-classics: 175 CE, Luoyang: outside the Imperial Academy, rows of tall stone tablets stand under a tiled shelter, their surfaces covered in fine indistinct marks; stonemasons chisel, scholars in robes compare texts, and students make ink rubbings on paper. Carts of visitors crowd the street. Bright day. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, grey and black pigments.
tanshihuai-defeats-han: 177 CE, the Yanmen frontier in Shanxi: three columns of Han cavalry ride out from a pass of rammed-earth walls and watchtowers onto the steppe, where vast numbers of Xianbei horsemen in fur hats wait on the horizon; later, scattered riders return. Wide sky, riders without stirrups, small figures. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
sale-of-offices: 178 CE, the Western Garden in Luoyang: in an ornate pavilion beside a lake, officials and wealthy men queue with chests of coins and bolts of silk, a clerk weighing coins on a balance and handing over official seals with ribbons; eunuchs supervise. Lavish garden, willows. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and gold pigments.
hongdu-gate-school: 178 CE, Luoyang: at an academy by the Hongdu Gate, young students in robes kneel at desks practising brushwork on silk, painting landscapes and figures, others reciting rhapsodies; a master guides a student's brush. Gate tower behind, soft daylight. Rolls of silk, pigment dishes and brush racks crowd the low tables, while a few Confucian officials in black caps frown from the doorway of the hall.
