Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
battle-of-changshe: 184 CE, Changshe in Henan: at night under strong wind, Han soldiers carrying torches set fire to dry grass around a vast rebel camp of Yellow Turbans with yellow headscarves; flames and smoke billow, rebels flee across the plain, and Han cavalry charge from the city gate. Seen from afar, no gore. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black.
battle-of-guangzong: 184 CE, Guangzong in Hebei: Han troops with siege ladders storm the walls of a rebel-held city at dawn, Yellow Turban defenders in yellow headscarves on the ramparts, smoke rising over the gates; a river and fields beyond. Viewed from a distance, no gore, figures small. Banners stream in the wind above the advancing ranks. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
liangzhou-rebellion: 184 CE, Jincheng near Lanzhou: Qiang horsemen in wool cloaks and Han rebels in armour gather on a plain by the Yellow River, raising banners before a walled town; loess hills and snowy mountains in the distance. Wind-blown dust, figures small. Captured carts and herds of horses gather behind the rebel lines. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments.
provincial-governors: 188 CE, Luoyang: in a palace hall, several officials in rich robes kneel to receive seals, tallies and military banners on lacquered trays from court eunuchs and ministers, while their armed retinues wait with horses outside the gates. Bronze lamps, solemn mood, figures small. Painted beams and lacquered pillars frame the scene, and scribes record each appointment on bamboo slips. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
western-garden-colonels: 188 CE, the Western Garden in Luoyang: on a parade ground before a pavilion, a new army in armour drills in ranks under eight banners, eight colonels on horseback in front, while a eunuch commander in a tall cap reviews them from a platform beside the emperor's canopy. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
dong-zhuo: 189 CE, Luoyang: a long column of heavy cavalry and soldiers from the northwest frontier rides through the city gate under banners as frightened residents watch from doorways; in the palace, a young boy is led to the throne. Smoky, uneasy sky. Courtiers kneel along the palace steps as armoured guards take their places at every gate. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, galloping horses.
he-jin-eunuchs: 189 CE, Luoyang palace: smoke rises from a burning palace gate as soldiers storm through the courtyards and eunuchs in tall caps flee along colonnades; at a distance, palace walls and towers loom. Chaos shown from far, no gore. Soldiers with swords and torches pour across the courtyards, and frightened attendants hide behind pillars. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, dark red, ochre and black pigments.
zheng-xuan-annotations: 190 CE, Gaomi in Shandong: an elderly scholar in plain robes sits in a rustic courtyard school under an old tree, surrounded by hundreds of students kneeling on mats with bamboo-slip books, as he explains a text; thatched halls and fields beyond. Peaceful afternoon. Stacks of annotated slips lie beside him, and a few disciples copy his words with brushes. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
anti-dong-coalition: 190 CE, Luoyang: the great city burns behind its walls, smoke billowing over palaces and tiled roofs, while a long column of soldiers forces residents westward along a road with carts and bundles; on distant hills, coalition armies under many banners watch. Ash drifts across a red evening sky over the abandoned plain. Rendered in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
zhang-lu-hanzhong: 191 CE, Hanzhong basin: a Daoist community where travellers stop at a free hostel by a mountain road, rice and meat set out on a table for any guest; libationers in robes teach villagers, rice paddies and the Han River in a valley between forested mountains. Calm, misty morning. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red.
sun-jian-yangren: 191 CE, near Yangren and the ruins of Luoyang: a general in armour leads soldiers into a burned-out city of broken walls and blackened palaces, men clearing rubble and restoring the earthen mounds of imperial tombs; dark smoke trails remain. Melancholy grey light. Banners hang limp, a few survivors watch from broken gateways, and weeds grow over the stone paths. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
battle-of-jieqiao: 191 CE, Jieqiao in Hebei: a line of crossbowmen behind large shields kneels by a bridge over a river, firing volleys at a charging cavalry force mounted on white horses; dust clouds and fallen banners, viewed from a distance, no gore. Rows of banners stand on the far bank behind the archers. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, red, ochre and white pigments.
dong-zhuo-killed: 192 CE, Chang'an: at a palace gate, a large warlord's carriage halts while armed guards close in and a tall warrior with a halberd stands beside it; officials watch from the colonnade, crowds celebrate in the streets beyond. Seen from a distance, no gore. Banners fly over the gate towers and bare trees line the avenue. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
qingzhou-army: 192 CE, Shouzhang in Shandong: a vast crowd of Yellow Turban rebels and their families, with yellow headscarves, lay down weapons before a general on horseback, then are organised into new ranks with fresh banners; ox carts and fields around. Figures small. Officers record names on wooden boards as new recruits receive spears. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, yellow and red pigments.
xu-province-campaign: 193 CE, Xu province near Tancheng: a vast army marches across a plain past burning villages, smoke rising into a dark sky, refugees with carts and bundles fleeing along the banks of the Si River. Seen from far, no gore or bodies shown. Bare trees and empty fields line the road under drifting ash. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper, sombre composition.
battle-of-puyang: 194 CE, Puyang: a walled city on the plain, a burning gate at night, cavalry under one general charging out to meet a besieging army; a general on horseback escapes through flames, figures small. Seen from a distance, no gore. Torches and campfires glow across the dark plain, and the city walls loom above the smoke. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, red, ochre and black pigments.
sun-ce-jiangdong: 195 CE, crossing the Yangtze toward Wu: a young general in armour stands at the prow of a war boat as a fleet of wooden boats with matting sails carries soldiers across the wide river; on the southern shore, misty hills and walled towns of Jiangdong await. Banners snap in the wind above the oarsmen. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper.
emperor-xian-flight: 195 CE, near Anyi in Shanxi: a young emperor in tattered robes and a small band of officials and palace women travel east on foot and in a broken carriage across bleak hills, hungry and weary, with distant cavalry in pursuit; ruined fields and a grey sky. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, muted ochre and black.
heyin: 528 CE, Heyin on the Yellow River near Luoyang: a grey morning on the wide muddy river bank, hundreds of small figures of court officials in dark gauze caps and wide-sleeved robes gathered under guard by mounted Xianbei cavalry in lamellar armour with banners; a small boat drifts out on the brown current, Luoyang's walls faint on the far horizon. Tense, distant, no violence shown. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll, fine gossamer ink line, faded mineral colour on aged silk.
battle-of-fukou: 528 CE, Fukou pass near Handan: a compact column of Xianbei heavy cavalry in lamellar armour, riders with stirrups and long lances, bursts out of a narrow gorge in the Taihang foothills onto a plain crowded with a vast, disordered rebel host of peasant infantry and banners; dust rising, the rebels scattering into the distance. Seen from a high vantage, many tiny figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red and ochre outlines, earth pigments on plaster.
chen-qingzhi: 529 CE, approach to Luoyang: a disciplined southern army of some seven thousand foot soldiers, all in white robes over their armour, marches along a road between loess hills with white banners, escorting a prince's ox-drawn carriage; the great walls and Buddhist pagoda of Northern Wei Luoyang rise ahead in the haze. Morning light, long winding column. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, delicate gossamer line, pale colour on silk.
wen-xuan: 530 CE, Jiankang: inside a Liang palace library pavilion with lattice screens and a garden of willows beyond, a group of scholars in loose robes and gauze caps sit on mats at low tables sorting bamboo-rolled scrolls and paper rolls into lacquered boxes, brush stands and ink stones beside them; a young prince seen from behind presides. Soft afternoon light. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll, fine gossamer ink line, light mineral colour on aged silk.
erzhu-rong-killed: 530 CE, Luoyang palace: an autumn evening at a Northern Wei palace hall with tiled roofs and red columns, guards in lamellar armour hidden behind a side gate while a group of officials in dark robes waits on the stone terrace; outside the walls, a large Xianbei cavalry force with torches gathers ominously on the plain. Tense, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black, cinnabar and ochre, flat figures with fine line.
battle-of-hanling: 532 CE, Hanling near Anyang: on a broad plain, a small army arranged in a tight circular formation with ox-carts chained together and banners holds firm as it advances against a much larger cavalry host in lamellar armour; dust clouds, low hills behind, many small figures seen from afar, the larger army beginning to break. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, bold red outlines, ochre, green and black earth pigments on plaster.
xie-he-six-principles: 532 CE, Jiankang: a quiet studio pavilion open to a bamboo garden, a scholar-critic in a loose robe seated on a mat beside a low table, studying an unrolled painted handscroll of figures and horses with several other painted scrolls hanging on a stand; an attendant grinds ink. Calm daylight, pine and rock outside. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine gossamer line, delicate washes of colour on aged silk.
xiaowu-poisoned: 535 CE, Chang'an: a winter evening in a Western Wei palace courtyard, an inner hall with lamps glowing behind paper screens, a single wine cup on a lacquer tray carried by a servant along a covered corridor, armoured guards standing silently at the gate; snow on the tiled roofs. Mood quiet and ominous, no figures in close-up. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black ground, cinnabar and ochre, fine outlined figures.
shayuan: 537 CE, Shayuan near the Wei River: a marshy plain of tall reeds where a small Western Wei army lies hidden in the reed beds, archers and armoured cavalry with banners rising to ambush a vast enemy column marching along the river bank; the larger force breaking in confusion into the marsh. Distant view, autumn light, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Western Wei Dunhuang cave mural, lapis blue, malachite green, ochre ground.
battle-of-xiaoguan: 537 CE, Xiaoguan near Tong Pass: dawn in steep loess gorges beside the Yellow River, cavalry in lamellar armour pour down a narrow defile onto an encamped army whose tents and banners are scattered along the valley floor; the camp in disarray, dust and morning mist. Distant aerial view, many tiny figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, bold red outlines, ochre and green earth pigments on plaster.
battle-of-heqiao: 538 CE, Heqiao on the Yellow River near Luoyang: two armies of armoured cavalry and infantry clash around a long pontoon bridge of boats across the broad muddy river, banners of both sides tangled; behind, the ruined walls of Luoyang with smoke rising from burned temple pagodas. Distant view, no gore, many small figures. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine gossamer line, muted colour on aged silk.
su-chuo-six-edicts: 541 CE, Chang'an: inside a Western Wei government hall with timber columns and bracket sets, rows of officials in dark gauze caps and long robes kneel on mats reciting from bamboo slips and paper rolls, while a senior minister seated at a low desk drafts documents with a brush; lamps and a lacquer screen behind. Orderly, calm. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black, cinnabar and ochre, fine outlined figures.
battle-of-mangshan-543: 543 CE, Mangshan north of Luoyang: on the rolling loess ridge dotted with burial mounds, a great Eastern Wei cavalry charge sweeps over the hills, armoured horsemen with lances and banners driving the opposing army back towards the west; the Yellow River glints beyond. Distant panoramic view, dust clouds, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre, black and green earth pigments, procession-like rhythm.
yupian: 543 CE, Jiankang: a southern scholar in a loose robe and gauze cap sits at a low table in a study pavilion, surrounded by stacks of paper rolls and bundles of slips, carefully brushing characters on a long roll, which is not legible; an ink stone, brush rest and lamp beside him, a garden of plantain leaves outside. Quiet evening. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll, fine gossamer line, soft colour on aged silk.
qimin-yaoshu: 544 CE, Shandong countryside: a broad scene of farm life on a loess plain, farmers in short jackets plough with oxen, women tend mulberry trees, workers hoe millet rows, a courtyard farmhouse with tiled roof where jars of fermenting grain and wine stand by the wall; an official-scholar in a robe observes and takes notes. Spring daylight. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei tomb brick painting, quick red and black outlines on pale ground.
yutai-xinyong: 545 CE, Jiankang: a Liang palace garden at dusk, court ladies in high-waisted robes with flowing ribbons sit beside a jade-white terrace balustrade, one holding a mirror, others reading paper rolls of poems; a scholar compiles scrolls at a nearby table, lotus pond and willows beyond. Elegant, romantic mood. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll in the manner of the Admonitions Scroll, gossamer line, delicate colour on aged silk.
paramartha-arrives: 546 CE, Guangzhou harbour: a sea-going merchant ship with matting sails anchored in the Pearl River, an Indian monk in an ochre robe stepping ashore with bundles of palm-leaf manuscripts, greeted by local officials and Chinese monks; banana trees, a riverside town of timber houses, small boats. Warm humid light. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, lapis and malachite, flowing outlined figures.
yubi: 546 CE, Yubi fortress near Jishan: a walled hilltop citadel on a loess plateau above the Fen River, besieged by a vast army with siege towers, tunnels being dug and earth ramps rising against the walls; defenders on the ramparts with crossbows, smoke in places. Winter light, distant aerial view, many tiny figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre and black earth pigments on plaster.
luoyang-qielan: 547 CE, Luoyang: a lone scholar in a robe walking among the ruins of a once-great city, overgrown foundations of temples, a fallen bronze bell, broken stone lions and the charred base of a huge wooden pagoda, weeds and wild millet growing in the streets, crows overhead; in a dreamlike haze above, the faint outline of the city's former golden halls. Melancholy autumn light. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll, gossamer line, pale ink washes on aged silk.
battle-of-hanshan: 547 CE, Hanshan near Pengcheng (Xuzhou): a southern army has dammed the Si River with earth and timber, flood water spreading across the plain towards the walled city; northern cavalry in lamellar armour sweep down from low hills onto the southern camp on the riverbank. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, grey sky. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, muted colour on aged silk.
hou-jing-defects: 547 CE, Xuanhu in Henan: a general's camp on the plain south of the Yellow River, a mounted envoy in a gauze cap rides out from a tented encampment with banners carrying a sealed lacquer document case, heading south across fields towards distant hills; armoured cavalry escort him. Dusk sky. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black, cinnabar and ochre, flat outlined figures.
fubing: 550 CE, outside Chang'an: soldier-farmer families on a wide Wei River plain, men in short tunics drilling with spears and bows in formation on one side of the field, women and children working millet fields and farmhouses nearby; officers on horseback with banners grouped into units. Clear autumn day. Painted in the style of a Western Wei Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, lapis and malachite, lively small figures.
battle-of-baling: 551 CE, Baling (Yueyang) on Dongting Lake: a walled river town on the shore where defenders hold the ramparts while a fleet of warships with tiered decks and matting sails from downstream is stalled offshore; smoke over the water, distant hills and the wide lake. Overcast light, many small figures. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, pale blue-green colour on aged silk.
turkic-khaganate: 552 CE, Mongolian steppe: a vast grassland under a huge sky, a Turkic encampment of felt yurts and wolf-head standards, mounted warriors with long braided hair and bows gathered in a great circle around a chieftain's tent; herds of horses and sheep in the distance, a caravan arriving with bales of silk. Bright daylight. Painted in the style of a Sogdian mural from Panjakent, rich reds and blues, flat outlined figures.
western-wei-takes-shu: 553 CE, Chengdu: an army in lamellar armour with banners descends the steep plank roads and mountain passes of the Qinling into the green Sichuan basin, the walled city of Chengdu on the plain ahead with rivers and rice fields; mist on the mountains. Panoramic, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties Dunhuang cave mural landscape, malachite green hills, lapis sky, ochre ground.
book-of-wei: 554 CE, Ye: a court historian's office in a Northern Qi palace, scholars in gauze caps and long robes sit at low tables among stacks of paper rolls and bamboo archives, writing with brushes; officials in the background argue and gesture over a scroll. Indoor lamp light, timber columns. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, soft ochre and green, elegant figures.
western-liang-xiao-cha: 555 CE, Jiangling on the Yangtze: a small, partly ruined walled city on the river, northern troops in lamellar armour posted at the gates, while inside a modest palace hall a man in imperial robes, seen small and from behind, receives officials; burned quarters still visible, the river with boats beyond. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll, gossamer line, muted colour on aged silk.
wang-sengbian-killed: 555 CE, Shitou fortress at Jiankang: night on the Yangtze, the stone citadel on a riverside hill, soldiers with torches scaling the walls by surprise from boats and from the landward side, a palace compound inside lit up; the broad river reflecting firelight. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, dark ink and faint colour on aged silk.
qi-great-wall-2: 555 CE, Juyong Pass north of Beijing: a huge workforce of conscripted labourers in short tunics carrying earth and stones in baskets on shoulder poles, ramming earth walls between timber frames along steep mountain ridges, overseers on horseback; the wall snakes westward over barren hills into the distance. Autumn haze. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre and grey earth pigments.
battle-of-mufu: 556 CE, beneath Mount Mufu at Jiankang: rain-soaked fields along the Yangtze where a ragged southern army with banners charges out of the city gates against a northern camp below the rocky mountain; the northern troops break and flee towards the river. Distant panoramic view, grey rain, many small figures. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, pale ink and colour on silk.
yuwen-hu-kills-emperor: 557 CE, Chang'an: an empty Northern Zhou throne hall at dusk, the throne platform under a canopy left vacant, armoured guards lining the steps, a group of officials bowing towards a powerful regent seen small from behind at the hall's centre; long shadows on the stone floor. Quiet and ominous. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black ground, cinnabar and ochre.
yuan-clan-massacre: 559 CE, Ye: the grey Zhang River flowing quietly past the long rammed-earth walls of the Northern Qi capital under a heavy, overcast sky; a few torn pale silk banners drift on the current, a line of guards with spears stands far off along the bank, and empty palace halls with closed doors rise beyond the walls. Two fishermen watch silently from a small boat. A mood of loss shown only through emptiness: no bodies, no blood, no red in the water. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, muted ochre and grey pigments.
siege-of-jinyang: 563 CE, Jinyang (Taiyuan): deep winter, snow over the walled city in the Fen valley, a combined army of Northern Zhou infantry and Turkic horsemen in fur caps encamped beneath the walls, while defenders sally out from the gates; frozen river, mountains behind. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre, black and white pigments.
northern-qi-code: 564 CE, Ye: a Northern Qi court hall where officials in dark gauze caps and robes stand in rows as a large set of paper scrolls in lacquer cases is presented on a table before the throne platform; scribes copying documents at side tables, guards at the doors. Formal, calm daylight. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, soft ochre and green, elegant procession of figures.
prince-lanling: 564 CE, beneath the walls of Luoyang: a small band of five hundred armoured cavalry, their leader in a fearsome mask-like helmet seen small among them, charges through a siege camp to the city gate, defenders on the walls cheering; dust and banners, Mount Mang behind. Panoramic view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural like the Lou Rui tomb procession, red outlines, ochre and green, dynamic horses.
hua-jiao-revolt: 567 CE, the Yangtze near Dongting: a river battle between two fleets of warships with tiered decks and matting sails, archers on the decks, burning rafts drifting downstream; wide river and green hills, Changsha's region far off. Distant view, smoke, many small figures. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, blue-green colour on aged silk.
ashina-marriage: 568 CE, Chang'an: a bridal procession arrives at the city gate, a Turkic princess in a felt hat seen from afar in a curtained carriage, escorted by Turkic horsemen with braided hair and Zhou court officials; camels with gifts and silks, crowds along the wide avenue. Bright spring day. Painted in the style of a Northern Zhou Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre, procession of small figures.
yuwen-hu-killed: 572 CE, Chang'an palace: an inner chamber of the Northern Zhou palace with a lacquer screen, an elderly woman seated, an older official in robes reading from a scroll before her, a younger man in robes standing behind him raising a jade tablet; small distant figures, the moment before the blow, nothing violent shown. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei lacquer screen painting, black, cinnabar and ochre.
wu-mingche-expedition: 573 CE, Shouyang: labourers and soldiers build an earth and timber dam across the Fei River, the waters rising and flooding towards the walled city of Shouyang on the Huai plain; southern banners on the dykes, northern defenders on the walls. Distant aerial view, many small figures, summer clouds. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, pale colour on silk.
lanling-death: 573 CE, Ye: a quiet courtyard of a nobleman's mansion at dusk, a messenger with a lacquer tray holding a wine jar and cup arrives at the gate, servants watching; a lone figure in robes seen from behind stands on the veranda looking at the sky; a helmet and armour on a stand inside. Melancholy, no violence. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, soft ochre.
zhou-bans-buddhism: 574 CE, Chang'an: a Buddhist monastery being closed, monks and nuns in grey robes leaving through the gate carrying small bundles, officials in caps taking inventory as bronze statues and bells are loaded onto ox-carts for the state treasury; the pagoda stands silent behind. Overcast day, no violence. Painted in the style of a Northern Zhou Dunhuang cave mural, faded lapis and malachite, ochre ground.
zhiyi-tiantai: 575 CE, Mount Tiantai in Zhejiang: a misty mountain landscape of pines, waterfalls and stone bridges, a monk in plain robes, seen small, seated in meditation in a simple thatched hermitage on a ledge, a few disciples climbing a winding path below. Dawn mist. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll landscape in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, early blue-green mountains on aged silk.
battle-of-pingyang: 576 CE, Pingyang (Linfen) in the Fen valley: winter, a walled city held by Northern Zhou troops while a large Northern Qi relief army masses outside; Zhou cavalry in lamellar armour wheel in to attack across the frozen plain, banners streaming. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre, black and white pigments.
battle-of-lvliang: 578 CE, Lüliang near Pengcheng: northern troops sink lines of wheels and chains across the Si River behind a southern fleet, the boats trapped in the shallowing channel near the walled city; cavalry waiting on the banks. Wide aerial view, cold grey sky, many small figures. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, pale colour on aged silk.
yuchi-jiong-rebellion: 580 CE, Ye: a great army in lamellar armour encircles the walled city on the Zhang River plain, siege ladders against the walls; in the distance, dark smoke rising as parts of the old capital burn and townspeople leave in carts. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, red outlines, ochre and grey pigments on plaster.
kaihuang-code: 581 CE, Daxing (Chang'an): in a Sui palace hall with red columns and bracket sets, ministers in black gauze caps and red and purple robes present a new law code as rolls in lacquer cases on a long table; scribes copy, and in a courtyard outside instruments of harsh punishment are carried away. Clear daylight. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens.
daxing-city: 582 CE, Daxing: a bird's-eye view of a vast new capital being laid out on the plain south of the Wei River, a strict grid of broad avenues and walled square wards marked by surveyors with cords and poles, labourers ramming earth walls, the palace city taking shape in the north; the Qinling mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
chen-shubao-enthroned: 582 CE, Jiankang: a lavish Chen palace with tall pavilions of fragrant wood, gilded railings and pearl curtains, court ladies and poets gathered at a moonlit banquet on a terrace overlooking a garden pond; musicians playing pipa and zither. Night, lantern light. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, gossamer line, rich colours on aged silk.
gokturk-split: 583 CE, Baidao on the northern frontier: Sui envoys in black caps and robes ride between two separate Turkic encampments of felt tents on the steppe, each with its own wolf-head standard and horsemen; Sui troops guard a pass in the hills behind. Wide steppe landscape, autumn grass. Painted in the style of a Sogdian mural from Panjakent, rich red and blue, outlined figures.
abolish-commanderies: 583 CE, Daxing: a busy Sui government office courtyard with tiled roofs and red columns, clerks in black caps and round-collared robes carry out bundles of old registers and bronze seals on trays, while others stack new document boxes on wooden shelves; senior officials confer around a low table over a large unrolled map scroll of prefectures and counties. Orderly daylight. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, small figures.
battle-of-baidao: 583 CE, Baidao near Hohhot: in the grassy hills below the Yin Mountains, Sui cavalry in lamellar armour with stirrups, lances and red banners charge a Turkic horde of mounted archers in fur-trimmed caps; the Turkic horsemen wheel away across the open plain, abandoning tents and herds. Distant panoramic view, dust clouds, autumn grass, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, lapis blue, malachite green and ochre ground.
guangtong-canal: 584 CE, Wei River valley near Chang'an: thousands of labourers dig a straight canal alongside the meandering shallow Wei River, carrying earth in baskets; finished stretches already carry flat-bottomed grain boats pulled by trackers; the loess hills and Tong Pass in the distance. Spring light. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
dasuo-maoyue: 585 CE, a county town near Daxing: in a courtyard, Sui clerks in black caps sit at tables with paper registers, comparing faces of villagers who queue in families before them, old and young; an official checks heights and ages. Market-like crowd, daylight, tiled roofs. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, lively small figures.
western-liang-abolished: 587 CE, Jiangling on the Yangtze: a small riverside palace city being taken over peacefully, Sui troops in lamellar armour entering the opened gates while court officials and noble families in robes depart in boats downriver with their belongings; new banners being raised on the walls, townspeople watching quietly. Overcast morning, wide river. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, faded lapis and malachite, ochre ground.
jiangnan-revolt-590: 590 CE, near Wu (Suzhou): a water country of canals and lakes, local militias in boats and on dykes facing a Sui army with banners advancing along the waterways; smoke rising over a distant walled town. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, misty light. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian's Spring Outing, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
fubing-registered: 590 CE, countryside near Daxing: former soldiers lay down their armour and spears and take up hoes, receiving plots of land from county clerks in black caps who mark field boundaries with wooden stakes and note names in paper registers; families build rammed-earth farmhouses beside fields of millet, children and oxen nearby. Peaceful autumn daylight. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, lively small figures.
renshou-palace: 593 CE, Linyou in the Shaanxi hills: a lavish summer palace of halls, terraces and galleries built across a mountain valley, thousands of labourers hauling timber and stone up ramps, overseers with whips at a distance; some exhausted workers resting under trees. Summer haze. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
anji-bridge: 595 CE, Zhao County, Hebei: a single long, flat stone arch spans the Xiao River, with two small open arches in each shoulder; stonemasons finish the carved balustrade while ox-carts and travellers in Sui dress cross the bridge; willows on the banks. Clear spring day. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
first-goguryeo-war: 598 CE, Liao River region: a huge Sui army struggles across flooded plains in heavy summer rain, ox-carts stuck in mud, soldiers in sodden armour, while out at sea a fleet of ships is tossed by a storm; dark clouds. Distant panoramic view, no corpses. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and malachite, ochre ground.
yami-qaghan-submits: 599 CE, Ordos near Hohhot: a Turkic encampment of felt tents beside a newly built walled town, a Sui princess's curtained carriage arriving with escorts, Turkic horsemen and herds settling on the grasslands inside the Yellow River bend; Sui officials greet a khagan seen small. Bright day. Painted in the style of a Sogdian mural from Panjakent, rich red and blue.
yang-yong-deposed: 600 CE, Daxing palace: a long covered corridor in the Sui palace, a crown prince in robes, seen small and from behind, being escorted out of the Eastern Palace by guards, while in a distant hall a group of figures, an empress and ministers, watch from behind a screen; autumn leaves in the courtyard. Quiet intrigue, no violence. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens.
qieyun: 601 CE, Daxing: a lamplit evening gathering in a scholar's home, several friends in robes and black caps seated around low tables discussing pronunciation, one writing notes with a brush on paper rolls, ink stones and wine cups around them; bamboo outside the window. Calm, intellectual mood. Painted in the style of a Sui court painting in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, soft mineral colours on silk.
liu-fang-vietnam: 602 CE, Longbian in the Red River delta: a Sui army in lamellar armour with banners arrives at a walled riverside town amid rice paddies and palm trees; local leaders in simple robes come out of the gate to submit, bowing before the general's mounted party. Humid green landscape, river boats. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
yang-accession: 604 CE, Daxing: the Sui palace's great hall at dawn, a broad single-eaved timber hall with dark grey tiled roof, plain red columns and white plastered walls standing on a high rammed-earth platform with a long ramped stair; rows of ministers in black caps and purple and red robes bow in a packed-earth courtyard, a new emperor seen small at the top. No yellow glazed tiles, no carved white marble railings. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
yang-liang-revolt: 604 CE, Jinyang (Taiyuan): an army marches out of a walled northern city in the Fen River valley under banners, while across the plain a loyal imperial army advances in formation; mountains of Shanxi behind, autumn dust. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, no gore. Rammed-earth watchtowers and millet fields line the route. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
eastern-capital-luoyang: 605 CE, Luoyang: a vast construction site on the Luo River, huge numbers of labourers raising rammed-earth walls and timber palace halls, rafts of great logs floating downriver, ox-carts carrying stone; a grid of new streets and a bridge across the Luo, households arriving with carts of belongings. Panoramic view, hazy sunlight. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
champa-expedition: 605 CE, the Cham capital near Trà Kiệu: Sui soldiers carry chests and golden tablets out of a brick tower-temple of Cham style among palm trees, war elephants of the defeated Cham standing riderless in the distance; humid jungle, a river with ships waiting. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Cham sandstone bas-relief, carved figures in shallow relief, warm stone tones.
ono-no-imoko: 607 CE, Luoyang: a Japanese envoy in Asuka-period court dress with a lacquered cap and his small retinue, seen from behind, present a lacquer document box in a vast Sui palace courtyard, Chinese officials in black caps and red robes lining the steps; the emperor small and far away on the hall terrace. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben's Tribute Bearers, mineral colours on silk.
pei-ju-xiyu: 607 CE, Zhangye in the Hexi Corridor: a busy frontier market below snowy Qilian Mountains, Sogdian merchants in caftans and pointed hats with camel caravans, a Sui official seated at a low table under an awning interviewing them, a scribe sketching maps and costumes on paper rolls. Bright daylight, dusty market. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
yongji-canal: 608 CE, north China plain towards Zhuojun: a long straight canal being dug across flat farmland, over a million labourers, men and women alike, carrying earth in baskets and digging with spades, grain boats already moving on finished stretches; overseers on horseback. Hazy summer light, vast scale. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
tuyuhun-conquered: 609 CE, beside Qinghai Lake: a Sui army with banners and cavalry spreads across high grassland around the vast blue lake, Tuyuhun horsemen in fur hats fleeing towards distant snowy mountains, abandoned felt tents and yak herds; thin high-altitude light. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, lapis and malachite, ochre ground.
yang-zhangye: 609 CE, Zhangye: below the snowy Qilian Mountains, a magnificent imperial reception tent and pavilion, rulers and envoys of many Western Regions states in caftans, turbans and fur hats arriving with camels, horses and gifts; Sui guards with banners lining the route, crowds of musicians. Bright summer day. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, procession of small figures.
liuqiu-expedition: 610 CE, Liuqiu (Taiwan): Sui war junks with matting sails anchored off a green mountainous island coast, soldiers wading ashore onto a sandy beach towards a village of thatched stilt houses among palms; islanders watching from the forest edge. Bright subtropical light, sea haze. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
luoyang-spectacle: 610 CE, Luoyang: a great avenue at night lit by thousands of lanterns, trees wrapped in silk, acrobats, pole-climbers, musicians and dancers performing on stages, foreign envoys and merchants in caftans and turbans dining at open-air tables; vast crowds. Festive, glowing atmosphere. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, crowded lively figures.
sui-uprisings: 611 CE, Changbai Mountain near Zouping in Shandong: peasant farmers in short tunics with hoes, staves and a few bows gather on a wooded mountainside, refusing conscription; below, a road where an empty column of carts heads north. Overcast sky, autumn trees. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, muted lapis and malachite, ochre ground, small figures.
yang-xuangan: 613 CE, outside Luoyang: a rebel army with banners besieges the walls of the great eastern capital, supply carts and barges from the canal camps behind them; defenders line the ramparts, an imperial relief army appears on the horizon. Distant panoramic view, smoke, no gore. Canal barges lie moored along the Luo River below the walls. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
third-goguryeo-war: 614 CE, Liaodong: an exhausted Sui army encamped by the Liao River under grey autumn skies, ragged tents and thin horses; a small Goguryeo delegation crosses the river by boat under a white banner to the Sui camp, bringing a bound captive. Distant view, bleak landscape. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre and red outlines on plaster, flat figures.
siege-yanmen: 615 CE, Yanmen in northern Shanxi: a small walled frontier town in the mountains surrounded by countless Turkic horsemen and felt tents on the hills, defenders crowded on the walls, arrows flying; late summer, dusty light. Distant aerial view, many tiny figures. Inside, tiny figures of courtiers and guards crowd the town's single main street. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
yangdi-jiangdu: 616 CE, the Grand Canal towards Jiangdu: a huge flotilla of ornate multi-storey dragon boats and barges towed along the canal by hundreds of trackers on the willow-lined banks, the emperor's boat largest; the abandoned north fading behind in mist. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
li-mi-luokou: 617 CE, Luokou granary near Gongyi: huge rows of underground grain pits and storehouses on a hillside by the Luo River, rebel soldiers throwing open the granaries, crowds of hungry peasants carrying sacks of grain away in baskets and carts; banners of the Wagang army. Autumn daylight. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, lapis and malachite.
li-yuan-takes-changan: 617 CE, Daxing: a great army in lamellar armour enters the grid-planned Sui capital through the Mingde Gate, cavalry and infantry streaming along the broad avenue between walled wards, townspeople watching from gates; a palace on the northern skyline. Winter light, orderly. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk.
li-yuan-taiyuan: 617 CE, Taiyuan: an army gathers on the parade ground outside the walls of Jinyang, banners raised, cavalry and infantry assembling in formation for the march west, mountains of the Fen valley behind; a commander's small mounted party reviews them. Summer morning. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, many small figures.
dou-jiande-king: 617 CE, Leshou in Hebei: a modest rebel court in a walled county town, a rough-hewn hall with banners where followers in simple armour and peasant dress bow before a leader seen small from behind on a raised mat; captured soldiers being freed and fed in the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, muted blues and greens.
battle-of-qianshuiyuan: 618 CE, Qianshuiyuan in the loess highlands of Shaanxi: Tang cavalry in lamellar armour sweep down from a ridge onto a larger army on a plateau cut by deep gullies, the enemy turning to flee; dust clouds, late autumn. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Loess terraces and a few poplars dot the slopes. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
battle-of-hulao: 621 CE, Hulao Pass near Xingyang: a fortified pass in loess hills above the Yellow River, a small Tang force of black-armoured cavalry charging out of the gate into a vast army drawn up on the plain below; the enemy line collapsing, dust clouds. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis blue, malachite green, ochre ground.
kaiyuan-tongbao-issued: 621 CE, Chang'an: a Tang state mint workshop, workers pouring molten bronze into clay coin-tree moulds, others filing and stringing round coins with square holes onto cords; finished strings piled in baskets, officials inspecting. Furnace glow, smoke. Clerks weigh coin strings on balance scales and record them at a side table. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural of labouring figures, mineral colours, ochre ground.
tang-conquers-liang-xiao-xian: 621 CE, Jiangling on the Yangtze: a large Tang fleet of warships with tiered decks and matting sails sails downriver through the gorges and arrives before the walled city; the gates open and a delegation in white robes comes out to surrender. Distant view, misty river. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, gold-outlined mountains, mineral colours.
liu-heita-executed: 623 CE, Mingzhou in Hebei: on a winter plain by a frozen river, a Tang army under banners closes around a dwindling rebel force; the rebels' camp broken, horsemen fleeing across the snow. Distant panoramic view, grey sky, many small figures, no gore. Bare poplars and a distant walled town stand on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
wude-equal-field-edict: 624 CE, a village near Chang'an: county officials in black caps measure fields with cords and rods, allotting strips of land to adult farmers, while villagers bring sacks of grain, bolts of silk and hemp cloth to a tax collection table; mulberry trees and loess hills. Clear day. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural of farming scenes, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
fu-gongshi-suppressed: 624 CE, Danyang (Nanjing): a Tang army and river fleet converge on a walled city by the Yangtze, warships on the river, troops scaling the walls by ladders; smoke rising over the southern capital, green hills of Zhongshan behind. Distant view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
reign-of-zhenguan: 627 CE, Chang'an: a Tang palace hall where ministers in black futou caps and purple and red round-collared robes stand in rows, one stepping forward with a memorial tablet to speak boldly before the throne, the emperor small and distant; simple, frugal furnishings. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
liang-shidu-destroyed: 628 CE, Shuofang on the edge of the Ordos desert: a walled frontier town of rammed earth besieged by Tang troops, Turkic horsemen hovering far off on the dunes; the gates opening as defenders surrender. Dusty light, sparse grassland. Distant view, many small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
tang-campaign-against-tuyuhun: 634 CE, Qinghai highlands: a long Tang army with banners and supply camels marches across high snowy plateaux and windswept grasslands near the blue lake, Tuyuhun horsemen in fur hats retreating into the distance; thin cold air, distant snow peaks. Panoramic view, many small figures. Yaks and abandoned felt tents dot the slopes. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
alopen-arrives-changan: 635 CE, Chang'an: a Christian monk of the Church of the East in dark robes with a small group of companions carrying scrolls arrives at the western gate, welcomed by a Tang minister in a black futou cap and red robe with an escort; camels and Silk Road travellers in the crowd. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
battle-of-songzhou: 638 CE, Songzhou (Songpan) in northern Sichuan: night in a mountain valley, Tang troops with torches raid a large Tibetan encampment of black tents below snowy peaks, horses stampeding, the camp in disarray; a walled frontier town on a hill. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and malachite, ochre accents.
battle-of-nuozhenshui: 641 CE, Nuozhen River in Inner Mongolia: on the open steppe by a winding river, Tang infantry and cavalry in lamellar armour withstand a charge of Xueyantuo horsemen, then counterattack; the steppe riders flee across the grassland. Distant panoramic view, dust clouds. Tang supply wagons are drawn up in a ring behind the line. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
death-of-wei-zheng: 643 CE, Chang'an: the modest home of a minister, mourners in white hemp robes in a simple courtyard, a bronze mirror on a stand by the coffin hall, a dignified figure in imperial robes seen from behind standing silently before it; winter trees. Quiet, solemn mood. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, fine line, muted mineral colours on silk.
siege-of-ansi: 645 CE, Ansi fortress in Liaodong: a stone-walled mountain fortress on a hill, a huge earthen ramp built by Tang troops rising against its walls, siege engines and banners; defenders on the ramparts. Autumn turning to winter, first snow on the hills. Distant view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and ochre outlines on plaster.
xueyantuo-destroyed: 646 CE, Mongolian Plateau: Tang envoys and armoured cavalry ride into a vast steppe encampment of felt tents, tribal chiefs of the Tiele in fur caps kneel offering horses and furs; herds and endless grassland under a wide sky. Bright summer light. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, many small figures.
wang-xuance-india: 648 CE, Tirabhukti in the Ganges plain of Bihar: a mixed army of Tibetan cavalry and Nepali soldiers led by a small Tang diplomatic party advances across a river plain towards a walled city with brick temples and palms; war elephants in the defending line. Distant view, hot hazy light. Painted in the style of an Ajanta cave mural, warm ochres and earth reds, flowing figures.
tang-campaign-against-kucha: 648 CE, Kucha in the Tarim Basin: Tang armies under banners besiege an oasis city of mud-brick walls and Buddhist stupas beneath the Tianshan, Turkic auxiliary cavalry beside them; poplar groves and desert. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Camels and supply carts wait among the poplar groves behind the lines. Painted in the style of a Kizil cave mural, lapis blue and malachite green, diamond-shaped mountain pattern.
tang-code: 653 CE, Chang'an: Tang ministers and legal scholars in black futou caps and robes gather around a long table piled with paper rolls of the law code and its commentary, scribes copying, an official reading aloud; a palace hall with red columns. Calm, orderly daylight. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
wu-becomes-empress: 655 CE, Chang'an: a grand investiture in the Daming Palace courtyard, ranks of officials in red and purple robes bowing, court ladies in high-waisted dresses with shawls, a new empress seen small and from behind ascending the stone steps of the hall under a canopy; banners and musicians. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk.
battle-of-irtysh-657: 657 CE, Irtysh River: winter, deep snow on the steppe by a broad river, Tang cavalry in lamellar armour charge through a Western Turkic encampment of felt tents, Turkic horsemen scattering into the snow; pine forests and mountains. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Abandoned banners lie scattered on the snow. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and white.
xinxiu-bencao: 659 CE, Chang'an: in a palace workshop, physicians and scholars in black caps sort medicinal herbs, roots and minerals on trays, painters illustrate plants on paper rolls, others compile texts; jars, dried plants hanging from beams. Bright daylight. Bundled scrolls are tied with silk cords and stacked on shelves along the wall. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
zhangsun-wuji-death: 659 CE, Qianzhou (Pengshui) in the mountains of southeast Sichuan: a remote exile's lodging in steep green gorges by a river, an elderly man in plain robes seen from behind gazing at the mountains, an envoy with an edict arriving by the path below. Misty, melancholy light. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
tang-silla-conquer-baekje: 660 CE, Sabi (Buyeo) on the Baekma River: a Tang fleet crosses the river while Silla troops advance overland, the walls of the Baekje capital on a wooded hill above, defenders surrendering at the gate. Distant panoramic view, smoke on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Korean Three Kingdoms tomb mural, ochre, red and green outlines on plaster.
xue-rengui-tianshan: 662 CE, Khangai Mountains in Mongolia: in a high mountain valley, a Tang general in white armour on horseback draws a bow before his army, three steppe champions on horseback before the Tiele host far away; the tribal army wavering. Wide landscape, no gore. Pine-dotted slopes and snow-capped summits frame the scene. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
shangguan-yi-executed: 664 CE, Chang'an palace: a dim study inside the palace, an official in a black futou cap kneeling at a low table drafting an edict with a brush, while in the doorway an attendant hurries away down a corridor; a lamp, silk curtains. Tense mood, no violence. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk.
xuanzang-dies: 664 CE, Yuhua Palace in the mountains of Tongchuan: a former palace turned monastery among wooded hills, monks in robes gathered in a translation hall full of stacks of sutra scrolls, a lamp burning before an empty meditation seat; autumn leaves. Peaceful, solemn mood. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
goguryeo-falls: 668 CE, Pyongyang: Tang and Silla armies with banners surround the walled city on the Taedong River, the gates opening, a royal procession in Goguryeo dress led out to surrender; smoke over the city. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Stone fortress walls follow the ridges of the hills behind the city. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre, red and black outlines on plaster.
battle-of-dafeichuan: 670 CE, Dafeichuan on the Qinghai plateau: a Tang army in lamellar armour is surrounded by masses of Tibetan cavalry on a high grassland valley, snowy mountains around; the Tang ranks broken, supply wagons abandoned. Distant panoramic view, no gore, many small figures. Black yak-hair tents of the Tibetans dot the far slopes. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
silla-tang-war: 670 CE, the Imjin River in Korea: Silla troops in lamellar armour hold a fortress on a hill above the river, while Tang soldiers withdraw across the water on boats and pontoons; autumn forests. Distant panoramic view. Silla banners fly from the ramparts and small boats crowd the riverbank. Painted in the style of a Korean Three Kingdoms tomb mural, ochre, red and green outlines on plaster.
longmen-vairocana: 675 CE, Longmen Grottoes by the Yi River near Luoyang: a colossal 17-metre seated Buddha carved into a limestone cliff, flanked by disciples and bodhisattvas, scaffolding of timber still against the rock, stone carvers at work and monks and court officials visiting below; the river in front. Morning light. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
huineng-ordained: 676 CE, Faxing Temple in Guangzhou: a temple courtyard shaded by a great banyan and a bodhi tree, a lean monk of humble southern origin, seen small, having his head shaved before an assembly of robed monks at an ordination platform; banners flutter in the breeze, and lay people in Tang dress watch from the galleries. Warm humid light, tiled temple halls and incense smoke. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
pei-xingjian-suyab: 679 CE, Suyab in the Chu valley: below the snowy Tianshan, a Tang diplomatic caravan escorting a Persian prince in a jewelled cap camps beside a river; Turkic chiefs ride in to a hunting gathering, and in the distance labourers raise the rammed-earth walls of a new garrison town. Bright summer grassland, felt tents, camels and horses. Painted in the style of a Sogdian mural from Panjakent, rich red and lapis blue, outlined figures.
second-turkic-khaganate: 682 CE, Yin Mountains in Inner Mongolia: on rocky slopes above the steppe, a band of Turkic warriors with long braided hair, bows and wolf-head standards gathers around a newly raised banner, horsemen streaming in from every valley to join them; a distant Tang frontier fort on the plain below. Wind-blown grass, dramatic clouds. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre, many small figures.
li-jingye-rebellion: 684 CE, Yangzhou: in a canal-side city of tiled roofs and bridges, a rebel army in lamellar armour musters on the parade ground beneath banners, while a scribe reads out a manifesto from a scroll to the assembled troops and townspeople; boats crowd the Grand Canal. Early autumn light, willows along the water. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
cruel-officials-petition-boxes: 686 CE, Luoyang: before the gate of the imperial palace stands a large square bronze box with slots on each side, a queue of people in Tang dress dropping folded letters into it, while officials in black futou caps and red robes watch from the steps; a gloomy prison building faintly visible behind the walls. Overcast light, tense mood. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk.
li-zhen-rebellion: 688 CE, Yuzhou (Runan) on the Henan plain: a small rebel force of Tang princes' retainers with banners rides out from a walled county town, while a much larger imperial army advances in formation across flat wheat fields towards them; dust on the horizon. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
khitan-revolt-yingzhou: 696 CE, Yingzhou (Chaoyang) on the Liaoxi frontier: Khitan horsemen with shaved crowns and side locks, wearing fur and felt, pour out of wooded hills towards a walled frontier town, a Zhou army in lamellar armour broken in a valley below; grey autumn sky, birch forests. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Liao-type steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, fine ink and light colour on silk.
balhae-founded: 698 CE, Mount Dongmou near Dunhua: in forested mountains of Manchuria, a migrating people of Mohe and Goguryeo origin, with carts, horses and families, build a stone-walled hilltop fort beside a river; a leader seen small among them raises a banner. Autumn forests of birch and pine. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre, red and black outlines on plaster.
shenlong-coup: 705 CE, Luoyang: before dawn, armed palace guards with torches pour through the Xuanwu Gate of the palace city, ministers in black caps and robes leading them; in an inner hall far away, an aged ruler seen only as a small figure behind screens, attendants scattering. Night, torchlight on tiled roofs. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk.
three-surrender-cities: 708 CE, north of the Yellow River loop near Baotou: Tang soldiers and labourers build three rammed-earth fortresses on the open steppe north of the river, beacon towers rising on the hills between them; Turkic horsemen watch from afar. Wide sky, autumn grass, the great river glinting behind. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre, many small figures.
tanglong-coup: 710 CE, Chang'an: a summer night in the Daming Palace, troops of the palace guard with torches storm across a vast courtyard towards the inner halls, a young prince on horseback seen small at their head; court ladies flee along covered galleries. Distant view, no gore, firelight on red columns. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk.
princess-jincheng-tibet: 710 CE, approach to Lhasa: a long bridal procession of a Tang princess in a curtained carriage with court ladies, musicians and pack animals laden with silks and books, crossing a high valley below snowy mountains; Tibetan horsemen in fur-lined robes ride out to welcome them, a hilltop fortress palace in the distance. Clear thin air. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre, procession of small figures.
first-jiedushi-hexi: 711 CE, Liangzhou (Wuwei) in the Hexi Corridor: a frontier general's headquarters in a walled oasis city, a commander seen small receiving a seal and a banner of office before ranks of armoured cavalry and infantry on the parade ground; snowy Qilian Mountains and camel caravans beyond. Bright, dry light. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
xiantian-coup: 713 CE, Chang'an: in the courtyard of a grand mansion, palace guards arrest members of a powerful faction, while a messenger carrying an edict on a lacquer tray walks through a silent hall towards a lady's inner chamber hung with silk curtains. Dusk, quiet tension, no violence shown, distant figures. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk.
yao-chong-locusts: 716 CE, Henan plain: at dusk, villagers in short jackets light bonfires at the edges of millet fields and dig long trenches, swatting a dark cloud of locusts into the fire and burying them in the trenches; officials in black caps on horseback supervise. Smoky orange light over flat farmland. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural of farming scenes, ochre ground, mineral blues and greens.
abe-no-nakamaro-arrives: 717 CE, Chang'an: members of a Japanese embassy in Nara-period court dress with young students among them, seen from behind, enter the great southern gate of the city along a broad avenue; Tang officials in black futou caps lead them, crowds of Sogdians and townspeople watch. Spring sunlight, walled wards and pagodas. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk.
fubing-to-mubing: 723 CE, Chang'an: in a palace guard barracks courtyard, recruiting officers in black caps sit at a table enrolling volunteer soldiers who line up to receive pay in strings of coins and bolts of cloth, while elsewhere professional guards drill with spears and bows. Bright daylight, rammed-earth walls and tiled gatehouse. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
yixing-survey: 724 CE, an observation station: on a flat plain at noon, astronomers in robes measure the shadow of a tall upright gnomon on a long stone scale, a monk in robes supervises and a scribe records on paper; in the background a mountain landscape. Bright midday sun, short shadow. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, mineral blues and greens on silk.
yuwen-rong-census: 724 CE, a county town near Chang'an: an official commission in black futou caps seated at tables under awnings registers families of returning vagrants, who arrive with bundles and carts and children; clerks write in thick paper registers. Busy daylight, walled courtyards and tiled roofs. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, lively small figures.
dayan-calendar: 729 CE, Chang'an: at the imperial observatory terrace, astronomers in robes operate a large bronze armillary sphere with a water clock beside it, while officials present a new calendar as scrolls on a lacquer tray; the night sky with stars above the palace roofs. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, mineral blues and greens on dark silk.
li-linfu-dominance: 736 CE, Chang'an: an upright elderly minister in plain robes walks out alone through a palace gate holding a folding fan, while inside the hall a smiling courtier is surrounded by bowing officials; autumn leaves falling in the courtyard. Small figures, symbolic contrast. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk.
nanzhao-unification: 738 CE, Taihe near Erhai Lake in Yunnan: beneath the Cangshan mountains, chiefs of six tribes in local dress with turban-like headcloths gather before a hall of stone and timber, swearing allegiance; a Tang envoy in black cap and red robe presents a seal of investiture. Blue lake and green mountains. Painted in the style of the Nanzhao Picture Scroll, fine line, bright mineral colours on paper.
ten-jiedushi: 742 CE, a northern frontier: a vast army camp of tents, horse lines and rammed-earth forts stretching across a wide steppe-edge valley, ranks of professional soldiers in lamellar armour drilling under the banner of a frontier general, beacon towers along the hills. Panoramic view, many tiny figures, dusty light. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
li-bai-du-fu: 744 CE, near Luoyang: two poets in loose scholar's robes, seen small and from behind, walk together along a country path by a river among autumn hills, one tall and carefree with a wine gourd, the other younger and slender; a servant follows with a donkey. Golden autumn light, maples and pines. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
uyghur-khaganate-founded: 744 CE, Orkhon Valley in Mongolia: in a broad river valley of green grassland, a vast gathering of Uyghur horsemen and felt tents around a large golden tent, chieftains raising a new khagan on a felt carpet; a Tang envoy's party with banners arrives; herds of horses beyond. Bright summer day. Painted in the style of a Sogdian-Uyghur mural, rich reds and blues, outlined figures.
gao-xianzhi-little-balur: 747 CE, the Pamirs and Darkot Pass: a Tang army of infantry and cavalry in lamellar armour climbs a narrow icy pass among towering snow peaks and glaciers, soldiers leading horses on foot along precipices, a mountain fortress far below in a green valley. Thin cold light, dramatic scale. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Zhaodao's Emperor Minghuang's Journey to Shu, mineral colours on silk.
shibao-fortress: 749 CE, Shibao in the Qinghai highlands: a stone fortress on a steep rocky crag, a huge Tang army surging up the slopes with ladders and banners, while defenders on the walls hurl stones; smoke drifting, snowy ridges behind. Distant panoramic view, no gore, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
tianbao-war-nanzhao: 751 CE, Erhai Lake in Yunnan: beneath the Cangshan mountains, a Tang army in lamellar armour is trapped in the narrow plain between lake and mountains, Nanzhao warriors with long spears and shields descending from the slopes; abandoned banners in the reeds. Distant panoramic view, misty light, no gore. Painted in the style of the Nanzhao Picture Scroll, fine line, mineral colours on paper.
jianzhen-japan: 753 CE, the Yangtze mouth near Yangzhou: a wooden sea-going ship with matting sails sets out at night from the riverbank, an elderly blind monk in robes guided aboard by disciples, a few monks carrying sutra boxes and Buddhist images; a Japanese envoy's ship waits offshore. Moonlit water. Painted in the style of a Japanese Nara-period illustrated sutra or Kamakura emakimono of Ganjin's voyage, fine line, mineral colours.
luoyang-falls-755: 755 CE, the Yellow River near Luoyang: winter, rebel cavalry in fur-lined coats and lamellar armour cross the frozen river on ropes and boats, a vast host advancing across the plain towards the walls of Luoyang; smoke rising from outlying villages. Distant panoramic view, grey sky, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
tong-pass-756: 756 CE, Tong Pass: a narrow road between the Yellow River and steep loess cliffs, a Tang army marching out from the fortified pass into a defile where enemy troops wait hidden above; dust and smoke, ox-carts set alight, the army in confusion along the river. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and malachite, ochre.
suzong-lingwu: 756 CE, Lingwu on the Yellow River in Ningxia: a modest frontier town with rammed-earth walls, a simple ceremony on a raised earthen platform as officials in black caps and soldiers bow to a new emperor seen small and from behind; frontier cavalry assemble outside. Windy, dusty light, desert hills. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
yan-gaoqing-changshan: 756 CE, Changshan (Zhengding) in Hebei: a walled city on the north China plain, loyal defenders on the walls with banners raised, citizens carrying stones and arrows to the ramparts, while a rebel army in heavy armour encircles the city; winter sky. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
zhang-xun-yongqiu: 756 CE, Yongqiu in Henan: night outside a small walled town, defenders on the walls lower hundreds of straw figures in black clothes on ropes, enemy archers below shooting arrows into them, the straw men bristling with arrows; moonlight, torches on the walls. Rebel tents and campfires spread across the plain beyond the moat. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and ochre, small figures.
suiyang-siege: 757 CE, Suiyang (Shangqiu): a walled city on the Huai plain under a long siege, a vast rebel army encamped around it with siege towers and ladders, thin defenders on battered walls, empty fields and stripped trees; autumn haze. Distant aerial view, no gore, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, muted lapis, malachite and ochre.
changan-recaptured-757: 757 CE, south of Chang'an: Tang infantry in lamellar armour and Uyghur cavalry in fur caps advance across the plain beside the great city walls, the rebel army retreating; townspeople open the gates and welcome the troops with banners. Autumn light, the Qinling mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre, many small figures.
prince-yong-revolt: 757 CE, the lower Yangtze near Danyang: a fleet of warships with banners sailing downriver is met by imperial troops on the banks; ships turning and scattering, smoke rising. Wide river, green hills, overcast sky. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
salt-monopoly-diwu-qi: 758 CE, a coastal salt works: workers in short jackets boil brine in great iron pans over fires, raking white salt from flats along the sea coast, while government officials in black caps weigh sacks and stamp them for transport by canal boat. Bright, hazy coastal light. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural of labouring figures, mineral colours, ochre ground.
battle-of-yecheng: 759 CE, Yecheng (Anyang): a huge besieging camp of nine Tang armies around a flooded walled city, suddenly struck by a great sandstorm; banners torn, tents blown, soldiers scattering in all directions, a relief army emerging from the dust. Distant panoramic view, yellow murk, no gore. Floodwater from a breached dyke surrounds the city walls. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, ochre and lapis.
du-fu-three-officials: 759 CE, the road near Shihao village in Henan: dusk at a mud-walled village, an officer with a lantern knocking at a farmhouse gate, an old woman in plain dress at the door, an old man slipping over the back wall; a traveller in scholar's robe, seen from behind, lodging nearby watches. Melancholy blue dusk. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
classic-of-tea: 760 CE, Huzhou near Lake Tai: a scholar in plain robe sits in a thatched pavilion amid green tea terraces and bamboo, brewing tea over a small charcoal brazier with a cauldron and bowls, tea leaves drying on bamboo trays; pickers in the hills. Misty morning light. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
shi-siming-killed: 761 CE, Luyuan near Sanmenxia: a rebel camp at night in the loess hills by the Yellow River, a commander's tent lit by lamps, armed guards slipping in through the shadows; the camp otherwise quiet under stars. Small distant figures, tense mood, no violence shown. Horses stand tethered in lines and banners droop in the still night air. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and ochre.
end-of-an-shi-rebellion: 763 CE, Wenquan Forest near Lulong in Hebei: a lone rider and a few followers in tattered armour enter a dark winter forest of bare trees, abandoned banners on the snow behind them; distant Tang troops on the plain. Bleak, quiet scene, no body shown. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, muted lapis, ochre and white.
hebei-three-garrisons: 763 CE, Weibo (Daming) in Hebei: a powerful provincial governor's walled headquarters, generals in lamellar armour receiving a Tang envoy who presents edicts and seals of office; troops in their own uniforms and banners drilling in the courtyard. Bright winter sun. Rammed-earth walls and watchtowers surround the compound on the flat plain. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
liu-yan-grain-transport: 764 CE, Yangzhou on the Grand Canal: busy transfer depots where grain sacks are loaded from large river boats into smaller canal barges, officials in black caps record cargo, trackers pull boats along the willow banks; warehouses and bridges. Bright day. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
pugu-huaien-revolt: 764 CE, Lingwu in Ningxia: a frontier army with Tibetan and Uyghur allied cavalry in fur hats marches southeast along the Yellow River towards the passes; beacon fires burn on the hills. Wide dusty landscape, autumn sky. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Supply camels and carts trail behind the long column of horsemen. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
guo-ziyi-uyghurs: 765 CE, Jingyang near Chang'an: an elderly Tang general without armour rides with a few attendants into a vast Uyghur camp of felt tents, Uyghur chiefs in fur caps dismounting to bow before him; huge army around them. Golden autumn light. Distant view, small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
yu-chaoen-killed: 770 CE, Chang'an palace: a grand hall during a feast at night, the emperor seen small on his dais, a powerful commander in red robes walking out of the hall, palace guards waiting in the dark corridor beyond; lamps flickering. Tense, no violence. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhou Fang, mineral colours on silk.
nestorian-stele: 781 CE, Chang'an: in a temple courtyard with Tang-style halls, a tall carved stone stele crowned by entwined dragons and a small cross stands on a tortoise base, monks of the Church of the East in dark robes with Tang officials gathered around it for its dedication; no legible inscription. Clear daylight. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens.
four-princes-rebellion: 781 CE, Hebei and Shandong plains: several provincial armies with banners gather on a flat plain, their governors' tents pitched together, envoys riding between them; a distant imperial army advancing from the west. Panoramic view, dusty sky, many small figures. Each army flies different coloured banners, and supply carts crowd the roads between the camps. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
jingyuan-mutiny: 783 CE, Chang'an: soldiers in rain-soaked armour storm into the palace through the Danfeng Gate, townspeople fleeing along the broad avenue, an imperial carriage with a few guards hurrying out through a northern gate in the distance. Wet grey day, no gore. Shops along the avenue have their shutters closed. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
treaty-of-qingshui: 783 CE, Qingshui in Gansu: on an open hillside, a Tang delegation in black caps and red robes and a Tibetan delegation in fur-lined robes and turbans gather around an altar of earth for a treaty ceremony, horses and banners behind each side; loess hills. Clear sky. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
fengtian-penitential-edict: 784 CE, Fengtian (Qianxian): a besieged hilltop town, inside a modest hall a scholar-official in a black cap drafts an edict on a scroll by lamplight, a few officers and the emperor small at the back; outside the walls, enemy camp fires. Night, tense mood. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, muted mineral colours on silk.
yan-zhenqing-killed: 785 CE, Caizhou in Henan: an elderly scholar-official in plain robes stands calmly in a bare courtyard of a rebel stronghold, facing armed guards with folded hands, a brush and ink stone on a table beside him; grey winter sky. Small distant figures, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, muted mineral colours on silk.
pingliang-ambush: 787 CE, Pingliang in Gansu: a treaty pavilion on a high loess plateau, Tang officials in red robes and Tibetan delegates, Tibetan cavalry suddenly charging out of a hidden ravine, a Tang general on horseback galloping away; banners falling. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Overturned altar tables and scattered silk gifts lie on the ground. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
tea-tax-introduced: 793 CE, a river port near tea-growing hills: merchants unload bales and bricks of tea from boats, government officials in black caps weigh them on scales and collect a tenth in a warehouse, porters carry loads; tea terraces on the hills behind. Bright day. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
cangshan-alliance: 794 CE, the Cangshan mountains above Erhai Lake: a solemn oath ceremony at a mountain shrine, a Nanzhao king in local dress, seen small, and Tang envoys in red robes sacrifice at an altar, attendants and warriors around them; mist on the peaks and blue lake below. Painted in the style of the Nanzhao Picture Scroll, fine line, mineral colours on paper.
eunuchs-command-shence: 796 CE, Chang'an: the Shence Army parade ground inside the palace's northern park, rows of armoured soldiers with banners, two beardless palace eunuch officers in robes and caps reviewing them from a pavilion while ministers in black caps watch from afar.
