me-crucifixion-of-jesus: c. 30 CE, Jerusalem: a distant view of the walled city with Herod's great temple gleaming white and gold, and outside the walls on a rocky rise three small dark wooden crosses silhouetted against a stormy darkened sky, tiny figures of mourning women and Roman soldiers in red cloaks far off, olive trees in the valley. Painted in the style of a Byzantine icon, gold ground and deep blues, figures indistinct and far away.
me-siege-of-jerusalem-70: 70 CE, Jerusalem: Roman legions with siege towers and battering rams ring the walled city, smoke billowing from the great Temple on its vast platform, soldiers with red shields on the breached walls, the Mount of Olives and Roman camp in the foreground. Rendered in the style of the Arch of Titus relief combined with Roman fresco colour, crowded figures in profile, ochre and grey stone tones, no bodies shown.
me-capture-of-valerian: 260 CE, near Edessa, northern Mesopotamia: on a plain before the walled city, a Sasanian king on horseback with a billowing ribboned crown and his armoured cavalry receive a Roman emperor in a purple cloak kneeling before the horse, Roman soldiers laying down standards, Persian banners in the wind. Rendered in the style of a Sasanian rock relief at Naqsh-e Rustam, carved figures in warm stone, no faces in detail.
me-palmyrene-empire: c. 270 CE, Palmyra, Syrian desert: a great oasis city with long colonnaded streets, the Temple of Bel and a monumental arch, palm groves around, a queen in a diadem and long robes riding with armoured cavalry and archers along the colonnade, seen small from behind, camel caravans arriving from the desert. Painted in the style of a Palmyrene funerary relief and Roman fresco, warm limestone and ochre tones.
me-council-of-nicaea: 325 CE, Nicaea, Anatolia: a large basilica-like imperial hall by a lake, hundreds of bishops in white and dark robes seated on benches in a great semicircle, an emperor in purple on a raised throne at the far end, small and distant, a scroll held up, lakeshore and hills through tall windows. Painted in the style of a Byzantine fresco or icon of the council, gold ground, flat figures with haloes omitted.
me-birth-of-muhammad: c. 570 CE, Mecca, Arabian Peninsula: a desert valley among barren rocky hills, with a cluster of flat-roofed houses of stone and mud brick around the cubic Kaaba sanctuary, a camel caravan resting at a well, palm fronds, and a clear night sky full of stars over the town, no people shown up close. Painted in the style of an Ottoman manuscript painting of Mecca, gold sky and flat architectural forms, landscape only.
me-first-revelation: c. 610 CE, Mount Hira near Mecca: a steep barren rocky mountain at night, a small dark cave opening high on its slope, a narrow path winding up, the valley of Mecca with its houses and the Kaaba faintly visible below, an immense starlit sky and a soft glow of light over the peak, no person depicted. Painted in the style of an Ottoman or Persian miniature, deep blue sky with gold, landscape only.
me-hijra: 622 CE, the road from Mecca to Medina, Arabia: a small caravan of camels seen from far away crossing a vast rocky desert at dawn, a palm-fringed oasis of Medina with mud-brick houses and date gardens on the horizon, townspeople gathering at its edge, no figure shown in detail. Painted in the style of an Ottoman manuscript painting, gold sky, ochre desert, flat stylised forms, tiny figures with veiled or unshown faces.
me-battle-of-nineveh-627: 627 CE, near the ruins of Nineveh, northern Mesopotamia: on a foggy December plain beside the Tigris, Byzantine armoured cavalry with lances and Christian banners clash with Sasanian cataphracts in mail and plumed helmets, the old mounds of Nineveh in the background, mist and pale winter light. Painted in the style of a Byzantine manuscript illumination such as the Madrid Skylitzes, flat colours, gold, small stylised figures, no bodies.
me-conquest-of-mecca: 630 CE, Mecca, Arabia: a large host of riders on camels and horses enters the valley peacefully from the surrounding hills, townspeople watching from flat roofs, the cubic Kaaba in its open courtyard at the centre, broken wooden idols lying nearby, desert mountains around, no central figure depicted. Painted in the style of an Ottoman manuscript painting of Mecca, gold ground, flat architectural forms, tiny figures.
me-battle-of-yarmuk: 636 CE, Yarmuk River, Syria-Jordan border: on a high plateau cut by deep gorges, Arab cavalry in mail and turbans with lances sweep across the plain against Byzantine infantry ranks with red shields and banners, dust storms blowing, the steep wadi of the Yarmuk below. Painted in the style of a medieval Persian manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, gold sky, stylised horses and riders at a distance, no bodies shown.
me-battle-of-qadisiyyah: 636 CE, al-Qadisiyyah, Iraq: on a plain between the desert edge and Euphrates canals, Arab horsemen and camel riders face a Sasanian army with armoured war elephants carrying archers in towers, the great Persian banner of leather and jewels in the centre, dust and smoke, palms in the distance. Painted in the style of a Persian Shahnameh miniature, bright flat colours, gold sky, stylised small figures, no bodies.
me-arab-conquest-of-jerusalem: 637 CE, Jerusalem: outside the city's stone walls and gates, an elderly patriarch in Byzantine robes with clergy walks out to meet a small group of plainly dressed Arab riders on camels, Christian churches with domes and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre visible inside, olive trees and Judean hills. Painted in the style of a medieval Islamic manuscript painting, flat colours and gold, small figures, no faces in detail.
me-battle-of-siffin: 657 CE, Siffin, upper Euphrates, Syria: two great Arab armies of horsemen in mail and turbans face each other across a plain by the river, and along the front line riders raise bound manuscript pages on the tips of their lances, the fighting halted, tents and camels behind both lines. Painted in the style of a medieval Persian manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, gold sky, many small stylised figures, no central figure shown.
me-umayyad-caliphate: 661 CE, Damascus, Syria: a walled city with Roman colonnades and Byzantine churches beside the green Ghouta orchards and the Barada river, Arab horsemen and courtiers gathering at a palace near the great temple enclosure, envoys arriving with gifts, Mount Qasioun behind. Painted in the style of an Umayyad mosaic like those of the Great Mosque of Damascus, gold background, green trees and buildings, no human figures in detail.
me-battle-of-karbala: 680 CE, Karbala, Iraq: a vast flat desert plain near the Euphrates at dusk, a small encampment of tents standing alone, a large army camped at a distance across the sand, palm trees along the river beyond reach, a lone riderless white horse in the foreground under a red sky. Painted in the style of a Persian Qajar-era manuscript painting, deep reds and ochres, sorrowful and solemn mood, no faces depicted, no blood.
me-dome-of-the-rock: c. 691 CE, Jerusalem: on the broad stone platform of the Temple Mount, a newly finished octagonal shrine with a gleaming gilded dome, its walls covered in glass mosaics of green and gold vegetal designs, craftsmen and masons finishing work, cypress trees and the walled city around, Mount of Olives behind. Painted in the style of an Umayyad gold-ground mosaic, glittering gold, green and blue tesserae, no human figures in detail.
me-siege-of-constantinople-717: 717 CE, Constantinople: the massive triple Theodosian land walls and sea walls of the city, domed Hagia Sophia rising above, a huge Arab fleet of lateen-sailed galleys on the Bosphorus being sprayed with jets of Greek fire from Byzantine dromons, a vast army camp before the walls in winter. Painted in the style of a Byzantine manuscript illumination like the Madrid Skylitzes, flat colours, gold, small stylised figures, no bodies.
me-abbasid-revolution: 750 CE, the Great Zab River, northern Iraq: on the banks of a fast-flowing river below rolling hills, an army carrying black banners and wearing black clothes advances against Umayyad troops under white banners, a pontoon bridge across the river, horsemen in mail and turbans, dust and spring grass. Painted in the style of a medieval Arab manuscript miniature such as the Maqamat of al-Hariri, flat bright colours, stylised figures, no bodies.
me-baghdad-founded: 762 CE, Baghdad on the Tigris: surveyors and thousands of workers lay out a perfectly circular city with double mud-brick walls and four gates, a great green-domed palace and mosque at its centre, lines traced in ash on the ground, boats on the Tigris, palm groves around. Painted in the style of a medieval Persian or Arab manuscript painting, flat bright colours, gold sky, tiny figures, a bird's-eye view.
me-house-of-wisdom: c. 830 CE, Baghdad: a library hall with arches and wooden shelves of manuscripts and scrolls, scholars in turbans and robes sitting on carpets, some reading Greek scrolls and translating into Arabic codices, an astrolabe and celestial globe on a table, a garden courtyard with fountain beyond. Painted in the style of the Maqamat of al-Hariri illustrations by al-Wasiti, flat bright colours, gold accents, no legible text.
me-buyids-take-baghdad: 945 CE, Baghdad on the Tigris: a column of Daylamite soldiers from the Caspian highlands, on foot with javelins and tall shields, and Buyid horsemen in mail and turbans, ride along the riverfront past palaces and domed mosques, while in a palace hall a robed caliph sits small and distant, receiving the newcomers, boats crowding the river. Painted in the style of a medieval Persian manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, gold sky, small stylised figures.
me-battle-of-manzikert: 1071 CE, Manzikert, eastern Anatolia: on a high grassy steppe ringed by mountains, Seljuk Turkish horse archers in felt caps and long coats wheel around the Byzantine army of armoured cavalry and infantry with banners, dust clouds rising, the walled town of Manzikert and distant snowy peaks beyond. Painted in the style of a Byzantine manuscript illumination like the Madrid Skylitzes, flat colours with gold, stylised small figures, no bodies shown.
me-crusaders-take-jerusalem: 1099, Jerusalem: crusader knights in mail hauberks and conical helmets with cross-marked shields climb a wooden siege tower against the city's stone walls, dark smoke rising from inside the walls above the domes and towers, the Mount of Olives and crusader camp in the foreground under a hot July sky. Painted in the style of a medieval French illuminated manuscript, gold leaf, flat jewel colours, small stylised figures, no bodies or blood.
me-krak-des-chevaliers: c. 1142, Krak des Chevaliers, western Syria: a massive concentric castle of pale limestone with round towers, a sloping glacis and inner and outer walls on a high hilltop, masons on wooden scaffolds rebuilding the walls, Hospitaller knights in black surcoats with white crosses riding up the road, green valley and Homs Gap plains below. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold sky and flat colours, small figures.
me-fall-of-edessa: 1144, Edessa, northern Mesopotamia: a walled city on a rocky citadel above spring-fed pools, Turkish soldiers with sappers burning timber props under a section of wall that collapses in dust, the army of Mosul with black banners pouring in, churches and towers inside, a December sky. Painted in the style of a medieval Persian or Arab manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, gold sky, small stylised figures, no bodies shown.
me-battle-of-hattin: 1187, the Horns of Hattin, Galilee: a twin-peaked volcanic hill above a dry summer plain, the exhausted crusader army huddled on the slopes around a red royal tent, Muslim cavalry surrounding them, brushfires sending smoke across the field, the blue Sea of Galilee glittering below. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated chronicle manuscript, gold leaf sky and flat colours, small figures at a distance, no bodies or blood.
me-siege-of-acre-1191: 1191, Acre, coast of Palestine: the walled port city on a peninsula ringed by crusader camps of tents and banners, wooden siege towers and trebuchets hurling stones at the walls, galleys with cross-marked sails blockading the harbour, the Muslim relief army on hills in the distance. Painted in the style of a thirteenth-century illuminated manuscript such as the Chronicles of Matthew Paris, flat colours, ink outlines, small figures, no bodies.
me-siege-of-baghdad-1258: 1258, Baghdad on the Tigris: a Mongol army encircles the city with siege engines and catapults, smoke rising from domed mosques and palaces, the river full of floating manuscripts darkening the water, horsemen in fur hats and lamellar armour on the plain, palm groves around. Painted in the style of an Ilkhanid Persian manuscript miniature from the Jami al-Tawarikh, flat colours and fine line, small figures at a distance, no bodies shown.
me-battle-of-ain-jalut: 1260, Ain Jalut, Jezreel Valley, Palestine: in a green valley beside a spring at the foot of Mount Gilboa, Mamluk cavalry in mail and turbans with banners charge from hidden hills against Mongol horsemen in fur-trimmed helmets, dust clouds rising across the plain, wheat fields and distant hills. Painted in the style of a Mamluk-era manuscript painting, flat bright colours, gold accents, small stylised horses and riders, no bodies shown.
me-fall-of-acre-1291: 1291, Acre, coast of Palestine: Mamluk siege engines and sappers before the battered walls of the crusader city, smoke rising from towers, small boats and galleys crowded with fleeing townspeople sailing out to sea toward ships waiting offshore, the harbour and Mediterranean under a hazy May sky. Painted in the style of a late medieval illuminated manuscript, flat colours, gold, small stylised figures, no bodies or blood.
me-battle-of-ankara: 1402, Çubuk plain near Ankara, Anatolia: a vast army of Timurid cavalry and Indian war elephants clashes with Ottoman Janissaries in white caps and armoured sipahi horsemen on a hot July plain, dust and banners everywhere, the citadel of Ankara on its hill in the distance. Painted in the style of a Timurid Persian manuscript miniature, brilliant flat colours, gold sky, stylised small figures, no bodies shown.
me-battle-of-marj-dabiq: 1516, Marj Dabiq, north of Aleppo, Syria: on a broad green plain, Ottoman artillery and Janissaries with matchlock muskets behind a line of chained carts fire on charging Mamluk cavalry in plumed helmets and mail, cannon smoke drifting, the Ottoman sultan's tent and horsetail standards on a rise. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature from a sixteenth-century Süleymanname, flat bright colours, gold, small stylised figures, no bodies.
me-tanzimat: 1839, Gülhane park, Istanbul: in the rose garden beside Topkapı Palace, ministers and officials in fezzes and long dark frock coats, foreign diplomats in tailcoats and religious scholars in turbans gather in rows before a pavilion as a decree is read aloud, the Bosphorus and domes of the city behind. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century Ottoman court watercolour, soft colour and fine detail, many small figures, no legible text.
me-gallipoli: 1915, Gallipoli Peninsula: steep scrub-covered cliffs above a narrow beach, Ottoman soldiers in khaki tunics and cloth helmets in trenches along the ridges, Allied troopships and battleships far out on the Aegean, small boats near the shore, smoke from shells drifting over the hills. Rendered as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour sketch by a war artist, muted khaki and blue-grey, figures small and distant, no bodies shown.
me-arab-revolt: 1916, the Hejaz, Arabia: a long column of Bedouin camel riders in flowing robes and headcloths with rifles crosses a vast desert of dunes and black lava hills toward a railway line, a stone station and telegraph poles in the distance, a few British officers in khaki among them, seen small. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, sand gold, ochre and sky blue, soft broad washes.
me-british-take-jerusalem: 1917, Jerusalem: on a grey December day, a small group of British officers in khaki on foot walk through the stone Jaffa Gate of the Old City, crowds of townspeople in fezzes, keffiyehs and robes watching from walls and balconies, the domes and minarets of the city behind. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, muted stone, khaki and grey, many small figures, no faces in detail.
me-republic-of-turkey: 1923, Ankara, Turkey: a modest two-storey stone parliament building in a small Anatolian town of tiled-roof houses, deputies in fezzes, frock coats and military uniforms gathering outside, townspeople and carriages in the dusty square, the old citadel on its rocky hill above, autumn steppe light. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, soft ochres and greys, many small figures, no portraits in detail, no flags with emblems.
me-israel-founded: 1948, Tel Aviv: a white modernist Bauhaus-style building on a palm-lined boulevard in spring, a crowd gathered quietly in the street outside, men in open-necked shirts and suits and women in summer dresses, cars and a bus parked, the Mediterranean glimpsed at the end of the street. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale whites and sky blues, small anonymous figures, calm and neutral, no flags or lettering.
me-six-day-war: 1967, Jerusalem: a June view across the valley toward the walls of the Old City, its golden dome and church towers above the stone ramparts, a haze of distant smoke over the hills, army vehicles small on a road below, olive trees and empty terraces in the foreground. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm stone, olive and pale blue, landscape-focused, figures tiny and distant, calm and neutral.
me-gulf-war: 1991, the desert outside Kuwait City: a flat sand plain under a sky blackened by towering plumes of smoke from burning oil wells, flames visible at their bases on the horizon, abandoned vehicles scattered far off on a highway, the city's water towers faintly visible in the haze. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, black, ochre and orange tones, no people in view, landscape only, calm and neutral.
me-syrian-civil-war: 2011, Daraa, southern Syria: a quiet view over a low town of flat-roofed concrete houses, minarets and olive groves on a fertile basalt plain in spring, a small crowd gathered at a distance near a mosque, wheat fields and the hazy Hauran plateau beyond. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greys, greens and ochres, tiny anonymous figures, calm and neutral, no weapons, no flags.
na-old-copper-complex: c. 3000 BCE, western Great Lakes, Wisconsin: on a rocky lakeshore among birch and pine forest, hunter-gatherers in hide clothing heat lumps of native copper in a fire and hammer them with stone hammers on flat rocks into spear points, awls and crescent knives, birchbark canoes pulled up on the shore, a vast blue lake behind. Painted in a rock-art-inspired palette on stone, red ochre, charcoal and cream, simplified figures.
na-poverty-point: c. 1700 BCE, Poverty Point, Louisiana: an aerial view at dawn of six huge concentric C-shaped earthen ridges on a bluff above a bayou, a great earthen mound rising behind them, people carrying baskets of soil on their heads, traders with canoes bringing stone and copper, forest and wetlands all around. Rendered as a documentary watercolour reconstruction in the manner of an eighteenth-century survey illustration, soft greens and earth browns, tiny figures.
na-adena-culture: c. 800 BCE, Chillicothe, Ohio valley: in a clearing of oak and hickory forest, people in hide and woven-fibre garments carry baskets of earth up a rounded burial mound being raised over a log tomb, a few small gardens of sunflower and squash nearby, pottery vessels and copper bracelets set as offerings, a river glinting below. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Native American ledger art and rock painting, flat ochre, red and green.
na-hopewell-tradition: c. 100 BCE, Mound City, Ohio: a rectangular earthen enclosure with an embankment wall containing many rounded burial mounds, people in feathered capes and copper ornaments carrying offerings of mica cut-outs, obsidian blades and conch shells, traders arriving along the Scioto River in canoes, forested hills beyond. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Native American ledger art, flat ochre, red and blue-green, simplified figures and a bird's-eye view.
na-hohokam-canals: c. 300 CE, Salt River valley, Arizona: in the Sonoran Desert with saguaro cactus and rocky mountains, Hohokam farmers with digging sticks and baskets dig and maintain long irrigation canals feeding green fields of maize and cotton, pit houses of brush and mud nearby, a red-on-buff pot on the ground, hot clear sky. Painted in the style of Hohokam red-on-buff pottery painting, flat red figures on buff ground, simple stylised forms.
na-chaco-canyon: c. 850-1100 CE, Chaco Canyon, New Mexico: a vast D-shaped multi-storey stone great house, Pueblo Bonito, against the sandstone canyon wall, with hundreds of rooms, round kivas, ladders and flat roofs, people carrying pine beams and baskets of turquoise along a straight road, desert mesas under a clear blue sky. Painted in the style of an Ancestral Puebloan kiva mural, flat earth reds, ochre and black on plaster, stylised figures.
na-lanse-aux-meadows: c. 1000 CE, L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland: on a grassy cove beside a cold grey sea, Norse settlers in woollen tunics and cloaks build turf-walled longhouses, a small iron-smelting hut smokes, a clinker-built knarr ship lies beached on the shore, bog and low spruce forest behind under a cloudy sky. Painted in the style of a medieval Norse-inspired tapestry like the Bayeux Tapestry, wool-coloured stitching tones on linen.
na-cahokia: c. 1050 CE, Cahokia, Illinois: the vast earthen Monks Mound with a thatched temple on its summit rising over a great plaza, smaller platform mounds, a wooden palisade and a ring of tall posts, thousands of people in feathered and woven garments, some playing chunkey with stone discs, maize fields and the Mississippi floodplain beyond. Painted in the style of Mississippian shell-gorget engraving and ledger art, flat earth tones and fine lines.
na-mesa-verde: c. 1190 CE, Mesa Verde, Colorado: the stone towers, rooms and round kivas of Cliff Palace tucked into a huge sandstone alcove high in a canyon wall, people climbing toe-hold trails and wooden ladders with baskets of maize and water jars, juniper and pinyon trees on the mesa above, late afternoon golden light. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour of the American Southwest, warm sandstone tones, tiny figures.
na-iroquois-confederacy: c. 1450, Onondaga, New York: in a forest clearing beside a lake, a council of Haudenosaunee chiefs in deerskin and feathered caps sits around a fire before a bark longhouse, a tall white pine tree towering above them, wampum belts of purple and white shell laid out on a mat, autumn maples around. Painted in the style of Native American ledger art, flat bright colours on lined paper, simplified figures, no faces in detail.
na-cabot-voyage: 1497, Bonavista, Newfoundland: a small three-masted English caravel, the Matthew, anchored in a rocky cove with steep cliffs and dark spruce forest, a boat landing a few sailors in doublets and caps who raise a wooden cross and banner on the shore, icebergs far out to sea, cold June light. Painted as a sixteenth-century engraving after a voyage illustration, fine hatched lines with soft hand colouring.
na-ponce-de-leon-florida: 1513, Atlantic coast of Florida: three Spanish caravels anchored offshore beyond a white sand beach lined with palms and mangroves, a longboat landing soldiers in steel morion helmets and padded jackets with a priest carrying a cross, flowering plants and wading birds in the dunes, bright spring sky. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century engraving by Theodor de Bry, fine line with soft hand colouring.
na-cartier-voyages: 1534, Gaspé Bay, Quebec: two French ships anchored in a deep bay ringed by forested cliffs, sailors in doublets and caps raising a tall wooden cross on the headland, Iroquoian people in deerskin with birchbark canoes watching from the shore, fish drying on racks, misty July morning. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century engraving with hand colouring, fine hatched lines and soft greens and blues.
na-de-soto-expedition: 1540, Mabila, Alabama: in a pine forest clearing, a palisaded Native town of thatched houses behind a tall log wall, Spanish soldiers in steel helmets and breastplates with lances, horses and a herd of pigs camped outside, smoke rising from the town, Mississippian warriors on the walls. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century engraving by Theodor de Bry, fine line with soft hand colouring, small figures at a distance, no bodies shown.
na-coronado-expedition: 1540, Hawikuh, New Mexico: a terraced adobe Zuni pueblo of flat-roofed stone houses on a low hill in a high desert, Spanish horsemen in steel helmets and breastplates with lances and Mexican Indian allies approaching across sagebrush plains, Zuni people watching from the rooftops, red mesas under a vast sky. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century colonial manuscript illustration, ink line and soft watercolour, small figures.
na-st-augustine: 1565, St. Augustine, Florida: a Spanish fleet anchored off a sandy inlet, soldiers in steel helmets and colonists unloading barrels, cannon and livestock, a priest raising a cross on the shore, a timber and earthwork fort under construction, Timucua people with tattooed skin watching from among palmettos and live oaks. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century engraving after Jacques Le Moyne and Theodor de Bry, fine line with soft hand colouring.
na-roanoke-colony: 1590, Roanoke Island, North Carolina: an abandoned English settlement inside a palisade of logs among sandy pine woods, empty thatched cottages overgrown with grass, rusted armour and a sea chest left open, a weathered wooden post at the gate with faint carved marks, sailors in doublets arriving from a ship in the sound. Painted in the style of a John White watercolour of the 1580s, fine line, soft blues and greens, no legible letters.
na-jamestown: 1607, Jamestown, Virginia: on a marshy peninsula of the James River, English colonists in doublets and helmets build a triangular wooden palisade fort with thatched huts, three small ships, the Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery, anchored close to shore, Powhatan people watching from the forest edge, humid summer haze. Painted in the style of an early seventeenth-century engraving with hand colouring, fine hatched lines, small figures.
na-quebec-founded: 1608, Quebec, St. Lawrence River: at the foot of a high cliff by the wide river, French settlers in doublets and wide-brimmed hats build a timber habitation of three linked buildings with a gallery, moat and palisade, a small ship anchored nearby, Innu and Algonquin traders in birchbark canoes bringing beaver pelts. Painted in the style of an early seventeenth-century engraving from Champlain's Voyages, fine line with soft hand colouring.
na-first-africans-virginia: 1619, Point Comfort, Virginia: a wooden English ship with patched sails anchored off a low sandy point at the mouth of the James River, a small boat bringing a group of Africans in worn clothing toward shore, a few colonists in doublets and wide hats waiting by a rough timber fort, marsh grass and pines under a heavy August sky. Painted as a sombre seventeenth-century-style engraving with muted hand colouring, small figures, dignified.
na-mayflower-compact: 1620, Cape Cod and Plymouth, Massachusetts: the small three-masted Mayflower anchored in a grey November harbour, inside its cramped lamplit cabin a group of men in plain dark doublets and tall hats gathered around a sheet of paper on a sea chest, and through a porthole a snowy wooded shore. Painted as a nineteenth-century American oil history painting, warm candlelight and deep browns, figures seen from the side and back, no legible text.
na-king-philips-war: 1675, Mount Hope, Rhode Island: a forested hill above Narragansett Bay in autumn, Wampanoag warriors in deerskin with muskets moving through the woods, a small English colonial village of clapboard houses and a meetinghouse in the distance with smoke rising, militia in buff coats marching along a road. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century New England woodcut and engraving with soft hand colouring, figures small and distant, no bodies shown.
na-pueblo-revolt: 1680, Santa Fe, New Mexico: in the high desert below the snowy Sangre de Cristo mountains, Pueblo warriors and families surround the adobe Palace of the Governors and a small mission church, smoke rising from the church roof, a line of Spanish colonists with ox carts and horses leaving south along the road. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century New Mexican hide painting, earthy browns and reds on tanned hide, small figures.
na-french-and-indian-war: 1754, Fort Necessity, Great Meadows, Pennsylvania: a small round log stockade with a storehouse in a rainy grassy meadow surrounded by wooded hills, Virginian militia in blue coats and tricorn hats in shallow trenches, French troops in white coats and Native allies firing from the treeline, gun smoke in the drizzle. Painted as an eighteenth-century engraving with hand colouring, fine hatched lines, figures small and distant, no bodies shown.
na-plains-of-abraham: 1759, the Plains of Abraham, Quebec: on a grassy plateau above the cliffs of the St. Lawrence, long scarlet lines of British infantry in tricorns fire volleys against advancing French regulars in white coats, gun smoke rolling across the field, the walled city and its church spires behind, British ships on the river. Painted as an eighteenth-century oil history painting, golden September light, figures small, no bodies shown.
na-stamp-act: 1765, New York City: a street of brick and timber Georgian houses near the harbour, a crowd of colonists in tricorn hats, waistcoats and aprons gathered around a bonfire burning bundles of papers, merchants watching from doorways, ships' masts visible at the end of the street, evening light. Painted as an eighteenth-century colonial engraving with hand colouring, fine hatched lines, many small figures, no legible text.
na-boston-tea-party: 1773, Boston Harbor: on a cold December night, colonists, some disguised in blankets and feathers, stand on the decks of three moored merchant ships at Griffin's Wharf, breaking open wooden tea chests and tipping them into the dark water, a crowd watching silently from the wharf by lantern light, the town's church spires behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century American lithograph with hand colouring, moonlit blues, small figures.
na-lexington-concord: 1775, Lexington, Massachusetts: at dawn on 19 April, on a village green with a white wooden meetinghouse and clapboard houses, a small group of colonial militia in farm clothes and tricorns stand facing columns of British soldiers in red coats and white crossbelts, gun smoke beginning to drift, bare spring trees. Painted in the style of the Amos Doolittle engravings of 1775, hand-coloured, simple figures, no bodies shown.
na-declaration-of-independence: 1776, Philadelphia: the red-brick Pennsylvania State House with its white wooden steeple on a summer day, inside its tall-windowed assembly room delegates in powdered wigs, waistcoats and knee breeches seated at green-covered tables, a small group presenting a document at the front, seen from the back of the room. Painted in the style of a late eighteenth-century American oil history painting, warm light, many small figures, no legible text.
na-saratoga: 1777, Saratoga, New York: in an autumn meadow along the Hudson River, a long column of British and German soldiers in red and blue coats lays down muskets and grounded colours before a line of American Continental troops in brown and blue coats, wooded hills in red and gold foliage behind. Painted as a late eighteenth-century American oil history painting in the manner of John Trumbull, warm October light, many small figures.
na-yorktown: 1781, Yorktown, Virginia: on an open field outside the earthwork defences of the town by the York River, British troops in red coats march between long lines of French soldiers in white and American soldiers in blue to lay down their arms, French warships in the river and smoke drifting from the battered town. Painted in the style of a late eighteenth-century oil history painting by John Trumbull, many small figures, golden October light.
na-treaty-of-paris-1783: 1783, Paris: an elegant eighteenth-century hotel room with tall windows, gilded mouldings and a marble fireplace, a small group of diplomats in powdered wigs, silk coats and knee breeches gathered around a table with quills, inkwell and documents bearing wax seals, Paris rooftops seen outside. Painted as an eighteenth-century French oil painting, soft pastel colours and warm light, figures seen from the side, no faces in detail, no legible text.
na-constitutional-convention: 1787, Philadelphia: a hot summer day in the tall-windowed assembly room of the State House, its windows shuttered, delegates in dark coats and wigs seated at tables covered in green cloth, a high-backed chair at the front with a carved sun, papers and quills on the tables, seen from the back. Painted as a nineteenth-century American oil history painting, warm muted browns and greens, many small figures, no legible text.
na-washington-inauguration: 1789, New York City: on 30 April, the balcony of Federal Hall on Wall Street with its classical columns, a small group of figures in dark suits and powdered hair standing at the railing, seen from far below, a vast crowd of townspeople in tricorns and bonnets filling the street and rooftops, Trinity Church spire beyond. Painted as an early nineteenth-century American engraving with hand colouring, many small figures.
na-louisiana-purchase: 1803, New Orleans: in the plaza before the Spanish-colonial Cabildo and the cathedral with its towers, French troops lower one flag and American soldiers in blue coats raise another on a tall pole, townspeople of many backgrounds in summer dress watching, ships on the Mississippi behind. Painted as an early nineteenth-century oil history painting, warm December light, many small figures, flags without detailed emblems.
na-lewis-and-clark: 1805, the Columbia River and Pacific coast, Oregon: an expedition party in buckskin and fur caps paddles dugout canoes down a broad river between forested mountains toward the misty Pacific, a Shoshone woman with an infant on a cradleboard in one canoe, a log fort with smoke at the river mouth. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour of the American West, as by Karl Bodmer, soft greens and greys.
na-erie-canal: 1825, Albany, New York: a long canal with stone locks and towpaths meeting the wide Hudson River, a flotilla of decorated canal boats pulled by mules arrives as a cannon fires a salute, crowds of townspeople in top hats and bonnets lining the banks, warehouses and church spires behind. Painted as an early nineteenth-century American oil painting in the Hudson River School manner, luminous autumn light, small figures.
na-trail-of-tears: 1838, Cherokee lands in Georgia and Tennessee: a long line of Cherokee families in coats, turbans and shawls, with wagons, horses and bundles, trudging along a muddy road through bare winter forest under grey skies, a few US soldiers on horseback alongside, smoke from campfires ahead. Painted as a sombre nineteenth-century documentary oil painting, muted browns and greys, figures small and distant, dignified, no bodies shown.
na-california-gold-rush: 1848-1849, Coloma, California: a wooden sawmill on the American River among oak-covered foothills, miners in flannel shirts and slouch hats panning for gold and working wooden rockers in the shallows, tents and log cabins along the bank, a group of Chinese miners in queues and broad straw hats working a claim nearby. Painted as a nineteenth-century hand-coloured lithograph, warm golden light, many small figures.
na-uncle-toms-cabin: 1852, Brunswick, Maine: a modest white clapboard house in a snowy New England college town, through a lamplit window a woman in a dark dress and lace collar writes at a kitchen table cluttered with manuscript pages while children play nearby, and in a bookshop window in town stacks of newly bound volumes, townspeople in bonnets and top hats reading. Painted as a mid-nineteenth-century American genre oil painting, warm lamplight, figures seen from a distance, no legible text.
na-lincoln-elected: 1860, Springfield, Illinois: on a November night, crowds of townspeople in frock coats, top hats and shawls fill the square around the domed state capitol, torchlight parades and bonfires, a telegraph office window glowing with men reading dispatches, brick storefronts and horse-drawn wagons along the muddy streets. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving such as Harper's Weekly, fine black-and-white line with tonal hatching, many small figures, no legible text.
na-civil-war: 1861, Charleston Harbor, South Carolina: at dawn on 12 April, the brick pentagonal Fort Sumter on its island in the harbour under bombardment, arcs of shells and puffs of smoke over its walls, shore batteries firing from Fort Johnson and Morris Island, townspeople watching from rooftops and the waterfront of Charleston. Painted in the style of a Currier and Ives hand-coloured lithograph, soft pink dawn sky, small figures at a distance, no bodies shown.
na-emancipation-proclamation: 1863, Washington, D.C.: on New Year's Day, a gathering of freedpeople and abolitionists in a candlelit church with wooden pews, waiting together for midnight, and through the window the snowy city with the unfinished Capitol dome under scaffolding, a man in the aisle reading aloud from a newspaper. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century American engraving with hand colouring, warm candlelight, many small figures, dignified and hopeful, no legible text.
na-gettysburg: 1863, Gettysburg, Pennsylvania: on a hot July afternoon, long lines of Confederate infantry in grey and butternut with battle flags advance across a wide open field of wheat and fences toward a low stone wall on Cemetery Ridge held by Union troops in blue, cannon smoke rolling over the ridge, wooded hills and a small town with church steeples behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century panoramic battle painting in the cyclorama style, figures small and distant, no bodies shown.
na-lincoln-assassination: 1865, Washington, D.C.: on a damp April night, the brick facade of Ford's Theatre with its arched doorways lit by gas lamps, carriages and horses waiting on the cobbled street, a crowd gathering outside in alarm, soldiers in blue greatcoats arriving, and across the street the lit windows of a small boarding house. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, black and white tonal hatching, small figures, no violence shown.
na-appomattox: 1865, Appomattox Court House, Virginia: a quiet April afternoon outside a modest two-storey brick farmhouse with a wooden porch, a few officers in blue and grey uniforms on horseback and on foot waiting in the yard, a grey horse tied at the gate, soldiers resting under budding trees, rolling green Virginia hills. Painted as a nineteenth-century American oil history painting, soft spring light, figures small, no faces in detail.
na-transcontinental-railroad: 1869, Promontory Summit, Utah: two steam locomotives with tall flared smokestacks meet face to face on a single track in a high sagebrush valley, crowds of railway workers in shirtsleeves, Chinese labourers in broad hats and blue cotton tunics standing beside the line, officials in top hats gathered around the last tie, snowy mountains beyond. Painted as a nineteenth-century American oil painting, clear May light, many small figures.
na-little-bighorn: 1876, Little Bighorn River, Montana: a vast landscape of rolling grassland hills above a winding river lined with cottonwoods, a huge Lakota and Cheyenne camp of hundreds of painted tipis along the valley floor, mounted warriors riding up the bluffs through dust and smoke, the summer sky enormous. Painted in the style of Lakota ledger art drawn by participants, coloured pencil and ink on lined paper, flat stylised horses and riders, no bodies shown.
na-compromise-of-1877: 1877, the American South: a column of federal soldiers in blue uniforms with packs marching out of a small Southern town to a railway station, a red-brick courthouse with a white portico behind, Black families watching quietly from the porches of wooden houses, white townspeople in the street, spring trees. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving like those of Harper's Weekly, black-and-white tonal hatching, small figures, sombre mood.
na-canadian-pacific-railway: 1885, Craigellachie, British Columbia: a single railway track cutting through a dense forest of tall cedars and firs in a mountain pass, a small crowd of workers in caps and wool coats and officials in top hats gathered around the last spike, Chinese labourers who built the mountain section standing at the edge, snowy Monashee peaks behind. Painted as a late nineteenth-century Canadian oil painting, cool November light, small figures.
na-wounded-knee: 1890, Wounded Knee Creek, South Dakota: a bleak winter landscape of snow-covered rolling prairie hills under a heavy grey sky, a small wooden church on a rise, a creek lined with bare trees, scattered empty tipis and abandoned wagons half buried in snow, a single riderless horse in the distance. Painted as a sombre nineteenth-century documentary watercolour, muted greys and whites, landscape only, quiet and mournful, no people or bodies shown.
na-us-enters-wwi: 1917, Washington, D.C.: on an April evening, the white domed Capitol lit up at dusk, a crowd in hats and long coats gathered on the steps and lawn, motor cars and streetcars on Pennsylvania Avenue, and nearby a recruitment line of young men in straw boaters outside a brick building. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour illustration, soft blue dusk and warm lamplight, many small figures, no posters or legible text.
na-wall-street-crash: 1929, Wall Street, New York City: in October, a narrow canyon of tall stone bank buildings with classical columns, a dense anxious crowd of men in overcoats and fedoras filling the street outside the stock exchange, police at the doors, ticker tape strewn on the ground, grey autumn light. Rendered as a 1930s American lithograph in the style of the social realist printmakers, black and grey tones, many small figures, no legible signs.
na-new-deal: 1930s, rural America: a work crew of young men in denim overalls and work shirts building a stone dam and a new road in a green valley, trucks and wheelbarrows, a row of tents of a work camp nearby, a new hydroelectric dam and power lines in the distance under a clear sky. Painted in the style of a 1930s WPA public mural, sturdy simplified figures, warm earthy colours, optimistic but neutral, no lettering or portraits.
na-manhattan-project: 1942-1945, Los Alamos, New Mexico: a cluster of plain wooden laboratory buildings, water towers and army huts on a pine-covered mesa high above deep canyons, scientists in shirtsleeves and army personnel walking between them, jeeps on dirt roads, and far off across the desert at dawn a distant pale glow on the horizon. Painted as a muted 1940s documentary watercolour, ochre, pine green and pale blue, small anonymous figures, calm and neutral.
na-montgomery-bus-boycott: 1955-1956, Montgomery, Alabama: a quiet morning street of brick storefronts and churches, an empty city bus passing by, while crowds of Black residents in coats and hats walk together on the sidewalks to work, and a line of private cars gives rides to others, autumn trees. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft warm tones, many small figures seen from a distance, dignified and calm, no legible signs.
na-cuban-missile-crisis: 1962, Washington, D.C.: on an October night, the White House lit from within, a dim cabinet room seen through tall windows with men in dark suits seated around a long table covered with aerial reconnaissance photographs and maps, and on the Atlantic far away a grey navy destroyer at sea under a moonlit sky. Painted as a muted 1960s documentary gouache illustration, deep blues and amber light, figures small and indistinct, calm and neutral.
na-march-on-washington: 1963, Washington, D.C.: on a hot August day, an immense crowd of about a quarter million people in summer clothes stretches along both sides of the long Reflecting Pool from the white columned Lincoln Memorial to the Washington Monument, seen from high above, trees along the edges, a small speaker's platform far away on the memorial steps. Painted as a documentary watercolour, warm summer light, thousands of tiny figures, no legible signs.
na-apollo-11: 1969, Kennedy Space Center, Florida: on a bright July morning, the towering white Saturn V rocket lifts off from its launch pad beside a red steel launch tower, a vast plume of flame and white smoke billowing across the flat marshland and lagoons, crowds of spectators watching from a beach and causeway in the foreground. Painted as a documentary gouache illustration in the style of 1960s NASA art, bold flat colour, figures tiny and anonymous.
na-september-11: 2001, New York City: a calm wide view across the harbour from the water on a clear blue September morning, the lower Manhattan skyline with a great grey cloud of smoke drifting south over the towers, the Statue of Liberty small in the foreground, ferries and boats on the water. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greys and blues, landscape only, solemn and quiet, no aircraft, no fire up close, no people shown.
sam-aspero: c. 3000 BCE, Aspero, Supe River mouth, Peru: on a bare desert coast by the cold Pacific, fishing people in cotton loincloths carry woven bags of stones to build up small stepped platform mounds, cotton fishing nets drying on poles, gourd floats and anchovies in baskets, a green river valley behind and dry brown hills under a hazy sky. Painted in the style of a Moche ceramic fine-line painting, red-brown figures on cream, simplified forms.
sam-caral: c. 2600 BCE, Caral, Supe Valley, Peru: a desert terrace above a green river valley with large stepped stone-and-mud pyramids, round sunken ceremonial plazas, and clusters of houses, people in cotton tunics carrying stones in woven shicra bags up the stairways, musicians playing condor-bone flutes, dry brown hills under a clear sky. Painted in the style of Andean ceramic fine-line painting, red-brown and cream, flat stylised figures, many small figures.
sam-kotosh: c. 2300 BCE, Kotosh, Huánuco, highland Peru: in a green mountain valley, a small square stone temple with plastered walls and niches, a central sunken fire pit with smoke rising through a hole in the roof, and below one niche a modelled clay relief of two crossed forearms, villagers in woollen ponchos bringing offerings. Painted in the style of an Andean ceramic fine-line painting, earth reds and cream with black outline, stylised figures.
sam-sechin-alto: c. 1800 BCE, Sechín Alto, Casma Valley, Peru: in a wide desert valley with irrigated fields, a massive platform mound of stone and adobe rising above a long series of plazas and sunken circular courts, workers hauling stone blocks with ropes, people in cotton tunics gathering in the plazas, dry mountains behind. Painted in the style of an Andean ceramic fine-line painting, red-brown on cream, flat stylised figures, bird's-eye view.
sam-cerro-sechin: c. 1600 BCE, Cerro Sechín, Casma Valley, Peru: a stone temple platform at the foot of a granite hill, its outer wall lined with hundreds of upright carved granite slabs showing tall striding warriors holding staffs, sculptors working on a new slab, the desert valley and fields beyond. Rendered in the style of Andean incised stone relief, shallow carved lines on pale granite, stylised profile figures only, no injuries, wounds or body parts shown.
sam-chavin-de-huantar: c. 900 BCE, Chavín de Huántar, Andes of Peru: in a deep valley where two rivers meet below snowy peaks, a great stone temple with a sunken circular plaza and walls studded with carved stone heads, pilgrims in woollen ponchos arriving with llamas, priests in feathered headdresses blowing conch-shell trumpets at the entrance to dark stone galleries. Painted in the Chavín art style, carved jaguar, snake and eagle motifs, flat black, red and stone grey.
sam-paracas: c. 800 BCE, Paracas Peninsula, Peru: on a windswept desert coast above the blue Pacific, Paracas weavers sit beneath reed shades embroidering brilliantly coloured woollen mantles with repeated figures of flying beings and animals, finished textiles and bundles laid out, pottery and baskets, sea lions and seabirds on the rocks below. Painted in the style of a Paracas embroidered textile, deep red, gold, blue and green, flat repeating stylised figures, no bodies shown.
sam-chavin-decline: c. 500 BCE, Chavín de Huántar, Peru: the great stone temple in its Andean valley grown quiet, a few villagers building simple houses against its walls in the plaza, weeds growing between the carved stone heads, no pilgrims on the empty paths, snowy peaks and clouds above. Painted in the Chavín art style, carved jaguar and serpent motifs as a border, muted stone greys and faded red, melancholy and still.
sam-nazca: c. 100 BCE, Cahuachi, Nazca Valley, Peru: in a dry river valley, a pilgrimage centre of adobe stepped mounds and plazas on low hills, pilgrims in brightly patterned tunics arriving with offerings, potters nearby painting polychrome vessels with killer whales and birds in red, orange, white and black, desert plains and mountains beyond. Painted in the style of Nazca polychrome pottery painting, flat bright colours with black outlines, stylised figures.
sam-nazca-lines: c. 1 CE, Nazca Desert, Peru: on a vast flat plain of reddish desert stones under a cloudless sky, small groups of Nazca people in tunics clear dark surface stones into rows with wooden stakes and cords, revealing pale lines that form a gigantic hummingbird and long straight lines across the plain, seen from high above. Painted in the style of Nazca polychrome pottery painting, earthy red, cream and black, simplified forms.
sam-moche: c. 100 CE, Huacas de Moche, Trujillo, Peru: in the coastal desert near the Moche River, the immense adobe brick Huaca del Sol rising beside the terraced Huaca de la Luna with painted relief walls, workers carrying adobe bricks, potters shaping stirrup-spout vessels, reed boats on the river, irrigated fields and dry mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Moche fine-line ceramic painting, red-brown figures on cream slip, flowing outlines.
sam-sipan: c. 250 CE, Sipán, Lambayeque, Peru: inside an adobe platform mound, a burial chamber of adobe walls, a wooden coffin surrounded by grave goods: gold and silver peanut-bead necklaces, turquoise ear ornaments, a golden crescent headdress, copper sceptres and pottery vessels, attendants in cotton tunics laying offerings by lamplight. Painted in the style of a Moche fine-line ceramic painting, red-brown on cream with gold accents, no body shown.
sam-tiwanaku-rise: c. 400 CE, Tiwanaku, Bolivian altiplano: on the high cold plain near Lake Titicaca, a growing city of stone and adobe, the walled Kalasasaya platform temple with tall stone pillars, farmers working raised fields with channels of water between them, llama herds, people in woollen tunics and four-cornered hats, the snowy Cordillera Real behind. Painted in the style of a Tiwanaku polychrome ceramic and textile, flat red, ochre, black and white, stylised figures.
sam-wari: c. 600 CE, Huari, Ayacucho, Peru: on a high Andean plateau, a large walled city of rectangular stone compounds with long straight walls and courtyards, roads leading off across the mountains, administrators with knotted string records, llama caravans carrying goods, people in tunics woven with bold interlocking geometric patterns. Painted in the style of a Wari tapestry tunic, bold geometric reds, golds and blues, stylised flat figures.
sam-gate-of-the-sun: c. 600 CE, Tiwanaku, Bolivian altiplano: a single great andesite stone gateway standing at the edge of a stone platform, carved across its top with a central staff-holding figure and rows of winged attendants, stone masons polishing it, priests in woollen tunics and four-cornered hats, Lake Titicaca and snowy peaks on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Tiwanaku polychrome textile, flat red, gold and blue, stylised figures.
sam-chan-chan: c. 1000 CE, Chan Chan, Trujillo, Peru: a vast city of adobe on the desert coast, with high walled royal compounds whose walls are decorated with relief friezes of fish, birds and waves, walk-in wells, courtyards and storerooms, Chimú lords in gold ear ornaments, craftsmen working gold and silver, reed boats on the Pacific shore. Painted in the style of Chimú relief and ceramic art, earthen tones with gold and silver highlights, stylised figures.
sam-wari-collapse: c. 1000 CE, Tiwanaku, Bolivian altiplano: the stone temples and platforms of Tiwanaku left half deserted on the cold high plain, raised fields dry and cracked from drought, Lake Titicaca shrunk back from its shores, a few families leading llamas away into the hills, toppled stone statues among the grass. Painted in the style of a Tiwanaku polychrome textile and ceramic, faded reds, ochres and greys, melancholy mood.
sam-cusco-kingdom: c. 1200 CE, Cusco valley, Peru: a band of Andean people in woollen tunics and mantles with llamas, carrying bundles and a golden staff, descends from the mountains into a green highland valley with rivers and small fields, a leader and his companions walking ahead, seen small from behind, and the first stone and thatch houses being built. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript illustration like Guaman Poma's chronicle, ink line with soft colour.
sam-pachacuti: 1438, Cusco, Peru: in the green mountain valley, Inca warriors in quilted tunics with slings, maces and round shields repulse a Chanka attack on the hillsides above the city, and below, workers begin rebuilding Cusco with finely fitted stone walls and thatched roofs, the young Inca ruler seen small and distant directing them. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line drawing with soft colour, no bodies shown.
sam-machu-picchu: c. 1450, Machu Picchu, Peru: on a narrow mountain ridge high above the green Urubamba river gorge, Inca workers in woollen tunics lay finely fitted granite blocks to build temples, houses with steep thatched roofs and long agricultural terraces, llamas grazing, the sugarloaf peak of Huayna Picchu wreathed in cloud behind. Painted in the style of a colonial Cusco School painting, rich earth tones with gold highlights, misty atmospheric mountains, small figures.
sam-qhapaq-nan: c. 1450, the Andes of Peru: a stone-paved Inca road with steps winding across steep mountains, a woven grass rope suspension bridge spanning a deep river gorge, a chaski runner in a tunic with a conch shell running across it, a stone waystation with storehouses, llama caravans, snowy peaks behind. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line drawing with soft watercolour.
sam-chimor-conquest: c. 1470, Chan Chan, north coast of Peru: Inca armies in patterned tunics with slings and spears march across the coastal desert toward the walled adobe city of Chan Chan, and a long line of Chimú metalworkers with their tools and baskets of gold and silver objects being led away on the road to the mountains. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line drawing with soft colour, no bodies shown.
sam-maule: c. 1480, Maule River, central Chile: on the banks of a wide river in green rolling country with forests and distant snowy Andes, an Inca army in patterned tunics with spears and slings halted on one bank, Mapuche warriors in woollen ponchos with long spears holding the opposite bank, a standoff at a distance. Painted in the style of a colonial-era Andean manuscript illustration, ink line with soft watercolour, small figures, no bodies.
sam-cabral: 1500, Porto Seguro, Bahia, Brazil: a Portuguese fleet of carracks with red-cross sails anchored off a tropical coast of white beaches and dense green forest, sailors in caps and doublets landing in boats, a priest raising a wooden cross on the beach, Tupi people with feather ornaments watching from the trees. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Portuguese manuscript illumination and early engraving, fine line with soft hand colouring.
sam-huayna-capac: c. 1527, Quito, Ecuador: a sombre Inca palace of fine stone walls and thatched roofs in an Andean valley ringed by volcanoes, attendants in woollen tunics and mourning women gathered quietly in the courtyard, a litter covered with cloth set down, smoke from incense rising, grey clouds over the mountains. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line with muted watercolour, small figures, restrained, no sickness shown in detail.
sam-inca-civil-war: c. 1529-1532, the Andes of Peru: two great Inca armies in patterned tunics with slings, spears and feathered standards face each other across a mountain valley, litters of their commanders carried behind each force, storehouses and terraced fields on the slopes, dust rising. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line drawing with soft colour, small figures, no bodies shown.
sam-cajamarca: 1532, Cajamarca, Peru: a large trapezoidal plaza surrounded by long stone buildings in a green highland valley, thousands of unarmed Inca attendants in tunics around a golden litter carrying a ruler, small and distant, a handful of Spanish soldiers in steel helmets and horses hidden in doorways, a friar with a book stepping forward. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line with soft colour, no bodies.
sam-atahualpa: 1533, Cajamarca, Peru: a stone room in an Inca palace being filled to a painted line high on the wall with gold and silver objects, plates, vessels and statues, Inca porters bringing more in baskets, Spanish soldiers in steel helmets watching and tallying, and outside, a grey sky over the plaza. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript illustration, ink line with muted colour, small figures, no execution or violence shown.
sam-manco-inca: 1536, Cusco, Peru: thousands of Inca warriors encamped on the green hillsides around the city, slings hurling burning stones onto thatched roofs, smoke rising from the town, Spanish horsemen penned in a central plaza, the great zigzag stone walls of Sacsayhuamán fortress on the hill above. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean manuscript by Guaman Poma, ink line with soft colour, small figures, no bodies shown.
sam-potosi: c. 1545-1600, Potosí, Bolivia: the great red cone of the Cerro Rico mountain riddled with mine shafts rising above a high cold valley, long lines of Andean labourers in ponchos climbing with heavy sacks of ore on their backs, llama trains, stone furnaces with smoke, water-driven stamp mills and a growing Spanish colonial town below. Painted in the style of a colonial Andean oil painting, earth reds and browns, many small figures.
sam-sugar-slavery: c. 1550-1600, Pernambuco, Brazil: a sugar plantation with a water-driven mill and boiling house beside a river, enslaved Africans cutting tall green cane in the fields and carrying bundles, oxcarts, a white-washed plantation house and chapel on a hill, palm trees and tropical forest beyond. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century Dutch colonial painting of Brazil like those of Frans Post, clear light, small figures, dignified and sombre.
sam-palmares: c. 1605-1690, Serra da Barriga, Alagoas, Brazil: on a forested hill ridge, a large free settlement of thatched houses and gardens surrounded by a wooden palisade, people of African descent farming maize and cassava, a council gathered under a large tree, children playing, the tropical forest and mountains around under a bright sky. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour of Brazil, like those of Jean-Baptiste Debret, soft greens and earth tones.
sam-jesuit-reductions: c. 1609-1700, San Ignacio Miní, Misiones, Argentina: a mission town in subtropical forest with a large red sandstone baroque church, a broad grassy plaza and long rows of tiled-roof houses, Guaraní people in white cotton working in carpentry and weaving workshops and fields, a Jesuit priest in a black cassock small in the distance. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century colonial South American engraving with hand colouring, warm red and green.
sam-gold-rush: c. 1693-1750, Ouro Preto, Minas Gerais, Brazil: a mountain mining town of white houses, tiled roofs and baroque church towers on steep green hills, miners and enslaved Africans in a river below washing gold gravel in wooden pans and sluices, mule trains carrying goods up the cobbled streets, misty mountains beyond. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour of Brazil by Johann Moritz Rugendas, soft green and earth tones.
sam-tupac-amaru-ii: 1780, Tinta, near Cusco, Peru: in a high Andean valley, a huge gathering of Quechua peasants in ponchos and woollen caps with slings and farm tools rallying around a horseman in a colonial-style black coat and tricorn hat, seen small from behind, a colonial church and adobe village behind and snowy peaks beyond. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Cusco School colonial painting, rich earth tones and gold, many small figures, no violence shown.
sam-court-to-rio: 1808, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a Portuguese royal fleet of tall sailing ships anchored in Guanabara Bay beneath the Sugarloaf mountain, boats bringing courtiers in silk coats and powdered wigs ashore to a crowded waterfront of white colonial buildings and churches, townspeople, soldiers and enslaved Africans watching, tropical green hills behind. Painted in the style of a Jean-Baptiste Debret watercolour, soft clear colour, many small figures.
sam-may-revolution: 1810, Buenos Aires, Argentina: a rainy May day in the plaza before the white colonial Cabildo with its arched arcades and small bell tower, crowds of townspeople in top hats, cloaks and umbrellas gathered waiting, a few holding sky-blue and white ribbons, horse-drawn carriages and the cathedral nearby. Painted as a nineteenth-century South American oil history painting, soft grey light, many small figures, no flags with emblems, no legible text.
sam-venezuela-independence: 1811, Caracas, Venezuela: in a colonial chapel converted into an assembly hall with whitewashed walls and dark wooden beams, delegates in dark coats, high collars and cravats standing and seated around a table with documents and quills, townspeople crowding the doorway, the green Ávila mountain visible through the windows. Painted as a nineteenth-century Latin American oil history painting in the manner of Martín Tovar y Tovar, warm light, figures small, no legible text.
sam-crossing-andes: 1817, the Andes between Argentina and Chile: a long column of soldiers in blue uniforms and ponchos with muskets and cannon on mules, cavalry and pack trains winding along a narrow trail across snowy high mountain passes beneath towering peaks, a general on horseback seen small from behind, condors circling. Painted as a nineteenth-century Latin American oil history painting, cold blue and white mountain light, many small figures.
yu-assembly-at-tushan: c. 2065 BCE, Mount Tu near the Huai River: on a grassy terrace below a wooded hill, a great gathering of tribal chiefs in plain hemp and undyed wool robes with feathered headdresses kneel in rows on mats, presenting jade bi discs, jade cong and bolts of silk to a leader seated beneath a thatched open hall of timber posts; smoke rises from sacrificial fires, river marshes glint in the morning haze. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, soft earth tones, many small figures.
qi-battle-of-gan: c. 2060 BCE, the plain of Gan near the Wei valley: two Neolithic-Bronze Age war bands face each other across a loess field at dawn, warriors on foot with stone and bronze dagger-axes, wooden shields painted with clan emblems and bows of horn and wood; no chariots or horses. A leader on a low earthen mound raises a jade axe before his ranks, banners of feathers and hide flutter, dust drifts over terraced loess hills. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, flat stylised figures seen at a distance.
nine-tripod-cauldrons: c. 2060 BCE, Yangcheng in the Song mountain foothills: an open-air casting ground beside rammed-earth walls, where workers in short hemp tunics pour glowing molten bronze from clay crucibles into large ceramic piece-moulds; nine massive three-legged cauldrons in various stages stand in a row, their surfaces cast with abstract beast-mask patterns, charcoal smoke rising against wooded hills. Elders in long robes watch from a timber platform. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, warm firelight glow.
shimao-stone-city: c. 2050 BCE, Shimao on the Loess Plateau of northern Shaanxi: a vast hilltop city of dry-laid stone walls and stepped stone terraces crowning a pyramid-like central platform, a gated enclosure with bastions and an outer wall winding across eroded yellow loess ridges and gullies; small figures in hemp and fur carry stone blocks and herd sheep, jade pieces set into the walls catch the light, thin smoke from pit houses. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, ochre and cinnabar, wide panoramic view at dusk.
feast-at-juntai: c. 2030 BCE, Juntai near Yuzhou: on a raised rammed-earth terrace under a thatched timber hall, lords in plain wrapped robes sit on reed mats in two long rows, sharing millet, roast meat and millet wine from early bronze jue vessels and painted pottery; a young ruler sits at the head on a slightly higher platform, drummers with clay drums and dancers holding feather wands perform in the courtyard below, loess hills beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, festive evening light.
lajia-disaster: c. 2000 BCE, Lajia on the upper Yellow River in Qinghai: a small Neolithic village of semi-subterranean houses on a river terrace lies half-buried under fresh mud and reddish silt after an earthquake and flood, collapsed thatched roofs, cracked earth, the swollen brown river beyond under a heavy grey sky; in the foreground, an upturned brown clay bowl rests on the mud, thin noodles visible within. No people shown. Ink and wash on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, subdued ochre and grey.
houyi-usurps-xia: c. 1980 BCE, Zhenxun near the Luo River: while a royal hunting party with bows and dogs rides away on foot far across the river through reed beds, a band of archers led by a tall bowman carrying a great recurved bow marches through the open gate of a rammed-earth palace compound, guards falling back, thatched halls and granaries inside. Early afternoon, low hills behind. No chariots or horses. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, stylised flat figures in a long frieze.
zhongkang-eclipse: c. 1960 BCE, Zhenxun: the sun darkens to a black disc ringed with pale corona over a rammed-earth palace compound; in the courtyard people beat clay and wooden drums and shoot arrows toward the sky in alarm, officials run with torches, while in a side hall two astronomers lie slumped asleep among overturned wine vessels beside their observing gnomon. Dim, eerie midday light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, deep indigo and ochre.
shao-kang-restoration: c. 1950 BCE, Zhenxun near Luoyang: a young leader and his loyal followers in hemp robes, armed with bronze dagger-axes and bows, approach a rammed-earth palace gate at sunrise as townspeople open it and kneel to welcome them; an old banner of feathers is raised again above the thatched halls, fields of millet and the Luo River beyond. Small figures, broad landscape, hopeful dawn colours. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of bronze-age lacquer painting.
qijia-copper: c. 1900 BCE, Qijiaping in the upper Yellow River valley of Gansu: a village of semi-subterranean houses on a loess terrace, where metalworkers in hide and hemp clothing heat copper ore in a small clay furnace with bellows of animal skin, pour metal into stone moulds and polish small knives, round mirrors and ring ornaments; painted pottery jars and sheep pens nearby, the river and dry hills beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, earthy reds and ochres.
jie-of-xia: c. 1650 BCE, the Xia capital at Zhenxun: a lavish palace hall on a high rammed-earth platform, lit by torches, where a ruler lounges amid dancers, musicians with stone chimes and piles of bronze wine jue and jade, while below the platform lines of weary labourers haul earth in baskets and thin villagers look on from parched fields. Evening, contrast of glow and shadow. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, figures small and stylised.
tang-conquers-kunwu: c. 1610 BCE, Kunwu near Puyang on the North China plain: a Shang war band on foot with bronze dagger-axes, spears and bows advances under banners toward a rammed-earth walled town; smoke rises from inside the walls, defenders retreat through a gate, and a leader directs troops from a low rise. No chariots. Flat plain, river willows, midday haze. Seen from a distance, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
yanshi-shang-city: c. 1600 BCE, Yanshi on the Luo River plain: a vast rectangular rammed-earth city wall rises under construction, labourers tamping earth between wooden plank frames with pestles, others carrying baskets; inside, a palace compound with a row of timber halls on raised platforms and a pond. Supervisors in long robes stand on the wall top, the older settlement of Erlitou visible to the west across fields. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, panoramic view.
tang-prays-at-mulberry-grove: c. 1590 BCE, the Mulberry Grove near Shangqiu during a long drought: under a grove of gnarled mulberry trees beside cracked dry fields, a king with cut hair and trimmed nails kneels on a woven mat before a heap of firewood and an altar, offering himself to Heaven; crowds of people and officials kneel around him; overhead, dark rain clouds gather and the first drops fall. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, parched ochre turning to cool grey.
yi-yin-exiles-taijia: c. 1570 BCE, near the early Shang capital of Bo: an elderly chief minister in long dark robes stands at the gate of a modest rammed-earth compound with a simple thatched hall beside a royal burial ground, gesturing as a young king in plain clothes is escorted inside by attendants; cypress trees and earthen tomb mounds beyond, quiet overcast day. Small figures, nobody harmed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted greens and browns.
zhengzhou-shang-city: c. 1500 BCE, Zhengzhou: an enormous rammed-earth city wall nearly seven kilometres around encloses palace halls on raised earthen platforms; outside the walls, bronze foundries smoke, potters fire kilns and bone workshops cluster by streams; workers tamp new wall sections in layers between plank frames, ox carts carry earth, millet fields stretch to the horizon. Bird's-eye panorama in morning light. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, many tiny figures.
panlongcheng: c. 1450 BCE, Panlongcheng near the Yangtze at Wuhan: a compact walled town of rammed earth on a lakeside hill surrounded by water and reeds, a palace hall with a hipped thatched roof on a platform at its centre; dugout canoes unload copper ingots at the shore, craftsmen cast Shang-style bronze vessels near the walls, lush subtropical trees and the broad river beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, green and ochre, humid haze.
zhongding-moves-to-ao: c. 1420 BCE, Ao near Zhengzhou: a long procession of the Shang court moves across the plain to a new capital, nobles in robes walking beside ox carts and porters carrying bronze ritual vessels, chests of oracle bones and bundles; at the front, workers are already raising rammed-earth walls by a river. Banners on poles, dust in the air, late afternoon. No chariots. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze-like composition.
zu-yi-moves-to-xing: c. 1400 BCE, from flooded Xiang to Xing near the Taihang foothills: in the background, a river has burst its banks around an abandoned rammed-earth town; in the foreground, the Shang court treks to dry higher ground below wooded mountains, carrying bronze vessels and grain, while a minister in long robes directs the laying out of a new palace platform. Grey sky clearing over the hills. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, soft blues and ochres.
huanbei-shang-city: c. 1350 BCE, Huanbei on the Huan River at Anyang: a huge square rammed-earth walled city on a flat plain, its palace compound of large courtyard halls on earthen platforms half finished; in one area the halls show scorch marks and stand abandoned while workers carry goods out through the gates toward the river. Willows, millet fields, a pale autumn sky. Bird's-eye view. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, many small figures.
wu-ding-appoints-fu-yue: c. 1250 BCE, Fuyan near Yin: at a road cutting through hills, convict labourers in rough hemp tunics tamp rammed earth between wooden plank frames to build a wall; a royal party of nobles in fine robes, with attendants and banners, has halted, and an official bows to a lean labourer holding a tamping pestle, inviting him to come forward. Midday, dusty loess slopes. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
wu-ding-guifang: c. 1230 BCE, the northern frontier mountains of Shanxi: a Shang army moves along a rocky valley, two-horse wooden chariots with spoked wheels carrying an archer, a driver and a halberdier, followed by long columns of foot soldiers with bronze dagger-axes and hide shields; on distant ridges, Guifang warriors watch from stone hilltop forts. Autumn grass, windswept sky, viewed from afar. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, stylised frieze of figures.
wu-ding-wars-on-qiang: c. 1220 BCE, the western frontier between Henan and Shanxi: a massed Shang levy of thousands of foot soldiers with bronze dagger-axes, bows and hide shields assembles on a loess plain below a royal command post, where a diviner holds a cracked ox scapula; war chariots stand ready at the flanks, smoke signals rise from distant hills where the Qiang herders' camps lie. Viewed from a distance, dawn light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
fu-hao: c. 1200 BCE, Yin near Anyang: a Shang royal army on a wide plain, a woman commander in a dark robe and bronze-studded leather armour stands in a two-horse spoked-wheel chariot holding a large ceremonial bronze yue axe, seen small from behind as ranks of foot soldiers with dagger-axes and banners march past; the royal city's rammed-earth halls and the Huan River behind. Morning light. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze composition.
xingan-dayangzhou-tomb: c. 1200 BCE, Xin'gan in the Gan River valley of Jiangxi: inside a timber-lined burial pit in a sandy riverside mound, hundreds of bronze vessels, bells, weapons with tiger-shaped handles and jade ornaments are carefully arranged by attendants in hemp robes, while a chief's funeral gathering watches from above; green subtropical hills and the broad river behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, jade greens and bronze browns.
four-goat-square-zun: c. 1200 BCE, Ningxiang in the hills of Hunan: in a foundry clearing under tall trees, bronze casters in hemp tunics lift away sections of a clay piece-mould to reveal a large square wine vessel, four curly-horned goats projecting from its corners and shoulders with dragon motifs; charcoal furnaces glow, clay mould fragments lie around, misty green hills beyond. Close but not of any face. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, warm metallic sheen.
houmuwu-ding: c. 1190 BCE, Yin near Anyang: in a large foundry yard, dozens of workers in hemp tunics pour molten bronze from many clay crucibles at once into a giant rectangular clay mould for a four-legged ding cauldron, others pump skin bellows at furnaces; a finished heavy rectangular cauldron stands nearby. Smoke and sparks rise, overseers in robes watch from a platform, palace roofs beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, fiery orange and soot black.
wu-yi-shoots-heaven: c. 1140 BCE, the plain between the Yellow and Wei rivers: a king in a chariot draws a bow at a leather bag hanging from a tall wooden pole, courtiers watching, a human-shaped wooden effigy set on a board nearby; on the horizon storm clouds churn and a bolt of lightning strikes a distant hunting ground. Late afternoon, ominous dark sky over yellow grass. Figures small, no injury shown. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
gugong-danfu-zhouyuan: c. 1130 BCE, the Zhouyuan plain below Mount Qi: a long migration of Zhou people on foot crosses a river and climbs onto fertile loess land, elders leading, families carrying children and bundles, oxen pulling wooden carts, flocks of sheep; an elder chief points to the plain at the foot of the mountain where first huts and fields are laid out. Clear morning, golden loess slopes. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
wen-ding-kills-jili: c. 1101 BCE, Yin near Anyang: inside the walled Shang palace compound, a foreign leader in Zhou-style robes is led by Shang guards with dagger-axes through a courtyard toward a closed timber hall, his attendants held back at the gate; nobles watch from the steps of a hall on a high earthen platform. Grey, tense evening light. Figures small, no violence shown. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
king-zhou-excesses: c. 1070 BCE, Zhaoge: a lavish Shang palace garden at night, a large rectangular pool of wine where revellers in fine robes drink from bronze vessels, and racks of hanging meat like a grove of trees; musicians play bronze bells and stone chimes, dancers whirl, a raised terrace of rammed earth glows with torches, while far beyond the walls grain stores rise at Juqiao. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, deep red and gold.
