bai-qi-floods-yan: 279 BCE, Yan near Yicheng in Hubei: a long diverted channel brings a torrent of river water rushing toward a walled Chu city, its walls already surrounded by floodwater, roofs barely visible; Qin soldiers on embankments watch from afar. Grey sky, wide view, no bodies shown. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
bai-qi-takes-ying: 278 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: Qin troops in dark armour enter the Chu capital among lakes, smoke rising from distant royal tombs at Yiling on the hills; a long line of Chu refugees and nobles flees northeast along the roads. Seen from afar, no bodies. Grey sky. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red with drifting smoke.
battle-of-huayang: 273 BCE, Huayang near Xinzheng: a Qin army sweeps across a plain in a surprise attack, Wei and Zhao forces scattering; in the distance, soldiers flee toward the broad Yellow River. Seen from far above, dust and banners, no bodies. Grey early morning, Han city walls visible on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-destroys-yiqu: 272 BCE, the Ganquan Palace in the northern Shaanxi hills: a palace of timber halls on a hilltop at dusk, lamps lit, a Rong chief's horses tethered outside; in the valley below, Qin troops march north into the grasslands to occupy the Yiqu lands. Figures small, no violence shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and indigo.
battle-of-yuyu: 270 BCE, Yuyu near Heshun in the Taihang mountains: Zhao troops race up a steep mountain ridge to seize the high ground above a narrow pass, while the Qin army below struggles to climb; banners, rocks and pine trees. Seen from a distance, no bodies. Dramatic rugged landscape. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
zou-yan-five-phases: c. 270 BCE, Linzi: in a hall of the Jixia academy, a scholar in robes sits before a large circular diagram painted on silk showing five coloured segments for wood, fire, earth, metal and water, symbolised by trees, flames, earth, bronze and waves; listeners in robes sit in a circle. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
fan-ju: 266 BCE, Xianyang: in a Qin palace hall, a strategist in robes kneels before the king and points at a large painted map on silk spread on the floor, indicating distant states and nearby ones; ministers in black robes listen. No legible writing. Lamplight. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
chu-long-persuades-queen: 265 BCE, Handan: in the Zhao palace, an elderly minister in robes, leaning on a staff, sits talking gently with a royal lady in silk robes; in the background, a young prince prepares a chariot with attendants and gifts for a journey to Qi. Warm afternoon light. Figures small, no close-up faces. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
shangdang: 262 BCE, Shangdang near Changzhi: on a high mountain plateau, Han officials hand over bronze tallies and keys at a fortress gate to Zhao officers; Zhao banners rise on the walls while in the distance the Qin army camps in the valleys. Cold mountain wind, rugged Taihang ridges. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
handan-siege: 259 BCE, Handan: the Zhao capital surrounded by a vast Qin siege camp with tents, earthworks and siege towers; defenders on the walls. On the far horizon, relief armies with Wei and Chu banners approach. Smoke, dust, winter sky over the brown Hebei plain. Seen from afar, no bodies. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
xinling-steals-tally: 257 BCE, Daliang (Kaifeng): at night, a lady in silk robes slips out of a palace bedroom carrying a small bronze tiger-shaped tally; at a military camp outside the city, a lord in robes and a strongman present the tally to a general's tent, troops waiting. Moonlight and torches. Figures small, no violence shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
bai-qi-forced-suicide: 257 BCE, Duyou near Xianyang: an old general in plain robes, seen from behind, sits alone on a mat in a bare roadside dwelling, a royal envoy standing at the door with a sword in its scabbard on a tray; beyond, a road leads away from the capital. Grey dusk. No violence shown. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zhou-ends: 256 BCE, Luoyang: a weary king in plain robes leads a small procession of officials out of the Zhou palace gate, carrying bronze vessels and registers toward a Qin army waiting under black banners; the old palace halls behind are quiet and worn. Overcast sky, autumn leaves. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
dujiangyan: c. 256 BCE, Dujiangyan in Sichuan: on the Min River at the edge of the Chengdu plain, thousands of workers build a fish-mouth levee of bamboo baskets filled with stones that splits the river in two, others cut a channel through a rocky hill; an official in robes oversees from the bank. Green mountains, misty sky, irrigated fields beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chu-destroys-lu: 256 BCE, Qufu: Chu troops in southern armour enter the old Lu capital, its ancient temple halls and cypress trees quiet; a last duke in plain robes leaves the city gate in a simple carriage. Overcast autumn day, townspeople watching quietly from doorways. Figures small, no violence. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red.
xunzi-at-lanling: c. 255 BCE, Lanling in southern Shandong: in a modest official's hall, an elderly scholar-magistrate in robes sits teaching two younger students in robes, bamboo slips spread before them; outside, farmers work orderly fields and a small walled town. Warm afternoon light, a willow by the gate. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
yan-attacks-zhao-hao: 251 BCE, Hao near Gaoyi: a veteran Zhao army with chariots and cavalry riding without stirrups surges across the northern plain, the Yan invaders retreating northward; later the Zhao army camps before the walls of the Yan capital. Autumn fields and poplars. Seen from afar, dust, no bodies. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
lu-buwei-chancellor: 249 BCE, Xianyang: in the Qin palace hall, a newly crowned king sits on the dais as a man in fine merchant-turned-official robes receives the seal and cords of chancellor; officials in black robes kneel in rows. Bronze vessels gleam. Figures small, no faces in close-up. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qin-ends-eastern-zhou: 249 BCE, Gong near Gongyi: Qin troops in dark armour and black banners occupy a small walled town in the hills by the Luo River, Zhou nobles in robes surrender bronze vessels and tallies; the old ancestral temple doors are closed. Grey sky, terraced fields on the slopes. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
xinling-defeats-qin: 247 BCE, Hangu Pass near Lingbao: an allied army of five states with many coloured banners pursues a retreating Qin army through the loess plain to the narrow pass, whose gate towers rise between steep cliffs. Seen from afar, dust clouds, no bodies. Bright day, the commander's chariot on a rise. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
ying-zheng-king: 246 BCE, Xianyang: in the Qin palace courtyard, a boy king in black royal robes is led up the steps to the throne hall, seen small from behind, while a regent chancellor in fine robes walks beside him and officials kneel in long rows. Bronze bells and banners, clear sky. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
zhengguo-canal: 246 BCE, Jingyang in Shaanxi: thousands of labourers dig a vast canal from the Jing River across the Guanzhong plain, carrying earth in baskets on poles, iron spades and wooden mallets in hand; an engineer in robes directs, and newly watered fields turn green beside the finished channel. Bright day, loess hills. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
last-vertical-alliance: 241 BCE, Zui near Lintong: an allied army of five states camps on the plain near Mount Li, its many banners drooping; tents are being struck as armies withdraw eastward, while Qin troops watch from distant walls. Seen from afar, overcast sky, smoke from abandoned campfires drifting over the fields. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
chu-moves-to-shouchun: 241 BCE, Shouchun in Shou County: a long procession of the Chu court on boats and carts arrives at a walled city by the Huai River and lakes, with bronze vessels, lacquerware and bamboo slip bundles; workers build palaces and walls. Misty, green landscape. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black, red and gold.
lushi-chunqiu: 239 BCE, Xianyang: in a grand hall of the chancellor's mansion, dozens of retainers in robes sit at low tables writing on bamboo slips and arguing, while bundles are stacked high; at the city gate outside, a finished text is displayed with a pile of gold beside it as a challenge. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
eu-878-battle-of-edington: 878, Edington in Wiltshire: on open chalk downland under a grey spring sky, a dense Anglo-Saxon shield wall of men with round painted shields, spears and iron helmets advances against a Danish army on a far ridge, small banners raised, a hill fort earthwork behind; no stirruped knights, only foot soldiers and a few mounted thegns at the rear. Depicted in the style of a tenth-century Anglo-Saxon illuminated manuscript, flat colours, ink outlines, vellum ground.
eu-882-kievan-rus: 882, Kyiv on the high bank of the Dnieper: a fleet of Viking-style longships with square sails beaches below wooded hills, where a timber-palisaded Slavic hillfort with log houses stands; armed Norse warriors and Slavic townsfolk in linen tunics meet on the shore, a small leader figure seen from behind among his retinue, smoke rising from hearths. Painted as a medieval Russian chronicle miniature in the manner of the Radziwiłł Chronicle, light watercolour washes and ink line.
eu-911-normandy-founded: 911, near Rouen on the Seine: in a riverside meadow a small Carolingian king in a crown and cloak sits among Frankish nobles and clergy, while Viking chiefs in cloaks and mail, with longships drawn up on the riverbank, gather opposite to make a pact; the timber and stone town of Rouen and its church on the far bank. Rendered as a Carolingian illuminated manuscript miniature, gold highlights, purple and green pigments on vellum.
eu-962-holy-roman-empire: 962, Old Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome: inside the long early-Christian basilica with columns and a timber roof, a pope in white pallium places a crown on a kneeling king in a mantle, seen from behind and small, surrounded by Saxon nobles, bishops with croziers and candlelight; mosaics glimmer in the apse. Painted in the style of an Ottonian illuminated manuscript from the Reichenau school, gold leaf ground, deep purple and green, stylised figures.
eu-1054-east-west-schism: 1054, Hagia Sophia in Constantinople: beneath the vast dome lit by windows, three Latin papal legates in Western mitres walk up the nave and lay a sealed parchment bull on the high altar, while Byzantine clergy in dark robes and courtiers watch from a distance; golden mosaics, marble columns, lamps hanging on chains. Painted in the manner of a Byzantine illuminated chronicle miniature like the Madrid Skylitzes, gold background, bright reds and blues.
eu-1066-battle-of-hastings: 1066, Senlac Hill near Hastings: Norman knights on horseback with kite shields and lances charge uphill at an English shield wall of housecarls with long Danish axes, arrows arcing overhead, banners on the ridge, the autumn sea and ships far off; seen at middle distance with many small figures. Rendered in the style of the Bayeux Tapestry, wool embroidery on linen, limited ochre, green and blue thread, decorative border of animals.
eu-1077-walk-to-canossa: January 1077, the castle of Canossa in the Apennines: a lonely figure in a plain woollen penitent's robe stands barefoot in deep snow before the closed gate of a hilltop stone fortress with three walls, a small retinue waiting below, grey winter sky and snowy peaks around. Painted in the manner of a twelfth-century Romanesque illuminated manuscript, flat stylised figures, earthy reds and blues on vellum, simple architectural frame.
eu-1088-university-of-bologna: Late eleventh century, Bologna: in a vaulted room of a brick town house, a master of Roman law in a dark gown sits at a raised lectern reading from a large codex, while rows of students of different ages in hooded cloaks listen and take notes on wax tablets; tall brick towers seen through an arched window. Depicted in the style of a medieval Italian tomb relief and illuminated manuscript of a lecture scene, warm tempera colours.
eu-1204-fourth-crusade: 1204, Constantinople: seen from the Golden Horn, Venetian galleys and round ships with flying bridges press against the sea walls, crusader knights with crosses on surcoats climbing ashore, smoke rising above domed churches and palaces in the distance, small figures carrying off bronze horses and treasures on carts. Painted as a late medieval French illuminated chronicle miniature in the style of Villehardouin manuscripts, bright blues, reds and gold, diaper-patterned sky.
eu-1215-magna-carta: June 1215, Runnymede meadow beside the Thames: under a striped pavilion a small crowned king sits at a table with a large parchment and a wax seal, surrounded by armed barons in mail and surcoats, clerics, and tethered horses; willow trees, the river and green meadows in summer light. Painted in the style of a thirteenth-century English illuminated manuscript in the manner of Matthew Paris, ink line and pale green, red and blue washes on vellum.
eu-1237-mongol-invasion-of-rus: 1240, Kyiv in winter: across the frozen Dnieper a vast Mongol army of mounted archers with fur hats and horse-tail standards encircles the walled city on its hill, siege engines hurling stones, smoke rising over golden church domes, all seen from far away across the snow. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Russian illuminated chronicle miniature from the Illustrated Chronicle of Ivan the Terrible, ochre, cinnabar and green, stylised rocks and walls.
eu-1337-hundred-years-war: 1346, Crécy in northern France: on a gentle slope English longbowmen in rows loose clouds of arrows, men-at-arms dismounted behind stakes and a windmill on the hill, while French mounted knights with heraldic banners charge up from a valley in late afternoon light; distant, many small figures. Painted as a fifteenth-century illuminated miniature from Froissart's Chronicles, bright heraldic colours, gold leaf, patterned fields and tents.
eu-1347-black-death: 1347, the harbour of Messina in Sicily: Genoese galleys lie at anchor beneath the hills while townspeople in hooded medieval clothes draw back from the quay, a few figures carry covered litters and a priest leads a small procession with a cross and candles past stone churches; quiet empty streets, hazy light. Painted in the style of a fourteenth-century Italian fresco of the Sienese school, muted earth tones, gold-tinged sky.
eu-1429-siege-of-orleans: May 1429, Orléans on the Loire: French troops with banners and lances pour out of the city gates across the bridge toward English wooden siege bastilles, led by a small armoured rider on a white horse carrying a white standard, seen from a distance; the walled town with church spires, river and smoke from the forts. Painted as a fifteenth-century French illuminated manuscript miniature in the manner of the Vigiles de Charles VII, gold and lapis blue.
eu-1440-printing-press: c. 1440, a workshop in Mainz: in a timbered room with leaded windows, craftsmen in tunics and caps work a large wooden screw press, one inking type with leather ink balls, another lifting a freshly printed sheet, cases of small metal type, hanging sheets drying on lines, a master examining a page at a bench. Depicted in the style of a sixteenth-century German woodcut, bold black line, hand-coloured in soft red and ochre.
eu-1453-fall-of-constantinople: 1453, the Theodosian land walls of Constantinople: a huge Ottoman bronze cannon on a wooden carriage fires against the massive triple walls, rows of tents and Janissaries with white felt caps and banners across the plain, the domed city behind the battered walls and ships on the Golden Horn, smoke drifting at dawn. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Ottoman miniature, flat perspective, bright mineral colours, gold sky.
eu-1492-columbus-first-voyage: August 1492, the port of Palos de la Frontera in Andalusia: two small caravels and a larger carrack with square and lateen sails, red crosses on the canvas, slip down the Rio Tinto at dawn, sailors in caps hauling ropes, townspeople and friars watching from the bank near a whitewashed monastery on a hill. Painted as a sixteenth-century Spanish oil painting with fine detail, warm morning light, calm water.
eu-1492-fall-of-granada: January 1492, Granada: before the red walls and towers of the Alhambra on its hill, with snowy Sierra Nevada behind, a Nasrid ruler on horseback with a small retinue in turbans and robes rides out to hand over the city keys to the Castilian king and queen, small figures among a host of knights, banners and lances. Rendered in the style of a sixteenth-century Spanish choir-stall carving and history painting, warm earth tones.
eu-1497-vasco-da-gama: July 1497, Belém on the Tagus near Lisbon: four Portuguese ships, carracks and a caravel with crosses of the Order of Christ on their sails, prepare to depart while sailors in doublets and caps row out in boats, monks and families wave from a sandy shore beside a small chapel. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Portuguese illuminated armada book, ships drawn in fine ink with watercolour, pale blue sea with wave patterns.
eu-1508-sistine-chapel-ceiling: c. 1510, the Sistine Chapel in Rome: a tall wooden scaffold rises under the great barrel vault; small painters in smocks reach up to brush fresco onto fresh plaster, buckets of pigment and rolled paper on the planks; part of the vault already glows with bright painted architecture, sky-blue fields and draped robed figures, the rest still bare plaster; light falls from high windows. Painted as a Renaissance chalk and wash drawing with soft colour, all figures fully clothed.
eu-1517-ninety-five-theses: 1517, Wittenberg in Saxony: at the wooden door of the Gothic Castle Church, a small Augustinian friar in a black habit, seen from behind, fixes a large sheet of parchment with a hammer, while townspeople in late-medieval caps and cloaks pause in the cobbled square, autumn trees and the steep roofs of the town behind. Rendered as a sixteenth-century German woodcut in the style of Lucas Cranach's workshop, hand-coloured.
eu-1534-english-reformation: 1534, Westminster in London: in a long Tudor hall with hammerbeam roof, lords in robes and clergy in black sit on benches while a clerk reads a parchment act, a small crowned king on a canopied throne at the far end, tapestries on the walls and leaded windows showing the Thames. Painted in the manner of a Tudor panel painting with fine detail, rich crimson, black and gold, flat Tudor perspective.
eu-1545-council-of-trent: 1545, the cathedral of Trento in the Alps: inside a vaulted Romanesque church, tiers of bishops in white mitres and red-robed cardinals sit in rows facing a presiding table, secretaries with books and quills in the centre, Alpine mountains visible through the open door. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Italian oil painting of a council, crowded but orderly figures, warm candlelit interior, deep reds and whites.
eu-1618-thirty-years-war: May 1618, Prague Castle: from a tall Renaissance window of the castle above the city, small figures of two officials in black are being thrown out by a crowd of angry Protestant noblemen in ruffs and cloaks; below a dungheap and moat, the red roofs and spires of Prague and the Vltava in the distance. Rendered as a seventeenth-century copperplate engraving in the style of Matthäus Merian, fine hatched lines, sepia tone.
eu-1648-peace-of-westphalia: 1648, the town hall of Münster in Westphalia: in a wood-panelled Gothic hall with chandeliers, a crowd of envoys in black doublets, white collars and broad hats stand around a table, raising right hands to swear an oath over signed treaty documents; windows show stepped gables of the town. Painted as a Dutch Golden Age oil painting in the manner of Gerard ter Borch, many small careful portraits, dark tones, warm light.
eu-1789-storming-of-the-bastille: 14 July 1789, Paris: the eight round stone towers of the Bastille fortress loom over a crowd of Parisians in tricorne hats, waistcoats and caps, armed with muskets and pikes, crossing a lowered drawbridge, cannon smoke drifting across the towers, guardsmen joining the crowd. Painted in the manner of an eighteenth-century French gouache, like the views of Jean-Pierre Houël, warm summer light, many small figures.
eu-1792-battle-of-valmy: September 1792, Valmy in Champagne: on a rolling wet plain, French revolutionary infantry in blue coats and bicorne hats stand in lines around a windmill on a ridge with tricolour flags, artillery firing through drifting smoke at distant lines of Prussian troops, grey autumn clouds. Painted in the style of a late eighteenth-century French battle oil painting by Horace Vernet, panoramic, muted greens and browns, small figures.
eu-1799-coup-of-18-brumaire: November 1799, the Orangery of the Château de Saint-Cloud: in a long hall with tall windows, deputies of the Council of Five Hundred in red togas and toques crowd and shout, while grenadiers in bearskins enter with bayonets and a small general in a dark coat stands amid the commotion. Rendered as an early nineteenth-century French history painting in oil, dramatic light, many figures, neoclassical interior.
eu-1805-battle-of-trafalgar: October 1805, off Cape Trafalgar: two lines of tall wooden ships of the line with three masts and many gun decks cut through a French and Spanish fleet, sails filled and billowing white smoke from broadsides, flags at the mastheads, the coast of Spain faint on the horizon under a stormy sky. Painted as an early nineteenth-century British marine oil painting in the manner of Nicholas Pocock, detailed rigging, grey-green sea.
eu-1805-battle-of-austerlitz: December 1805, near Austerlitz in Moravia: from a hill at dawn, French infantry columns in blue coats emerge from a winter fog and climb the Pratzen Heights, the sun breaking through, cavalry on the flanks and Allied armies in white and green coats on the slopes, a village and frozen ponds below. Painted as a Napoleonic French battle panorama in oil, in the manner of François Gérard, golden light, many small figures.
eu-1812-french-invasion-of-russia: Winter 1812, a road in Russia: a long column of exhausted soldiers of the Grande Armée in tattered greatcoats, shakos and blankets trudges across a snowy plain, abandoned wagons and cannon, horses struggling, birch forests and a grey sky, seen from a distance without gore. Painted in the manner of a nineteenth-century Russian oil painting by Illarion Pryanishnikov, cold whites and greys, subdued sombre light.
eu-1815-battle-of-waterloo: June 1815, near Waterloo in Belgium: across rolling wheat fields, squares of red-coated British infantry stand firm while French cuirassiers with gleaming breastplates ride around them, the walled farm of Hougoumont burning, cannon smoke over ridges, Prussian columns appearing on the horizon. Painted as a nineteenth-century British battle panorama in oil in the manner of William Sadler, warm evening light, many small figures.
eu-1848-revolutions-of-1848: February 1848, Paris: a narrow old street of tall plain stone houses with shutters, blocked by a barricade of paving stones, carts and furniture, workers in blouses and caps and students in top hats holding a tricolour flag, smoke in the air and onlookers on balconies. Rendered as a mid-nineteenth-century French lithograph in the manner of Honoré Daumier, black crayon texture, dramatic contrast.
eu-1861-italian-unification: 1861, Turin: in a grand Baroque palace hall, the Palazzo Carignano, deputies in black frock coats and top hats gather around a parliamentary chamber with tiers of seats, sunlight through tall windows, flags of the Italian tricolour, crowds outside in the arcaded square, a small figure of a king in uniform greeting them from afar. Painted as a nineteenth-century Italian oil painting of the Macchiaioli school, sunlit patches of colour.
eu-1871-german-unification: January 1871, the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles: in the long gilded gallery lined with mirrors and chandeliers, crowds of German officers in dark blue uniforms with spiked helmets raise swords in salute toward a raised platform where a small elderly sovereign stands with princes, regimental flags held aloft. Painted in the style of a late nineteenth-century German academic history painting in oil, cool winter light reflecting on gold.
eu-1914-sarajevo-assassination: June 1914, Sarajevo: a sunny riverside street along the Miljacka with an old stone bridge, minarets and Austro-Hungarian buildings; an open touring motorcar with officials in plumed hats has stopped by the corner while crowds in fezzes and summer hats watch from the pavement, a sudden stir among them, seen from a distance. Painted as an early twentieth-century illustrated newspaper drawing, halftone texture, muted colour, no gore.
eu-1917-october-revolution: October 1917, Palace Square in Petrograd: at night, armed Red Guards in caps and greatcoats and sailors with rifles gather beneath the green-and-white Baroque façade of the Winter Palace, searchlights cutting the dark, the Alexander Column in the square, armoured cars and small fires. Painted as an early twentieth-century Russian watercolour sketch, loose washes of dark blue and amber, documentary and neutral, no banners or text.
eu-1919-treaty-of-versailles: June 1919, the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles: a long table in the gilded gallery where diplomats in dark morning coats sit and stand, one delegation leaning to sign documents, crowds of officers and journalists packed behind, sunlight through tall windows reflecting in mirrors and chandeliers. Painted as an early twentieth-century British oil painting in the manner of William Orpen, pale golden light, small figures under a vast ceiling.
eu-1939-invasion-of-poland: 1 September 1939, Westerplatte on the Baltic near Gdańsk: at dawn an old grey battleship with tall funnels fires from the harbour canal at a small wooded peninsula with low concrete barracks and a guardhouse, smoke rising through pine trees, the cranes of the port beyond. Painted as a mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, sombre grey and green washes, quiet distance, no figures in detail.
eu-1942-battle-of-stalingrad: Winter 1942–43, Stalingrad on the Volga: a ruined industrial city of broken brick factories and shattered apartment blocks under snow, smoke columns rising, small figures of soldiers in winter coats moving among the rubble, the frozen Volga beyond, seen from far away. Painted as a mid-twentieth-century Soviet documentary woodcut and watercolour, restrained greys and browns, solemn and neutral, no gore.
eu-1944-normandy-landings: 6 June 1944, Omaha Beach in Normandy: from the sea, flat-bottomed landing craft open their ramps on a wide grey beach below green bluffs, small soldiers in helmets wading ashore past steel obstacles, battleships and barrage balloons on the horizon under low clouds, smoke drifting. Painted as a 1940s war artist's documentary watercolour, muted blue-grey palette, loose wash, distant figures only.
eu-1945-battle-of-berlin: May 1945, Berlin: a devastated city centre of ruined stone buildings and the damaged Reichstag with its skeletal dome, smoke drifting over rubble-strewn streets, tanks and small groups of Soviet soldiers in the distance, civilians clearing bricks; quiet after the fighting. Painted as a mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour by a war artist, grey and ochre washes, solemn, no flags or text.
eu-1961-berlin-wall-built: August 1961, Berlin: a quiet street of nineteenth-century apartment blocks cut by a new barrier of concrete blocks and barbed wire, workmen laying bricks under guard, a few people looking across from windows and from the other side, a watchtower and a cobbled road ending at the wall. Painted as a mid-century documentary gouache illustration, muted greys and greens, overcast summer light, small distant figures.
eu-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall: November 1989, the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin: at night the neoclassical gate with its chariot sculpture is lit by floodlights, while a large crowd stands on and around a graffiti-free section of the concrete wall in front, some chipping at it with hammers, others climbing, figures small and seen from a distance. Painted as a documentary watercolour, cool night blues with warm lamplight, loose brushwork.
eu-1992-maastricht-treaty: February 1992, Maastricht in the Netherlands: a modern conference hall near the river Maas, where a long table with blue cloth holds open treaty folders and pens, chairs pushed back, small figures of delegates gathering at the far end, windows showing the old brick town and a bridge. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, cool blues and greys, soft daylight, no faces in detail and no legible text.
ir-proto-elamite-script: c. 3000 BCE, Susa in Khuzestan: in a mud-brick storeroom, scribes in simple wrapped garments sit on reed mats pressing a reed stylus into small rectangular clay tablets, baskets of grain and sealed jars nearby, cylinder seals rolled on clay, the low acropolis mound and palm groves outside. Rendered in the style of an ancient Near Eastern painted pottery and cylinder-seal frieze, flat silhouettes, ochre, black and cream, no legible signs.
ir-shahr-e-sukhteh: c. 3000 BCE, Shahr-e Sukhteh in the Sistan plain: a sprawling Bronze Age town of mud-brick houses on a terrace beside a marshy delta, craftsmen working lapis lazuli, carnelian beads and painted pottery, donkeys laden with goods arriving from the east, reed boats on the lake and flat desert horizon. Painted in the style of Bronze Age Iranian painted ceramics, with friezes of figures and animals, black on buff, simple geometric borders.
ir-jiroft-culture: c. 2500 BCE, the Halil River valley at Jiroft: craftsmen in a riverside workshop carve dark green chlorite vessels with designs of serpents, scorpion-men and palms, finished pots inlaid with coloured stones arranged on mats, a caravan of donkeys being loaded for Mesopotamia, date palms and mountains behind. Rendered in the style of a carved Jiroft chlorite vessel relief itself, dark green stone, inlaid turquoise and carnelian highlights.
ir-akkad-conquers-elam: c. 2300 BCE, before Susa: Akkadian soldiers with spears, axes and helmets advance in a disciplined column toward the walled mud-brick city of Susa on its mound, a commander leading on foot, Elamite captives with hands bound walking in a line, a palm-lined river beside. Rendered in the style of an Akkadian victory stele relief, carved in pinkish limestone, figures in profile, sharply defined musculature.
ir-puzur-inshushinak: c. 2100 BCE, Susa: in a temple courtyard of mud brick, stone carvers erect a tall limestone stele and a statue of a seated goddess, while a king in a fringed robe and round cap watches from a distance with attendants, lions carved on the stone base, offerings of goats and grain. Rendered in the style of an Elamite stone relief and bitumen-mastic carving, soft grey-brown stone tones, lines of figures in profile, no legible script.
ir-chogha-zanbil: c. 1250 BCE, Chogha Zanbil near Susa: a massive stepped ziggurat of fired and mud brick rises in tiers within walled courts, glazed blue tiles and gilded doors gleaming, priests in fringed robes climbing processional stairways, workers in the foreground stamping bricks in the plain beside a river, heat haze over the Khuzestan lowland. Painted in the manner of an ancient Near Eastern glazed brick panel, blue, gold and ochre.
ir-zoroaster: c. 1200 BCE, an oasis in Bactria: in a village of mud and timber houses below snowy mountains, a small robed priest seen from behind tends a fire on a stone altar while herdsmen and families in wool garments sit around listening, cattle grazing by irrigation channels, dawn light. Rendered in the style of a Sasanian silver plate engraving, chased silver with gilded highlights, figures in profile, circular composition.
ir-shutruk-nakhunte-babylon: c. 1158 BCE, Babylon: Elamite soldiers in fringed tunics haul a tall dark basalt stele and other carved monuments onto ox-drawn sledges outside a ziggurat city of mud brick, palms and the Euphrates nearby, a king in a high cap watching from a chariot, captive Babylonians standing aside. Rendered in the style of an Elamite stone relief, carved figures in profile, warm brown stone with low raking light, no legible inscriptions.
ir-median-kingdom: c. 700 BCE, Ecbatana at the foot of Mount Alvand: a hill city ringed by seven concentric walls rising in tiers, each battlement painted a different colour from white to gold, Median horsemen in felt hoods and trousers riding up a road with tribal elders, flocks on the plains and snowy peaks behind. Painted in the style of an Achaemenid glazed brick relief, coloured tiles, stylised processional figures.
ir-ashurbanipal-sacks-susa: 647 BCE, Susa: an Assyrian army with conical helmets, bows and siege ladders storms the walls of Susa, flames rising from temple towers, soldiers carrying off statues and treasure in a long procession, captives leading cattle across a river in the foreground. Rendered in the style of an Assyrian palace relief from Nineveh, carved gypsum in low relief, registers of small figures in profile, pale stone tones.
ir-battle-of-the-eclipse: 585 BCE, the Halys River in Anatolia: two armies of Median horsemen in felt caps and Lydian hoplite-style infantry with round shields stand on a plain under a sudden darkened sky with a blackened sun ringed by light; soldiers lower weapons and look up in awe, the river winding below. Painted in the style of a sixth-century BCE Lydian or East Greek painted pottery frieze, black figure on orange, with an engraved sun disc.
ir-cyrus-founds-empire: c. 550 BCE, Pasargadae in Fars: on a broad plain with mountains behind, stone palaces with columns and gardens laid out with water channels, Persian nobles in long robes and Median riders gather around a small figure in a tall crown on horseback, banners with eagle emblems, cypress trees. Painted in the manner of an Achaemenid relief rendered in colour, processional figures in profile, ochre, lapis blue and gold.
ir-behistun-inscription: c. 520 BCE, the cliff at Behistun on the road to Ecbatana: high on a sheer limestone rock face, tiny workers on scaffolding carve a great relief panel of a king with captives in a row beneath a winged disc, with blocks of chiselled script beside it shown as blank textured panels, caravans passing on the road below near a spring. Painted as a nineteenth-century traveller's engraving with watercolour, dramatic scale, no legible writing.
ir-persepolis-founded: c. 518 BCE, Persepolis on the Marvdasht plain: on a vast stone terrace against a rocky mountain, workers raise tall fluted columns with double-bull capitals, while processions of delegates in different national dress carry tribute — horses, vases, textiles — up wide staircases. Rendered in the style of the Apadana staircase relief at Persepolis, carved grey limestone, long processional registers of small figures in profile, cypress trees between them.
ir-royal-road: c. 500 BCE, the Persian Royal Road: a mounted courier on a fast horse gallops along a dusty road through rolling hills toward a mud-brick relay station with a fresh horse waiting, attendants in Persian dress handing over a sealed message, a caravan of camels on the road behind and a distant river crossing. Painted in the style of an Achaemenid relief and Persepolis Fortification seal impression, profile figures, ochre and stone tones.
ir-xerxes-invades-greece: 480 BCE, the straits of Salamis off Attica: in a narrow channel between rocky islands, hundreds of oared triremes with bronze rams crowd and collide, Greek ships with painted eyes on their prows driving into the Persian fleet, a royal canopy and throne on a hill above the shore, smoke rising from Athens on the horizon. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, black ground with terracotta figures, fine line detail.
ir-persepolis-burned: 330 BCE, Persepolis: at night the great columned halls of the palace terrace burn, flames and smoke rising above stone gateways with winged bulls, Macedonian soldiers with crested helmets and sarissas carrying off treasure chests on mules down the staircase, the dark mountain behind. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii in the manner of the Alexander Mosaic palette, earthy reds, ochres and blacks, distant view.
ir-ai-khanoum: c. 280 BCE, Ai-Khanoum at the meeting of the Oxus and Kokcha rivers: a Greek city with a hillside stone theatre, a colonnaded gymnasium and a Corinthian-columned palace court stands beneath a fortified acropolis, Greek settlers in chitons and local Bactrians in trousers mingle in the street, irrigated fields and steppe hills beyond. Painted in the manner of a Hellenistic wall painting, soft fresco colours, warm afternoon light.
ir-greco-bactrian: c. 250 BCE, Bactra in the Oxus plain: within massive mud-brick city walls, a Greek-style ruler on horseback wearing a kausia hat and diadem rides out from a gateway with cavalry in Hellenistic helmets, while Bactrian farmers with camels and horses line the road, orchards and snow-capped Hindu Kush behind. Rendered in the style of a Greco-Bactrian silver coin relief enlarged into a frieze, chased silver with gilt highlights.
ir-arsaces-founds-parthia: c. 247 BCE, Nisa at the foot of the Kopet Dag: Parni horsemen in soft caps, trousers and long tunics ride across a grassy steppe toward a fortified mud-brick citadel, mounted archers turning in the saddle to shoot, herds of horses, and a chieftain seen from behind leading the band under a pale sky. Painted in the style of a Parthian wall painting and ivory rhyton carving, warm ochres and reds, profile figures.
ir-mithridates-i-mesopotamia: 141 BCE, Seleucia on the Tigris: Parthian cavalry, armoured cataphracts on armoured horses and mounted archers, ride through the gates of a great Hellenistic city of colonnades and temples beside the river, Greek citizens in himations watching from rooftops, boats on the Tigris and palm groves. Painted in the manner of a Hellenistic-Parthian wall painting from Dura-Europos, frontal figures, earthy reds, ochres and blues.
ir-han-envoys-anxi: c. 115 BCE, near Hecatompylos in Parthia: on a broad plain a small group of Han Chinese envoys in long robes and black caps, holding a yak-tail staff of office and with laden camels and horses, is met by a huge host of Parthian horsemen in caps and trousers stretching to the horizon; an officer offers ostrich eggs in a basket. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, lively brush outlines, red and black on pale plaster.
ir-kushan-empire: c. 30 CE, Bactria: Yuezhi chiefs in long belted coats, trousers and boots gather on horseback in a valley below snowy mountains, five tribal banners held aloft, a leader seen from behind receiving their pledges before a felt tent and a mud-brick fort, camels and grazing horses around. Rendered in the style of a Gandhara schist relief, grey stone, carved figures in Hellenistic-Indian manner, arched frame.
ir-ardashir-founds-sasanian: 224 CE, the plain of Hormozdgan: two armies of armoured horsemen clash on open ground, knights in mail with long lances and streaming ribbons, horses with caparisons, one rider unseating another; in the distance the round walled city of Gor at Firuzabad. Rendered in the style of the Sasanian rock relief at Firuzabad, carved in the cliff face, dynamic jousting figures in profile, warm sandstone tones.
ir-khosrow-i-reforms: c. 540 CE, Ctesiphon on the Tigris: before the vast brick arch of the Taq Kasra palace hall, scribes in tall caps sit at low tables measuring fields and recording grain with surveyors, while armoured cavalry parade under four standards and a king in a winged crown sits far off on a throne. Painted in the manner of Sasanian silver plate engraving and gilt reliefs, ochre, gold and deep blue.
ir-battle-of-nahavand: 642 CE, the valley of Nahavand in the Zagros: on a broad plain between mountains, a Sasanian army with armoured cavalry, war elephants and banners faces lines of Arab horsemen and infantry with lances and round shields, mountains and a walled town behind, dust clouds rising, seen from far away. Painted in the style of a later Persian miniature from a Tabari manuscript, flat bright colours, golden sky, small figures.
ir-yazdegerd-iii-killed: 651 CE, near Merv in Khorasan: a lone, weary royal fugitive in rich robes, seen from behind, rests beside a small water mill on a river in a quiet landscape of poplars and reed beds at dusk, his horse tethered, the walls of the oasis city of Merv far away. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature from a Shahnameh manuscript, delicate colours, lapis and gold, stylised trees and rocks.
ir-abbasid-revolution: 747 CE, outside Merv in Khorasan: a great gathering of Persian and Arab soldiers on horseback and foot, all dressed in black and carrying black banners, assembles on the plain outside a mud-brick walled oasis city, campfires smoking at dusk, camels and tents. Painted in the style of a fourteenth-century Persian manuscript miniature from Bal'ami's Tarikh, flat composition, black and red against a gold background, no faces in detail.
ir-babak-revolt: c. 830 CE, Babak Fort in the mountains of Azerbaijan: a stone fortress perched high on a sheer rocky crag above forested gorges, rebels in red clothing guarding narrow paths, a distant Abbasid army camped on the valley floor with tents and banners, mist drifting around the peaks. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, stylised rocky mountains in pink and purple, gold sky, small figures.
ir-saffarids: c. 861 CE, Zaranj in Sistan: in a dusty mud-brick town by the Helmand river, a coppersmith's workshop with hammered pots gives way to a crowd of armed volunteers on horseback gathering behind a leader in plain dress, seen from behind, banners raised, windmills on the flat horizon. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature from a later historical manuscript, flat bright colours, gold and lapis, decorative borders.
ir-al-razi: c. 900 CE, Rey near Tehran: in a hospital courtyard with arched brick galleries and a fountain, a physician in a turban and robe examines a patient on a mat while assistants prepare medicines with mortars and glass flasks, students taking notes on manuscripts, other patients resting under arcades. Painted in the style of a thirteenth-century Arabic manuscript illustration like the Maqamat of al-Hariri, flat colours, gold ground.
ir-shahnameh: c. 1010, Tus in Khorasan: in a garden pavilion under a plane tree, an elderly poet in a turban, seen from behind, writes on a long manuscript scroll by lamplight, stacks of books beside him, while miniature visions of armoured heroes, a white horse and a simurgh float in the night sky above. Painted in the style of a Safavid Persian miniature from the Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, jewel colours, gold, intricate detail.
ir-canon-of-medicine: 1025, Hamadan: in a lamp-lit study of a brick house, a scholar in a turban writes in a thick bound codex at a low desk, surrounded by shelves of books, a brass astrolabe, herbs, glass flasks and anatomical diagrams shown as unreadable sketches, students listening seated on carpets. Painted in the style of a Persian manuscript miniature of the Timurid period, gold, lapis and vermilion, patterned tiles.
ir-battle-of-dandanaqan: 1040, the desert near Merv: on a dry plain with a ruined caravanserai, Seljuk Turkic horse archers in fur caps and quilted coats swirl around a Ghaznavid army of armoured cavalry and war elephants, dust and heat haze, the Ghaznavid lines breaking far away. Painted in the style of a fourteenth-century Persian miniature from the Jami al-Tawarikh, Mongol-period, ink outlines with red and blue washes, sparse background.
ir-nizam-al-mulk: c. 1067, a Nizamiyya college: in a courtyard surrounded by brick iwans with turquoise tile decoration, students in turbans sit in circles around teachers reading from books, a fountain in the centre, scribes copying manuscripts in an arcade, an elderly vizier in rich robes visiting with attendants. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature of the Herat school, bright mineral colours, gold, geometric tilework.
ir-rubaiyat: c. 1100, a garden outside Nishapur: under blossoming fruit trees by a stream, a scholar-poet in a turban sits on a rug with a book of verses, a jug and a cup beside him, a companion playing a lute and an astrolabe leaning on a cushion, the evening moon above distant domes. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Safavid style, delicate lines, rose, gold and turquoise, flowering border.
ir-mongols-nishapur: 1221, Nishapur in Khorasan: seen from a hill, Mongol horsemen with horse-tail standards encircle a large walled city, catapults ranged against its walls, smoke rising above domes and minarets, refugees and carts on the road below; distant, no gore. Painted in the style of a fourteenth-century Ilkhanid miniature from the Jami al-Tawarikh, ink line with sparse washes, Chinese-influenced clouds and mountains.
ir-hulagu-ilkhanate: 1256, the Alborz mountains: the castle of Alamut stands on a sheer rock pinnacle above a deep valley, while a great Mongol army with felt tents, mangonels and horse-tail standards camps below, Ismaili envoys descending a mountain path toward the camp. Painted in the style of an Ilkhanid Persian miniature from the Jami al-Tawarikh, Chinese-style mountains in ink, red and blue garments, gold highlights.
ir-maragheh-observatory: 1259, Maragheh on a hilltop in Azerbaijan: astronomers in turbans work in an observatory complex with a great stone meridian arc, brass armillary spheres, quadrants and a library, one scholar taking readings while others record tables; the town and plains below at twilight with stars appearing. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Ottoman miniature of an observatory, flat bright colours, many instruments, gold sky.
ir-ghazan-converts: 1295, Tabriz: a Mongol khan in a broad hat and robe, seen from behind and small, stands among Mongol nobles and Persian scholars in turbans in a tiled courtyard of a new mosque, crowds gathered in rows, Mongol tents and horses outside the walls of the city. Painted in the style of an Ilkhanid miniature from Rashid al-Din's Jami al-Tawarikh, red and blue tones on paper, Chinese-influenced clouds, no religious figures depicted.
ir-abu-said-death: 1335, Soltaniyeh: the great turquoise-domed mausoleum of Öljaitü rises over a royal city of tents and brick palaces, while Mongol nobles in mourning dress gather in the plain and different factions ride off in separate directions under rival banners, dust trailing behind them. Painted in the style of an Ilkhanid-Jalayirid Persian miniature, delicate lines, lapis blue domes, gold sky, stylised mountains.
ir-hafez: c. 1360, a garden in Shiraz: beside a stream among cypress trees, roses and a pavilion, a poet in a turban sits with friends on a carpet, one playing a lute and another holding a book of verses, wine cups and fruit on a cloth, nightingales in the trees and the city's domes beyond. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature of the Shiraz school, rich gold, rose and turquoise, flowering border.
ir-timur-herat: 1381, Herat in the valley of the Hari River: a Timurid army with banners, armoured horsemen and siege engines camps before the walls and citadel of Herat, envoys carrying gifts walking out to the conqueror's camp, the domes of the city and mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Timurid miniature from the Zafarnama, bright colours, gold sky, many small figures, stylised rocks.
ir-shah-rukh-herat: c. 1417, Herat: builders lay glazed turquoise and blue tiles on the domes and minarets of a new mosque and madrasa complex, while scholars in turbans walk in shaded courtyards and calligraphers sit copying manuscripts, a royal couple seen far off in a garden pavilion. Painted in the style of a Herat-school Timurid miniature, crisp line, lapis and gold, geometric tilework details.
ir-behzad-herat: c. 1488, the court workshop of Herat: in a garden pavilion with tiled walls, painters in turbans sit on carpets painting miniatures with fine brushes, grinding pigments in shells, a calligrapher and bookbinder working beside them, a sultan seen in the distance admiring a finished page. Painted in the style of the Herat school itself, Behzad's manner, vivid jewel colours, lively figures, geometric architecture.
ir-ismail-founds-safavid: 1501, Tabriz: a young ruler in a turban wound around a tall red cap, seen small among his followers, rides into the city as a Safavid army of Qizilbash warriors wearing red twelve-gored turbans fills the square, banners raised, the brick Blue Mosque and bazaar domes around, crowds on rooftops. Painted in the style of an early Safavid Persian miniature, intense colours, gold, decorative tiles, many small figures.
ir-battle-of-chaldiran: 1514, the plain of Chaldiran: Ottoman cannon chained together in a line behind wagons fire through clouds of smoke while Janissaries with muskets stand behind them, and Safavid Qizilbash cavalry in red turbans charge toward the guns, mountains around the plain. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Ottoman miniature from the Selimname, flat bright colours, gold sky, small figures in neat rows.
ir-abbas-isfahan: c. 1610, Isfahan: the vast rectangular Naqsh-e Jahan Square lined with two-storey arcades, the turquoise domes of the Shah Mosque and the Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, the Ali Qapu palace with its columned balcony, polo players on horseback in the square and merchants in the bazaar around it. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century Persian miniature of the Isfahan school, Reza Abbasi manner, gold and soft colours.
ir-new-julfa: c. 1610, New Julfa on the Zayandeh River in Isfahan: Armenian families in traditional dress arrive with mules and carts and build brick houses and a domed church with a bell tower, merchants unloading bales of raw silk, the Safavid bridge Si-o-se-pol arching over the river. Painted in the style of an Armenian manuscript illumination mixed with Persian miniature colours, fine line, red, gold and blue.
ir-capture-of-hormuz: 1622, Hormuz Island in the Persian Gulf: English East India Company galleons fire broadsides at a Portuguese stone fortress on a rocky red island, while Persian soldiers in turbans land from rowing boats with ladders and besiege the walls, smoke drifting over turquoise water, the barren mainland coast and the small port that became Bandar Abbas far off. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch-style marine engraving, hand-coloured, detailed ships and rigging.
ir-treaty-of-zuhab: 1639, Qasr-e Shirin in the Zagros foothills: in a camp of rich Ottoman and Safavid tents, envoys in Ottoman kaftans and turbans and Persian robes sit on carpets exchanging sealed documents, horses and guards around, ruined Sasanian arches of Qasr-e Shirin in the background. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century Ottoman miniature, flat perspective, bright reds and greens, gold sky, no legible writing.
ir-fall-of-isfahan: 1722, the plain of Gulnabad near Isfahan: a compact force of Afghan tribal horsemen in turbans and loose robes charges a much larger Safavid army arrayed with war elephants, bronze cannon, armoured cavalry and gilded banners, the domes and minarets of Isfahan on the horizon, dust clouds and a pale winter sky. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Persian miniature, flat bright colours, gold sky, small figures in rows.
ir-nader-shah-crowned: 1736, the Mughan plain: an enormous tent camp spreads across a wide steppe beside rivers, tens of thousands of soldiers, nobles and clerics gathered around a vast royal pavilion, a small figure of a general in a jewelled turban seated within, horses and camels everywhere. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Persian lacquer painting, rich reds and golds, fine detail, flat perspective.
ir-karim-khan-zand: c. 1765, Shiraz: the brick citadel of Karim Khan with round corner towers stands beside a new bazaar with vaulted halls and a garden with tall cypresses, merchants, craftsmen and townspeople at work, a ruler on a carpet in a garden pavilion seen far off. Painted as an eighteenth-century Zand-period Persian oil painting, warm reds, browns and gold, decorative flowers.
ir-qajar-dynasty: 1796, Tehran: in a palace courtyard with a long pool and plane trees, a Qajar court of nobles in long robes and tall black lambskin hats stands in rows before a throne hall with mirrored columns, a small figure seated on a jewelled throne under a canopy, the Alborz mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Qajar court oil painting, rich red, gold and black, flat stylised figures.
ir-treaty-of-turkmenchay: February 1828, the village of Turkmenchay in Azerbaijan: inside a heated village house, Russian officers in green uniforms with epaulettes and Persian envoys in long robes and tall black lambskin hats sit at a table spread with treaty documents and sealing wax, snow-covered flat roofs outside, Cossacks and horses waiting in the cold. Painted as a nineteenth-century Russian lithograph with watercolour, fine detail, cool winter tones, no legible writing.
ir-tobacco-protest: 1891, Tehran: in a bazaar lane under brick vaults lit by skylights, tobacco sellers' shops stand shuttered, men in robes and turbans or felt caps set aside their water pipes and pile them unused in a corner, women in chadors walk past, a quiet, determined crowd in a city where no one is smoking. Painted as a late nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light watercolour, fine hatching, warm brown and grey tones.
ir-constitutional-revolution: Summer 1906, Tehran: thousands of merchants, clerics and townspeople in robes, turbans and felt hats camp in the walled gardens of the British legation, rows of white tents under tall plane trees, people reading pamphlets, cooking in large pots and talking in groups, the city domes and Alborz mountains in the distance. Painted as an early twentieth-century Persian watercolour sketch, soft washes of green and ochre, calm documentary mood.
ir-oil-discovered: May 1908, Masjed Soleyman in the Zagros foothills: a tall wooden derrick stands on a barren rocky hillside, a jet of dark oil gushing up from it, European drillers in shirtsleeves and Persian workers in felt caps running toward it, steam boilers, mules and tents around, Bakhtiari tribesmen watching from a ridge in dawn light. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, ochre and grey washes, wide landscape.
ir-reza-shah: 1926, Golestan Palace in Tehran: in a mirrored hall with columns and painted tiles, an army officer in a caped military uniform stands small and seen from behind before the Peacock Throne, surrounded by officials in frock coats and Pahlavi caps, soldiers outside in the courtyard. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, muted gold and green, careful architectural detail, figures small.
ir-anglo-soviet-invasion: 1941, the road into Tehran: British and Soviet military trucks and armoured cars roll along a dusty road past poplar trees and mud-brick villages, soldiers in different uniforms waving to each other, the Alborz mountains in the distance and a railway line with a supply train. Painted as a 1940s war artist's watercolour sketch, loose washes of ochre and green, documentary and neutral.
ir-1953-coup: August 1953, central Tehran: a wide avenue lined with plane trees and 1950s low-rise buildings, where tanks stand at a crossroads and crowds gather at a distance, smoke rising from a building on the next street, people watching from balconies and rooftops, the Alborz mountains hazy behind. Painted as a muted 1950s documentary gouache illustration, grey and ochre tones, small figures, neutral and calm, no signs or text.
ir-white-revolution: 1963, a village near Tehran: farmers in felt caps and women in floral scarves gather in a dusty square where officials in suits hand out land deeds at a table, while elsewhere a schoolroom with young literacy teachers in uniforms teaching villagers is seen through a window; mud-brick houses and mountains behind. Painted as a 1960s documentary gouache illustration, warm muted colours, no legible text.
ir-iranian-revolution: Early 1979, Tehran: the white arched Azadi Tower stands over a vast avenue filled with a huge crowd seen from far above, small figures stretching to the horizon, men and women in winter coats and chadors, the snow-topped Alborz mountains under a pale winter sky. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft grey and blue washes, distant and calm, no banners, faces or text.
ir-mahsa-amini-protests: Autumn 2022, Tehran: a calm evening view of the city under the Alborz mountains, the Milad Tower on the skyline, streetlights coming on along a tree-lined avenue, small groups of people far away gathered on a pavement, an empty headscarf lying on a bench in the foreground. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool blue and amber tones, quiet and neutral, no faces or text.
jp-sannai-maruyama: c. 3000 BCE, Sannai-Maruyama in northern Honshu: a large Jōmon village of thatched pit dwellings and a long communal hall, a tall structure of six massive chestnut pillars rising above, people in woven bark clothing carrying baskets of chestnuts, cord-marked pots drying, groves of chestnut trees and forested hills. Painted as a quiet documentary watercolour reconstruction in earth tones, inspired by Jōmon pottery textures.
jp-oyu-stone-circles: c. 2000 BCE, Ōyu in Akita: on a grassy terrace among forested mountains, Jōmon people in bark-cloth garments lay out river stones in two great rings, with a standing stone surrounded by radiating stones like a sundial at the centre of each, a ceremony at sunset with fires and clay figurines. Painted as a documentary watercolour reconstruction, soft greens and golds, inspired by Jōmon earthenware.
jp-rice-reaches-kyushu: c. 500 BCE, Itazuke in northern Kyushu: newly dug paddy fields with irrigation channels and wooden weirs beside a river plain, farmers in simple hemp clothes planting rice seedlings with wooden hoes, a small moated village of thatched houses and raised granaries, a boat arriving from the sea. Painted as a watercolour in the style of Yamato-e earth palette, soft green and ochre washes.
jp-yoshinogari: c. 300 BCE, Yoshinogari in Saga: a large Yayoi settlement enclosed by deep V-shaped ditches and wooden palisades, tall timber watchtowers at the corners, thatched pit dwellings and raised-floor storehouses inside, warriors with wooden shields and bronze spears guarding the gate, villagers carrying rice, paddies spreading across the plain to the hills. Painted as a documentary watercolour reconstruction, warm earth tones, soft light.
jp-dotaku: c. 100 BCE, Kamo Iwakura in Shimane: on a forested hillside, Yayoi villagers in hemp garments bury dozens of tall bronze bells with decorative bands in a pit, a ritual specialist holding one bell aloft, rice fields and thatched houses below. Painted in a style inspired by the line drawings cast on dōtaku bells, simple stick figures, deer and herons, bronze-green and ochre palette.
jp-wa-great-disturbance: c. 180 CE, Makimuku in Nara: a fortified compound of raised timber buildings with thatched roofs surrounded by wooden palisades, moats and watchtowers, chiefs and warriors on foot from many Wa states gathering at the gate with wooden shields, bows and iron-tipped spears, wearing simple hemp tunics, some carrying jars of rice offerings; a secluded palace in the centre where a shaman queen lives unseen, mist over the Yamato hills. No horses, no saddles. Painted in the style of a Kofun-era wall painting, red, white and black pigments, simple flat figures, no text.
jp-hashihaka-kofun: c. 250 CE, Makimuku in Nara: workers carry baskets of earth and stones to build a giant keyhole-shaped burial mound, its terraces faced with river stones and lined with cylindrical clay haniwa, a moat being dug around it, the green Miwa mountain behind. Painted as a watercolour in the style of Japanese archaeological reconstruction illustration, soft earth and green tones, many tiny figures.
jp-wani-books: c. 405, Yamato: a scholar from Baekje in a long robe and cap arrives at a timber palace with thatched roofs, presenting bamboo-slip and scroll books to the Yamato court, courtiers in Kofun-period dress with beaded necklaces watching, a boat on a river behind. Painted in the style of a Heian-period Yamato-e handscroll, flat colours, gold clouds, delicate line, figures small.
jp-daisen-kofun: c. 450, Sakai near Osaka Bay: an immense keyhole-shaped tomb mound with three tiers, surrounded by triple moats, rises from a plain, thousands of labourers with baskets and wooden sledges hauling earth and stones, rows of haniwa figures being placed on terraces, the sea beyond. Painted as a watercolour reconstruction, aerial view, soft earth tones and blue water, tiny figures.
jp-iwai-rebellion: 527, northern Kyushu: an army of warriors in iron armour plates and helmets with spears and bows faces Yamato troops on a plain, a large burial mound with stone figures of men and horses on a hill behind, smoke rising from a burning village, seen at a distance. Painted in the style of a decorated Kofun tomb mural from Kyushu, red, black and white geometric patterns and simplified figures.
jp-buddhism-arrives: 538, Asuka: Korean envoys from Baekje in long robes present a gilt bronze Buddha image and sutra scrolls in lacquered boxes to the Yamato court gathered in a timber hall with thatched roof, courtiers in Kofun-period dress bowing or frowning, a boat on the river behind. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period emakimono handscroll illustrating temple history, flat mineral colours, gold clouds.
jp-soga-mononobe: 587, Mount Shigi near Nara: two armies of Kofun-period warriors in iron plate armour with bows and swords clash in a forest of tall cryptomeria trees, one side's chief shooting from a tree, a young prince with a small figure of a Buddhist guardian carved from wood seen at the back. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period illustrated handscroll of Shōtoku's life, flat colours, gold clouds, small figures.
jp-seventeen-article: 604, Oharida Palace in Asuka: in a timber hall with thatched roof and red pillars, officials in caps of rank in different colours and long robes sit in rows on mats listening to a reading from a scroll, a young prince in white seated on a dais in the distance, a garden with a pond outside. Painted as a Yamato-e handscroll, flat mineral colours, gold clouds, delicate line.
jp-horyu-ji: 607, Ikaruga in Nara: carpenters in hemp clothing raise the five-storey wooden pagoda and Golden Hall of a temple with sweeping tiled roofs, red pillars and white walls, monks in robes carrying sutras, cypress beams stacked nearby, a small prince and courtiers watching from afar, pine-clad hills behind. Painted in the style of a Heian-period Yamato-e handscroll, mineral colours of vermilion, green and gold, fine line, small figures.
jp-taika-reform: 645, Naniwa Palace near Osaka Bay: officials in Tang-style robes and caps sit at low tables writing household registers and land surveys on scrolls, while surveyors with measuring ropes mark rice fields outside the palace, thatched houses and a harbour with ships on the bay. Painted in the style of a Yamato-e handscroll, flat mineral colours, gold clouds, delicate line, no legible writing.
jp-jinshin-war: 672, Seta Bridge over the Seta River at Lake Biwa: two armies of warriors in iron armour face each other across a long wooden bridge, archers shooting from both banks, planks being pulled up in the middle, banners flying, hills and the lake under a summer sky. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period emakimono battle scroll, fine line and mineral colours, gold clouds, small figures.
jp-taiho-code: 701, Fujiwara-kyō: in a palace hall with red pillars and green-glazed tile roofs on a grid-planned capital, scholar-officials in Tang-style robes and black caps read and copy long scrolls of law, rows of clerks writing at low tables, the Yamato mountains seen beyond the walls. Painted in the style of a Nara-period Buddhist sutra illustration, flat bright colours, gold accents, no legible writing.
jp-heijo-kyo: 710, Heijō-kyō in Nara: a new capital laid out on a grid like Chang'an, with a wide avenue leading to a red-pillared palace gate with tiled roofs, officials in robes and caps, ox-carts and porters bringing goods, temples and pagodas rising among green hills. Painted in the style of a Nara-period Buddhist painting and Shōsōin treasures, rich vermilion, gold and green, aerial view, small figures.
jp-todai-ji-buddha: 752, Tōdai-ji in Nara: inside a vast wooden hall with huge pillars, a giant seated bronze Buddha glows with gold leaf while a crowd of monks in robes from Japan, China and India gather for the eye-opening ceremony, court nobles in robes and banners hanging; the Buddha shown from far below. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period temple-history handscroll, mineral colours, gold, fine line.
jp-heian-kyo: 794, Heian-kyō: a new capital laid out on a grid in a valley ringed by green mountains, a wide central avenue leading to the red Rashōmon gate, ox-carts and officials in robes and caps, workers building tiled-roof palaces and temples, the Kamo River glinting in the morning light. Painted in the style of a Heian-period Yamato-e handscroll, flat mineral colours, gold clouds, fukinuki-yatai perspective, small figures.
jp-tamuramaro: 802, Isawa in northern Honshu: on a river plain among forested hills, court soldiers in lamellar armour with bows build the earthen walls, wooden gate towers and palisade of a new frontier castle, while Emishi warriors in fur and bark-cloth garments, on horseback, arrive at a distance to surrender, a general on horseback seen from behind. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period illustrated handscroll, flat mineral colours, gold clouds, small figures.
jp-yoshifusa-regent: 866, Heian-kyō: at night the great Ōtenmon gate of the palace burns, red flames and smoke rising above its tiled roof while courtiers in black court caps and robes and guards with torches gather in the courtyard, ox-carts waiting, the dark palace halls behind. Painted in the style of the Ban Dainagon Emaki handscroll, flowing line, vivid flames, crowds of lively small figures, mineral colours on paper.
jp-end-tang-missions: 894, Heian-kyō: in a palace hall with raised wooden floors and bamboo blinds, a court scholar in black cap and robes kneels presenting a memorial scroll, while through the open side a large Japanese envoy ship with mat sails lies idle at a distant harbour on a painted screen, courtiers listening on mats. Painted in the style of the Kitano Tenjin Engi handscroll, flat colours, gold clouds, delicate line.
jp-kokin-wakashu: 905, Heian-kyō: in a palace room with sliding screens and bamboo blinds opening onto a garden of plum blossoms and a pond, court poets in black caps and layered robes sit on mats writing on fine coloured paper with brushes, scrolls spread out, one reading aloud. Painted in the style of a Heian-period Yamato-e handscroll, fukinuki-yatai roofless view, soft mineral colours, gold flecks, no legible writing.
jp-masakado: 939, the Bandō plain in eastern Japan: mounted warriors in early ō-yoroi armour with long bows ride across wide marshy grasslands and rice fields under Mount Tsukuba, a fortified manor with wooden walls burning in the distance, provincial officials fleeing on ox-carts. Painted in the style of a late Heian battle handscroll, lively ink line, mineral colours, gold clouds dividing scenes, small figures.
jp-tale-of-genji: c. 1008, Heian-kyō: in a palace chamber with sliding doors and bamboo blinds, a court lady in many-layered robes, seen from behind with long black hair spread on the floor, writes at a low lacquered desk by lamplight, other ladies-in-waiting asleep behind screens, an autumn garden with maple leaves under the moon. Painted in the style of the Tale of Genji Emaki handscroll, tsukuri-e opaque colours, fukinuki-yatai roofless view.
jp-byodo-in: 1053, Uji near Kyoto: the Phoenix Hall with its central hall and outstretched corridor wings, vermilion pillars and bronze phoenixes on the roof, reflected in a still lotus pond, a few courtiers in robes and caps crossing a bridge, a golden seated Amida Buddha glimpsed through the open doors. Painted in the style of a Heian Pure Land painting, gold and soft mineral colours, serene morning light.
jp-insei: 1086, Heian-kyō: a retired emperor in Buddhist monk's robes, seen from behind, sits in a palace pavilion hidden by blinds, while courtiers and samurai guards called the Northern Guards gather in a gravel courtyard, ox-carts arriving, the Imperial Palace roofs in the distance. Painted in the style of a late Heian Yamato-e handscroll, fine line, rich mineral colours, gold clouds.
jp-hogen: 1156, Heian-kyō at night: mounted warriors of the Taira and Minamoto in colourful ō-yoroi armour attack a palace compound, archers shooting, flames rising from the tiled roofs and wooden halls, courtiers in black caps fleeing in ox-carts, the dark sky lit orange. Painted in the style of the Heiji Monogatari Emaki handscroll, dynamic ink line, red flames, crowded small figures.
jp-kiyomori: 1167, the port of Ōwada at Fukuhara near Kobe: a large Song Chinese trading junk with battened sails unloads silk, porcelain and copper coins at a harbour, while a Heian court in black caps and robes and Taira samurai watch from a pavilion, a chancellor in monk's robes seen from behind among them. Painted in the style of a late Heian Yamato-e handscroll, gold clouds, fine line and mineral colours.
jp-genpei-war: 1180–1185, Japan: Minamoto warriors with white banners on horseback in ō-yoroi armour ride along a coastal cliff path while below, Taira warships with red banners sail across a strait, a burning wooden temple on a far hill, the sea and mountains under a stormy sky. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century Tale of the Heike folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bright mineral colours, small figures.
jp-dan-no-ura: 1185, the strait of Dan-no-ura: hundreds of wooden boats with red Taira and white Minamoto banners crowd the narrow sea, archers shooting from the decks, a court lady in layered robes on one boat holding a child wrapped in silk, the tide turning, green hills on both shores. Painted in the style of an Edo-period Tale of the Heike folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, brilliant colours, many small figures.
jp-yoritomo-shogun: 1192, Kamakura: a new warrior capital on the coast between wooded hills and the sea, with a broad avenue leading to the vermilion Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine, samurai on horseback and in armour gathering in the courtyard of a shogunal residence, a small figure seated in court robes under a canopy. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period illustrated handscroll, fine line, mineral colours, gold clouds.
jp-jokyu-war: 1221, the Uji River near Kyoto: Kamakura samurai on horseback ford a swift river in spring flood, horses swimming, archers shooting across, court troops on the far bank behind wooden shields, the bridge planks removed, Kyoto's hills in the background, spray rising in the cold morning air. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period battle handscroll, ink line with bright colours, gold clouds, many small figures.
jp-fall-of-kamakura: 1333, Kamakura: Nitta Yoshisada's warriors wade along the beach at Inamuragasaki at low tide past a rocky cape into the city, white banners flying, smoke rising from halls and temples in the valleys, Hōjō warriors defending the hills, the sea behind. Painted in the style of a Muromachi-period illustrated handscroll, ink and colour on paper, small figures, gold clouds, no gore.
jp-ashikaga-shogunate: 1338, Kyoto: in the courtyard of a shogunal residence, a warrior lord seen from behind in court robes and tall cap accepts an imperial appointment scroll from a court envoy, samurai in armour kneeling in rows, a Zen temple pagoda and Kyoto's hills behind. Painted in the style of a Muromachi-period ink and colour handscroll, soft washes, delicate line, small figures, gold clouds.
jp-onin-war: 1467, Kyoto: a burning city seen from a hill, smoke rising from temples and mansions, two armies of samurai and foot soldiers called ashigaru with long spears fighting in the streets under red and white banners, townspeople fleeing with bundles. Painted in the style of a Muromachi-period Rakuchū-rakugai folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bird's-eye view, many small figures, ink and colour.
jp-tanegashima: 1543, Tanegashima island off Kyushu: a Chinese junk with mat sails anchors in a sandy cove, Portuguese traders in doublets and hats demonstrate a matchlock gun to a local lord and his samurai, a puff of smoke, Japanese smiths watching closely, pine trees and the sea. Painted in the style of a Momoyama-period nanban folding screen, gold-leaf ground, bright colours, small figures.
jp-xavier: 1549, Kagoshima Bay: a Chinese junk with mat sails arrives beneath the smoking volcano Sakurajima, a small group of European Jesuits in black cassocks, seen from behind, steps ashore with a Japanese companion, local people in kimono and samurai watching from the shore, fishing boats drawn up on the black sand. Painted in the style of a Momoyama-period nanban folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, vivid colours, small figures.
jp-okehazama: 1560, Okehazama in Owari: in a narrow wooded valley during a sudden thunderstorm, a small force of samurai with banners rushes down the hillside onto a large camp of tents and curtains, soldiers scrambling, horses rearing, rain lashing the trees, lightning flashing over the pine-covered ridge. Painted in the style of an Edo-period nishiki-e woodblock print, bold outlines, dramatic rain lines, vivid colours, no gore.
jp-nagashino: 1575, Shitaragahara near Nagashino: rows of ashigaru musketeers behind wooden palisade fences fire volleys of matchlock smoke across a stream at Takeda mounted samurai charging with banners, low hills and a castle in the distance, a lone horse running riderless beside the stream far off. Painted in the style of the Edo-period Battle of Nagashino folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bright colours, many small figures in orderly rows.
jp-honno-ji: 1582, Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto at dawn: soldiers with banners surround the walled temple compound, flames rising from the wooden halls and tiled roofs, archers and musketeers at the gates, the city roofs and hills dark around it, seen from a distance, tiny figures running across the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, bold colours, dramatic flames, no gore.
jp-odawara-1590: 1590, Odawara: the great castle on a hill by the sea is surrounded by a vast besieging army with thousands of banners and tents, a new castle on a hill opposite, ships in the bay, ashigaru camps and tea pavilions in the siege lines. Painted in the style of a Momoyama-period folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bright colours, bird's-eye view, many tiny figures.
jp-imjin-war: 1592, Nagoya Castle at Karatsu in Kyushu: a large castle with a multi-storey keep on a hill overlooking the sea, the harbour crowded with hundreds of Japanese warships and transports with banners loading samurai and horses, camps of daimyo around the hills. Painted in the style of the Momoyama-period Hizen Nagoya Castle folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, vivid colours, tiny figures.
jp-sekigahara: 1600, Sekigahara in Mino: on a misty valley floor ringed by hills, two great armies of samurai with sashimono banners and ashigaru with spears and muskets clash, smoke rising, generals' curtained camps on hilltops, the fog lifting in the morning. Painted in the style of the Edo-period Battle of Sekigahara folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bright colours, many small figures, no gore.
jp-tokugawa-shogunate: 1603, Edo: a new castle town on a bay, the white multi-storey keep of Edo Castle rising above moats and stone walls, samurai mansions and townsmen's streets around it, workers filling marshland and digging canals, ships in the bay and Mount Fuji in the distance. Painted in the style of an early Edo-period folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bird's-eye view, vivid colours.
jp-siege-of-osaka: 1615, Osaka Castle: a great black-and-gold keep on massive stone walls is surrounded by besieging armies with countless banners, smoke rising from the burning castle town and outer defences, the river and sea beyond, boats crowding the castle moats. Painted in the style of the Edo-period Siege of Osaka summer campaign folding screen, gold-leaf clouds, bright colours, many small figures, seen from a distance.
jp-sankin-kotai: c. 1635, the Tōkaidō road: a long daimyo procession of samurai with spears, palanquins, lacquered chests and banners winds past rice fields and a post town, local people kneeling by the roadside, Mount Fuji rising in the distance. Painted in the style of an Edo-period ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Hiroshige, bold colours, clear blue sky, small figures.
jp-shimabara: 1638, Hara Castle on the Shimabara peninsula: a ruined castle on a cliff above the sea, defended by peasants with crosses on banners, surrounded by shogunate armies with tents and siege towers, a Dutch ship firing from the sea, smoke rising, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of an Edo-period folding screen, gold clouds, vivid colours, small figures, no gore.
jp-sakoku: c. 1641, Dejima in Nagasaki harbour: a small fan-shaped artificial island linked to the town by a single bridge, Dutch warehouses and a flagpole with a tricolour, a Dutch East India Company ship at anchor, Chinese junks nearby, Japanese guards at the gate, hills of Nagasaki behind. Painted in the style of an Edo-period Nagasaki-e woodblock print, bright colours, bird's-eye view.
