jp-shakushain: 1669, Shizunai on the Hokkaido coast: Ainu men in elm-bark robes with geometric embroidery and bows gather near a river mouth below forested hills, salmon drying on racks and a Japanese trading boat on the shore, a small wooden fort in the distance. Painted in the style of an Edo-period Ainu-e painting by Hirasawa Byozan, fine line, soft colours, detailed clothing.
jp-basho: 1689, northern Honshu: a lone traveller in a straw hat and monk's robe with a walking stick and a companion walk along a mountain path past pine trees and a waterfall, a thatched farmhouse and rice fields below, distant peaks. Painted in the style of a haiga, Yosa Buson's illustrations of Bashō's journey, light ink and colour, spare brushwork, much empty space.
jp-dojima: 1730, Dōjima in Osaka: along a canal lined with warehouses, rice merchants in kimono gather in a crowded open-air market, shouting and signalling bids with hand gestures, rice bales stacked on barges, ships at the docks, Osaka Castle in the distance, porters with shoulder poles crossing a wooden bridge. Painted in the style of an Edo-period ukiyo-e woodblock print, many small figures, bright colours, bird's-eye view.
jp-kaitai-shinsho: 1771, Edo: in a lamp-lit room with sliding doors, a group of Japanese doctors in kimono with shaved crowns sit around a low table with an open Dutch anatomy book showing a skeleton diagram, comparing it with notes and dictionaries, brushes and ink stones beside them. Painted in the style of an Edo-period Rangaku illustration, fine ink line and pale colour, no legible writing.
jp-hokusai: 1831, Edo: in a woodblock printmaker's workshop, carvers in kimono cut cherry-wood blocks and printers press paper onto inked blocks, while sheets showing a giant wave and a small Mount Fuji hang drying on lines, a print shop facing the street outside, a publisher counting stacks of finished sheets. Painted in the style of an Edo-period ukiyo-e print, Prussian blue and soft colours, bold outlines.
jp-perry: July 1853, Uraga in Edo Bay: four dark American warships, two paddle-wheel steamers with smoking funnels and two sailing sloops, anchor in the bay, while samurai and townspeople in kimono watch anxiously from the shore beside a small fort and boats, a few small rowing boats of officials heading out toward the ships. Painted in the style of an Edo-period kawaraban woodblock print, bold outlines, bright colours, exaggerated black ships.
jp-taisei-hokan: 1867, the Ninomaru Palace of Nijō Castle in Kyoto: in a great audience hall with painted gold-leaf screens of pine trees and tatami floors, rows of daimyo and officials in formal robes kneel before a raised dais where a shogun in court dress sits, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era history painting in oil, soft light, gold and dark tones.
jp-boshin-war: January 1868, Toba-Fushimi south of Kyoto: imperial troops in Western-style uniforms with rifles and Armstrong cannon fire across rice fields at shogunate soldiers in mixed armour and uniforms, smoke drifting over a village and a river, the imperial brocade banner flying, thatched farmhouses burning on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, vivid colours, dynamic composition, many small figures.
jp-abolition-han: 1871, Tokyo: in a Western-style hall with tall windows, officials in frock coats and some in samurai topknots and kimono sit at long tables while former daimyo bow, castles in the distance through the window, documents and seals on the table. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, aniline reds and blues, Western perspective, no legible text.
jp-satsuma-rebellion: 1877, Shiroyama near Kagoshima: a wooded hill overlooking the bay with the smoking volcano Sakurajima, rebel samurai in kimono and swords on the hilltop surrounded by conscript army soldiers in dark Western uniforms with rifles and cannon, smoke rising, seen from a distance, townspeople watching from boats in the bay. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, vivid colours, no gore.
jp-meiji-constitution: February 1889, the Imperial Palace in Tokyo: in a grand Western-style throne room with chandeliers and parquet floors, officials in dark ceremonial uniforms with gold braid and foreign diplomats stand in rows as a constitution document is presented, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print by Yōshū Chikanobu, bright aniline colours, Western perspective.
jp-tsushima: May 1905, the Tsushima Strait: grey steel battleships with tall funnels and gun turrets fire across a rough sea, smoke and spray filling the sky, a damaged Russian ship listing in the distance, a Japanese flagship flying signal flags, torpedo boats darting between the larger ships, the island of Tsushima faint on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, dramatic waves, bright colours, bold outlines.
jp-mukden-incident: September 1931, Liutiaohu near Shenyang: at night a railway line runs across flat Manchurian fields of sorghum, a small cloud of smoke rising from the tracks, Japanese soldiers in khaki with rifles and lanterns gathered nearby, the dark walls of a Chinese army barracks in the distance. Painted as a 1930s Chinese woodcut print, black and white with stark contrast, simple shapes, neutral.
jp-pearl-harbor: December 1941, Pearl Harbor in Hawaii: seen from a distant hillside, columns of black smoke rise from battleships moored in the harbour, small aircraft circling above, palm trees and green mountains framing the scene, the morning sky clear, small boats moving across the water toward the ships. Painted as a 1940s war artist's documentary watercolour, muted blues and greys, loose wash, no figures in detail.
jp-atomic-bombings: August 1945, Hiroshima: a vast, quiet plain of flattened ruins seen from a distance under a pale sky, a lone domed building's steel frame standing beside a river, a few small figures walking through the rubble, the mountains around the city, the hills green and untouched in the far distance. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft grey and ochre washes, solemn and still, no gore.
jp-occupation: 1945–46, Tokyo: a wide avenue near the moat of the Imperial Palace with the Dai-ichi Seimei building, American military jeeps and trucks, Japanese civilians in kimono and Western clothes walking past, farmers receiving land deeds at a village office far off, children playing beside a ruined wall. Painted as a muted 1940s documentary watercolour, soft greys and greens, small figures, no faces in detail.
jp-constitution-1947: May 1947, Tokyo: the granite National Diet Building with its stepped central tower rises above a broad plaza where crowds in coats and hats gather on a spring day, children with families, cherry trees in leaf, a calm, celebratory mood, the sky clearing after rain. Painted as a muted 1940s documentary watercolour, soft blue and green washes, distant figures, no text or banners.
jp-san-francisco: September 1951, San Francisco: inside the War Memorial Opera House, a stage with long tables and microphones where delegates in dark suits sit and sign documents, a large audience in rows below, the hall lit softly, an orchestra pit empty and the curtains drawn aside. Painted as a muted 1950s documentary gouache illustration, warm golds and greys, figures small and seen from behind, no legible text.
jp-economic-miracle: Late 1950s–60s, Tokyo: a busy cityscape of new concrete office buildings, elevated highways under construction, cranes, crowded trains and streets full of small cars and bicycles, factory chimneys and Tokyo Tower in the distance under a hazy sky, a new bullet train crossing a viaduct. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm grey and ochre washes, many small figures, no legible signs.
jp-minamata: 1956, Minamata in Kumamoto: a quiet fishing village by a calm bay, wooden boats pulled up on the shore, nets drying, a large chemical factory with chimneys and waste pipes on the far side of the bay, a few villagers looking toward it. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greys and blues, calm but sombre, no figures in detail.
jp-tokyo-olympics-1964: October 1964, the National Stadium in Tokyo: a vast oval stadium packed with spectators under a clear autumn sky, rows of athletes from many nations in coloured blazers marching on the red track, a cauldron on the stands, a jet trail of rings in the blue sky. Painted as a documentary watercolour illustration, bright but soft colours, crowds seen from above, no faces, flags or text legible.
jp-kawabata-nobel: 1968, Kamakura: a traditional Japanese house with a tiled roof and sliding paper doors in a quiet garden of pines and moss, a writing desk with brushes and manuscript pages on tatami, snow falling outside, the hills of Kamakura behind, a single plum branch in a vase. Painted as a Shōwa-era watercolour, soft greys and greens, still and contemplative, no people and no legible writing.
jp-okinawa-reversion: May 1972, Naha in Okinawa: a coastal city of white concrete houses with red-tiled roofs under a rainy sky, crowds with umbrellas gathered in a square at a distance, a large military airbase with aircraft visible beyond, the turquoise sea and green hills, a jet taking off over the water. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft blues and greens, calm, no faces or text.
jp-plaza-accord: September 1985, New York: the grand Plaza Hotel by Central Park seen from Fifth Avenue on a sunny autumn day, yellow taxis and pedestrians, a few dark limousines parked at the entrance, trees turning gold, inside a room with a long table and empty chairs glimpsed through a window. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, warm golds and greys, no faces or text.
jp-bubble-burst: Early 1990s, Tokyo: a dusk view of Marunouchi with glass office towers, an empty trading floor with darkened screens seen through tall windows, office workers in suits walking home, cranes standing idle on an unfinished building, rain on the streets, a single taxi waiting under a streetlight. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool grey and blue washes, quiet mood, no legible signs or faces.
jp-hanshin-earthquake: January 1995, Kobe: a winter morning view of a city with collapsed houses and a toppled elevated highway, smoke rising from fires in the distance, rescuers and residents in coats moving among the debris, the mountains behind and the harbour, a temporary tent shelter in a schoolyard. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, grey and ochre washes, solemn and calm, distant figures, no gore.
jp-sarin-attack: March 1995, Kasumigaseki station in Tokyo: at a subway entrance among government buildings, emergency workers in white protective suits and masks and ambulances gather on the street in the morning, commuters in coats waiting on the pavement, seen from a distance, a closed station gate behind them. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool grey and white washes, calm, no faces or legible signs.
jp-koizumi: Early 2000s, Tokyo: the granite National Diet Building at dusk, its stepped tower lit, cars passing on the avenue, a quiet neighbourhood post office with red postboxes in the foreground, cherry trees beside it, office workers in suits walking home along the pavement as small distant silhouettes. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft amber and blue washes, no people in detail and no legible text.
jp-tohoku-earthquake: March 2011, Ishinomaki in Miyagi: a coastal town after the tsunami, seen from a hill, wrecked houses and boats tossed inland across flat land, water pooled in fields, snow-dusted mountains behind, a few rescue workers walking in the distance, a broken sea wall along the shore and gulls overhead. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cold grey and blue washes, solemn and still, no gore.
jp-fukushima: March 2011, Ōkuma on the Fukushima coast: a nuclear power plant with boxy reactor buildings and a tall exhaust stack on the seashore, white steam rising from damaged roofs, an empty town and road leading away, abandoned cars and blossoming trees in the foreground. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale grey and green washes, quiet and empty, no people.
jp-abenomics: 2013, Tokyo: the stone façade of the Bank of Japan in Nihonbashi on a bright winter morning, office workers in dark coats crossing a busy street, a glass trading room nearby glimpsed through tall windows with rows of glowing screens, construction cranes over new towers in Marunouchi and a train passing on an elevated track. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool blue and grey washes with warm sunlight, small distant figures, no faces, no legible signs or numbers.
jp-reiwa: May 2019, Tokyo: the moats, stone walls and white turrets of the Imperial Palace seen across the Nijūbashi bridge on a calm spring day, pine trees on the banks, crowds of visitors in light coats gathered far off on the gravel plaza, the glass towers of Marunouchi rising behind. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft green and grey washes, quiet and ceremonial, no individual people shown in detail, no flags or text.
jp-abe-assassination: July 2022, outside Yamato-Saidaiji Station in Nara: a quiet station plaza at a road junction on a summer afternoon, a guardrail and a small traffic island, a pile of flower bouquets laid by the kerb, the station building and low-rise shops around it, a few distant passers-by bowing their heads. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft grey and green washes, still and sombre, no figures in detail, no gore and no legible signs.
jp-takaichi: October 2025, Tokyo: the stepped granite tower of the National Diet Building and the modern Prime Minister's Office nearby in autumn light, ginkgo trees turning gold along the avenue, press vans parked at the kerb and small distant groups of reporters waiting, the city skyline beyond. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm gold and grey washes, calm and neutral, no individual people shown in detail, no flags or legible text.
kr-amsa-dong: c. 3000 BCE, Amsa-dong on the Han River: a Neolithic village of round thatched pit houses on a sandy riverbank, people in hide and woven-fibre clothing fishing with nets from dugout canoes, women shaping pointed-based pots incised with comb patterns, acorns and shellfish being prepared beside a hearth, wooded hills across the wide river. Painted as a documentary watercolour reconstruction, warm earth tones and river blues, soft morning light, small figures.
kr-bangudae: c. 3000 BCE, Bangudae by the Daegok Stream near Ulsan: Neolithic hunters with stone tools carve pictures of whales, deer, tigers and boats into a smooth vertical cliff face beside a quiet stream, a small fire burning on the gravel bank, forested hills around. Rendered in the style of the Bangudae petroglyphs themselves, pecked outline figures of whales and boats on warm brown stone, with soft natural light across the rock surface and tiny human figures at its foot.
kr-rice-farming: c. 1500 BCE, Daepyeong near Jinju: a Bronze Age village of rectangular pit houses on a river terrace, surrounded by ditches, farmers in hemp clothing working small rice paddies and dry fields with wooden hoes and polished stone reaping knives, plain undecorated Mumun pots drying in the sun, the Nam River and hills beyond. Painted as a documentary watercolour reconstruction, soft greens and ochres, gentle daylight, many small figures at work.
kr-dolmens: c. 1000 BCE, Gochang: on a grassy hillside, Bronze Age villagers haul a massive flat capstone on log rollers with ropes toward upright supporting stones, a chief's burial ceremony beginning, many other dolmens scattered across the slope, rice paddies and low hills behind under a wide sky. Painted as a documentary watercolour reconstruction, earthy greys and greens, long evening shadows, many small figures straining at the ropes.
kr-qin-kai: c. 300 BCE, Liaodong: an army of the Warring States kingdom of Yan with bronze-tipped halberds, crossbows and horse-drawn chariots advances across the Liao River plain, while Gojoseon warriors with bronze daggers and bows withdraw toward hills in the southeast, walled towns and fields in the distance. Painted in the manner of a Warring States lacquer painting, black, cinnabar and ochre palette, flat silhouette figures in a long frieze.
kr-wiman: c. 194 BCE, Wanggeom-seong near the Taedong River: a refugee leader in a topknot and Korean-style robe, seen from behind, leads a band of followers through the gate of an earthen-walled royal city, a mounted guard escorting them, traders with ox-carts and bundles of goods on the road, river boats and hills beyond. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red, black and ochre on white plaster, lively outline figures.
kr-four-commanderies: c. 108 BCE, Lelang near Pyongyang: Han Chinese officials in black lacquered caps and long robes oversee the building of an earthen-walled commandery town with tiled-roof halls, scribes recording at tables, local people bringing tribute of furs and grain, soldiers with crossbows at the gate, the Taedong River behind. Painted in the style of a Han tomb mural, brisk ink outlines with red and ochre on pale plaster, figures in profile.
kr-silla-founded: 57 BCE, the Gyeongju basin: chiefs of six villages in hemp garments gather in a forest clearing near a spring, where a white horse kneels beside a large egg glowing in the light, the chiefs bowing in wonder, thatched villages and rounded hills around the basin. Painted in the style of the Silla Cheonmachong painted birch-bark saddle flap, simple line and flat red, white and black, the legend shown as a gentle, mythical scene.
kr-goguryeo-founded: 37 BCE, Jolbon near Huanren: a mountain fortress city rising on a flat-topped peak with sheer cliffs above a river valley, horsemen in feathered caps with bows riding along the riverbank, a young archer prince seen from behind leading a band of followers, forested mountains all around. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural from the Ji'an area, vivid outlines, red, yellow and black on white plaster, lively hunting figures.
kr-baekje-founded: 18 BCE, Wiryeseong on the Han River: settlers in hemp clothing build earthen walls and wooden palisades around a new town on the south bank, thatched houses and storehouses inside, boats on the wide river, a young leader seen from behind directing the work, the hills of the Han basin behind. Painted in the style of a Baekje stamped-tile landscape relief, soft clay tones, stylised mountains and clouds, small figures.
kr-lelang-falls: 313, Pyongyang: a Goguryeo army of mounted warriors in lamellar armour with lances and banners rides through the gates of an earthen-walled Chinese commandery town on the Taedong River, Han-style tiled halls and tombs beyond, officials in robes leaving with ox-carts. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural procession scene, armoured horses, flat red, ochre and black on white plaster, figures in profile.
kr-geunchogo: 371, Pyongyang fortress: a Baekje army of armoured soldiers with spears, crossbows and banners storms the earthen and stone walls of a hilltop fortress by the Taedong River, arrows flying, mounted warriors in the foreground, smoke rising from inside the walls, seen at a distance. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural battle scene, vigorous outlines, red, ochre and black on plaster, small figures.
kr-gwanggaeto: c. 391, Gungnae near Ji'an on the Yalu: a young king in a feathered gold crown, seen small from behind on horseback, reviews an army of armoured cavalry with long lances and caparisoned horses on a broad plain below the stone-walled Gungnae fortress; on the wooded hills behind stand low, squat, flat-topped stepped tombs built of cut granite blocks in a few broad terraces, like the General's Tomb, half hidden by pines. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural such as Anak Tomb No. 3, lively procession of figures, red, ochre and black, no text.
kr-pyongyang-capital: 427, Pyongyang: a royal procession of ox-carts, palanquins and armoured horsemen moves along a road toward a new capital on the Taedong River, workers building palace halls with tiled roofs and earthen walls around Mount Daeseong, boats on the river, the old capital far behind in the mountains. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural procession scene, flat colours, red and ochre, many small figures.
kr-hanseong-falls: 475, Hanseong on the Han River: a Goguryeo army with banners encircles the earthen walls of a city on the south bank, smoke rising from halls inside, and a long column of Baekje refugees with ox-carts and boats moving south along the river toward distant mountains, seen at a distance. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, red and ochre outlines on plaster, small figures, no gore.
kr-han-river: 553, the lower Han River: Silla soldiers in armour with banners occupy a hill fortress overlooking the broad river, while boats with sails sail toward the Yellow Sea, a commander seen from behind on horseback pointing west, farmers working fields in the valley. Painted in the style of an early Korean Buddhist landscape painting, fine line, mineral colours of green, red and gold, small figures.
kr-nine-provinces: 685, Gyeongju: in a palace hall with tiled roofs and red pillars, Silla officials in robes and caps of rank bend over a large painted map of the peninsula divided into regions, scribes writing on scrolls, envoys departing on horseback through the palace gate toward distant provinces. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting adapted to a court scene, fine gold line, deep red and green mineral colours, no legible writing.
kr-bulguksa: c. 751, Bulguksa on the slopes of Mount Tohamsan: masons build stone terraces, double staircases and two stone pagodas of a temple with wooden halls and tiled roofs, monks in grey robes watching, while higher up workers carve granite blocks for a domed cave shrine with a seated Buddha. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, fine gold line, mineral greens and reds, misty mountains, small figures.
kr-dharani: 751, Bulguksa temple in Gyeongju: inside the stone three-storey Seokgatap pagoda, a monk places a small rolled paper scroll into a reliquary box alongside gilt bronze reliquaries and beads, other monks holding lamps in a quiet chamber, the temple courtyard at dusk outside. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, fine gold line on dark silk, red and green mineral pigments, no legible text on the scroll.
kr-sanggyeong: 755, Sanggyeong near Ning'an in Manchuria: a walled capital laid out on a grid like Chang'an, a broad central avenue leading to a palace with tiled roofs and stone foundations, Balhae officials in robes and caps, horsemen in fur hats, a lake and forested mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty court painting, mineral blues and greens, bird's-eye view, small figures, fine architectural line.
kr-jang-bogo: 828, Cheonghaejin on Wando island: a fortified naval base with earthen walls on a hilltop overlooking a sheltered harbour, Silla trading ships with mat sails and oars anchored below, sailors unloading ceramics and silk, armed guards on the walls, islands scattered across a calm sea. Painted in the style of a Goryeo-era landscape painting, fine ink line with soft mineral blues and greens, small figures and boats.
kr-choe-chiwon: 881, Yangzhou on the Grand Canal: in a Tang military headquarters with tiled roofs and red columns, a young Silla scholar in a Tang official's robe and cap writes at a lacquered desk with brush and ink, a general and officers seen in the background, canal boats outside the window. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours, fine line, no legible writing.
kr-later-baekje: 900, Wansanju, present Jeonju: a former Silla officer in armour, seen from behind on horseback, leads soldiers with banners through the gates of a walled town in a green valley, townspeople and farmers lining the road, hills of the southwest around, a new palace being built. Painted in the style of a Goryeo-era Buddhist painting adapted to a narrative scene, fine gold line, red and green mineral colours, small figures.
kr-taebong: 901, Songak, present Kaesong: a one-eyed monk-turned-warlord in a black robe, seen from behind, stands before a hall with tiled roofs and red pillars among his followers and armoured soldiers, banners flying, the slopes of Mount Songak rising behind the town. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist narrative painting, fine gold line, mineral colours of deep red and green, small figures, misty mountains.
kr-goryeo-founded: 918, Songak, present Kaesong: generals in armour kneel before a tent on a hillside at night, offering leadership to a figure in a red robe seen from behind, torches lighting the scene, the palace halls of the capital below and Mount Songak behind. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting adapted to a court scene, fine gold line on dark silk, deep reds and greens, solemn atmosphere.
kr-illicheon: 936, the plain of Illicheon near Gumi: two armies clash beside a river, Goryeo cavalry with banners and armoured infantry advancing, Later Baekje troops wavering and turning back, wooded hills and the Nakdong River in the distance, dust and banners in the sunlight. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary battle painting, ink line with soft colour, bird's-eye view, many small figures in orderly formations.
kr-gwageo: 958, Gaegyeong: in a palace courtyard with tiled roofs, rows of young scholars in robes and black caps kneel on mats at low desks writing examination essays with brushes, officials patrolling between them, a Chinese scholar adviser and the king seen far off on a raised hall. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary painting of an examination, fine line, soft colours, many small figures, no legible writing.
kr-seo-hui: 993, Anju near the Cheongcheon River: in a Khitan army camp of felt tents and banners on a plain, a Goryeo envoy in a long robe and official cap sits on a mat facing a Khitan commander in fur hat and armour, both seen from the side and small, interpreters and guards around. Painted in the style of a Yuan-dynasty steppe handscroll, fine line, muted colours, horses and tents.
kr-gwiju: 1019, Gwiju in northwestern Korea: on a wide plain, Goryeo armoured cavalry and infantry with banners charge a retreating Khitan army of mounted archers in fur hats, a sudden wind blowing dust and banners toward the Khitan lines, a walled town on a hill behind, seen at a distance. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary battle painting, ink and soft colour, bird's-eye view, many small figures.
kr-samguk-sagi: 1145, Gaegyeong: in a palace library with shelves of scrolls and bound books, an elderly scholar-official in Goryeo robes and cap, seen from behind, directs scribes copying texts at low desks, stacks of manuscripts and bamboo slips around them, a pine tree visible through the window. Painted in the style of a Goryeo-era court painting, fine ink line with soft colours, warm candlelight, no legible writing.
kr-military-coup: 1170, the Bohyeonwon pavilion near Gaegyeong: armed military officers in armour and helmets surround a garden pavilion where civil officials in robes and caps scatter, the king's procession stalled on the path, overturned wine tables and fallen banners, mountains and pine trees around, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Goryeo narrative painting, fine line and mineral colours, small figures, no gore.
kr-tripitaka: 1236–1251, Haeinsa temple in the Gaya mountains: monks and craftsmen carve thousands of wooden printing blocks with knives, stacking them on long shelves in a timber hall with slatted windows, others inking blocks to print test sheets, misty forested mountains around the temple. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, fine gold line, deep mineral colours, many small figures, no legible text on the blocks.
kr-sambyeolcho: 1270, Jindo island: soldiers in armour with banners build earthen walls and wooden palisades around a fortress on a hill overlooking the sea, war boats drawn up on the shore, a fleet of Goryeo-Mongol ships approaching across the strait, islands in the distance. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary painting, fine ink line with soft colour, bird's-eye view, many small figures and boats.
kr-jikji: 1377, Heungdeoksa temple in Cheongju: in a temple workshop, monks set small cast metal type pieces into a frame, ink them and press paper on top, a finished bound book on the table, a clay mould and crucible for casting type nearby, the temple courtyard and pagoda outside. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, fine gold line, deep red and green mineral colours, no legible characters.
kr-wihwado: 1388, Wihwa Island in the Yalu River: a great Goryeo army camped on a flat river island in summer rain, the swollen river brown and wide, a general on horseback seen from behind turning his army around, soldiers crossing back on boats and pontoons toward the south, mountains of Liaodong beyond. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary painting, ink and soft colour, bird's-eye view, small figures.
kr-joseon-founded: 1392, Gaegyeong: in the Suchang palace courtyard, officials in red and blue robes and black gauze hats bow in rows before a hall where a general in a dragon robe, seen from behind and small, takes the throne, banners and attendants on either side, Mount Songak behind. Painted in the style of a Joseon court documentary painting (uigwe), fine line, bright colours, orderly rows of small figures.
kr-hanyang: 1395, Hanyang: the new palace of Gyeongbokgung with tiled roofs and red pillars rises below Mount Bugaksan, a long stone wall and the Gwanghwamun gate in front, workers carrying timber and stone, officials in robes walking the wide avenue, the city wall winding over the surrounding hills. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era map-landscape painting, blue-green mountains, fine line, bird's-eye view, small figures.
kr-hangul: 1446, Gyeongbokgung palace in Seoul: in a palace hall with painted beams, scholars of the Hall of Worthies in robes and gauze hats study a newly printed book with simple geometric letter shapes, a king seen from behind seated on a raised platform, scribes and printing blocks nearby. Painted in the style of a Joseon court painting, fine line and bright colours, no legible writing on the pages.
kr-gyeongguk: 1485, Seoul: in a government office courtyard with tiled roofs, officials in robes and black hats read from bound volumes of a law code at long tables, scribes copying, clerks carrying stacks of books, a magistrate's court in session in the background with petitioners kneeling. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era genre painting in the manner of Kim Hong-do, light ink and soft colours, lively small figures, no legible writing.
kr-hansan: August 1592, off Hansan Island: Korean panokseon warships and a turtle ship with a dragon head and iron-spiked roof form a crane-wing arc around a fleet of Japanese ships with banners, cannon smoke drifting over the water, green islands around the bay. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary painting of a naval battle, fine ink line, soft blue and green colours, many small boats, bird's-eye view.
kr-myeongnyang: 1597, the Myeongnyang Strait: a small line of thirteen Korean panokseon warships holds a narrow channel between rocky hills as a strong tidal current churns white water, a huge fleet of Japanese ships with banners crowding in and colliding, cannon smoke rising. Painted in the style of a Joseon-era documentary painting, ink and soft colour, dramatic swirling waves, bird's-eye view, many small ships.
kr-hwaseong: 1796, Suwon: the fortress walls of Hwaseong with gate towers, archery platforms and bastions wind over a hill, workers using a wooden crane with pulleys and ox-carts to lift stone blocks, a royal procession with banners on a nearby bridge. Painted in the style of the Joseon court documentary painting Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe, fine ink line and bright colours, bird's-eye view, many small figures.
kr-ganghwa-treaty: 1876, Ganghwa Island: Japanese steam warships with smoke rising anchor off the coast, Japanese officers in Western-style uniforms and Korean officials in robes and broad black horsehair hats sit across a table in a tent, guards and cannons on the shore, fortified walls of Ganghwa behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light watercolour, fine hatching, no legible writing.
kr-donghak-revolution: 1894, Gobu in Jeolla: thousands of peasants in white clothes and headbands, carrying bamboo spears and farming tools, gather on a hill above rice fields, a leader in a white robe seen from behind among them, a county office with tiled roofs below. Painted in the style of a late Joseon genre painting with light ink and colour, many small figures, autumn landscape, neutral tone.
kr-eulmi: October 1895, Gyeongbokgung palace in Seoul: at dawn, a quiet inner palace courtyard with tiled roofs and the Geoncheonggung residence, mist hanging over the pond and pavilion, an overturned lantern and scattered footprints on the gravel, distant guards hurrying through a gate. Painted in the style of a late Joseon court painting, fine ink line and muted colours, solemn mood, no figures in detail, no gore.
kr-korean-empire: October 1897, Hwangudan altar in Seoul: a round three-tiered stone altar where an emperor in a golden-yellow ritual robe and crown, seen from behind, conducts a ceremony to heaven, officials in red robes in rows, banners and musicians, the city walls and mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Joseon court documentary painting (uigwe), fine line, bright colours, many orderly small figures.
kr-eulsa: November 1905, Deoksugung palace in Seoul: a Western-style stone pavilion in the palace grounds at night, its windows lit, Japanese soldiers with rifles standing guard outside, Korean officials in black hats and robes walking in with heads bowed, a stone gate and bare winter trees. Painted as an early twentieth-century illustrated newspaper drawing with light watercolour, sombre greys and browns, small figures, no legible text.
kr-annexation: August 1910, Seoul: a grey day over the Gyeongbokgung palace gate and the old city walls, Korean townspeople in white clothes and black hats standing quietly in the streets, Japanese military police at the gate, the mountains of Seoul shrouded in cloud. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, muted greys and whites, calm and sombre, small figures, no flags or text.
kr-march-first: March 1919, Tapgol Park in Seoul: under bare trees, crowds of people in white hanbok and black hats, students in uniforms and women in long skirts gather around a stone pagoda and an octagonal pavilion, a figure reading from a paper to the crowd, others spreading into the street beyond. Painted as an early twentieth-century woodcut print, bold black and white, peaceful mood, no legible text.
kr-liberation: August 1945, the 38th parallel: a quiet country road through rice fields and low hills, a simple wooden barrier across the road, American soldiers in khaki on one side and Soviet soldiers in green on the other, Korean villagers in white clothes waiting with bundles, summer clouds overhead. Painted as a muted 1940s documentary watercolour, soft greens and ochres, small figures, no flags or text.
kr-korean-war: June 1950, the Ongjin peninsula: dawn over low hills and rice paddies near the coast, smoke rising from distant villages, columns of soldiers and trucks moving along a dirt road, refugees in white clothing carrying bundles walking south in the foreground, a burned bridge across a river. Painted as a muted 1950s documentary watercolour, grey-green and ochre washes, small figures, sombre and neutral, no gore.
zhu-takes-nanjing: 1356, Jiqing (Nanjing) on the Yangtze: a rebel army in red headscarves and padded jackets streams through a great brick city gate beneath grey walls, banners without lettering lifted high, townspeople in plain Yuan-era robes watching from doorways; the Zhongshan hills and the broad river behind, boats moored at the waterfront, a small mounted commander seen from behind in the middle of the column. Painted as a late Yuan handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, fine line, misty river distance.
shangdu-burned: 1358, Shangdu on the open grassland: plumes of smoke rise over the walled Mongol summer capital, its palace halls and square earthen walls burning, while a column of Red Turban horsemen and foot soldiers in red headcloths rides away across rolling steppe; felt yurts abandoned in the foreground, distant low hills under a wide sky. Seen from far off, no figures in close-up. Painted in the manner of a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in the style of Liu Guandao, ink and pale colour on silk.
battle-of-longwan: 1360, Longwan on the Yangtze outside Nanjing: a fleet of tall multi-decked war junks with batten sails crowds into a reed-lined river bend as ambushing troops burst from the banks and small boats close in, arrows arcing, smoke drifting over the water; low hills and the city wall faint in the distance. Large scale, figures small, no gore. Painted as an early Ming narrative handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, rippling wave patterns and dense reeds.
pipa-ji: 1360, Ningbo region: an open-air stage of timber with a carved roof in a village temple courtyard, where actors in Yuan-Ming costume perform a southern drama; a young wife in plain mourning white holds a pipa lute and walks a road carrying a scroll of her parents' likeness, while villagers in straw hats crowd below with musicians on drum and flute at the side. Lanterns hang from eaves at dusk. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print drama illustration, crisp black line with light hand colouring.
chaghan-temur-killed: 1362, before the walls of Yidu (Qingzhou) in Shandong: a Yuan siege camp of round felt tents and banners spreads across a winter plain facing a walled city; at night a few figures slip out of a large commander's tent lit by a single lantern while guards sleep by braziers, the camp otherwise silent under a cold moon. Seen from a distance, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Yuan-dynasty ink handscroll, muted ink washes on silk.
zhu-prince-of-wu: 1364, Yingtian (Nanjing): a timber palace hall with red columns and grey tiled roofs, where rows of civil officials in round-collared robes and black gauze caps and armoured generals bow in a stone courtyard toward a distant figure seated beneath the eaves; ceremonial parasols, incense smoke, drummers at the side, city walls and hills beyond. Formal symmetrical composition, figures small. Painted as early Ming court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk.
han-liner-drowned: 1366, Guabu on the Yangtze near Nanjing: a single ornate river boat with a small cabin lists and capsizes in grey swirling water under an overcast sky, its oars scattered, while escort boats keep their distance and soldiers on them watch without moving; wide reed banks, a distant pagoda, cold mist over the river. No figures in close-up. Painted as a Yuan-Ming ink landscape handscroll, sombre ink washes on silk with faint colour.
northern-expedition-1367: 1367, outside Yingtian (Nanjing): a vast army in lamellar armour and red-tasselled helmets marches north from the city gates in long columns of infantry, cavalry and supply carts, banners and drums leading; two generals on horseback seen from behind at the head, crowds lining the road, the Yangtze crossing with ferries in the distance. Morning light, epic scale. Painted as an early Ming court handscroll, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed figures.
pingjiang: 1367, Pingjiang (Suzhou): a besieged canal city surrounded by earthworks and siege towers, army camps encircling its moated walls; wooden siege platforms overlook the battlements, boats blockade the water gates, smoke rising from inside after ten months of siege; a tall pagoda and tiled roofs within, Lake Tai flat and silver beyond. Distant viewpoint, small figures. Painted as an early Ming handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, Jiangnan water landscape.
xu-da-takes-dadu: 1368, Dadu (Beijing): Ming troops in red jackets and lamellar armour pour through the great gate of the Yuan capital's rammed-earth walls, while far to the north a small train of Mongol carts and horsemen flees through a mountain pass; inside the walls the broad avenues and Yuan palace roofs lie quiet. Viewed from high above, autumn light. Painted as an early Ming court handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
jingdezhen-imperial-kiln: 1369, Jingdezhen in Jiangxi: an imperial porcelain workshop among green hills, with long dragon kilns climbing a slope and smoke drifting; potters in plain robes throw vessels on wheels, painters brush cobalt designs on white jars and dishes, labourers carry racks of drying ware and stack firewood, and boats on the Chang River wait to be loaded. Busy daytime scene. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour, clear detailed line.
battle-of-yingchang: 1370, Yingchang on the Inner Mongolian grassland: Ming cavalry sweep over a low rise toward a Mongol encampment of white yurts and wagons beside a lake, horsemen of the Northern Yuan scattering across the plain, captured carts and herds of horses being led away; wide sky, distant hills. Seen at a distance, no gore. Painted in the style of a Ming court painting of a frontier campaign, ink and colour on silk.
prince-fiefs-hongwu: 1370, Nanjing: in a palace courtyard several young princes in red robes and winged caps kneel to receive investiture, each followed by an escort of armoured soldiers and horses waiting by the gate; beyond, columns depart along roads toward distant walled cities under a broad sky. Figures small and seen from behind. Painted as an early Ming court painting, mineral blue and green with gold, ink line on silk.
ming-conquest-of-xia: 1371, Chongqing at the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers: a broad horizontal river view filling the whole picture, a Ming war fleet of junks with batten sails and red banners moving upstream between steep green cliffs, while on the riverbank before the hilly walled city a line of officials in plain robes comes out to surrender, carrying a sealed box; mist clinging to the hills. Distant composition, small figures, no visible mounting or border. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
battle-of-lingbei: 1372, the steppe near Karakorum in Mongolia: a long Ming column of infantry and cavalry straggles back across a vast barren plain under leaden skies, wagons broken, banners lowered, while Mongol horse archers ride along distant ridges; scattered stones and dry grass, no buildings. Seen from far away, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Yuan-Ming steppe handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
ryukyu-tribute: 1372, Shuri on Okinawa: a Ryukyuan tribute ship, a broad junk with a high stern and woven sails, is loaded at a harbour below a hill fortress of curving limestone walls; envoys in Ryukyuan robes and turban-like headwraps carry boxes, horses and bundles of sulphur aboard while a Ming envoy's ship is moored nearby; subtropical trees, turquoise sea. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
hu-weiyong: 1380, Nanjing: a vast empty palace courtyard in grey dawn light, an official's black gauze cap and court tablet lying on the stone steps of a closed hall, guards in armour standing in rows, a few officials in red robes kneeling far off; tiled roofs and the city wall beyond. Austere and quiet, no figures in close-up. Painted as an early Ming court painting in ink and subdued colour on silk.
ming-conquest-of-yunnan: 1381, Kunming and Dian Lake: Ming armies in lamellar armour advance across the red-earth plateau toward a walled city beside a broad lake, cavalry on the flanks, Yi and Bai villagers watching from terraced fields; blue Western Hills rising beyond the water, clouds low. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
yellow-registers: 1381, Nanjing: inside a large government archive hall, clerks in plain round-collared robes and black caps sit at long tables copying household registers bound in yellow covers, stacks of yellow-covered books piled on shelves, village elders waiting at the door with bundles; beyond the windows, the archive buildings on the island in Xuanwu Lake. No legible writing. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine black line with light colour.
embroidered-uniform-guard: 1382, Nanjing: a line of imperial guards in red and gold embroidered robes with flying-fish patterns, black hats and long sabres at their hips, stands at attention before a palace gate; others ride out on horses through a misty street at dawn, townspeople stepping aside. Figures at a moderate distance. Painted as early Ming court painting, rich mineral red, gold and green on silk with fine line.
guo-huan-case: 1385, Nanjing: a long granary yard with rows of tiled storehouses and grain sacks, where inspectors with abacuses and ledgers count stores while guards lead a line of officials away in chains through a gate; anxious landlords wait outside under willow trees. No violence shown, figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, clear black line with light hand colouring.
battle-of-buir-lake: 1388, Buir Lake on the eastern steppe: at dawn after a sandstorm, Ming cavalry charge out of yellow haze toward a vast camp of Mongol yurts and wagons on the lakeshore, Mongol horsemen scattering and herds of horses and camels stampeding; flat grassland and pale sky. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of a Ming frontier campaign handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
lan-yu-case: 1393, Nanjing: an imperial palace gate under a heavy grey sky, rows of soldiers with halberds lining the approach, the deserted mansion of a great general with its gate sealed with strips of paper and armour racks left empty in the courtyard; crows on the roof ridge. Quiet, sombre, no figures in close-up, no violence. Painted as an early Ming court painting in ink and muted colour on silk.
great-ming-code: 1397, Nanjing: in a palace hall with red pillars, officials in red robes and black winged caps present thick bound volumes on a lacquered table, while clerks carry copies out to messengers on horseback waiting in the courtyard to ride to the provinces; morning light through lattice doors. No legible writing. Painted as an early Ming court painting, mineral colours and ink on silk.
north-south-list-case: 1397, the examination compound in Nanjing: rows of tiny cubicles under long tiled roofs, candidates in blue scholar robes and square caps crowding before a high wall where a list has just been posted, northerners and southerners in separate clusters; guards at the gate, a watchtower above. The posted list is blank or illegible. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine black line with light colour.
jianwen-reduces-fiefs: 1398, Nanjing: in a palace audience hall a young emperor sits small on a dais far off while two scholar-officials in red robes kneel presenting memorials; through the open doors couriers ride out with sealed orders toward distant princely cities, their seals in lacquered boxes. Figures small, symmetrical composition, autumn light. Painted as an early Ming court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk.
battle-of-dongchang: 1400, Dongchang (Liaocheng) on the North China plain: in winter, imperial infantry with firearms and crossbows form a tight square around a walled city, cannon smoke drifting, while a rebel cavalry charge breaks against their lines across frozen fields; bare trees, grey sky. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the manner of an early Ming battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
grand-secretariat: 1402, a hall inside the Nanjing palace: several Hanlin scholars in red and blue robes with black winged caps sit at desks with brushes, ink stones and stacks of memorials, drafting responses by lamplight, a eunuch carrying papers toward an inner gate; screens and bookshelves behind. Quiet scholarly atmosphere, no legible writing. Painted as a Ming court painting, fine line and soft colour on silk.
fang-xiaoru-executed: 1402, Nanjing: a palace hall where a scholar in white mourning robes stands defiantly before a raised throne, a brush thrown on the floor and a blank sheet of paper beside it, armoured guards stepping forward, officials shrinking back; the emperor is a distant shape on the dais. No violence shown, figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light colour.
tally-trade-japan: 1404, Kyoto: at the Kitayama villa with its gilded pavilion beside a pond, Japanese courtiers in court robes and lacquered caps receive a Ming envoy in red robes and black hat carrying gifts and a boxed letter; servants carry bolts of silk and copper coins; pine trees and maple. Figures small and in a group. Painted in the style of a Muromachi-period Japanese handscroll, ink and light colour on paper.
forbidden-city-construction: 1406-1420, Beijing: a huge construction site where thousands of labourers haul giant nanmu logs on rollers and sledges, masons cut white marble terraces, carpenters raise red-pillared timber frames for great halls, and kilns supply golden glazed tiles; scaffolding of bamboo, oxen and carts, the Western Hills hazy beyond. Panoramic daytime view, tiny figures. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and colour on silk, architectural ruled line.
ming-conquest-of-dai-viet: 1406, near Thang Long (Hanoi) on the Red River: a Ming army with banners and cannon crosses the broad brown river on rafts and junks, while Vietnamese defenders on the far bank man earthen ramparts and war elephants stand among palms; rice paddies and karst hills in mist. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming campaign handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
yongle-encyclopedia: 1408, Nanjing: in the vast Wenyuan Pavilion hundreds of scholars in blue and red robes sit in long rows at low tables copying texts with brushes, stacks of thick yellow-bound volumes piled high on shelves to the ceiling, attendants carrying more books on poles; lattice windows let in pale light. No legible writing. Painted as a Ming court painting, fine line and soft colour on silk.
nurgan-commission: 1409-1413, Tyr above the lower Amur River: on a high cliff over the wide river stands a small Buddhist temple and stone steles, Ming soldiers and officials in robes at the site, while Nivkh and Jurchen people in fur and fish-skin clothing arrive in birch-bark canoes with sable furs; dense taiga forest, cold mist. No legible inscriptions. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape scroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
yongle-first-northern-campaign: 1410, the Onon River in Mongolia: an enormous Ming army camps along a winding river on the steppe, rows of tents, banners, horses and supply wagons stretching to the horizon, cavalry fording the water, supply camels resting on the bank; Mongol riders retreating over distant hills. Expansive view, small figures. Painted as a Ming court campaign handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
grand-canal-restored: 1411, Jining in Shandong: tens of thousands of labourers with shovels and baskets dig and line a canal channel with stone, building lock gates with timber sluice boards, while the first grain barges with square sails are towed upstream by men on the towpath; willows, embankments, farmland. Busy daytime panorama. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, crisp black line and light hand colour.
guizhou-province: 1413, Guiyang in Guizhou: a new walled prefectural city rising among steep green karst mountains, Ming officials in robes arriving on horseback with soldiers, Miao and Buyi villagers in indigo clothing and silver ornaments watching from terraced fields and stilt houses; clouds wrapping the peaks and a new stone road winding up the valley. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape hanging scroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
eastern-depot: 1420, Beijing: a narrow walled lane beside the palace at dusk, where eunuch agents in dark robes and tall hats slip through a gate into a compound, others watching an official's mansion from a teahouse window; lanterns just lit, the red walls of the palace beyond. Atmospheric and quiet, no violence. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with muted colour.
tang-saier-rebellion: 1420, the hills of Shandong near Qingzhou: a crowd of poor peasants armed with farm tools and spears gathers on a rocky mountainside camp, led by a woman in a plain dark robe holding a sword, seen from behind; corvée roads and a walled town below, autumn trees. Distant view, figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration of a popular tale, black line with light colour.
yongle-dies-yumuchuan: 1424, Yumuchuan on the Inner Mongolian grassland: a long imperial army column halted on the autumn steppe at dusk, a large yellow tent with silent attendants around it, banners drooping, horses grazing, soldiers standing quietly; low sun, rolling hills, a mood of sudden stillness. No figures in close-up. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and subdued colour on silk.
ming-withdrawal-vietnam: 1427, Chi Lang pass in Lang Son: a narrow valley between jagged limestone karst peaks shrouded in mist, where a Ming army column stalls on a muddy road as Vietnamese troops emerge from forested slopes; later in the scene, Ming soldiers march north out of the pass in long lines. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming landscape handscroll, ink washes and pale colour on silk.
zheng-he-death: 1433, Calicut on the Malabar coast: giant Ming treasure ships with many masts and red batten sails lie at anchor off a palm-fringed shore, small boats carrying goods to and from the beach, Kerala traders in white cloth and turbans on the sand; on one ship's deck, mourners gather quietly at a draped bier at sunset. Figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with hand colouring.
luchuan-campaigns: 1438, the Longchuan region on the Yunnan-Burma frontier: Ming troops in red jackets struggle through humid jungle hills with pack mules and baggage, crossing a rope bridge over a ravine, while Shan war elephants and wooden stockades appear in the misty valley ahead; banana trees and bamboo. Distant view. Painted as a Ming campaign handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
wang-zhen-dominance: 1442, Beijing palace: in an inner hall a eunuch in a richly embroidered robe stands beside a young emperor's throne, receiving memorials from kneeling officials while other eunuchs crowd near; ministers bow outside in the snowy courtyard beneath bare plum trees. Figures small, seen from a distance or behind. Painted as a Ming court painting, ink and rich colour on silk.
deng-maoqi-rebellion: 1448, Shaxian in the mountains of Fujian: tenant farmers and miners with hoes, picks and bamboo spears gather in a terraced valley below a landlord's compound, carrying baskets of rice, while smoke rises from mine entrances on the slopes; tea bushes, misty green hills. Distant view, figures small, no violence. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, black line and light colour.
defense-of-beijing-1449: 1449, Beijing: autumn outside the Deshengmen gate, Ming soldiers with firearms, cannon and crossbows mass on the walls and before the gate towers, while Oirat Mongol cavalry gather on the plain in the distance under smoky skies; fortified moat, banners on the ramparts. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming court painting of a battle, ink and colour on silk.
yingzong-returns: 1450, Beijing: a small carriage escorted by a few horsemen arrives through a city gate on a grey day, received by a modest group of officials; inside the palace, a quiet secluded compound with closed gates and bare trees, guards at the entrance. Subdued mood, figures small. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and muted colour on silk.
duomen-coup: 1457, Beijing: before dawn, a band of soldiers with torches and ladders breaks open the gate of the walled Southern Palace and escorts a figure in yellow toward the Fengtian hall; officials hurry across moonlit courtyards and bells ring from the gate tower. No figures in close-up, no violence. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with night-blue wash.
big-rattan-gorge: 1465, Big Rattan Gorge near Guiping in Guangxi: a deep river gorge between forested cliffs, where giant rattan vines once spanned the river; a Ming army camps along the banks and soldiers cut through the vine bridges with axes while smoke rises from hill stockades. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape scroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
western-depot: 1477, Beijing: a newly built office compound with grey brick walls near the Imperial City, eunuch agents in dark embroidered robes and tall black hats riding out through its gate on horseback, while officials in red robes outside the palace gate kneel with petitions raised in protest; spring willows along the moat, palace roofs gleaming beyond. Figures small and seen at a distance. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, crisp black line with light colour.
eight-legged-essay: 1487, the Beijing examination compound: long rows of narrow brick cells under tiled roofs, each holding a candidate in a blue robe bent over a plank desk with brush, ink stone and paper, a lamp and small food basket beside him; guards patrol the lanes and a watchtower rises at the centre. No legible writing on the papers. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, dense fine black line with light colour.
hongzhi-restoration: 1488, the Beijing palace: an orderly morning audience in a wide stone courtyard, ranks of civil officials in red robes with embroidered rank badges and black winged caps standing in neat lines before a great hall, a few senior ministers walking up the marble steps to present memorials; peaceful spring light, blossoming trees by the walls. Figures small. Painted as a Ming court painting, mineral colours and gold on silk.
wu-school-painting: 1500, Suzhou: a literati garden with taihu rocks, bamboo and a pond pavilion, where several scholar-painters in loose robes gather around a long table unrolling a landscape handscroll, one painting while others sip tea and a servant boy grinds ink; canals and whitewashed houses beyond the garden wall. Figures small, no legible writing. Painted in the Wu School manner of Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming, ink and light colour on paper.
longchang: 1508, Longchang in the mountains of Guizhou: a small rough stone cave dwelling and thatched hut among steep green karst peaks wreathed in night mist, a lone scholar in a plain robe sitting cross-legged at the cave mouth beneath a moonlit sky, a few local villagers' stilt houses below. Figure tiny, seen from behind. Painted as a Ming ink landscape hanging scroll in a spare literati style, ink and light colour on paper.
liu-jin-executed: 1510, Beijing: officials and soldiers carry chests out of a grand mansion with tiled gate roofs, unloading confiscated gold, silver ingots, jade and armour into carts in the courtyard, clerks recording with abacus and ledgers; crowds of curious townspeople watch from the street outside the gate. No violence shown, figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light hand colouring.
tome-pires-embassy: 1517, the Pearl River at Guangzhou: Portuguese carracks with square sails and high castles anchor off the walled city, firing a salute of smoke, while a small party of Europeans in doublets and hats is rowed ashore to meet Ming officials in red robes under parasols on the quay; junks, sampans and pagodas along the river. Figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour, crisp outlines.
prince-of-ning-rebellion: 1519, Poyang Lake in Jiangxi: a great fleet of rebel war junks chained together burns on the wide lake as fire boats drift into them, smoke billowing under a windy sky, while government ships in disciplined lines close in; the walled city of Nanchang far off on the shore, distant mountains. Panoramic, no gore. Painted as a Ming battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
great-rites: 1521, Beijing: outside the Zuoshunmen palace gate, scores of officials in red robes and black caps kneel on the stone pavement in protest, court tablets raised, while palace guards with staves approach along the side; tall red walls and yellow-tiled gate towers loom. No violence shown, figures small and seen from behind. Painted as a Ming court-style painting in ink and mineral colour on silk.
battle-of-tunmen: 1521, Tunmen (Tuen Mun) on the coast near the Pearl River estuary: Ming war junks with batten sails and fire arrows press in on a few Portuguese carracks anchored in a green-hilled bay, cannon smoke drifting across the water, small boats rowing between; rocky islands and fishing villages on the shore. Distant panorama. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print sea-battle illustration with light colour.
romance-three-kingdoms-printed: 1522, a Beijing print shop: craftsmen in plain robes carve pear-wood blocks, ink them and press sheets of paper, which are hung to dry and stitched into thread-bound volumes; one block shows an illustration of armoured horsemen at a peach orchard. Shelves of books, a customer browsing. No legible text. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, crisp black line with light colour.
ningbo-incident: 1523, Ningbo harbour: two rival Japanese tribute ships with matting sails moored at a quay beside a Ming customs building, armed Japanese retainers in kimono and topknots brandishing swords in the street as Chinese townspeople flee and smoke rises from a burning warehouse; the city wall and pagoda behind. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with muted colour.
water-margin-circulates: 1540, Hangzhou: a bookseller's open-fronted shop on a bustling street by West Lake, stacks of thread-bound volumes on tables, customers in scholar robes and merchants' caps leafing through illustrated pages showing heroes at a marshland stockade; a storyteller performs to a crowd at the teahouse next door. No legible text. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine line with light hand colouring.
shuangyu-raid: 1548, Shuangyu island in the Zhoushan archipelago: a smuggling harbour of wooden warehouses and Portuguese-style huts burns at dusk as Ming soldiers land from war junks, while foreign carracks and Chinese junks sail away from the cove; rocky green islands, gulls, and a rough grey sea under low clouds. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
gengxu-raid: 1550, the outskirts of Beijing: Mongol horsemen in fur hats drive off herds of cattle and carts of goods from burning villages on the plain, smoke rising across the fields, while the massive city walls and gate towers stand closed in the distance with soldiers watching from the battlements. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Ming court painting, ink and colour on silk, wide landscape.
shaanxi-earthquake: 1556, Huazhou in Shaanxi on the Wei River plain: the aftermath of a great earthquake in winter, collapsed loess cave dwellings along cracked hillsides, fallen city walls and toppled pagoda, survivors in padded robes gathering in open fields around small fires, the Hua Mountains looming in grey dawn. No bodies shown. Painted as a Ming ink landscape scroll with muted washes on paper.
wang-zhi-executed: 1559, Hangzhou: a richly dressed merchant-pirate captain in silk robes is led by guards through the gate of a provincial government compound, his junk with tall sails anchored in the bay behind, Ming officials in red robes waiting on the steps; West Lake hills and pagoda beyond. No violence shown, figures small and seen from behind. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, black line with light colour.
taizhou-wokou: 1561, Taizhou on the Zhejiang coast: Ming soldiers in disciplined twelve-man mandarin-duck formations, with long bamboo multi-branched spears, shields and halberds, advance across paddy fields toward pirate bands with long swords near a coastal walled town, drums and signal flags behind them; hills and the sea beyond. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print military manual illustration, crisp black line with light colour.
yan-song-falls: 1562, Beijing: a grand mansion with lacquered gates being closed by officials, a white-bearded elderly man in plain robes departing in a carriage under escort, servants carrying trunks and scrolls; spring rain on tiled roofs, onlookers holding umbrellas at the street corner. Figures small and from behind. Painted as a Ming court-style painting in ink and subdued colour on silk.
hai-rui-memorial: 1566, Beijing: an austere official in a plain worn robe and black cap kneels before a palace gate holding a sealed memorial in a box, a simple wooden coffin standing behind him on the pavement, servants waiting; massive red walls and yellow-tiled gate tower above. Figure small, seen from the side at a distance. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light colour.
longqing-trade: 1567, Yuegang (Haicheng) on the Jiulong River estuary in Fujian: a busy harbour where large ocean-going Fujian junks with red batten sails are loaded with silk and porcelain crates, merchants and porters crowding the quays, a customs office on the shore, chests of silver coins being counted; green hills and river mouth. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine line with light colour.
qi-great-wall: 1568, the mountains near Jizhou north of Beijing: the Great Wall snakes along steep ridges, labourers and soldiers carrying bricks up stone paths to build hollow two-storey brick watchtowers with arched windows, kilns smoking in the valley, mules hauling loads; autumn colours on the hills. Panoramic view, small figures. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
altan-peace: 1571, Datong border market at a Great Wall gate: Mongol herders in fur-trimmed robes lead horses and sheep to trade, Chinese merchants unpack bolts of silk, tea bricks and iron pots under awnings, officials supervise from a platform; the wall and beacon towers on the brown hills behind. Lively peaceful scene, figures small. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
manila-galleon-silver: 1573, Manila Bay: a Spanish galleon with tall masts and square sails anchored beside Chinese junks with batten sails, Chinese merchants unloading bales of silk and crates of porcelain onto the beach while Spanish soldiers and officials in morions and doublets count silver coins into chests; nipa huts, palm trees and a wooden fort. Painted as a late sixteenth-century colonial-era illustrated manuscript, ink and watercolour.
bencao-gangmu: 1578, Qizhou in Hubei: an elderly doctor in a plain robe works in a study crowded with dried herbs, roots, minerals and specimen jars, his manuscript pages spread across a long table, an assistant pounding medicines in a mortar; through the window, a herb garden and hillsides where he gathered plants. Figures small. No legible writing. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print herbal illustration, fine black line with light colour.
pan-jixun-river: 1578, Huai'an at the Yellow River and Huai confluence: crews of labourers build long earthen dikes reinforced with bundles of sorghum stalks and stone, narrowing a broad muddy yellow river, officials in robes inspecting on horseback with surveyors, boats carrying stone; willow-lined embankments and flat plain. Panoramic, small figures. Painted as a Ming hydraulic-works handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
wanli-land-survey: 1580, the countryside near Beijing: teams of surveyors with measuring ropes and bow-shaped measuring rods pace out rice and wheat fields, clerks in robes recording on scrolls under parasols, village elders and landlords standing by, boundary stakes in the soil; distant walled town and hills. No legible writing. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, crisp black line with light colour.
single-whip: 1581, a county yamen courtyard in north China: farmers in short jackets and straw hats line up to pay taxes in silver, clerks weighing small silver ingots on balance scales at a long table, cash boxes and ledgers, a magistrate in robes watching from the hall; carts outside the gate instead of labour gangs. No legible writing. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, black line with light colour.
zhang-juzheng-dies: 1582, Beijing: a large mansion with its gates sealed and guarded by soldiers, officials carrying confiscated chests and scrolls out through the courtyard, family members in white mourning clothes waiting quietly by the wall; autumn leaves drifting across the paving and a grey sky. Figures small and seen at a distance. Painted as a Ming court-style painting in ink and subdued colour on silk.
zhu-zaiyu-equal-temperament: 1584, Huaiqing in Henan: a prince-scholar's study where rows of bamboo pitch pipes of graded lengths lie on a table beside a long zither and an abacus, an elderly man in a simple robe calculating, an attendant tuning bells on a wooden rack; a courtyard garden beyond. Figure seen from behind, no legible writing. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
succession-dispute-wanli: 1586, Beijing palace: a vast empty audience hall with closed doors, officials in red robes kneeling in the courtyard with memorials raised, piles of unanswered memorials stacked on tables inside while eunuchs pass by; snow falling softly on golden roofs and marble balustrades. Figures small, no close-ups. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and mineral colour on silk.
journey-to-the-west: 1592, a Nanjing printing workshop: block carvers and printers in plain robes press sheets from carved woodblocks, freshly printed pages hanging to dry, one illustration showing a monk on a white horse with a monkey, a pig and a sandy-haired companion on a mountain road; customers browse finished books. No legible text. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, crisp line with light colour.
ordos-campaign: 1592, Ningxia (Yinchuan) beside the Yellow River: Ming troops build a long earthen dike around the walled city and divert river water to flood it, the walls rising from a brown lake, boats with soldiers floating near the gate, army camps on dry ground; the Helan Mountains behind. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Ming campaign handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
mining-tax-eunuchs: 1596, a busy canal city in the late Ming: a eunuch tax commissioner in embroidered robes arrives by boat with armed retainers, while merchants and shopkeepers close their shops and an angry crowd of townsmen gathers at the toll station on the canal bank, shaking fists; tiled shops and bridges. Figures small, no violence. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light colour.
battle-of-noryang: 1598, the Noryang Strait off Namhae in Korea at dawn: a great night sea battle ends as Korean panokseon warships and Ming junks surround and burn Japanese ships trying to escape, fire arrows and cannon smoke over the dark water, islands and mountains silhouetted against a red sky. Distant panorama, no individual figures in close-up, no gore. Painted in the style of a Joseon documentary painting, ink and colour on silk.
peony-pavilion: 1598, Linchuan in Jiangxi: a garden with a peony bed, rockeries, a willow and a small pavilion in spring, a young woman in Ming dress dreaming on a garden seat while a scholar appears among the blossoms; in the background, a playwright's study with a desk and lamp. Figures small and graceful. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print drama illustration in the Huizhou style, fine line with light colour.
bozhou-campaign: 1599, the Hailongtun mountaintop fortress near Zunyi in Guizhou: Ming armies in many columns climb steep forested ridges toward a stone fortress with gates on a high peak, cannon smoke rising, banners on every slope, clouds drifting through the deep valleys and gorges. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
kunyu-wanguo-quantu: 1602, Beijing: a scholar's hall where a huge printed world map on six joined panels hangs on a wall, showing oval-projected continents and seas with tiny ships and sea creatures, a Jesuit in Chinese scholar's robes and a Chinese official studying it with an armillary sphere on a table; no legible text. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
li-zhi-dies: 1602, a prison in Tongzhou east of Beijing: a bare cell with a straw mat, a small window letting in pale light, a few books and a brush on a low table, a lone elderly scholar in a plain robe seated with his back turned, gazing at the window; a guard's shadow at the door. Sombre and quiet, no violence. Painted as a Ming ink painting on paper, spare monochrome line.
donglin-academy: 1604, Wuxi: a modest academy compound with white walls and grey tiled roofs beside a stream, scholars in blue robes and square caps gathering in a lecture hall to listen to a teacher, others debating in a courtyard under old pines; boats on the canal outside. Figures small, no legible inscriptions. Painted as a Ming literati painting in the Wu School manner, ink and light colour on paper.
euclid-chinese: 1607, Beijing: a study where a Chinese scholar-official in a black hat and a Jesuit in Chinese scholar's robes sit at a table covered with geometric diagrams of triangles and circles, compasses, rulers and ink brushes, a globe and astrolabe nearby; a lattice window opens onto a winter courtyard. Figures seen from the side at a distance, no legible text. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
ryukyu-invaded-satsuma: 1609, Shuri on Okinawa: samurai troops from Satsuma in lacquered armour with matchlock muskets and banners advance up the hill toward the red-roofed castle on curving limestone walls, Ryukyuan defenders on the ramparts, ships anchored in the harbour below; subtropical trees, turquoise sea. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of an Edo-period Japanese handscroll, ink and colour on paper.
attack-with-club-case: 1615, the Beijing palace at dusk: a lone ragged man with a wooden club runs through a palace gate toward the heir's residence, eunuchs and guards in robes rushing to restrain him in a courtyard, lanterns swinging; red walls and yellow-tiled roofs. Figures small and at a distance. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light colour.
fall-of-fushun: 1618, Fushun on the Liaodong frontier: Jurchen banner cavalry in coloured armour and fur caps gather beneath banners of yellow, white, red and blue outside a walled Ming town, smoke rising from the gate towers, horsemen streaming through the gate; snowy hills and forests. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of an early Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk.
jin-ping-mei-printed: 1618, Suzhou: a late Ming book shop by a canal, merchants and scholars examining thread-bound illustrated novels, one leaf showing a wealthy merchant's household courtyard with gardens and women in fine robes; printers and binders at work in the back room with woodblocks and ink. No legible text. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine line and light colour.
feng-menglong-sanyan: 1620, Suzhou: an editor in a scholar's robe works at a desk piled with manuscripts beside a window overlooking a canal and arched stone bridge, while outside in the street a storyteller entertains a crowd of townspeople, porters and shop clerks; tiled roofs and boats. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
red-pill-case: 1620, the Beijing palace at night: in a dim imperial bedchamber, a lacquered tray holds a small dish of red pills beside a tea bowl, a silk-curtained bed in shadow, eunuchs and physicians waiting anxiously outside the door with lanterns; the courtyard silent under the moon. No figures in close-up. Painted as a Ming court painting, ink and deep mineral colour on silk.
palace-removal-case: 1620, the Beijing palace: before the great Palace of Heavenly Purity, officials in red robes stand in the courtyard while a procession of palace women and eunuchs carrying chests moves out through a side gate to another palace; a boy-emperor's sedan chair waits under parasols. Figures small. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and mineral colour on silk.
fall-of-shenyang-liaoyang: 1621, Liaoyang in Liaodong: Later Jin banner cavalry and infantry with siege ladders surround the walled city beside the Taizi River, smoke rising from the gate towers, Ming defenders on the walls, the white Liaoyang pagoda standing above the roofs; spring fields and distant hills. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of an early Qing battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
she-an-rebellion: 1621, Yongning in the mountains of southern Sichuan: Yi warriors in dark cloaks and turbans with spears and shields gather on a high mountain ridge above deep valleys, their fortified hilltop villages behind, a Ming walled town visible far below; clouds and terraced fields. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape scroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
battle-of-guangning: 1622, Guangning (Beizhen) in western Liaodong: a long Ming column of soldiers, refugees and ox-carts retreats westward across a frozen winter plain toward distant mountains, the walled town with its tall brick pagoda left behind, Later Jin banner cavalry visible on the far horizon; smoke from abandoned camps, bare trees and snow. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a late Ming ink handscroll with pale colour on silk.
sino-dutch-penghu: 1622-1624, the Penghu islands in the Taiwan Strait: a small square Dutch fort of earth and stone on a flat windswept island, Dutch East India Company ships with square sails anchored offshore, while a large fleet of Ming war junks and many soldiers land on the beach and set up camps around it; low coral-stone walls, choppy sea. Distant panorama. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch engraving, fine hatched line, lightly coloured.
dutch-formosa: 1624, Tayouan (Anping) in southwestern Taiwan: Dutch builders and Chinese labourers raise a square brick fort with angled bastions on a sandbar beside a lagoon, East India Company ships at anchor, Siraya villagers in loincloths watching from coconut palms on the mainland shore. Bright tropical day, figures small. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch topographical engraving with light watercolour, fine line.
donglin-purge: 1625, Beijing: the grim stone gate of the imperial guard prison on a cold grey morning, guards in embroidered robes leading several scholar-officials in plain robes and chains through the entrance, their families and students kneeling in the snowy street outside; crows on the wall.
