eg-alexandria-founded: 331 BCE, the Mediterranean coast of Egypt: surveyors and architects in Greek chitons mark out a grid of streets on a sandy strip between the sea and a lake, using barley meal sprinkled on the ground, flocks of birds pecking at it, ships in a harbour and an island offshore. Painted as a Hellenistic mosaic, small tesserae, pale blue sea and sandy ochres.
eg-library-of-alexandria: c. 283 BCE, Alexandria: a colonnaded hall of the Mouseion with shelves of papyrus rolls in pigeonholes, scholars in Greek himations reading and copying at tables, one drawing geometric figures on a wax tablet, a garden courtyard with a fountain outside and the harbour in the distance. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic Roman fresco, soft ochre, red and green.
eg-eratosthenes: c. 240 BCE, Alexandria: a scholar in a Greek himation stands in a sunlit paved courtyard of the Museum, beside a tall granite obelisk and a vertical bronze rod casting a short noon shadow on the flagstones, measuring the shadow's angle with a simple bronze instrument. Assistants hold wax tablets and a measuring cord; colonnades, palm trees and the distant harbour with the Pharos lighthouse lie beyond under a bright sky. One single continuous scene, no inset, no frame, no lettering. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic Roman fresco, warm light and earth colours.
eg-battle-of-zama: 202 BCE, Zama in Tunisia: on a dusty plain, Roman legionaries in bronze helmets and oval shields open lanes in their ranks as Carthaginian war elephants charge through, Numidian cavalry sweeping around the flanks, dust and olive trees, seen from a distance. No gore. Trumpeters sound horns from both lines, and distant hills frame the plain. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic, small coloured tesserae, warm earth tones.
eg-masinissa-numidia: c. 202 BCE, Cirta in Numidia: a fortified city on a rock plateau above a deep gorge, a Berber king on horseback with a beard and a diadem riding with light Numidian cavalry, horses without saddles, herds and wheat fields around the plateau. Village women carry water jars along the gorge path. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic of North Africa, warm ochres and greens.
eg-rosetta-stone-decree: 196 BCE, Memphis: inside a temple courtyard, a stone carver chisels a dark granite slab divided into three bands of fine script rendered as an illegible texture, priests in white linen and shaven heads standing around, a statue of a Ptolemaic king nearby, lotus columns behind. Painted in the style of a Ptolemaic Egyptian temple relief, flat colour and fine outlines.
eg-destruction-of-carthage: 146 BCE, Carthage: smoke and flames rise over a great harbour city with a circular naval harbour and tall houses on the Byrsa hill, Roman legionaries in bronze helmets on the walls, Roman ships in the bay, fleeing citizens far away. No gore. Siege towers stand against the broken walls, and the empty market lies covered in ash. Painted in the manner of a Roman fresco, smoky reds and dark ochres.
eg-jugurthine-war: c. 108 BCE, Numidia: Roman legionaries in mail with oval shields climb a rocky desert slope toward a Numidian stronghold on a high crag, Numidian horsemen fighting from the hilltop, and in the foreground Roman officers in a camp counting chests of silver. Pack mules wait at the foot of the slope under a hot sky. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic, warm ochres, reds and dark outlines.
eg-cleopatra-death: 30 BCE, Alexandria: Roman warships and legionaries arriving in the great harbour beneath the tall lighthouse of Pharos, the royal palace on the shore with its columned halls and a closed mausoleum building, Egyptian courtiers in mourning, a small cobra symbol carved on a pillar. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, deep red and black with soft modelling.
eg-ptolemy-almagest: c. 150 CE, Alexandria: an astronomer in a Greek himation sits writing in a study with an armillary sphere of bronze rings and star charts, scrolls on shelves, a window opening onto the night sky over the harbour with the lighthouse lit. An oil lamp burns beside a bronze astrolabe, and a sundial stands in the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Roman-Egyptian fresco, warm ochres and a dark blue sky.
eg-septimius-severus: c. 203 CE, Leptis Magna on the Libyan coast: a new marble four-way triumphal arch and colonnaded forum with Corinthian columns rising beside the sea, Roman citizens in togas, workers on scaffolding, ships in a rebuilt harbour. Carved friezes of a triumphal procession decorate the arch, merchants unload amphorae on the quay, and a theatre with stone seats faces the turquoise sea. Painted as a Roman North African mosaic, rich ochres and blues.
eg-arian-controversy: c. 318 CE, Alexandria: inside a basilica church with columns and lamps, a group of bearded Christian clergy in long robes debate fiercely around a table with scrolls, the bishop seated at the head, crowds of laypeople listening from the aisles. Light falls through high windows onto the mosaic floor. Painted in the style of a Late Antique Coptic fresco, bold outlines and flat earth colours.
eg-augustine-of-hippo: c. 396 CE, Hippo Regius on the Algerian coast: a bishop in a simple robe sits writing at a desk in a whitewashed room with scrolls and codices, a window onto a basilica courtyard and the Mediterranean, olive trees on the hills. A lamp flickers on the desk, and a few clergy wait at the door. Painted in the manner of a Late Antique North African mosaic, small tesserae, soft colours.
eg-hypatia: c. 415 CE, Alexandria: a quiet scholar's lecture room with an astrolabe, a geometry diagram on a board and scrolls, an empty chair at the front, and outside the window a distant agitated crowd moving along a colonnaded street toward a church, a sombre late afternoon light. No violence depicted. Painted in the style of a Late Antique fresco, muted earth tones.
eg-vandals-take-carthage: 439 CE, Carthage: Vandal warriors with long hair, cloaks and spears pour through a gate in the great walls of a Roman city, citizens in tunics watching from colonnaded streets, Roman grain ships at anchor in the harbour being seized. No gore. Smoke rises from a single burning villa. Painted in the manner of a Late Roman North African mosaic, ochres, reds and blues.
eg-vandalic-war: 533 CE, Ad Decimum near Carthage: Byzantine cataphract cavalry in mail and plumed helmets charge across a dusty plain, Vandal horsemen scattering, the walls of Carthage on the horizon, dust rising, seen from far away. No gore. Byzantine infantry with round shields follow in close ranks, a general's banner flies above them, and olive groves line the road. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic, gold background and coloured stone tesserae.
eg-muslim-conquest-egypt: 641 CE, the Babylon fortress at Old Cairo: Arab horsemen in mail and turbans with lances set up camp beside the Nile near a Roman fortress with round towers, Byzantine soldiers on the walls, Coptic churches and palm groves around, boats on the river. Siege engines stand ready before the gates. Painted in the style of an early Islamic manuscript painting, flat colours and gold.
eg-kairouan-founded: 670 CE, Kairouan on the Tunisian plain: Arab soldiers and builders lay out a new garrison town in a flat scrubland, mud-brick walls and a first simple mosque with a courtyard and a square minaret rising, camels and tents around, olive trees. Workers dig a large cistern for water, and the hot sun beats down. Painted in the manner of an Islamic manuscript painting, warm ochres and soft blues.
eg-tariq-crosses: 711 CE, the Strait of Gibraltar: ships with lateen sails crowded with Berber and Arab soldiers cross the narrow strait from Tangier, the great limestone Rock of Gibraltar rising ahead, horses on deck, the African coast with mountains behind. Gulls circle above the waves, a small boat carries a commander ahead of the fleet, and morning mist clings to the rock's slopes. Painted in the style of an Andalusian Islamic manuscript painting, flat colour and gold.
eg-al-qarawiyyin: 859 CE, Fez: a mosque of whitewashed walls and green-tiled roofs being built in the narrow medina, a woman of means in a veil seen from behind with craftsmen, and students in robes sitting in a courtyard with a fountain around a teacher, books on low stands. Painted in the manner of a Moroccan and Andalusian Islamic manuscript painting, rich greens and gold.
eg-fatimid-caliphate-founded: 909 CE, Raqqada near Kairouan: Kutama Berber horsemen in white robes with banners ride into a palace city of domed buildings and gardens, a leader in robes received by crowds, palm trees and the Tunisian plain. Drummers and flag bearers lead the procession, while townspeople in turbans crowd the gates and rooftops, and a golden parasol is held over the rider. Painted in the style of an Islamic manuscript painting, flat colours and gold.
eg-fatimid-conquest-cairo: 969 CE, the Nile near Fustat: Fatimid soldiers and builders lay out the walls and gates of a new royal city in the desert, marking lines with ropes and stakes, camels carrying bricks, the Nile and the pyramids in the distance at dawn. Astrologers watch the sky for the auspicious hour. Painted in the manner of a Fatimid lustreware and manuscript painting, gold and ochre.
eg-saladin-ayyubid: 1171 CE, Cairo: a Friday prayer in a great mosque with a columned courtyard and wooden pulpit, a large crowd of worshippers seen from behind in turbans and robes, soldiers in mail at the doors, minarets of Cairo around. No religious figures depicted. Sunlight falls on carpets and hanging lamps, and the voice of a preacher seems to fill the hall. Painted in the style of an Islamic manuscript painting, gold and lapis blue.
eg-battle-of-mansurah: 1250, Mansurah in the Nile delta: Mamluk cavalry in turbans and mail with curved swords fight among narrow streets and canals against French knights in surcoats with crosses, crusader banners falling, palm trees, seen from a distance. No gore. Crowds of townspeople watch from rooftops, and broken lances litter the street while the river glints beyond the houses. Painted in the manner of a Mamluk manuscript painting, flat colours and gold.
eg-ibn-khaldun-muqaddimah: 1377, Qal'at Ibn Salama in western Algeria: a scholar in a turban and robe sits writing in a whitewashed room in a castle on a rocky hill, books and manuscripts around, a window over a wide valley with Berber tents and herds. Ink pots and reed pens lie on a low table, and a lamp burns at dusk. Painted in the manner of a Maghrebi manuscript painting, warm ochres and greens.
eg-battle-of-ridaniya: 1517, Ridaniya outside Cairo: Ottoman Janissaries with muskets and tall white caps and cannons fire across a dusty plain at Mamluk cavalry in mail and turbans, smoke rising, the minarets and citadel of Cairo in the distance. No gore. Banners of both armies fly above the dust, Ottoman cavalry wait in the wings, and camels carry supplies at the rear of the lines. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature, flat colours and gold.
eg-french-campaign-egypt: 1798, Embabeh near Cairo: French infantry squares in blue coats and bicorne hats fire on charging Mamluk horsemen in brilliant robes and turbans, smoke drifting, the Giza pyramids on the horizon. No gore. Palm trees line the Nile behind the battle, villagers watch from mud-brick houses at a distance, and French officers on horseback direct the fire inside the squares. Painted as a late eighteenth-century European history painting, oil on canvas, warm desert light.
eg-muhammad-ali-rise: 1805, Cairo: the citadel above the city with domes and minarets, a new governor in Ottoman dress and a turban seen small from behind on a terrace overlooking soldiers drilling in European style, a cotton field and a factory chimney below. Mosque domes catch the evening light over the city. Painted in the style of an early nineteenth-century watercolour by a European traveller, soft light.
eg-french-invasion-algeria: 1830, Sidi Fredj near Algiers: French troops in blue coats and red trousers land from rowing boats on a sandy beach, warships with sails in the bay, a small white tower on a peninsula, Algerian horsemen watching from the hills. Cannon are being hauled through the sand, smoke rises from a warship's guns, and supply crates pile up on the shore under a bright June sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century French history painting, oil on canvas.
eg-suez-canal-opens: 1869, Port Said: a procession of steamships with flags and smoking funnels enters the new canal, crowds watching from the banks and pavilions, sailing ships and boats in the harbour, desert stretching beyond. A long sandy embankment edges the straight channel, Egyptian dignitaries and European guests fill a decorated grandstand, and fireworks are prepared for the evening celebration. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine lines and many small figures.
eg-british-occupation: 1882, Tel el-Kebir in the eastern Egyptian desert: British infantry in red and khaki uniforms advance at dawn across sand toward earthwork entrenchments defended by Egyptian soldiers in tarbushes, smoke from cannon, a railway and canal nearby. No gore. The pale light of sunrise spreads over the dunes, bayonets glint in long lines, and cavalry and artillery follow behind the advancing infantry across the sand. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
eg-el-alamein: 1942, El Alamein in the Western Desert: a night artillery barrage lights the horizon, columns of tanks and trucks moving forward across flat sand, infantry in khaki shorts and helmets, minefields marked with tape. No gore. Searchlights sweep the sky, dust trails rise behind the vehicles, and the dark outline of a ridge stands on the horizon. Painted as a 1940s war artist's watercolour, sand tones and orange flashes.
eg-revolution-1952: 1952, Cairo: tanks and army trucks halted in a broad city square at dawn, soldiers in khaki uniforms and caps standing beside them, a crowd of Cairenes in tarbooshes, galabiyas and summer suits gathering to watch. Belle Epoque apartment buildings with iron balconies line the square, people leaning from the balconies; tram cars and horse carts wait behind the tanks. Soft summer morning light and dust in the air. One single continuous street scene, no inset, no frame, no signs or lettering. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour.
eg-algerian-war: 1954, the Aures mountains in Algeria: a rugged, rocky landscape of steep ridges and Berber villages of stone houses, small groups of fighters in djellabas with rifles moving along a path at dusk, a French army post on a distant ridge. No violence shown. Olive trees and terraced fields cling to the slopes. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, earthy browns and greys.
eg-suez-crisis: 1956, Port Said: the canal entrance seen from the waterfront, dark smoke rising over the harbour, the hulls of ships sunk in the channel to block it, and paratroopers drifting down in the far distance. Egyptian civilians and a few soldiers watch from a quay lined with arcaded colonial buildings; fishing boats sit idle at the quay. A long stone breakwater runs out into the grey water with an empty stone pedestal at its end. No gore, no statues of torch-bearing figures, no lettering. Painted as a muted 1950s documentary watercolour, grey and blue tones.
eg-tunisian-revolution: 2010, Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia: a dusty provincial town street with whitewashed buildings, an abandoned wooden fruit cart in the foreground near a government building, and further along the road a crowd gathering at a distance under an overcast December sky. No figures in close-up. Shop shutters are half closed, and a scrawny palm leans over the road. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale ochre and grey.
eu-stonehenge: c. 3000 BCE, Salisbury Plain, Wiltshire: Neolithic farmers in hide and woven wool garments dig a great circular ditch with red-deer antler picks, piling white chalk into a bank, while others carry baskets of earth; a ring of wooden posts marks the centre, cattle graze on the rolling green downland, and a low winter sun sets on the horizon. Painted in the manner of a modern archaeological reconstruction in watercolour, inspired by the earth tones of Neolithic chalk and grooved-ware pottery, soft light.
eu-troy-founded: c. 3000 BCE, the hill of Hisarlik near the Dardanelles: a small fortified settlement of mud-brick and stone houses with a thick stone wall and a gate on a low hill above a marshy plain, villagers in wool tunics carrying jars, fishing boats on a bay, the narrow strait and the hills of Thrace beyond. Painted in the style of an Early Bronze Age Aegean pottery painting, simple dark brown figures on a pale clay ground.
eu-bell-beaker: c. 2800 BCE, Zambujal, Portugal: a hilltop fortified settlement with round stone towers above a river valley, a potter shaping a tall bell-shaped cup decorated with bands of comb-impressed patterns, an archer with a stone wrist guard testing a bow, a smith casting a copper dagger over a small fire, pine trees and the distant Atlantic. Painted as a muted archaeological watercolour reconstruction, warm reddish earth and pale stone.
eu-knossos-palace: c. 1900 BCE, Knossos in Crete: a sprawling palace of many storeys around a great central court, red-painted downward-tapering wooden columns, light wells and painted walls, people in colourful flounced skirts and kilts carrying storage jars to magazines, horns of consecration on the roofline, olive groves and Mount Ida in the distance. Painted in the style of a Minoan fresco, vivid reds, blues and ochres, lively flowing figures.
eu-thera-eruption: c. 1600 BCE, Akrotiri on Thera: a towering column of grey and black ash rises from the volcano in the centre of the island, lightning flickering in the cloud, ash falling over the multi-storey stone houses of a harbour town, its people in boats rowing away across a darkened sea, empty streets with storage jars. No bodies. Painted in the style of the Akrotiri wall paintings, swallows and lilies in a frieze, ochres and blues.
eu-mask-of-agamemnon: c. 1550 BCE, Mycenae in the Argolid: in a circle of upright stone slabs on a rocky hillside, mourners in woollen robes lower a ruler wrapped in cloth into a deep shaft grave, a beaten gold mask over his face, bronze swords with inlaid daggers, gold cups and amber beads laid beside him, hills and olive trees behind. Painted in the style of a Mycenaean fresco, flat colour and bold outlines.
eu-mycenaeans-take-knossos: c. 1450 BCE, Knossos in Crete: Mycenaean warriors in boar's-tusk helmets and figure-of-eight shields arrive at the partly burned palace, scribes in a store room counting goods on small clay tablets of linear script rendered as indistinct marks, Minoan servants carrying jars, smoke-stained columns and a quiet central court. Painted in the style of a late Minoan-Mycenaean fresco, ochres, reds and blues.
eu-lion-gate: c. 1250 BCE, Mycenae: a massive gateway of enormous stone blocks with a huge lintel and above it a triangular relief of two standing lions facing a column, Cyclopean walls winding around the rocky citadel, a chariot drawn by two horses entering, soldiers in boar's-tusk helmets on the walls, olive trees and mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Mycenaean fresco, flat colours, bold outlines.
eu-trojan-war: c. 1200 BCE, the plain before Troy: high stone walls and towers of a citadel on a hill above a plain by the sea, a large camp of Greek ships drawn up on the beach, warriors in bronze armour, crested helmets and round shields in the distance, and a great wooden horse standing before the walls. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, black figures on an orange clay ground.
eu-dorian-invasion: c. 1100 BCE, Laconia: a long column of migrants in simple wool tunics and cloaks with herds of sheep and goats, ox carts and spears moving down a mountain pass into the fertile Eurotas valley, a ruined Mycenaean palace on a hill, the Taygetus mountains rising behind. Painted in the style of a Greek Geometric vase painting, black silhouettes in bands on pale clay.
eu-first-olympics: 776 BCE, Olympia in Elis: a footrace of young athletes on a simple earthen track in a green valley beside a sacred grove of olive and plane trees, spectators on the grassy slopes, an altar of Zeus with smoke rising, the river Alpheios flowing nearby. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, running figures in profile on an orange ground.
eu-syracuse-founded: 734 BCE, Syracuse in Sicily: Greek colonists in tunics land from wooden ships with square sails onto the island of Ortygia, carrying amphorae, tools and a sacred fire, men marking out plots, local Sicel people watching from the hills, the bright sea and sheltered harbour. Painted in the style of a Corinthian vase painting, animal friezes and figures in black and purple on cream.
eu-solon: c. 594 BCE, Athens: a bearded lawgiver in a himation seen from behind addresses citizens in the Agora, poor farmers with tools listening, wooden boundary stones marking mortgaged land being pulled up from the fields on the hillside, the rocky Acropolis rising behind. Merchants and sailors gather around the speaker, and a wooden board stands nearby. Painted in the style of an Attic black-figure vase painting, figures in profile on orange clay.
eu-cleisthenes: 508 BCE, Athens: citizens in himations gather on the Pnyx hill, some casting pebbles into urns, others scratching names on pottery sherds for ostracism, a council of men seated on benches in the Agora below, the Acropolis and its early temples above. Grey olive trees climb the slopes, and a herald stands on a speaker's platform. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on a black ground.
eu-marathon: 490 BCE, the plain of Marathon in Attica: Athenian hoplites in bronze crested helmets, greaves and round shields run in a dense line toward Persian soldiers in trousers and soft caps near the beach, Persian ships at anchor in the bay, marshes and mountains around. No gore. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, dynamic figures in profile.
eu-thermopylae: 480 BCE, Thermopylae: a narrow pass between steep mountain cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek hoplites with red cloaks and bronze shields standing shoulder to shoulder at a rebuilt stone wall, a vast Persian army stretching far away along the coast road. No gore. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on black.
eu-salamis: 480 BCE, the strait of Salamis: Greek triremes with bronze rams and three banks of oars ram larger Persian ships in narrow waters, the island of Salamis on one side and the mountains of Attica on the other, a royal throne on a hillside watching. No gore. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, ships in a frieze on orange clay.
eu-parthenon: c. 447 BCE, the Acropolis of Athens: a marble Doric temple under construction, workers on wooden scaffolding carving the frieze, oxen hauling marble drums up a ramp, a sculptor overseeing statues in a workshop, the city and the sea below. Painters apply bright colours to the finished metopes, and citizens climb the hill to watch the work. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, warm orange figures on black.
eu-peloponnesian-war: 431 BCE, Attica: Spartan hoplites in red cloaks and bronze helmets ravage olive groves and wheat fields outside Athens, smoke rising from farmhouses, Athenians watching from the Long Walls that run to the port of Piraeus with triremes in the harbour. No gore. Crowds of rural refugees shelter in makeshift huts between the walls, and the harbour bristles with masts. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting.
eu-socrates: 399 BCE, Athens: a simple stone prison cell lit by a small window, an old bearded man in a himation seated on a bed surrounded by grieving friends and students, a cup on a low stool, lamplight and evening shadows, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on a black ground.
eu-alexander-campaign: 334 BCE, the Granicus river: Macedonian cavalry with spears charge across a shallow river and up a steep bank against Persian horsemen, a young king with a white plumed helmet small in the centre, dust and water spray. No gore. Persian archers stand on the far bank, the plain stretching beyond to distant hills, and banners flutter in the wind. Painted in the style of the Alexander Mosaic from Pompeii, small stone tesserae, earth tones.
eu-first-punic-war: 241 BCE, the Aegates Islands off Sicily: Roman war galleys with corvus boarding bridges and bronze rams engage Carthaginian ships laden with supplies in a choppy sea, rocky islands on the horizon. No gore. Sails are lowered for battle, oars churn the water white, marines with shields crowd the decks, and gulls wheel above the masts under a windy spring sky. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, dark blue sea and red-brown ships.
eu-hannibal-alps: 218 BCE, the western Alps: a long column of soldiers, horses, mules and African war elephants struggling along a narrow snowy mountain path, steep cliffs and glaciers above, Gallic tribesmen watching from rocky ridges. Soldiers in cloaks lead pack animals by the bridle, an elephant's driver urges it forward, and snow swirls in a cold wind over the pass. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, cool whites and greys, figures small against vast mountains.
eu-cannae: 216 BCE, Cannae in Apulia: a dusty summer plain by the Aufidus river, a huge Roman army in dense ranks being slowly enclosed by Carthaginian, Spanish and Gallic infantry and Numidian cavalry, seen from far above. No gore. Dust rises from thousands of feet, the river glints on one side of the field, cavalry clash on the wings, and low hills frame the horizon under a hot sky. Painted in the style of a Roman mosaic, small tesserae, warm earth colours.
eu-pydna: 168 BCE, Pydna in Macedonia: Roman legionaries with oval shields and short swords press into gaps in the Macedonian phalanx, its long pikes tilting, the slopes of Mount Olympus in the background, a river and dust. No gore. Elephants stand at the edge of the field, cavalry wait in reserve, and the evening sun lights the dust above the struggling lines. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic relief, figures in profile, marble texture.
eu-third-punic-war: 146 BCE, Carthage, Tunisia: Roman soldiers and engineers pull down the walls of a captured harbour city, smoke rising from the Byrsa hill, the circular naval harbour empty, a plough being drawn symbolically across the scorched ground. No gore. Roman officers watch from horseback, the bay is crowded with Roman ships, and wisps of smoke drift across the empty streets toward the sea. Painted in the manner of a Roman fresco, smoky reds and dark ochres.
eu-gallic-wars: 52 BCE, Alesia in Burgundy: Roman legionaries build a double ring of wooden palisades, ditches and towers around a hilltop Gallic town, Gallic warriors with long hair and shields on the walls above, the green Burgundian hills around. Siege engines stand ready behind the earthworks, a relieving Gallic army gathers on a distant ridge, and Roman soldiers dig trenches under an overcast autumn sky. Painted in the style of a Roman relief, carved stone figures, a long horizontal frieze.
eu-rubicon: 49 BCE, the Rubicon in northern Italy: a Roman general on horseback seen from behind crosses a small river at a ford, followed by a legion with eagle standards and shields, a dawn mist over poplars and fields. Soldiers splash through the shallow water, horses tossing their heads, and a stone milestone stands by the road on the far bank. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, soft greens and ochres.
eu-caesar-assassinated: 44 BCE, Rome: the portico of the Theatre of Pompey, a group of senators in white togas crowding around one man at the far end of a columned hall, seen from a distance, a toga fallen on the floor, a statue on a pedestal. No gore. Daggers glint faintly in the crowd. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, deep red and ochre with soft modelling.
eu-augustus: 27 BCE, Rome: senators in white togas assemble in the Senate House, presenting an oak-leaf crown and a golden shield to a man in a toga seen from behind, the Forum outside with temples. Lictors with rods stand at the doors, citizens crowd the steps outside, and laurel trees frame the entrance under a bright sky. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, warm red and ochre, figures in a frieze.
eu-crisis-third-century: 235 CE, Moguntiacum on the Rhine: a Roman legionary camp of wooden and stone buildings by a wide river, soldiers in mail with oval shields gathered in an angry crowd around a commander's tent, smoke rising on the far bank, grey sky. No gore. Merchants close their shops near the gate, and a few coins lie scattered on the ground. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, dark tones.
eu-tetrarchy: 293 CE, Nicomedia in Bithynia: four emperors in purple cloaks and military dress stand together embracing on a palace terrace, guards in mail around, the Gulf of Izmit and hills behind. Ships sail on the gulf, and clerks with scrolls wait in the colonnade behind the emperors. Painted in the style of the Porphyry Tetrarchs sculpture rendered as a Late Roman mosaic, stiff stylised figures, purple and red.
eu-milvian-bridge: 312 CE, the Milvian Bridge near Rome: an army with shields painted with a Chi-Rho symbol crosses the Tiber on a stone bridge, the river crowded with boats and a wooden pontoon collapsing, Roman soldiers on horseback, a sign of light in the sky. No gore. Banners and trumpets crowd the riverbank. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, small coloured tesserae, warm earth tones.
eu-constantinople: 330 CE, Constantinople on the Bosporus: a new city of colonnaded streets, a large forum with a porphyry column and a statue on top, a hippodrome, a palace overlooking the sea, crowds at a dedication ceremony, ships in the Golden Horn. Priests and officials process with incense, and new marble statues line the avenue. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic, gold background and coloured tesserae.
eu-adrianople: 378 CE, Adrianople in Thrace: Gothic cavalry charge from the hills onto a Roman army on a dusty plain in summer heat, a circle of Gothic wagons, burning fields, Roman legionaries in mail with shields. No gore. Smoke from burning grass drifts over the field, Gothic infantry press forward from behind the wagons, and Roman standards lean and waver in the dust. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, earth colours.
eu-division-of-empire: 395 CE, Milan: in a single wide palace hall, two young emperors, Arcadius and Honorius, in purple robes and pearl diadems stand side by side at the centre on a raised marble step, seen at a distance. Courtiers in embroidered Late Roman tunics and cloaks and generals in scale armour gather on either side, turning toward one or the other brother. Tall columns and arched windows let light fall onto a patterned marble floor. One continuous scene, no panels, seams or frames, no lettering or maps with writing. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, gold and earth tones.
eu-sack-of-rome-410: 410 CE, Rome: Visigothic warriors with long hair and cloaks enter the city through the Salarian Gate at night, carrying away treasure, smoke rising over the temples and basilicas, citizens fleeing into churches. No gore. Torches light the narrow streets, carts are piled with silver vessels and fine cloth, the Colosseum looms dark in the background, and frightened families gather on the steps of a basilica. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, flat colours.
eu-catalaunian-plains: 451 CE, the Catalaunian Plains in Champagne: Roman and Visigothic armies with shields and banners meet Hunnic horse archers on a vast flat plain, dust rising, a wagon camp in the distance. No gore. Roman standards and Visigothic banners rise above the infantry, Hunnic riders draw bows at full gallop, a low ridge rises at the centre of the field, and a red sunset glows over the plain. Painted in the style of an illuminated manuscript, flat colours and gold.
eu-sack-of-rome-455: 455 CE, Rome: Vandal ships at the mouth of the Tiber being loaded with statues, gold vessels and treasure from the city, Vandal warriors carrying bronze tiles stripped from a temple roof, the city on its hills behind. No gore. Citizens watch quietly from the city walls, a bishop in robes stands at a gate, and warriors wheel carts of loot along a paved Roman road toward the river. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript.
eu-476-fall-of-western-roman-empire: 476 CE, Ravenna: a boy emperor in purple robes seen from behind hands over his diadem and robes to a Germanic general with long hair and a fur cloak, in a palace hall with mosaics on the walls, soldiers in mail around. Courtiers lower their eyes, and a lamp burns before an empty throne. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic from Ravenna, gold ground.
eu-496-baptism-of-clovis: 496 CE, Reims: a Frankish king with long hair kneels in a baptismal font in a stone church, a bishop pouring water from a vessel, Frankish warriors in cloaks watching, candles and incense. The scene is seen from the back of the nave, with the figures small, coloured light falling from high windows, monks singing, and a dove descending above the font. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold leaf and bright pigments.
eu-732-battle-of-tours: 732, between Tours and Poitiers: Frankish infantry in a dense shield wall with axes and spears stand on a wooded rise while Umayyad cavalry in mail and turbans charge from the plain, banners flying. No gore. Autumn leaves blow across the field, Frankish nobles on horseback wait behind the infantry, and the Roman road to Tours runs in the distance past forests and small fields. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, flat colours.
eu-793-lindisfarne-raid: 793, Lindisfarne off the Northumbrian coast: Viking longships with square sails beached on the sand of a small island, Norse raiders with axes carrying chests from a stone monastery, monks fleeing across the tidal flats, grey sea. No gore. Seabirds wheel over the dunes, and a stone cross stands on the shore. Painted in the style of an insular illuminated manuscript like the Lindisfarne Gospels.
eu-800-charlemagne-crowned: 800, Rome: in the basilica of Old St Peter's on Christmas Day, a tall king in a cloak kneels at the altar while a pope places a crown on his head, clergy and Frankish nobles around, mosaics and candlelight. The figures are seen small from the back of the crowded basilica, lamps hanging from the beams. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold leaf and lapis.
eu-843-treaty-of-verdun: 843, Verdun: three Carolingian kings in crowns and robes sit at a table in a tent or hall, a large parchment between them, nobles and bishops standing around, banners of three kingdoms outside. Clerks with quills copy the agreement, the walls of Verdun and the river Meuse are visible through an arched window, horses wait outside, and an autumn light fills the hall. Painted in the style of a Carolingian illuminated manuscript, gold and purple.
